Ben and Mia liked to play on the beach. They liked to dig in the sand and look for shells. One day, they found a big shell that was closed. They wondered what was inside.
"Maybe it is a pearl," Ben said.
"Maybe it is a treasure," Mia said.
They tried to open the shell, but it was too hard. They needed something to pry it open.
"Look, there is a rock," Ben said. He picked up the rock and hit the shell with it. But the shell did not open. It only made a loud noise.
"Stop, you are hurting it," Mia said. She took the rock from Ben and put it down. She looked at the shell and saw a tiny hole. She heard a soft voice coming from the hole.
"Please, don't hurt me," the voice said. "I am an oyster, and this is my home."
Ben and Mia were surprised. They did not know that shells could talk.
"Sorry, we did not know," Ben said.
"We just wanted to see what was inside," Mia said.
The oyster said, "I understand, but I need my shell to protect me. If you open it, I will die."
Ben and Mia felt sorry for the oyster. They did not want to hurt it or make it die.
"OK, we will not open it," Ben said.
"We will leave you alone," Mia said.
They put the shell back on the sand, gently.
"Thank you, you are very thoughtful," the oyster said.
The oyster said, "Can I ask you a favor?"
"Sure, what is it?" Ben and Mia said.
The oyster said, "Can you lend me some water? I am very thirsty, and the sun is very hot."
Ben and Mia nodded. They ran to the sea and filled their buckets with water. They poured some water over the shell, and the oyster smiled.
"Thank you, you are very kind," the oyster said.
Ben and Mia smiled, too. They felt happy that they helped the oyster. They said goodbye to the oyster and went to play some more. They decided to look for other shells that were open, and not bother the ones that were closed. They learned that shells had feelings, too.

As Pandy reached for the bamboo leaves, the branch broke and he started to fall. But just in time, his friend Ellie the elephant came running. She saw Pandy falling and knew she had to save him. Ellie used her long trunk to catch Pandy before he hit the ground. 
Pandy was so happy that Ellie saved him. He hugged Ellie and thanked her for being a great friend. From that day on, Pandy always made sure to look for broken branches before climbing trees. Her mom cuddled her and said “next time, sweetheart, don't ignore mommy.” Joy nodded and promised she would listen.

One sunny day, the bald squirrel was playing near a big tree. He saw a big nut on the ground. He picked it up and looked at it. The other squirrels saw the nut and wanted it too. They all ran to the bald squirrel, but something unexpected happened.
As the squirrels got closer, the big nut started to grow hair! The hair grew longer and longer. The bald squirrel put the nut on his head. Now, he had hair too! The other squirrels were amazed. They all wanted a nut like that. The bald squirrel smiled and shared the nuts with his friends. From that day on, they never mentioned the bald squirrel again.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play football in the park. They have a red ball and two goals. They take turns to kick the ball and score.
One day, a big boy comes to the park. He has a blue ball and a mean face. He says, "I want to play football with you. But I am better than you. I will win and you will lose."
Tom and Sam do not like the big boy. He is rude and competitive. They say, "No, thank you. We are having fun by ourselves. You can play somewhere else."
The big boy gets angry. He says, "No, I will play here. And I will take your red ball. It is mine now." He grabs the red ball and runs away.
Tom and Sam are sad and mad. They want their red ball back. They hope the big boy will be nice and give it back. They chase him and shout, "Stop! That is our ball! Give it back!"
The big boy laughs and runs faster. He thinks he is smart and strong. He does not care about Tom and Sam. He only cares about himself.
But he does not see a big rock in his way. He trips and falls. He drops the red ball and the blue ball. He hurts his knee and cries.
Tom and Sam catch up with him. They see him crying and holding his knee. They feel sorry for him. They say, "Are you okay? Do you need help?"
The big boy is surprised. He expects Tom and Sam to be mean and take his blue ball. He says, "Why are you nice to me? I was mean to you. I took your red ball."
Tom and Sam say, "Because we are friends. And friends are nice to each other. Even if they are different or competitive. You can have your blue ball. And we can have our red ball. Or we can share and play together."
The big boy feels ashamed. He says, "I am sorry. I was wrong. I was not a good friend. Can you forgive me? Can we play together?"
Tom and Sam smile and nod. They say, "Yes, we can. We can play football together. And we can have fun. And we can be friends."
They help the big boy up and give him a hug. They pick up their balls and go to the goals. They play football together. And they have fun. And they are friends.

Lily and Sam were playing in the park with their mom. They saw a big tent with many colors. They wanted to see what was inside.
"Can we go, mom?" Lily asked.
"Sure, but be careful and stay together," mom said.
Lily and Sam ran to the tent. They opened the flap and went in. It was wide and dark inside. They saw many things: a lamp, a rug, a basket, a book.
"Wow, look at this!" Sam said. He picked up the book and opened it. It had pictures of animals and places.
Lily saw the basket and looked inside. She found a hat, a scarf, a necklace, and a mask. She put them on and laughed.
"I'm a princess!" she said.
Sam put down the book and saw the mask. He wanted to try it too. He put it on and said:
"I'm a lion! Roar!"
They played with the things and pretended to be different people and animals. They had fun and forgot about the time.
Then they heard mom's voice outside.
"Lily, Sam, where are you? It's time to go home!"
They took off the things and put them back in the basket. They closed the book and left the lamp on. They ran out of the tent and hugged mom.
"Sorry, mom, we were playing," Lily said.
"We found a lot of things in the tent," Sam said.
"Did you have fun?" mom asked.
"Yes, we did!" they said.
They told mom what they saw and did in the tent. Mom smiled and said:
"You made a great discovery today. But remember, always ask before you touch other people's things. They might not like it."
Lily and Sam nodded and said:
"Okay, mom. We're sorry."
They said goodbye to the tent and went home. They were happy and tired. They dreamed of the things they saw and did in the tent.

Joey and Tim became friends. They played and talked for a long time. Joey knew he had to go home soon. "I have to go, Tim," said Joey. Tim said, "Wait! I have a gift for you." Joey did not know what the gift was, but he was excited.
When Joey got home, he found a shiny rock in his pocket. It was the gift from Tim. Joey smiled and knew he had made a special friend. From that day on, Joey always remembered his adventure in the hole and his tiny friend Tim.

"Work, work, work!" Tom said, as he scooped up some dirt and threw it over his shoulder. He did not use his bucket. He thought it was too slow. He wanted to make the pit deeper and bigger.
But Tom did not look where he was throwing the dirt. He did not see that Lily was behind him. He did not hear her say, "Hey, watch out!"
Splash! The dirt landed on Lily's head and face. She gasped and coughed. She felt the dirt in her eyes and mouth. She was angry and sad.
"Tom, you are mean!" Lily said, as she wiped the dirt off her face. "You threw dirt on me! You hurt me!"
Tom turned around and saw Lily. He saw the dirt on her. He felt sorry and scared. He did not mean to hurt her. He was just working.
"Lily, I am sorry!" Tom said, as he ran to her. "I did not see you! I did not mean to throw dirt on you! Are you okay?"
Lily looked at Tom. She saw that he was sorry. She felt a little better. She was still angry and sad, but she was also his best friend.
"I am okay," Lily said, as she hugged Tom. "But you have to be careful. You have to use your bucket. You have to watch out."
Tom nodded and hugged Lily back. He said, "I will be careful. I will use my bucket. I will watch out. I am sorry, Lily. You are my best friend."
Lily and Tom smiled and kissed. They were still workers, but they were also friends. They went back to the pit and worked together. They used their buckets and watched out. They had fun.

"No, I want it!" Ben says. "It is mine!"
They both grab the bear and pull it. They hear a rip sound. The bear's arm comes off.
"Oh no!" Lily and Ben say. "We broke the bear!"
They hear their mom coming up the stairs. They are in trouble. They hide the bear under the bed.
"Hi, kids. What are you doing?" Mom says.
"Nothing, Mom. Just playing," Lily says.
"Can I see what you are playing with?" Mom says.
Lily and Ben look at each other. They are scared. They pray in their hearts.
"Please, God, help us. We are sorry we broke the bear. We don't want Mom to be mad at us. Please, make her happy and kind," they pray.
Mom comes into the room. She sees the box.
"Oh, this is the box of things I wanted to donate to the orphanage. I forgot to take it out," she says.
She looks inside the box. She sees the books, the clothes, and the soft bear.
"Look, kids. There is a soft bear here. Do you want to give it to a child who has no toys?" she says.
Lily and Ben feel a warm feeling in their hearts. They take out the bear and show it to Mom.
"Mom, we are sorry. We broke the bear's arm. We wanted to keep it, but we fought over it," they say.
Mom smiles and hugs them.
"It's okay, kids. I'm not mad at you. I'm proud of you for telling me the truth and for being generous. We can fix the bear's arm and give it to someone who will love it. Do you want to do that?" she says.
Lily and Ben nod and smile.
"Yes, Mom. We want to do that. Thank you, God, for helping us," they say.

"Can we have some coffee, mom?" they asked.
"No, coffee is not for children. It is bitter and hot. You can have some juice instead," mom said.
But Lily and Tom did not listen. They waited until mom went to the bathroom and sneaked into the kitchen. They saw the coffee pot on the table and poured some into their cups.
"Let's drink it fast before mom comes back," Lily said.
They took a sip and made a face. The coffee was ugly. It tasted bad and burned their tongues. They spit it out and cried.
Mom heard them and came back. She saw the mess and was angry.
"What did you do? I told you not to touch the coffee!" she scolded.
"We are sorry, mom. We wanted to try it, but it was ugly," Tom said.
"You should have listened to me. Coffee is not for children. It can make you sick and hurt your teeth. You should drink healthy things like juice and water," mom said.
She cleaned the table and gave them some juice. She hugged them and said, "I love you, but you have to obey me. I know what is good for you."
Lily and Tom nodded and said, "We love you too, mom. We will obey you next time."
They learned their lesson and never touched the coffee again. They drank their juice and played with their toys. The coffee vanished from their minds.

"Look, Ben, that duck has a green head and a yellow beak. He is so pretty," Lily said, pointing to a duck.
"I see him, Lily. He is pretty. And look, that fish has a red tail and a blue body. He is so shiny," Ben said, gazing at a fish.
They gazed at the pond and saw many colors and shapes. They felt happy and curious.
But then, they heard a loud splash. They turned around and saw their dad in the water. He had slipped on a hard rock and fallen in the pond. He was wet and cold and looked funny.
"Oops, I'm sorry, kids. I was trying to take a picture of you and the ducks, but I lost my balance," dad said, trying to smile.
Lily and Ben gasped and then giggled. They thought it was funny to see their dad in the pond. Mom ran to help dad get out of the water. She gave him a towel and a hug.

Lila and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they found a big nut on the ground. It was brown and hard and had a crack in it.
"Look, a nut!" Lila said. "Maybe there is something yummy inside."
"Let's open it!" Ben said. "We can use this rock to smash it."
They picked up a regular rock that was not too big and not too small. They put the nut on a flat stone and took turns hitting it with the rock. But the nut was very hard and did not break.
"Ouch, my hand hurts!" Lila said. "This nut is too tough."
"Maybe we should try a bigger rock," Ben said. "Or a sharper rock."
They looked around for a different rock, but they did not see any. They only saw more regular rocks that looked like the one they had.
"Maybe we should give up," Lila said. "This nut is not worth it."
"No, we can do it!" Ben said. "We just need to hit it harder and faster."
He grabbed the rock and started to hit the nut again and again. He did not notice that Lila had moved away from him. He did not see that he was hitting the nut too close to the edge of the flat stone. He did not hear that the nut had finally cracked.
He only felt a sharp pain in his foot when the nut flew off the stone and hit him.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. "The nut bit me!"
Lila ran to him and saw that his foot was bleeding. She felt sorry for him and helped him sit down.
"I'm sorry, Ben," she said. "Are you okay?"
Ben looked at his foot and then at the nut. The nut was broken and he could see some white stuff inside. It did not look yummy at all. It looked dry and bitter.
He felt silly and sad. He had hurt himself for nothing.
"I'm okay, Lila," he said. "But I was stupid. I wanted the nut so much that I did not think. I did not listen to you. I did not care about anything else."
He gave her the rock and the nut. "Here, you can have them. I don't want them anymore."
Lila smiled and hugged him. "Thank you, Ben. But I don't want them either. I want you to be happy and safe. That's more important than any nut."
They threw the rock and the nut away and went to find a bandage for Ben's foot. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that some things are not worth fighting for. They learned that being friends is better than having nuts.

Ben and Lily were twins who loved to visit their grandparents on the farm. They liked to feed the chickens, pet the cows and ride the horses. But there was one animal they did not like: the mule. The mule was old and grumpy and did not let anyone touch him. He would kick and bite and make loud noises.
One day, Ben and Lily decided to try to make friends with the mule. They brought him some carrots and apples from the garden. They walked slowly and quietly to his pen and called his name.
"Hello, mule. We have some treats for you. Do you want some?" Ben said.
The mule looked at them with his big ears and snorted. He did not move from his spot.
"Please, mule. We want to be nice to you. We want to pet you and brush you and make you happy." Lily said.
The mule shook his head and stamped his feet. He did not want their treats or their kindness. He liked to be alone and spoil his mood.
Ben and Lily felt sad and hurt. They turned to leave, but then they heard a voice.
"Wait, children. Don't go. Let me talk to him." It was their grandfather, who was elderly and wise. He walked up to the mule and stroked his mane.
"Hello, old friend. Why are you so mean to these little ones? They only want to show you some love. Don't you remember how we used to play and work together? How we used to have fun and enjoy the sun? Don't you miss that?"
The mule looked at his old master and sighed. He remembered the good times they had, but he also felt old and tired and sore. He did not think anyone cared for him anymore.
"I'm sorry, sir. I'm just a stubborn old mule. I don't mean to be rude, but I don't like change. I don't like new people or new things. I like to be left alone and spoil my day." The mule said.
The grandfather smiled and hugged the mule. He understood how he felt, but he also wanted him to be happy.
"I know, old friend. I know. But you don't have to be alone or spoil your day. You have me, and you have these children, who love you and want to be with you. They are not here to bother you, but to help you. They can give you some food and water, some care and attention, some joy and laughter. They can make your day better, if you let them. Will you let them?"
The mule looked at the grandfather, then at Ben and Lily, who were waiting with hopeful eyes. He felt a warm and fuzzy feeling in his heart. He nodded and smiled.
"Okay, sir. Okay. I will let them. I will try to be nice and friendly. I will try to have some fun and enjoy the sun. I will try not to spoil my day." The mule said.
Ben and Lily cheered and ran to the mule. They gave him the carrots and apples, which he ate with delight. They petted him and brushed him, which he liked very much. They played with him and laughed with him, which he enjoyed a lot. They made his day better, and he made theirs too.
The grandfather watched them with a smile. He was happy to see his old friend and his grandchildren get along. He was happy to see them all have a good day. He was happy to see them all not spoil their day.

Once there was a little boy called Billy. He was three years old and he loved wearing his favourite red shirt. Every day, he would wear it and he would feel very excited.
One day, Billy heard some loud noises from outside. He looked out of the window and saw a lot of birds making a lot of noise. He thought it was strange and wanted to know why they were being so noisy.
So, he went outside and asked the birds: "Why are you making so much noise?". The birds looked at him and said: "We are singing". Billy was so happy to have an answer. 
He then waved goodbye to the birds, went back inside and put on his red shirt. He felt happy because he found an answer to his question.
The moral of this story is that it is always good to ask questions and try to find an answer. If you don't ask questions, you may never find out what the answer is.

Anna and Ben are friends who like to play together. One day, they see a big package outside their house. They are curious and want to open it.
"Maybe it has toys or candy inside," Anna says.
"Or maybe it is a surprise for us," Ben says.
They run to the package and try to tear the paper. But the paper is very strong and they cannot open it.
"Let's use scissors," Anna says.
"No, that is dangerous. We might cut ourselves," Ben says.
They look around and see a rock. They think they can use the rock to break the paper.
"Let's use the rock," Anna says.
"OK, but be careful," Ben says.
They take the rock and hit the paper with it. But the rock bounces back and hits Anna on the head. She cries out loud and falls down.
"Anna, are you OK?" Ben asks.
He drops the rock and runs to Anna. He sees blood on her head and feels scared.
"Help, help!" he shouts.
Their mom hears them and comes out. She sees Anna and Ben and the package. She is angry and worried.
"What are you doing? That is not your package. That is for the neighbor. You should not touch other people's things. And you should not use rocks or scissors to open them. You could hurt yourself or others. Look what you did to Anna. She needs to go to the doctor now," she says.
She picks up Anna and takes her to the car. She tells Ben to stay inside and wait for her. She drives to the doctor with Anna.
Ben feels sorry and sad. He wishes he did not try to open the package. He wishes he did not hurt Anna. He learns a lesson. He learns to respect other people's things. He learns to be careful with tools. He learns to solve problems in a better way. He hopes Anna will be OK. He hopes she will forgive him. He hopes they can still be friends.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. They like to swing and slide and run. One day, they see a big bunch of grapes on a table. The grapes are purple and shiny. They look yummy.
"Can we have some grapes?" Tom asks Mia.
"I don't know. Maybe they belong to someone else," Mia says.
"But I'm hungry. And they look so good," Tom says.
He reaches for a grape. Mia stops him.
"Wait, Tom. We should ask first. Or we can share our snacks. I have a banana and you have a cracker. That's fair," Mia says.
Tom thinks for a moment. He likes bananas and crackers. But he likes grapes more.
"OK, Mia. I promise I won't take the grapes. Let's eat our snacks," Tom says.
He puts his hand behind his back. He crosses his fingers. He thinks that means he can break his promise.
Mia smiles. She trusts Tom. She peels her banana and breaks it in half. She gives one half to Tom and keeps the other. She takes a bite.
"Thank you, Mia. This is good," Tom says.
He takes a bite of the banana. He also takes a bite of his cracker. He still wants a grape. He looks at the table. He sees no one around. He thinks it is safe.
He drops his banana and cracker. He runs to the table. He grabs a grape. He pops it in his mouth. He feels happy.
But then he hears a loud roar. He turns around. He sees a big dog. The dog is angry. The dog is hungry. The dog wants the grapes. The dog chases Tom.
Tom is scared. He runs away. He drops the grape. He cries for help.
Mia hears Tom. She sees the dog. She is brave. She is playful. She picks up a stick. She waves it at the dog. She makes a funny noise. She distracts the dog.
The dog stops chasing Tom. The dog looks at Mia. The dog is curious. The dog likes sticks. The dog likes noises. The dog forgets the grapes. The dog plays with Mia.
Tom runs back to Mia. He hugs her. He says sorry.
"I'm sorry, Mia. I broke my promise. I took a grape. I was greedy. I was wrong. The dog was scary. You saved me. You are a good friend," Tom says.
Mia hugs Tom. She says it's OK.
"It's OK, Tom. I forgive you. You made a mistake. You learned a lesson. The dog was scary. But he is also playful. He likes to play with us. He is a good dog," Mia says.
They pet the dog. They give him some of their snacks. They make friends with him. They play with him. They have fun.
They see a lady. She comes to the table. She sees the grapes. She sees the dog. She sees Tom and Mia. She smiles.
"Hello, kids. I'm glad you like my dog. His name is Spot. He is very playful. He loves grapes. But he also loves to share. Do you want some grapes?" she asks.
Tom and Mia look at each other. They nod. They say yes.
"Thank you, lady. Thank you, Spot. We love grapes. We also love to share. We are sorry we took a grape without asking. We won't do it again. We promise," they say.
They take a grape each. They eat it. They say it's delicious. They thank the lady again. They thank Spot again. They play with him some more. They are happy. They are friends.

Lily loved strawberries. She liked to pick them from the garden with her mom. She liked to wash them and eat them. She liked to share them with her friends.
One day, Lily saw a big basket of strawberries on the kitchen table. She wanted to have some, but her mom said no. She said they were for the party later. She said Lily had to wait.
Lily was sad. She waited and waited. She played with her toys. She read her books. She helped her mom. But she still wanted strawberries.
Then, she had an idea. She saw her mom go to the bathroom. She saw the basket on the table. She decided to take one strawberry. Just one. She thought her mom would not notice.
She rushed to the table. She reached for the basket. She grabbed a strawberry. She put it in her mouth. She smiled.
But then, she felt something. Something prickly. Something ouchy. She looked at the strawberry. It was not a strawberry. It was a fake strawberry. It was a pin cushion. It had pins in it.
Lily cried. She spit out the pin cushion. She ran to her mom. She said she was sorry. She said she was hungry.
Her mom hugged her. She said it was okay. She said she was sorry too. She said she should have told Lily. She said the basket was a trick. She said it was for the party game. She said the real strawberries were in the fridge.
She took Lily to the fridge. She opened it. She showed Lily a big bowl of strawberries. She said Lily could have some. She said Lily was generous. She said Lily could share them with her friends.
Lily smiled. She said thank you. She said she loved her mom. She said she loved strawberries. She took a strawberry. She ate it. It was sweet. It was juicy. It was yummy. She was happy.

Anna and Ben hug each other and thank the pigeon. They learn that winning is not as important as being kind and sharing. They play with the pigeon and have fun. They are happy and grateful.

Mr. Snowman did not say anything. He just smiled with his carrot nose.
Ben had an idea. He ran to the kitchen and got a big spoon. He came back to the snowman and said, "Look, Lily, I have a spoon. We can stir the snow and make it soft."

"Wow, this is so cool!" Ben said. "We can make a snow castle for Mr. Snowman."
Lily agreed. She said, "Yes, let's make a snow castle. Mr. Snowman can be the king."
They worked hard to make a snow castle. They used their spoons to make walls and towers. They used their hands to make windows and doors. They used their hats to make flags.
They were very proud of their snow castle. They showed it to Mr. Snowman.
"Look, Mr. Snowman, this is your castle!" Lily said. "You can live here and be happy."
Mr. Snowman did not say anything. He just smiled with his carrot nose.
Lily and Ben smiled too. They hugged Mr. Snowman and said, "We love you, Mr. Snowman. You are our friend."

Sara loves to play with her toys. She has many toys in her room. She has dolls, cars, blocks, and books. She likes to make stories with her toys. She pretends they are her friends.
One day, Sara is playing with her dolls. She makes them have a tea party. She gives them cups and plates. She says, "Here you go, Anna. Here you go, Elsa. Do you like the tea? It is very yummy." She makes them nod and smile.
Then, Sara hears a noise. She looks under her bed. She sees something moving. She is curious. She moves her dolls aside. She crawls under the bed. She discovers a sock. It is not her sock. It is a big sock. It is blue and green. It has stripes. It has a hole. She wonders who it belongs to.
She picks up the sock. She hears another noise. She sees a tail. It is a furry tail. It is brown and white. It wags. She follows the tail. She finds a dog. It is a small dog. It is hiding under the bed. It looks scared. It shivers. It has no collar. It has no name.
Sara feels sorry for the dog. She says, "Hello, dog. Are you lost? Are you cold? Do you want to be my friend?" She holds out the sock. The dog sniffs the sock. It licks the sock. It takes the sock. It cuddles the sock. It looks happy. It wags its tail. It barks.
Sara smiles. She says, "I think you like the sock. It is your sock now. It is a perfect sock for you. You can keep it. You can also stay with me. I will take care of you. I will give you food and water. I will give you love. I will give you a name. How about Spot? Do you like Spot?"
The dog nods. It licks Sara's face. It says, "Woof, woof." Sara hugs the dog. She says, "I like Spot, too. You are a perfect dog for me. You are my new friend. Come on, Spot. Let's go play with my toys. They will like you, too."
Sara and Spot crawl out from under the bed. They join the tea party. They share the tea and the cake. They play and laugh. They are happy. They are friends.

Lena's dad scratched his head and said, "Lena, remember it's important to mix up all the things in your life. Too much of anything can make you dizzy."
Lena understood. She thought about all the things she liked to do, like drawing, reading and playing tag. She smiled at her dad and said, "Okay, I'll take a break and go look at the file."
The moral of the story is that it's important to mix up your activities and not do too much of one thing. Too much of anything can make you dizzy.

Once, there was a boy who wanted to buy candy. He had saved his money and was excited to get something special. But the price of the candy was too high, and the boy was disappointed.
The boy's father said, "It's foolish to buy candy at that price. Ignore it and let's look for something else."
The boy replied, "But I want it!"
The father said, "What you want doesn't always mean it's best for you. The price we have to pay for something doesn't always tell us the true value of it. Let's look somewhere else for something better."
So the boy ignored the high price and the two of them looked for something else. They found something that the boy liked and that cost much less than the candy.
The moral to this story is that sometimes we need to ignore what looks good at first and remember that the price we pay doesn't always tell us the true value.

Lily and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big box. They think it is a good place to hide.
"Let's play hide and seek," says Lily. "I will count and you hide in the box."
"OK," says Sam. He goes inside the box and closes the lid.
Lily counts to ten. Then she looks for Sam. She does not see him. She hears a noise from the box. She opens the lid.
"Boo!" says Sam. He jumps out and scares Lily.
Lily laughs. She sees a paper in the box. She picks it up. It has words on it. It is a poem.
"Look, Sam, a poem," says Lily. "Can you read it?"
Sam shakes his head. He does not know how to read.
"Me neither," says Lily. "But maybe we can make up our own poem."
They sit on the grass and think of words that rhyme. They say them out loud.
"Box, fox, socks," says Sam.
"Park, bark, dark," says Lily.
They giggle. They like making poems.
A lady walks by. She sees the paper in Lily's hand. She stops and looks at it.
"Hey, that's my poem," she says. "I wrote it for a contest. How did you get it?"
Lily and Sam are surprised. They did not know the paper belonged to someone.
"We found it in the box," says Lily. "We are sorry. We did not mean to take it."
The lady is angry. She snatches the paper from Lily. She is bossy.
"Give me that," she says. "You should not touch things that are not yours. And you should not make fun of poems. Poems are serious and important."
Lily and Sam feel sad. They do not like the lady. They do not think poems are serious and important. They think poems are fun and silly.
They run away from the lady. They find another place to play. They forget about the poem. They make up their own games. They are happy.

Billy looked around the theatre and spotted a daisy growing from a crack in the wall. He clapped his hands again in delight.
The play started and Billy clapped loudly at every exciting bit. But the elderly man just scowled at him.
When the play finished, everyone in the theatre applauded loudly. Unfortunately Billy was so excited he clapped too loudly and the elderly man yelled at him.
Billy was so ashamed that he ran out of the theatre and never saw a play again.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They like to swing high, slide fast and run around. But one day, Tom is not in the park. Lily is sad. She misses Tom.
She asks her mom, "Where is Tom? Why is he not here?"
Her mom says, "Tom is sick. He has a cold. He has to stay at home and rest. He will come back soon."
Lily says, "I want to see Tom. I want to play with him. Can we go to his house?"
Her mom says, "No, we can't. We have to keep away from Tom. We don't want to make him sicker. But we can do something nice for him. We can make him a present."
Lily says, "A present? What can we make?"
Her mom says, "We can make him a card. We can draw a picture of the park and write 'Get well soon, Tom'. We can also give him some cookies. He likes cookies."
Lily says, "Yes, let's do that. I think Tom will like that. He will be happy."
They go home and make the card and the cookies. They put them in a bag. They walk to Tom's house. They ring the doorbell. Tom's mom opens the door. She says, "Hello, Lily and Lily's mom. What a nice surprise. How are you?"
Lily says, "We are good. We made a present for Tom. We miss him. We hope he gets better soon."
Tom's mom says, "That is very sweet of you. Thank you. Tom will love your present. He misses you too. He is in his room. He can't come out. But you can wave to him from the window."
Lily and her mom go to the window. They see Tom in his bed. He looks pale and tired. He smiles when he sees them. He waves back. Lily holds up the bag. She says, "This is for you, Tom. We made you a card and some cookies. We want you to swing high, slide fast and run around with us again."
Tom says, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend. I like your card and your cookies. They make me feel better. I want to swing high, slide fast and run around with you again too. I will be well soon. I promise."
Lily says, "OK, Tom. I will wait for you. I will see you in the park. Bye, Tom."
Tom says, "Bye, Lily."
Lily and her mom say goodbye to Tom's mom. They leave the bag at the door. They walk back to their house. Lily is still sad. But she is also happy. She knows Tom will be happy too. She knows they will play together again. She knows they are friends.

Tim said, "No, I want to go to the park." Bob refused to listen and said, "I'm the older one, so I should decide what to do." "No," said Tim, "I should also get to choose, that's not fair".
Bob and Tim argued until they got angry and started to march to the park without listening to each other. As they reached the park, they noticed that the nearby ice-cream stand had run out of ice-cream! They were so disappointed. 
Bob felt stupid for not listening to Tim and said, "I'm sorry, Tim. I should have listened to you. We could have gotten ice-cream if I had listened to you." 
Tim smiled, put his arm around Bob and said, "It's okay. Remember, it's important to always listen to your friend's opinions. That way, we can both have a good time!" 
 
The two friends hugged each other and enjoyed the rest of their day together.

Bella loved animals. She wanted to be a veterinarian when she grew up. She liked to read books about animals and ask questions to her mom and dad.
One day, she went to the library with her mom. She saw a big book with a picture of a lion on the cover. She wanted to read it. She asked her mom, "Can I borrow this book, please?"
Her mom looked at the book. It had many hard words that Bella could not read. She said, "This book is too difficult for you, honey. Why don't you choose another one?"
Bella was frustrated. She really wanted to learn about lions. She said, "But I want to know how lions live, and what they eat, and how they roar. Please, mom, let me have this book."
Her mom smiled. She had an idea. She said, "How about we go to the zoo tomorrow? There is a veterinarian there who takes care of the lions. Maybe he can answer your questions."
Bella was happy. She said, "Yes, yes, yes! Thank you, mom. I can't wait to meet the veterinarian and the lions."
The next day, they went to the zoo. They saw many animals, but Bella was most excited to see the lions. They were big and beautiful and loud. She saw a man wearing a white coat and a hat. He was holding a clipboard and a stethoscope. He was the veterinarian.
Bella ran to him. She said, "Hello, sir. I want to be a veterinarian like you. Can you tell me about the lions?"
The veterinarian smiled. He said, "Sure, little girl. I'm happy to answer your questions. What do you want to know?"
Bella asked him many questions. He answered them all. He told her how lions live in groups called prides, how they hunt and eat other animals, how they communicate with roars and purrs, and how he checks their health and treats their wounds.

Sara was a big girl who liked to do things by herself. She was independent and did not need help from anyone. She liked to play with her toys, read her books, and draw with her crayons. She did not like to nap or rest, because she thought it was boring.
One day, her mom came to her room and said, "Sara, it is time to relax. You have been playing all day, and you need to rest your body and mind. Come, let me read you a story and give you a message."
Sara did not want to relax. She said, "No, mom, I do not want to relax. I want to play more. I am not tired. I am independent. I can do what I want."
Her mom smiled and said, "I know you are independent, Sara, and I am proud of you. But everyone needs to relax sometimes, even big girls like you. Relaxing is good for you. It helps you grow, learn, and be happy. A message is when I rub your back, your arms, and your legs gently. It feels nice and makes you calm. A story is when I read you a book with pictures and words. It makes you imagine and dream. Do you want to try?"
Sara thought for a moment. She liked when her mom read her stories and gave her messages. She remembered how cozy and warm it felt. She decided to give it a try. She said, "Okay, mom, I will relax. But only for a little bit. Then I want to play again."
Her mom nodded and said, "Deal. Come, lie down on your bed and close your eyes. I will read you a story and give you a message. You will see how good it feels to relax."
Sara did as her mom said. She lay down on her bed and closed her eyes. Her mom read her a story about a princess and a dragon. She gave her a message on her back, her arms, and her legs. Sara felt her muscles relax and her mind drift. She felt happy and peaceful. She did not want to play anymore. She wanted to relax. She said, "Thank you, mom. I like to relax. I like your story and your message. You are the best mom ever."
Her mom kissed her forehead and said, "You are welcome, Sara. I love you. You are the best daughter ever. Now, sleep well and have sweet dreams."

Tom was a big boy who liked to help his dad. One day, his dad was chopping wood with an axe. Tom wanted to try too. He asked his dad, "Can I use the axe, please?"
His dad said, "No, Tom, the axe is too sharp and heavy for you. You might hurt yourself or someone else. You can help me by picking up the small sticks and putting them in the pile."
Tom was sad. He wanted to chop wood like his dad. He thought he could manage. He waited until his dad was busy with something else. Then he sneaked to the axe and grabbed it. He lifted it with both hands and swung it at a big log.
But the axe was too sharp and heavy for Tom. He lost his balance and fell down. The axe flew out of his hands and landed on his foot. Tom screamed in pain. His dad heard him and ran to him. He saw the axe and the blood on Tom's foot. He was very scared and angry.
He picked up Tom and carried him to the car. He said, "Tom, what have you done? You were very naughty and foolish. You could have lost your foot or worse. You should have listened to me. Now we have to go to the hospital."
Tom was very sorry and ashamed. He cried and said, "I'm sorry, dad. I wanted to chop wood like you. I thought I could manage. But the axe was too sharp and heavy for me. It hurt me a lot. Please don't be mad at me."
His dad said, "I'm not mad at you, Tom. I'm just worried about you. I love you very much. But you have to be careful and obey me. The axe is not a toy. It is a tool for grown-ups. You are still a little boy. You have to learn and grow before you can use it."
They went to the hospital. The doctor looked at Tom's foot. He said, "You are lucky, Tom. The axe did not cut your bone or your nerve. You only need some stitches and a bandage. You will be fine in a few weeks. But you have to rest and keep your foot clean. And you have to promise me that you will never touch the axe again."
Tom nodded and said, "I promise, doctor. I will never touch the axe again. I learned my lesson. I will be a good boy and help my dad in other ways. Thank you for fixing my foot."
The doctor smiled and said, "You're welcome, Tom. You are a brave boy. I hope you feel better soon."
Tom thanked the doctor and hugged his dad. His dad hugged him back and said, "I'm proud of you, Tom. You are a good boy. I'm sorry I yelled at you. I was just scared. I'm glad you are fine. I love you very much."
Tom said, "I love you too, dad. And I'm sorry I disobeyed you. I will listen to you from now on. You are the best dad in the world."
They went home and Tom rested on the couch. His dad gave him some juice and a cookie. He read him a story and sang him a song. Tom felt happy and safe. He knew his dad was right. The axe was not for him. He would wait until he was big enough to use it. He closed his eyes and fell asleep.

"Where can we find a key?" Lily wonders.

"This is my case. It has my things inside. Do you want to see?" he asks.
"Yes, please!" Lily and Ben say, eager.
The cop opens the case and shows them his things. He has a radio, a flashlight, a notebook, a pen, and a pair of handcuffs.

"That is so cool! You are a very smart cop," Lily says, impressed.
"Can we play with your things?" Ben asks, politely.
"Sure, but be careful. Don't shoot the radio or the flashlight. They are not toys," the cop says, kindly.

"Thank you for letting us play with your things. You are a very nice cop," Ben says, grateful.
"Thank you for being good kids. You are very smart and brave. Maybe you can be cops when you grow up," the cop says, friendly.

Lila was a lonely girl. She had no friends to play with. She only had her toys and her books. She liked to read stories about faraway places and brave heroes. She wished she could go on adventures like them.
Every night, Lila had a dream. She dreamed that she was flying on a big bird. The bird was soft and friendly. It took her to different lands, where she met new people and animals. They had fun and talked and laughed. Lila was happy in her dream.
One night, Lila woke up from her dream. She saw the bird outside her window. It was real! It looked at her with kind eyes and said, "Lila, come with me. I want to show you something."
Lila was scared and excited. She put on her coat and shoes and climbed out of the window. She held on to the bird's feathers and flew away with it. She felt the wind and the stars on her face. She smiled and said, "Thank you, bird. You are my friend."
The bird said, "You are welcome, Lila. You are my friend too. I have been watching you for a long time. I know you are lonely. I want to help you. I have a gift for you. It is a magic seed. If you plant it in your garden, it will grow into a beautiful tree. The tree will have fruits and flowers and leaves. It will keep you company and make you happy. It will also make your dreams come true."
Lila was amazed and grateful. She hugged the bird and said, "Thank you, bird. You are the best friend ever. I will plant the seed and take care of the tree. I will always remember you and our adventures."
The bird said, "You are welcome, Lila. I will always remember you too. But now, I have to go. It is time for me to fly back to my home. Goodbye, Lila. I hope you have a wonderful life."
Lila said, "Goodbye, bird. I hope you have a wonderful life too."
The bird flew away, leaving a trail of light behind. Lila watched it until it disappeared. Then, she went back to her room and put the seed under her pillow. She fell asleep, feeling warm and happy. She knew that tomorrow, she would have a new friend and a new dream. She was not lonely anymore.

Sara and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big tree with many acorns on the ground. Sara wanted to collect them and put them in her basket. Tom wanted to throw them and see how far they could go.
"Look, Sara, I can speed this acorn very far!" Tom said. He picked up an acorn and threw it as hard as he could. The acorn flew in the air and hit a bird that was sitting on a branch. The bird cried out and flew away.
"Tom, that was not nice!" Sara said. "You hurt the bird. The acorns are not for throwing. They are for the squirrels and the birds to eat. They need them for the winter."
Tom did not listen. He threw another acorn and hit a squirrel that was running on the grass. The squirrel squeaked and ran away.
"Tom, stop it!" Sara said. "You are scaring the animals. They are our friends. They live in the park. We should be kind to them."
Tom did not care. He threw another acorn and hit a boy who was riding a bike. The boy lost his balance and fell off his bike. He scraped his knee and started to cry.
"Tom, look what you did!" Sara said. "You hurt the boy. The acorns are not for hurting. They are for sharing. We should be nice to other people."
Tom felt bad. He saw that he had made a lot of trouble. He ran to the boy and said he was sorry. He helped him get up and gave him a band-aid. He ran to the bird and the squirrel and said he was sorry. He gave them some acorns from his pocket. He ran to Sara and said he was sorry. He gave her his basket.
"Sara, I was wrong. I was not having fun. I was being mean. I learned my lesson. The acorns are not for speeding. They are for giving. Can we still be friends?" Tom said.
Sara smiled and hugged him. "Of course we can, Tom. I'm glad you changed your mind. You are a good friend. Let's play together and share the acorns with the animals and the people. That is the right thing to do." Sara said.
They played in the park and had a lot of fun. They made new friends with the boy, the bird and the squirrel. They filled their baskets with acorns and gave them away. They were happy and proud. They learned that speeding is not always good. Giving is better.

One day, a prince went to the park to play. He saw a group of children playing with a ball. He wanted to join them, but he was shy.
"Hello, can I play with you?" he asked.
The children looked at him and smiled. They saw his crown and his nice clothes.
"Sure, you can play with us. What is your name?" one of them said.
"I am Prince Leo. What are your names?" he said.
The children told him their names. They were Tom, Anna, Ben, and Lily.
"Nice to meet you, Prince Leo. We are playing catch. Do you know how to play catch?" Tom said.
"Yes, I do. I like to play catch. It is fun." Prince Leo said.
"Great. Then you can be on my team. We are the red team. Anna and Ben are the blue team. Lily is the referee. She will say when to start and stop." Tom said.
They gave Prince Leo a red shirt to wear. They divided the ball in half. One half was red and the other half was blue.
"Ready, set, go!" Lily said.
The children started to throw the ball to each other. They tried to catch it and avoid dropping it. They laughed and cheered.
Prince Leo was happy. He made new friends. He played well. He caught the ball many times. He threw it to Tom, who threw it to Anna, who threw it to Ben, who threw it to Lily, who threw it back to Prince Leo.
"Wow, you are good at catch, Prince Leo. You have a strong arm and a fast hand." Anna said.
"Thank you, Anna. You are good too. You have a smart eye and a quick foot." Prince Leo said.
They played until it was time to go home. They said goodbye to each other. They hugged and thanked Lily for being a fair referee.
"Can we play again tomorrow?" Prince Leo asked.
"Of course, we can. You are our friend. You are always welcome to play with us." Tom said.
"Thank you, Tom. You are very kind. You are all very sweet." Prince Leo said.
He went back to his castle. He told his parents about his day. He said he had a lot of fun. He said he met nice children. He said he learned a new word.
"What word did you learn, my son?" his father asked.
"I learned the word 'include'. It means to let someone join and be part of something. The children included me in their game. They made me feel happy and special." Prince Leo said.
His parents smiled and hugged him. They were proud of him. They said he was a good prince. They said he was a good friend. They said he was a sweet boy.

The people laughed and agreed. So, Bob jumped up on the counter and used his jump to pay for the ice cream.

Ben and Mia liked to play in the sand near the sea. They made castles and tunnels and bridges with their buckets and shovels. One day, they saw something strange in the water. It was big and round and had eight arms. It was an octopus!
"Look, Ben, an octopus!" Mia said, pointing at the water.
"Wow, it is so cool!" Ben said. "Let's go closer and say hello."
They ran to the edge of the water and waved at the octopus. The octopus waved back with one of its arms. It looked friendly and curious.
"Hello, octopus!" Ben and Mia said together.
"Hello, kids!" the octopus said in a funny voice. "Do you want to play with me?"
"Yes, please!" Ben and Mia said. They were very excited to meet a talking octopus.
"OK, then. Let's play spray!" the octopus said. "I will spray water at you, and you will try to dodge it. If I hit you, you are out. If you hit me, I am out. Are you ready?"
"Yes, we are ready!" Ben and Mia said. They thought it sounded like a fun game.
"OK, then. Here I go!" the octopus said. It squirted a jet of water from its mouth at Ben and Mia. They jumped and ducked and ran to avoid it. They laughed and screamed as they got wet.
"Ha ha, you missed me!" Ben said.
"Not for long!" the octopus said. It aimed another jet of water at Ben.
"Watch out, Ben!" Mia said. She threw a handful of sand at the octopus.
"Ouch, that hurt!" the octopus said. It rubbed its eye with its arm. "You got me, Mia. You are very good at this game."
"Thank you, octopus. You are very good, too." Mia said. She smiled at the octopus.
They played spray for a while longer, until they were all soaked and tired. They had a lot of fun with the octopus. The octopus was very nice and funny.
"Thank you for playing with me, kids. You are very fun and brave." the octopus said.
"Thank you for playing with us, octopus. You are very smart and kind." Ben and Mia said.
They hugged the octopus and said goodbye. They promised to come back and play again soon.
They ran back to their parents, who were waiting for them with towels and snacks. They told them all about their adventure with the octopus. Their parents were very surprised and proud of them.
They ate their snacks and dried off. They looked at the water and waved at the octopus, who waved back. They were very happy. They had made a new friend.

"Ah, this feels good!" Lily said. "The fan makes cool air."
"Yes, and it makes a funny noise!" Ben said. "Listen, it goes whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!"
They laughed and tried to make the same noise as the fan. They also pretended to fly with the fan, waving their arms and legs.
But after a while, they started to feel cold. The fan was too strong, and it made them shiver.
"Brrr, I'm cold!" Lily said. "Let's turn off the fan."
"Me too!" Ben said. "But how do we turn it off?"
They looked at the fan, but they did not see a button or a switch. They tried to pull the cord, but it was too high. They tried to push the fan, but it was too heavy.
They did not know what to do. They shivered and hugged each other.
"Help!" they shouted. "We want to turn off the fan!"
Their mom heard them and came to the window. She saw them shivering and smiling.
"What are you doing, silly kids?" she asked. "You look like ice pops!"
She reached for the cord and turned off the fan. She opened the window and took them inside.
"Come on, let's get you some juice and a blanket," she said. "You don't want to catch a cold, do you?"
"No, mom," they said. "Thank you, mom."
They followed her to the kitchen, feeling warm and happy. They still liked the fan, but they liked their mom more.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit and a fox who were friends. One day, the fox was feeling very hungry. He asked the rabbit for some food, and the rabbit did not know what to do. The fox said that if the rabbit did not give him some food, he would have to surrender. The rabbit was scared, but he did not want to give the fox his food.
Then the rabbit had an idea! He took some hay and rolled it in a big ball. He said to the fox:"Here is some food, but you will have to try to catch it!" The fox was very happy and he ran after the hayball. But it was very hard for the fox to catch the ball, it was hairy and slippery!
The fox worked really hard, and eventually caught the ball. When he opened the ball, there was no food, only hay. The fox had worked really hard for nothing!
The moral of this story is that it is better to be clever than strong. Even when you are small and scared, you can always use your brain to outsmart those around you.

"Look, Lily, this is red lipstick. It makes your lips look like a rose," Anna said, and put some on her mouth.
"And this is blue eyeshadow. It makes your eyes look like the sky," Lily said, and rubbed some on her eyelids.
They laughed and admired each other in the mirror. They felt very lucky to have such fun things to play with.
But then, they heard the door open. It was mom, coming back home. They panicked and tried to hide the makeup box under the bed. But they were too late. Mom saw them and their messy faces.
"Girls, what have you done? You have destroyed my makeup! That was very naughty of you. You know you are not allowed to touch my things without asking," mom said, very angry.
Lily and Anna felt very sorry and scared. They started to cry and apologize.
"Mom, we are sorry. We just wanted to look pretty like you. We didn't mean to destroy your makeup," Lily said.
"Mom, we are sorry. We didn't know it was so important to you. We thought it was just for fun," Anna said.
Mom sighed and calmed down. She hugged them and wiped their faces with a wet cloth.
"I know you didn't mean to destroy my makeup, girls. But you have to understand that makeup is not a toy. It is something I use for special occasions. And it is very expensive and hard to replace. You have to respect my things and ask me before you use them. Do you understand?" mom said.
Lily and Anna nodded and said they understood. They promised to never touch mom's makeup again without permission. Mom smiled and kissed them.
"I love you, girls. You are very lucky to have each other. And you are pretty enough without makeup. Now, let's go and have some cookies and milk. And maybe later, we can play dress up with some old clothes and accessories. How does that sound?" mom said.
Lily and Anna cheered up and said that sounded great. They followed mom to the kitchen, holding hands. They learned their lesson and were happy to have a kind mom.

"Hello, little ones," the old man said. "Do you like pigeons?"

"Be gentle," the old man said. "Pigeons are smart and friendly. They can fly very far and see many things."

Sam and Lily were twins who liked to play in the yard. One day, they saw a big truck stop in front of their house. The truck had a lot of mail for their mom and dad. The driver got out and put the mail in a box near the door.
"Look, mail!" Sam said, running to the box.
"Wait for me!" Lily said, following him.
They opened the box and saw many letters and packages. Some had pictures and stickers on them. Some had funny shapes and colors. They wanted to see what was inside.
"Can we open them?" Sam asked.
"No, they are not for us. They are for mom and dad. We have to wait for them to come home," Lily said.
"But they are so pretty. Maybe there is a toy or a candy for us," Sam said.
He picked up a package that was round and soft. He felt something move inside. He was curious. He tried to open it, but it was tied with a tight string.
"Let me help you," Lily said.
She took the package and tried to untie the string. But it was too hard. She pulled and pulled, but it did not come off.
"Maybe we can twist it," Sam said.
He took the package and twisted it with his hands. He twisted it harder and harder, until...
Pop!
The package burst open and a big balloon flew out. It was red and shiny and had a smiley face on it. It made a loud noise as it flew around the yard.
"Wow!" Sam and Lily said.
They laughed and clapped and chased the balloon. They had fun with their new toy.
But they did not see the driver come back to the truck. He saw the open box and the empty package. He saw the balloon in the air. He was angry.
"Hey, you kids! What did you do to my mail? That was not for you! That was for my niece's birthday! You ruined it!" he shouted.
He ran to the yard and grabbed the balloon. He popped it with his keys. He threw it on the ground. He scolded Sam and Lily.
They were scared and sad. They did not mean to be bad. They did not know it was his mail. They said they were sorry.
But he did not listen. He took the rest of the mail and put it back in his truck. He drove away, leaving Sam and Lily alone.
They cried and hugged each other. They wished mom and dad would come home soon. They learned a lesson. They would never touch the mail again.

He would talk to his reflection in his most regal voice and act like he was travelling to mysterious lands. On one particular morning, he decided he needed a passport to make his adventures more real.
He opened his drawer and rummaged through old toys, until he found a small card with a big stamp on the back. It was a passport! Instantly, he knew his stories would be even more vivid.
He said to himself, “Now I must find a palace to stay in during my travels.” He created a beautiful palace out of his messy pillow and cushion covers. Then he jumped into the throne, embraced his passport tight and imagined bumpy flights over the sea. 
He said to his reflection, “Wear your kingly crown and let’s go on an adventure!” His passport was clutched in one paw and the other held his crown firmly in place. He said to his reflection, “Let’s go explore the world!” and he set off on his imaginary journey.

"Sure, but stay close to me," Mom said.
They went to the vendor and looked at his things. Tim saw a red balloon with a smiley face. He liked it very much. He asked the vendor how much it was.
"Only one coin, little boy," the vendor said. "Do you want it?"
"Yes, please," Tim said. He gave the vendor a coin and took the balloon.
Lily saw a hat with ears and whiskers. It looked like a cat. She liked it very much. She asked the vendor how much it was.
"Only one coin, little girl," the vendor said. "Do you want it?"
"Yes, please," Lily said. She gave the vendor a coin and put on the hat.
The vendor smiled and said, "You both look very nice. Have fun in the park."
"Thank you, mister," Tim and Lily said.
They walked away with Mom, holding their new things. They saw a big dog on a leash. The dog barked at them. Tim and Lily were scared. They hid behind Mom.
"Don't worry, kids," Mom said. "The dog is harmless. He just wants to say hello."
She went to the dog and rubbed his head. The dog wagged his tail and licked her hand. He was friendly.
"See? He's a good dog," Mom said. "Do you want to pet him?"
Tim and Lily nodded. They went to the dog and rubbed his fur. The dog liked it. He sniffed their balloon and hat. He did not bite them.
"Good boy," Tim and Lily said.
They made a new friend. They were happy.

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play at the zoo. They loved to see the animals and learn their names. One day, they saw a big animal with a horn on its nose. It was a rhinoceros.
"Wow, look at that!" Tom said. "It is so big and strong!"
"Yes, it is," Lily said. "But it is also gentle and kind. The zookeeper told me that it does not hurt other animals unless they bother it."
Tom wanted to show Lily that he was brave. He climbed over the fence and ran towards the rhinoceros. He wanted to touch its horn and make it angry.
"Tom, no!" Lily shouted. "That is not safe! Come back!"
But Tom did not listen. He reached the rhinoceros and pulled its horn. The rhinoceros did not like that. It snorted and shook its head. It pushed Tom away with its horn. Tom fell to the ground and hurt his arm.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried. "It hurt me! It is so harsh!"
Lily ran to help Tom. She was scared and sad. She called the zookeeper. The zookeeper came and took Tom to the nurse. He also scolded Tom for being foolish and rude.
"Tom, you should never do that again," the zookeeper said. "The rhinoceros is not harsh. It is just defending itself. You should respect the animals and their space. They are not toys. They have feelings too."
Tom felt sorry and ashamed. He said sorry to the zookeeper, the nurse, and the rhinoceros. He also said sorry to Lily. He learned his lesson. He promised to be more careful and kind.

Leo showed his whistle to his friends. They all wanted to try it. But Leo was scared that if he shared his whistle, it might break. So, he hid it under his bed. At night, Leo could hear the whistle calling him. It wanted to be played with.
The next day, Leo heard a loud roar in the jungle. It was a big, scary lion. All of Leo's friends were scared and didn't know what to do. Leo remembered his whistle. He ran back to his bed and got it. He blew the whistle as loud as he could. The big, scary lion was scared of the whistle's sound and ran away. Leo and his friends were safe, and they all cheered. From that day on, Leo shared his whistle with his friends, and they all played happily together.

The dragon smiled and said 'Well, it looks like you don't need me for protection anymore. I should go now'. With that, he flew off into the sky.

One day, Sally went to the beach with her mom. Sally brought a bucket with her. She ran over to the shoreline and filled it with sand. She was so excited to build her first sandcastle.
"Mom, can you help me make a tower?" Sally requested.
Mom smiled and said, "Let's do it together!"
Together, Sally and Mom built a tall tower. It was so high they could see the lighthouse in the distance. They both smiled, proud of their hard work.
Just then, a grumpy seagull appeared. He flew over to Sally and squawked loudly.
Sally got scared and stepped back. "Mom, I think he wants something!"
Mom laughed, "I think he's just looking for food. Remember, never feed wild animals!"
But the seagull squawked again, this time flying over to the bucket. He then stretched out his neck and pulled out a piece of sandwich Sally had forgotten.
Sally gasped, embarrassed, but mom just smiled. "See, he just wanted something to eat! Let's just finish our sandcastle and go home."
The seagull flew away, happy with his sandwich. Sally and her mom finished the sandcastle and went home with a smile, happy that Sally's simple request had been fulfilled.

"No, it's mine!" Ben says. "I helped you dig it out!"

"Oh no!" Sam says. "We broke the worm!"
"That's bad!" Ben says. "The worm is hurt!"
They feel sorry for the worm and want to help it. They look around and see a bird on a branch. The bird is alert and hungry. It sees the worm and flies down to get it.
"Watch out!" Sam says. "The bird is coming!"
"Run, worm, run!" Ben says. "Hide in the dirt!"
But the worm is too slow and the bird is too fast. The bird grabs the worm and flies away. Sam and Ben are sad and angry. They lost their worm and the bird got it.
They look at each other and realize they made a mistake. They should have shared the worm and been nice to it. They should have thanked the worm for being their friend.
They hug each other and say sorry. They promise to be better friends to each other and to the worms. They hope the worm is okay and the bird is happy. They go back to the garden and look for more worms. They find some and put them in the jar. They are gentle and careful with them. They thank the worms for being their friends. They are happy and alert. They play in the garden until it is time to go home.

"OK, Ben. That is a good idea. We can be friends and have fun," Sara says.

The next day, Tim ate his vegetables. He ate carrots, peas, and even spinach. He went back to the woods and met the rabbit again. The rabbit said, "Now, try to step on the rock." This time, Tim stepped on the rock easily.
Tim learned that eating vegetables can make him strong. He told his mom, "I will eat my vegetables from now on." His mom was happy. Tim was happy too, because he could step on big rocks now. The moral of the story is: eat your vegetables, they make you strong.

One day, a fox wanted to sail on a big lake. He saw a boat near the shore, but it was not his. It belonged to a duck who liked to swim and fish. The fox was sneaky and took the boat when the duck was not looking. He jumped in and pushed it with his paws.
"Ha ha, now I can sail and have fun!" the fox said.
But the boat was not a real boat. It was a fake boat made of wood and paper. The duck had made it to trick the fox, who often tried to catch him. The duck knew the fox could not swim very well.
Soon, the water soaked the boat and it started to sink. The fox was scared and wet. He cried for help.
"Help, help, I am sinking!"
The duck heard him and swam to him. He was angry and said:
"Fox, you are silly and mean. You took my fake boat and now you are in trouble. Why did you do that?"
The fox felt sorry and said:
"Duck, I am sorry and sad. I wanted to sail and have fun. I did not know it was your fake boat. Please help me!"
The duck felt sorry too and said:
"Fox, I will help you, but you have to promise me something. You have to promise me you will not try to catch me or take my things again. Can you do that?"
The fox nodded and said:
"Yes, duck, I promise. I will be nice and fair. Thank you for helping me!"
The duck helped the fox get out of the water and back to the shore. They dried themselves and became friends. They learned to share and play together. They both had fun.

One day, they went to the lake when the sun was mild and the sky was blue. Tim's dad said, "Let's see who can catch the most fish today." Tim said, "OK, dad, I will try hard." They put the worms on their hooks and threw them in the water.
Soon, Tim felt a big pull on his line. He said, "Dad, I have a fish, I have a fish!" He tried to reel it in, but it was too strong. It pulled and pulled and pulled, until Tim lost his balance and fell into the water.
Tim's dad was scared. He dropped his rod and grabbed the net. He tried to reach Tim with the net, but Tim was too far away. The fish dragged him deeper and deeper into the lake. Tim's dad shouted, "Tim, Tim, hold on, I'm coming!" But he could not catch up with Tim.
Tim was cold and wet and scared. He could not see his dad or the boat or the sky. He could only see the fish, a big, mean fish with sharp teeth and a long tail. The fish opened its mouth and bit Tim. Tim screamed, but no one heard him. The fish ate Tim and swam away. Tim's dad never saw him again. He was very sad and cried a lot. He wished he had never taken Tim to the lake. He wished he had never been a fisherman.

They went to the kitchen and found the waffle maker. They plugged it in and turned it on. They opened the fridge and took out the waffle mix and the syrup. They poured some waffle mix into the waffle maker and closed it. They waited for the beep.
But they did not hear the beep. They smelled something burning. They opened the waffle maker and saw a black waffle. It was not good. They threw it in the trash. They tried again with more waffle mix. But they put too much. The waffle mix spilled out of the waffle maker and made a mess on the counter.
"Oh no!" Lily said. "We have to clean this up!"
They grabbed some paper towels and wiped the counter. But they did not see the syrup bottle. It was on the edge of the counter. Ben bumped into it and it fell down. The syrup splashed on the floor and made it sticky.
"Oops!" Ben said. "We have to clean this up too!"
They got more paper towels and tried to mop the floor. But they did not notice the cord of the waffle maker. It was on the floor too. Lily stepped on it and stumbled. She fell down and hit her head on the table.
"Ow!" Lily said. "That hurts!"
She started to cry. Ben ran to her and hugged her. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Are you okay?"
Mom heard the noise and the crying. She woke up and came to the kitchen. She saw the mess and the kids. She said, "What happened here?"
Lily and Ben looked at Mom. They said, "We wanted to make waffles for you. But we made a big mess. And Lily got hurt. We're sorry, Mom."
Mom smiled and said, "It's okay, sweeties. I appreciate your effort. But next time, please wait for me to help you. Making waffles can be tricky. And dangerous. Come on, let's clean up together. And then we can have some waffles. I have some frozen ones in the freezer. They are easy to heat up. And they are yummy too."
Lily and Ben nodded and said, "Okay, Mom. Thank you, Mom. We love you, Mom."
Mom hugged them and said, "I love you too, Lily and Ben. You are my brave and kind waffle makers."

Bobo walked through the woods with the pole. He met his friend, a small grey rabbit named Riri. "Why do you have that pole, Bobo?" Riri asked. "I found it and thought it would be fun to play with," said Bobo. Riri wanted to play too, but the pole was too big for her. Bobo felt uncomfortable because the pole was too big for Riri to play with.
Bobo thought of an idea. He broke the pole into two smaller poles. Now, Riri could play with one and Bobo could play with the other. They played together all day and had lots of fun. In the end, they learned that sharing makes everyone happy.

Tim and Jen like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make roads with blocks and tape. They zoom their cars on the roads and make noises.
One day, Tim and Jen have a problem. They both want to use the same car. It is a big red car with shiny wheels. It is their favorite car. They both grab the car and pull hard.
"Mine!" Tim says.
"No, mine!" Jen says.
They pull and pull and pull. The car does not like it. It makes a loud crack. The car breaks in two. Tim and Jen are sad. They look at the broken car.
They hear a voice. It is Mom. She comes into the room and sees the mess. She is not happy.
"What happened here?" Mom asks.
"Tim and Jen broke the car!" they both say.
Mom shakes her head. She picks up the pieces of the car. She looks at them.
"This was a cheap car," Mom says. "It was not made well. It was not strong. It could not last in this world."
She puts the pieces in the trash. She looks at Tim and Jen.
"Next time, you need to share," Mom says. "You need to take turns. You need to yield. Do you know what yield means?"
Tim and Jen shake their heads.
"Yield means to let someone else go first," Mom says. "It means to be kind and fair. It means to not be greedy and selfish. Can you do that?"
Tim and Jen nod.
"Yes, Mom," they say.
Mom smiles. She hugs them.
"Good," she says. "Now, let's find another car to play with. A better car. A car that can yield."

Tom and Sam liked to play golf with their dad. They had a big bag of balls and sticks. They went to a field near their house. Their dad showed them how to hit the balls far and high. Tom and Sam tried to do the same, but they were not very good. Sometimes they missed the ball, sometimes they hit it too hard or too soft.
"Can I have more balls, dad?" Tom asked. He had lost many balls in the grass or the trees.
"Sure, son, you can have more balls. But be careful, don't hit them too close to the road. There are cars and people there. You don't want to hurt anyone or break anything," their dad said. He was a generous dad. He gave Tom and Sam many balls and sticks.
Tom nodded and took some more balls. He wanted to hit them as far as his dad. He saw a big hill on the other side of the field. He thought it would be fun to hit the balls over the hill. He did not know what was behind the hill.
He swung his stick hard and hit a ball. The ball flew over the hill. He did not see where it landed. He smiled and hit another ball. And another. And another.
Sam watched Tom and wondered what was behind the hill. He decided to follow one of the balls. He ran after it and climbed the hill. He was surprised by what he saw.
Behind the hill was a big house. It had many windows and a nice garden. It also had many holes and cracks. Some of the windows were broken. Some of the flowers were smashed. Some of the balls were stuck in the walls or the roof.
Sam heard a loud voice. It was a man. He was angry. He came out of the house. He had a ball in his hand. He threw it at Sam.
"Hey, you! Stop destroying my house! Who are you? Where is your dad? I'm going to call the police!" the man shouted.
Sam was scared. He did not know what to do. He ran back to the hill. He called Tom and their dad.
"Dad, dad, come quick! There is a man behind the hill. He is mad. He says we destroyed his house. He has some of our balls. He wants to call the police!" Sam said.
Their dad was shocked. He dropped his stick and ran to the hill. He saw the man and the house. He saw the damage. He felt sorry and ashamed.
He apologized to the man. He explained that he did not know there was a house behind the hill. He said that his sons were just playing golf. He said that he would pay for the repairs. He asked the man not to call the police.
The man was still angry, but he calmed down a bit. He saw that their dad was sincere and sorry. He saw that Tom and Sam were young and did not mean to destroy his house. He decided to be generous and forgive them.
He accepted their dad's apology and offer. He gave back their balls. He told them to be more careful next time. He told them to go home and not come back.
Their dad thanked the man and took Tom and Sam by the hand. He walked them back to their house. He was not happy. He scolded them for being careless and reckless. He told them that they had to learn to respect other people's property and safety. He told them that they could not play golf anymore until they were older and wiser.
Tom and Sam felt bad. They knew they had done wrong. They said they were sorry to their dad and the man. They promised to be more careful and respectful. They hoped that the man's house would be fixed soon. They hoped that he would not be mad at them forever. They learned a hard lesson that day. They learned that playing golf can be fun, but also dangerous. They learned that destroying things can have bad consequences. They learned that being generous can make things better.

Tim's dad called the fire helpers on the phone. The fire helpers came fast with a big red truck. They used water to make the fire go away. Tim, his mom, and his dad were very happy that the fire helpers saved the woods. They said thank you to the fire helpers. Tim learned that it is important to ask for help when something is unknown and scary.

Anna was very tired. She had played all day with her toys and her dog. She wanted to go to bed and have a nice dream. But her mom said she had to eat dinner first. Anna did not like dinner. It was green and smelly.
Anna pushed her plate away and said, "No, thank you. I want to sleep." Her mom said, "You have to eat, Anna. It is good for you. It will make you strong and healthy." Anna said, "No, no, no. I don't want it. I want to sleep."
Her mom got angry and said, "Anna, stop being naughty. You have to eat or you will go to bed hungry." Anna got angry too and said, "No, no, no. I don't care. I want to sleep." She got up from her chair and ran to her room.
But on the way, she bumped into the stove. It was hot and it hurt her. She cried out loud and fell to the floor. Her mom heard her and came to see what happened. She saw Anna crying and holding her hand. She said, "Oh, Anna, what did you do? You burned yourself on the stove. Come here, let me see."
She picked up Anna and hugged her. She took her to the sink and ran cold water over her hand. She said, "I'm sorry, Anna. I didn't mean to make you angry. I just wanted you to eat. But you should be careful around the stove. It is very hot and it can hurt you."
Anna stopped crying and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I didn't mean to bump into the stove. I was just tired and I wanted to sleep." Her mom said, "I know, Anna. I know. You are very tired. How about we eat a little bit of dinner and then you can go to bed and have a nice dream?"
Anna nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I will eat a little bit. But can I have something else? I don't like the green and smelly dinner." Her mom smiled and said, "Okay, Anna. I will make you something else. How about some cheese and bread and fruit?" Anna smiled and said, "Yes, please. I like cheese and bread and fruit. Thank you, mom."
Her mom kissed her and said, "You're welcome, Anna. I love you." Anna said, "I love you too, mom." They went back to the table and ate some cheese and bread and fruit. Then Anna went to bed and had a nice dream. She did not cry anymore. She was happy.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toy cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes, but their favorite was a big red truck that could make loud noises and move fast. They always took turns to drive the truck and have fun.
One day, they decided to play with the truck in the backyard, where there was a lot of space and grass. They pushed the truck along the ground, making it go forward and backward, and making it honk and roar. They pretended they were going on a big adventure, and they laughed and shouted.
"Look, Lily, I can make the truck go reverse!" Tom said, as he pulled the truck back with his hand.
"Wow, Tom, that's cool! Can I try?" Lily asked, reaching for the truck.
"OK, but be careful. Don't make it go too fast or too far," Tom warned, as he gave the truck to Lily.
Lily smiled and took the truck. She pushed it forward, then pulled it back, making it go reverse. She liked the feeling of the truck moving in her hand. She wanted to make it go faster and farther, to see how far it could go.
She pulled the truck back harder and harder, until it slipped from her hand and flew into the air. She gasped and watched as the truck soared over the fence and landed in the neighbor's yard, where there was a big dog.
The dog saw the truck and barked loudly. It ran towards the truck and grabbed it with its teeth. It shook the truck and tore it apart, making it break into pieces. It growled and snarled, enjoying its new toy.
Tom and Lily were shocked and scared. They heard the dog and the truck, and they knew they had made a big mistake. They ran to the fence and peeked over, hoping to see their truck. But all they saw was the dog and the broken pieces.
They felt sad and sorry. They had lost their favorite toy, and they had made the dog angry. They wished they had listened to Tom and been more careful. They wished they had not made the truck go reverse so hard.
They looked at each other and said, "We're sorry, truck. We're sorry, dog. We're sorry, mom and dad."
They hugged each other and went inside, where it was quiet. They hoped they could find another toy to play with, and another way to have fun. They hoped they could be more lively and happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a sailor that wanted to go on an adventure. He had a boat with a bright sail that was ready to take him wherever he wanted to go. The sailor piled coal into the boat and pushed it to the lake.
He looked up at the sky. The sun was bright and shining. The sailor smiled and called out, "Let's go sail!".
The boat started to move. The sailor laughed and said, "We are going on an adventure!".
The boat kept sailing until the sailor suddenly realized something. He had run out of coal and now the boat was stopped in the middle of the lake. The sailor looked around, feeling concerned.
"Oh no!" he said.
Suddenly, he saw a bright light in the distance. He grabbed a paddle and started rowing his boat towards the light. When he arrived, he saw a coal ship and the sailor smiled.
"Thank you!" he shouted. He loaded the coal onto his boat and sailed back to shore.
The sailor had learned an important lesson. Be prepared before you set sail. With the right preparation you'll always have a bright and safe journey.
