The structure was very tall and noisy. When Grandma put her hand on the logs, they shifted and creaked. This made Jack so excited, but Grandma told him it was too risky to climb on. Jack begged and pleaded until finally, Grandma allowed him to go on it.
Jack rushed up the logs and started playing, but soon the logs started to creak and crack even more than before. Grandma looked worried, so Jack quickly jumped off and ran back to her.
Grandma hugged Jack and said, "You have to listen to your elders, Jack! This structure wouldn’t have been safe for you to play on. Next time, make sure to follow my instructions.”
Moral of the story: Always listen to your elders, because they are wiser and know what is best for you.

"Look, Tom! A sunflower! It is so pretty and bright!" she said.
Tom followed her and nodded. He liked the sunflower too. He touched its petals and felt how soft they were.
"Can we pick it and take it home?" he asked.
Lily shook her head. She knew that the sunflower was happy in the garden. She did not want to hurt it.
"No, Tom. The sunflower likes to stay here. It likes to see the sun and the sky. If we pick it, it will be sad and fold its petals," she said.
Tom understood. He did not want to make the sunflower sad. He wanted to make it happy.
"Then can we give it a hug and say thank you?" he asked.
Lily smiled and nodded. She thought that was a good idea. She and Tom wrapped their arms around the sunflower and gave it a gentle hug.
"Thank you, sunflower, for being so pretty and bright. You make us happy too," they said.
The sunflower seemed to smile back at them. It swayed in the breeze and waved its petals. Lily and Tom felt warm and happy. They let go of the sunflower and ran to find more flowers and bugs to play with.

Lily wanted to help the baby swan. She thought maybe it was lost or hurt. She reached inside the box and gently picked up the baby swan. It felt soft and warm in her arms. She hugged it and whispered, "Don't worry, I'll take care of you."
She walked to the edge of the pond and looked for the big swan. She saw it on the other side, near some reeds. She waved and called, "Hey, swan, I have your baby! Come and get it!" But the big swan did not hear her. It was busy eating some plants.
Lily decided to take the baby swan to the big swan. She walked around the pond, holding the baby swan close. But the pond was bigger than she thought. She got tired and thirsty and hungry. She also got troubled. She wondered if the baby swan belonged to the big swan. She wondered if the big swan would be happy to see the baby swan. She wondered if the baby swan would fit in with the other swans.
She reached the reeds and saw the big swan. It looked up and saw her. It saw the baby swan in her arms. It made a loud noise and flapped its wings. It looked angry and scared. Lily felt afraid and sorry. She realized she had made a mistake. She put the baby swan down and ran away. She hoped the swan would forgive her. She hoped the baby swan would be okay. She learned a lesson. She learned that some things do not fit where they do not belong.

"Let's mix some season with our soup!" Ben said.
"OK!" Lily agreed. They poured some season into their bowls and stirred with spoons.
"Yum, this smells good!" Ben said.
"Can we taste it?" Lily asked.
"Sure, why not?" Ben said. He took a sip of his soup and made a funny face. "Blech! This is yucky!"
Lily tried her soup and spat it out. "Ew! This is spicy!"
They heard their mom coming into the kitchen. They quickly hid their bowls under the table.
"Hi, kids! What are you doing?" Mom asked.
"We are playing chefs!" Ben said.
"That's nice. Do you want to help me make some real soup?" Mom asked.
"Yes, please!" Ben and Lily said. They were polite and wanted to learn from Mom.

One day, a big bird saw Bob playing in the yard. The bird wanted to catch Bob and eat him. The bird flew down and said, "I will eat you, little cricket!" Bob was scared and wanted to escape.
Bob ran as fast as he could to his house. He shouted to his friends, "Help me! A big bird wants to eat me!" His friends came out and made loud noises to scare the bird away.
The bird was scared of the loud noises and flew away. Bob was safe now. He thanked his friends and said, "You saved me! I am so happy to have such good friends."
From that day on, Bob and his friends played together every day. They were always careful and looked out for each other. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Jack. One day, Jack decided to go on an adventure. He grabbed his favourite hat and ran outside. 
The sun was shining and was very hot. Jack felt a little dizzy. He stopped for a rest and found a beautiful leaf. He picked it up and smiled. 
He looked around and noticed a tree. He wanted to climb it and see the view. He started to climb up the branches but began to feel dizzy.
Jack: "Help!"
Suddenly, a friendly bird flew down from the sky and said,
Bird: "What are you doing little one?"
Jack: "I'm trying to climb the tree but I feel dizzy."
Bird: "Don't worry, I can help you. Take my wing and I will fly you to the top of the tree."
Jack grabbed the bird's wing and soon they were at the top. The view was stunning. Jack smiled and thanked the bird. He waved goodbye and climbed down the tree.
Jack was very proud of himself. He had an amazing adventure and learned that it's okay to ask for help when you feel dizzy!

When the door opened, two strange men were standing there. Anna's heart started to beat faster, and she began to tremble again. "Hello," one of the men said politely, "We're here to take your doll."
Instinctively, Anna hugged her doll tightly and tried to close the door. However, the men were too fast and hindered her. Kicking the door open, they snatched the doll away from her. Anna started to cry.
With the doll gone and the men walking away, Anna realized she had made a big mistake. The men had looked and acted like they didn't belong there, and she should have known to stay away from them. But she had been too polite and trusting, doomed to having her precious doll taken from her.

Tom and Mia liked to play with magnets. They had many magnets of different shapes and colors. They stuck them on the fridge, on the door, on the table. They made pictures and patterns with them.
One day, they found a big magnet in the garage. It was silver and round and very strong. Tom and Mia wanted to try it. They took it to the kitchen and stuck it on the fridge. It made a loud clack sound.
"Wow, this magnet is so interesting!" Mia said. "Look, it can hold many other magnets on it!"
"Let me try!" Tom said. He took some magnets from the fridge and put them on the big magnet. They also made a loud clack sound and stayed on the big magnet.
Tom and Mia had fun with the big magnet. They forgot about their mom, who was making lunch. She had a note on the fridge that said: "Don't forget to wash your hands before eating." The note had a small magnet on it.
But when Tom and Mia stuck the big magnet on the fridge, the note fell off. The small magnet was not strong enough to stay on the fridge with the big magnet. The note landed on the floor, under the table.
Tom and Mia did not see the note. They did not wash their hands. They played with the big magnet until mom called them for lunch.
"Come on, kids, it's time to eat!" mom said. "Did you wash your hands?"
Tom and Mia looked at each other. They did not remember to wash their hands. They remembered the big magnet.
"Sorry, mom, we forgot," Tom said.
"Why did you forget?" mom asked.
"Because we found a big magnet in the garage," Mia said. "It was so interesting!"
Mom looked at the fridge. She saw the big magnet and the other magnets on it. She did not see the note.
"Where is the note I left you?" mom asked.
Tom and Mia looked at the fridge. They did not see the note. They wondered where it was.
Mom looked under the table. She saw the note on the floor. She picked it up and showed it to Tom and Mia.
"Here is the note," mom said. "It says: Don't forget to wash your hands before eating. The big magnet made the note fall off. The big magnet did not remind you to wash your hands. It made you forget."
Tom and Mia felt sorry. They said sorry to mom. They went to the bathroom and washed their hands. They learned that magnets are interesting, but they are not good at reminding.

He began to cry and all the animals in the woods came to see what was wrong. A little rabbit saw the tears on the bear's face.
“Why are you crying?” said the rabbit. 
The bear sniffed and said “I am scared of the rain - I don't understand it.”
The rabbit smiled and said “It is okay, it's only water falling from the sky. We all suffer from the rain sometimes, but it helps the plants grow and keeps us cool.”
The bear felt much better after hearing this and decided he wasn't scared of the rain anymore. In fact, he enjoyed the refreshing feeling it gave him, and from then on he never suffered from the rain again.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a doll and Ben had a car. They were having fun, but they also wanted to do something else.
"Let's go outside and play in the snow," Lily suggested. "We can make a snowman and a snow fort."
Ben shook his head. "No, I don't want to go outside. It's too cold and wet. I want to stay here and play with my car."
Lily frowned. She was impatient. She wanted to go outside and have an adventure. She did not like Ben's car. It was boring and noisy.
"Please, Ben, let's go outside. It will be fun. We can wear our hats and gloves and boots. We can make a snow angel and a snowball fight," Lily pleaded.
Ben still said no. He was stubborn. He liked his car. It was fast and shiny. He did not care about the snow. He thought it was silly and messy.
Lily was angry. She did not want to play with Ben anymore. She grabbed her doll and ran to the door. She opened it and went outside.
"Fine, then. I will go outside by myself. You can stay here and play with your stupid car," Lily shouted.
Ben was surprised. He did not expect Lily to leave. He felt a pang in his heart. He did not want to hurt Lily's feelings. He liked Lily. She was his friend.
He looked at his car. It was not as fun as he thought. He felt lonely and bored.
He put down his car and ran to the door. He opened it and saw Lily outside. She was making a snowman. She looked happy and cheerful.
He felt sorry. He wanted to join her. He wanted to make up with her.
He put on his hat and gloves and boots. He grabbed a scarf and a carrot. He went outside and called her name.
"Lily, Lily, I'm sorry. Can I play with you? Can I help you make the snowman?" Ben asked.
Lily turned around and saw Ben. She smiled. She was glad. She missed Ben. She wanted to be his friend again.
She nodded. She gave him a hug. She handed him the scarf and the carrot.
"Of course, Ben. You can play with me. You can help me make the snowman. We can have fun together," Lily said.
They finished the snowman. They gave him a hat and a smile. They played in the snow. They made a snow angel and a snowball fight. They laughed and giggled.
They were happy. They were friends. They had a good time.

Tom and Amy were twins who liked to play in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with pots and pans. One day, they saw a big knife on the counter. Tom wanted to touch it, but Amy said no.
"It is sharp and can hurt you," Amy said. "Mom and Dad said we should not touch it."
"But it looks fun," Tom said. "I want to cut something with it."
He reached for the knife, but Amy pulled him back.
"Please, Tom, listen to me," Amy said. "The knife is not a toy. It is dangerous."
Tom did not listen. He pushed Amy away and grabbed the knife. He felt the blade and smiled.
"See, it is not so bad," he said. "I can cut this apple with it."
He put the apple on the cutting board and tried to cut it. But the knife was too big and heavy for him. He lost his balance and fell. The knife slipped from his hand and stabbed him in the chest. He screamed and dropped the apple.
Amy heard his scream and ran to him. She saw the blood and the knife. She was scared and sad.
"Tom, Tom, are you okay?" she cried. "I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I didn't mean to push you."
But Tom did not answer. He did not move. He did not breathe. He was dead.
Amy did not know what to do. She wanted to help him, but she did not know how. She wanted to call Mom and Dad, but she did not know where they were. She wanted to cry, but she had no tears. She just sat next to Tom and held his hand. She hoped he would wake up and play with her again. But he did not. He was dead.

"I wish for more flowers like this one. I wish they would bloom all over the garden and make it more beautiful. What do you wish for, Tom?"
Tom thought for a moment too. He had many wishes, but he wanted to share one with Lila. He smiled and said:
"I wish for more fun and games with you, Lila. I wish we would always be friends and play together. Do you think the flower will hear us, Lila?"
Lila nodded. She hoped the flower would hear them and make their wishes come true. She and Tom held hands and closed their eyes. They said their wishes out loud and thanked the flower.
Then they opened their eyes and gasped. The garden was full of red flowers like the one they had found. They were blooming everywhere, making the garden look like a firework. They were very happy and grateful. They never forgot the unknown flower that granted their wishes.

Anna was a shy girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had a big sister, Mia, who liked to play with her friends. Mia was not shy at all. She liked to talk and laugh and run.
One day, Mia and her friends came to Anna's room. They saw Anna's dolls and wanted to play with them. Mia said, "Anna, can we play with your dolls? They are so pretty and cute."
Anna felt scared. She did not want to share her dolls with Mia's friends. She did not know them. She said, "No, these are my dolls. You have your own toys. Go away."
Mia was angry. She said, "Anna, you are so mean and selfish. You have to share your toys. We are your guests. You have to be nice to us."
Anna said, "No, you are not my guests. You are Mia's guests. This is my room. You have to be nice to me."
Mia and her friends did not listen. They grabbed Anna's dolls and started to play with them. They made them talk and dance and sing. They did not care if they broke them or dirtied them.
Anna cried. She felt sad and angry. She wanted her dolls back. She said, "Stop it! Stop it! Give me my dolls! You are hurting them!"
Mia and her friends laughed. They said, "Anna, you are so silly and babyish. These are just dolls. They are not real. They do not feel anything. They do not need oxygen or food or water. They are just toys."
Anna said, "No, they are not just toys. They are my friends. They have names and stories and feelings. They need oxygen and food and water like me. They are real to me."
Mia and her friends did not understand. They thought Anna was weird and crazy. They said, "Anna, you are so weird and crazy. You need to grow up and play with real friends. You need to stop being so shy and have fun."
Anna said, "No, you are the ones who are weird and crazy. You do not know how to play with dolls. You do not know how to be gentle and kind. You do not know how to have fun."
Mia and her friends did not like Anna. They said, "Anna, you are no fun at all. We do not want to play with you. You are not our friend. You are just a baby."
Anna said, "I do not want to play with you either. You are not my friends. You are just mean and rude. You are just bullies."
Mia and her friends left Anna's room. They took some of her dolls with them. They said, "Bye, Anna. We do not care about you or your dolls. We have better things to do."
Anna was left alone in her room. She felt lonely and hurt. She hugged her remaining dolls and said, "I'm sorry, my friends. I love you. You are the best. You include me and make me happy."

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play pretend. They had a theater in their backyard, where they put on shows for their toys and parents. Tom liked to be the hero, and Lily liked to be the princess.
One day, a new boy moved in next door. His name was Max, and he had a lot of cool toys. He also liked to play pretend, and he asked Tom and Lily if he could join their theater. Tom and Lily said yes, and they welcomed Max to their group.
But soon, Tom noticed that Max always wanted to be the hero, and he always wanted to save Lily. Tom felt jealous, and he thought that Max was trying to take Lily away from him. He did not like that, and he wanted to make Max go away.
One day, they were playing a show about a dragon and a castle. Max was the hero, Lily was the princess, and Tom was the dragon. Tom decided to make the show more exciting, and he breathed fire at Max. He used a spray bottle and some red paper to make the fire look real.
"Watch out, Max!" Lily shouted. "The dragon is breathing fire at you!"
Max was scared, and he ran away from the fire. He tripped and fell on the ground, and he hurt his knee. He started to cry, and he called for his mom.
Tom felt bad, and he realized that he had done something wrong. He ran to Max, and he said he was sorry.
"I'm sorry, Max. I was just playing. I didn't mean to hurt you. Please don't be mad at me."
Max looked at Tom, and he saw that Tom was sorry. He stopped crying, and he said it was okay.
"It's okay, Tom. I'm not mad at you. I know you were just playing. But you should warn me before you breathe fire at me. That was scary."
Tom nodded, and he said he would warn him next time. He helped Max get up, and he gave him a band-aid for his knee. Lily came over, and she hugged them both.
"I'm glad you're both okay. You're both my friends, and I don't want you to fight. Can we play together again?"
Tom and Max smiled, and they said yes. They agreed to share the hero role, and to take turns saving Lily. They went back to their theater, and they played a new show. They had fun, and they learned to be nice to each other.

Mia nods. "Yes, I think he is nice. He has clear eyes. He looks happy."
Tom and Mia go closer to the picture. They want to say hello to Leo. But then they hear a loud roar. It is not Leo. It is a real leopard. He is behind the wall. He is angry.
"Run!" Tom and Mia shout. They run away from the wall. They are scared.
The leopard jumps over the wall. He sees Tom and Mia. He chases them. He is fast.
"Help!" Tom and Mia cry. They look for a place to hide.
They see a big tree. They run to the tree. They climb up the tree. They hold on tight.
The leopard reaches the tree. He cannot climb. He growls. He scratches the tree. He tries to get Tom and Mia.

Abigail was so happy. She quickly ran to the sink and washed her hands. When she was done, she returned to her desk and finished her quiz. She was finally able to hand in her very clean quiz.

The man smiles and says, "I am working, kids. I am making a new pond for the ducks and the fish. Do you like ducks and fish?"
Lily and Ben nod. They like ducks and fish. They think the pond will be nice.
The man says, "Working is hard, but it is good. It makes me strong and happy. Do you know what else makes me strong and happy?"
Lily and Ben shake their heads. They do not know.
The man says, "Eating good food makes me strong and happy. Food gives me energy to work. Do you know what food is good for you?"
Lily and Ben think. They say, "Fruits and vegetables are good for us. They make our stomachs happy. And milk and cheese are good for us. They make our bones strong."
The man nods. He says, "You are right, kids. Fruits, vegetables, milk and cheese are good for you. And so are meat, eggs, bread and water. They give you protein, carbs and fluids. Do you know what those are?"
Lily and Ben shake their heads. They do not know.
The man says, "They are things that help your body grow and work. You need them every day. But you also need something else. Do you know what that is?"
Lily and Ben think. They say, "Love?"
The man smiles. He says, "Yes, love. Love is the best thing for you. Love makes you happy and healthy. Love comes from your mom and dad, your family and friends, and from yourself. Do you love yourself?"
Lily and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, we love ourselves. And we love you, mister. Thank you for working and making the pond."
The man hugs them. He says, "You are welcome, kids. And thank you for loving me. You are very sweet and smart. Now, go and play. Have fun. And remember to eat well and love yourself."

Lila nods. She thinks it is a good idea. She picks up another stick.

"Go away, dog!" they yell. "This is our hut! You are not welcome here!"
The dog is surprised. It sees Lila and Tom with their sticks. It hears their loud voices. It thinks they are big and strong.

Lila and Tom cheer. They did it. They scared the dog. They are happy.

Lily liked to draw with her crayons. She had many colors, but her favorite was bright pink. She drew a big flower on the paper with bright pink petals and a yellow center.
"Look, Mommy, I made a flower for you!" Lily said, holding up her paper.
Mommy smiled and hugged Lily. "That's a very pretty flower, sweetie. Thank you for making it for me. Where did you get the bright pink crayon?"
Lily pointed to the box of crayons on the table. "It was in there, Mommy. I found it under the blue one."
Mommy nodded. "That's a nice crayon, Lily. But you know what? You have to be careful with crayons. They can make marks on things that are not paper. Like the wall, or the table, or your clothes."
Lily looked confused. "Why, Mommy? Crayons are for drawing."
Mommy took Lily's hand and walked to the wall. She pointed to a small bright pink mark on the white paint. "Do you see that, Lily? That's a crayon mark. You made it when you were drawing your flower. Crayons can make marks on the wall, and that's not good. The wall is not for drawing. It's for looking at."
Lily felt sorry. She did not mean to make a mark on the wall. She wanted to make Mommy happy, not sad. "I'm sorry, Mommy. I didn't know. How can I fix it?"
Mommy smiled again. She was not angry with Lily. She knew Lily was learning. She took an eraser from the drawer and gave it to Lily. "You can fix it with this, Lily. This is an eraser. It can wipe away crayon marks. Watch." She showed Lily how to rub the eraser on the wall gently. The bright pink mark faded away.
Lily clapped her hands. "Wow, Mommy, it's gone! The eraser is magic!"
Mommy laughed. "It's not magic, Lily. It's just a tool. But it's a very useful tool. You can use it to wipe away any crayon marks you make by mistake. But remember, only use crayons on paper, okay?"
Lily nodded. She hugged Mommy and said, "Okay, Mommy. I will only use crayons on paper. And I will use the eraser if I need to. Thank you for teaching me, Mommy. I love you."
Mommy kissed Lily and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are a very good and smart girl. And you make beautiful flowers."

Lily and Max felt very sorry and ashamed. They saw how gloomy mom was and how dirty the kitchen was. They wished they had shared the mixer and worked together.
"Mom, we are very sorry. We were bad and silly. We didn't mean to break the mixer and ruin the cake. We love you and we love baking with you. Can we help you clean up and make a new cake?" Lily and Max said.
Mom smiled and hugged them. She was still upset, but she forgave them.
"I love you too, Lily and Max. You made a mistake, but you learned from it. Next time, you have to share and cooperate. That's how we can have fun and make delicious cakes. Now, let's clean up and see if we have enough ingredients for a new cake." mom said.
Lily and Max nodded and helped mom clean up. They apologized to each other and promised to share and cooperate. They found some more flour, eggs, sugar, and chocolate. They made a new batter and baked a new cake. It was not as big as the first one, but it was still yummy and sweet. They enjoyed the cake with mom and felt happy and proud.
The moral of the story is: Sharing and cooperating are better than being selfish and greedy.

One day, Jane and her brother were playing in the garden. They were running after each other, when Jane saw a plant. She thought it was a special flower, so she decided to poke it with her finger.
But when she poked the flower the air filled with a horrible smell – it was poison! Jane was so scared that she quickly backed away.
Her brother smiled at her and said, “Don’t worry Jane. You were just being competitive and trying to be the best.” Jane and her brother ran away, happy that they were safe. And they never poked a poisonous flower ever again!

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy girl called Amy. She was very clumsy and often tripped over her own feet. 
One day, Amy decided to go to the park with her family. They arrived at the park and noticed a big, long stair. Amy looked up at it and got a little nervous. She had never seen a stair so big before! 
Her dad saw how scared she was and asked her, “What’s wrong, Amy?”.
“I don’t know if I can go up the stairs, they look so big!” replied Amy.
Her dad smiled and said, “No problem. We’ll go up together, one step at a time. I’ll help you.” 
With her dad’s help, Amy was able to go up the big stair without falling. She was relieved! 
Amy noticed that even if she was clumsy, she could still do incredible things with some help. She smiled and said, “Thank you, Dad!”

Soon, some kids came to look at their toys. Anna and Ben showed them what they had and asked for one or two coins for each toy. Some kids liked their toys and gave them coins. Some kids did not like their toys and said no thank you. Anna and Ben were happy to make some money and to give their toys to new friends.
But after a while, the sun became very hot and the box became very heavy. Anna and Ben started to feel uncomfortable and thirsty. They wanted to go home and drink some water and rest. They looked at their box and saw that they still had many toys left. They did not want to carry them all the way back home.
"Ben, what should we do?" Anna asked her brother.
"I have an idea," Ben said. "Let's give the rest of the toys to the kids who have no toys. Maybe they will be happy to have them."
"That's a good idea," Anna said. "Let's do that."
They looked around and saw a group of kids who had no toys. They walked over to them and said, "Hello, we have some toys for sale, but we are going home now. Do you want to have them for free?"
The kids looked surprised and happy. They said, "Yes, please, thank you very much!"
They took the toys from the box and hugged Anna and Ben. They said, "You are very kind and generous. We will take good care of your toys."
Anna and Ben smiled and said, "You're welcome. We hope you enjoy them."
They left the box and the paper under the tree and walked back home, holding hands. They felt tired but happy. They had sold some toys, made some money, and made some kids happy. They had a good day.

Once there was a Mama Bear and a Baby Bear. Mama Bear was making a delicious stew for dinner and Baby Bear had the honor of stirring it. 
Mama Bear said, “Stir the stew, Baby Bear. Make sure it’s nice and smooth.”
Baby Bear was stirring the stew as he thought, “Why do I have to do this? It’s so uncomfortable.” He was so focused on stirring that he didn’t realize that the stew was beginning to boil. 
Mama Bear watched and said, “Baby Bear, it looks like the stew is boiling. Don’t stir so hard, the heat is too strong.”
Baby Bear listened to Mama Bear and slowed down his stirring. He stirred softly and gently and soon the stew was nice and smooth. Baby Bear felt relieved and his heart filled with joy. 
Mama Bear smiled and said, “See, Baby Bear? Sometimes it’s best to be patient and gentle even when you feel uncomfortable.” 
And from that day on, Baby Bear understood that being gentle and patient was important and had a special place in his heart.

"Stop it, Tom!" Sam says. "That is my shark. You are hurting my toys. Give it back!"
"No, it is mine!" Tom says. He holds the shark tight. He does not want to share. He frowns at Sam.
Sam is angry and sad. He tries to take the shark from Tom. They pull and tug and fight. The shark is weak. It breaks in two. The water turns red.
Tom and Sam stop fighting. They look at the shark. They look at the water. They look at each other. They are scared. They cry.
Mom hears them cry. She runs to the bath. She sees the mess. She sees the broken shark. She sees the red water. She is mad.
"What did you do?" Mom says. "You are naughty boys. You ruined the shark. You wasted the soap. You made a mess. You are in trouble."
Tom and Sam are sorry. They say they are sorry. But Mom does not listen. She takes them out of the bath. She dries them and dresses them. She puts them in their beds. She does not read them a story. She does not kiss them good night.
Tom and Sam lie in their beds. They are wet and cold and sad. They miss their toys. They miss their mom. They wish they had shared the shark. They wish they had not fought. They wish they had a good ending.

One day, Tim and Lily were playing with Giraffe in their room. They threw Giraffe in the air and caught it. They hugged Giraffe and made it talk. They had fun with Giraffe.
But then, Tim had a bad idea. He wanted to see what was inside Giraffe. He took a pair of scissors and cut Giraffe's neck. He pulled out the white stuff and the red string. He laughed and said, "Look, Lily, Giraffe has a hole!"
Lily was very sad and angry. She loved Giraffe and did not want it to be hurt. She cried and said, "Tim, you are mean! You broke Giraffe! Giraffe is our friend, not a toy!"
Tim saw that Lily was crying and felt sorry. He realized that he had done a bad thing. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was curious. I didn't mean to break Giraffe. Can we fix it?"
Lily shook her head and said, "No, Tim, we can't fix it. You broke it too much. Now Giraffe is gone. You should be careful with your toys. They are not for breaking. They are for playing and loving."
Tim learned his lesson. He hugged Lily and said, "You are right, Lily. I was wrong. I will be good with my toys from now on. And I will be good with you, too. You are my sister and I love you."
Lily smiled and said, "I love you, too, Tim. But I still miss Giraffe."
Tim and Lily hugged each other and said goodbye to Giraffe. They buried Giraffe in the garden and planted a flower on top. They hoped that Giraffe was happy in the sky. They never broke their toys again. They were good children.

Anna was a wealthy girl who lived in a big house with many toys. She liked to play with her dolls and dress them in pretty clothes. But she was not happy. She wondered why she had no friends to play with. She felt lonely and bored.
One day, she saw a boy outside her window. He was wearing old clothes and had a dirty face. He was holding a ball and a stick. He was playing by himself, but he looked happy. He smiled and laughed as he threw the ball and hit it with the stick. Anna was curious. She wondered what it was like to play with him.
She opened the window and called out to him. "Hello, boy! What is your name?"
The boy looked up and saw her. He was surprised. He said, "Hello, girl! My name is Tom. What is your name?"
"My name is Anna. Do you want to play with me?" she asked.
Tom nodded. He said, "Yes, I do. But I have no toys. I only have this ball and this stick."
Anna said, "That's okay. I have many toys. You can come inside and play with me. I have dolls and cars and books and puzzles. You can choose what you like."
Tom smiled. He said, "Thank you, Anna. You are very kind. Can I bring my ball and my stick?"
Anna said, "Of course. They are your toys. Come on, let's go."
She helped him climb the window and they went inside. They played together for a long time. They shared their toys and stories and jokes. They had fun and became friends. Anna was happy. She wondered why she had never played with anyone before. She realized that having toys was not enough. She needed someone to share them with. She was glad that she met Tom. He was not wealthy, but he was happy. He taught her how to play with simple things. He made her laugh and smile. He was her friend.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big slide that looked fun. Ben wanted to go on the slide, but Lily was scared.
"Come on, Lily, it's not so high. I dare you to go on the slide with me," Ben said.
"No, Ben, I don't want to. It's too fast and too steep. I might fall and hurt myself," Lily said.
Ben was frustrated. He thought Lily was being silly. He wanted to show her that the slide was not scary at all. He had an idea.
"Look, Lily, I can make the slide even more fun. I can slide down holding this wire. It will make me go faster and smoother. Watch me," Ben said.
He grabbed a wire that was hanging from a nearby tree. He climbed up the ladder and sat on the slide. He held the wire with both hands and pushed himself down.
But Ben did not know that the wire was not strong enough to hold his weight. As he slid down, the wire snapped and he lost his balance. He tumbled down the slide and landed on the ground with a thud.
"Ow, ow, ow," Ben cried. He had scraped his knees and elbows and bumped his head.
Lily ran to him and helped him up. She was worried about him.
"Ben, are you okay? That was a bad idea. You should not play with wires. They can be dangerous. You could have hurt yourself more," Lily said.
Ben felt sorry and ashamed. He realized that Lily was right. He had been foolish and reckless. He hugged Lily and apologized.
"I'm sorry, Lily. You were smart and I was dumb. I should have listened to you. I won't dare you to do things that are scary or risky anymore. Can we still be friends?" Ben said.
Lily smiled and nodded. She forgave Ben and hugged him back.
"Of course we can, Ben. We are always friends. But next time, let's play something safer and nicer. How about the swings or the sandbox?" Lily said.
Ben agreed. He and Lily walked to the swings, holding hands. They forgot about the slide and the wire. They had fun together.

"Isabella, what are you doing?" Mommy said sternly. "You shouldn't stomp on the ants!"

"Look, Lily, a glass jar!" he said. "Let's open it and guess what's in it."
Lily came over and looked at the jar. She saw a label on it that said "Honey". She knew what honey was. It was sweet and sticky and good on bread.
"No, Ben, we can't open it," she said. "It's honey. Mommy said we can't have honey without asking. It's not for playing."
Ben didn't listen to Lily. He wanted to open the jar and taste the honey. He thought it would be fun to guess how much honey was in the jar. He grabbed the lid and twisted it hard. But the lid was too tight. He couldn't open it.
"Let me try, Ben," Lily said. "Maybe I can open it."
But Ben didn't want to share the jar. He pulled it away from Lily. He twisted the lid harder. He didn't see that the jar was slipping from his hand. He didn't hear Lily say "Be careful, Ben!"
The jar fell to the floor. It broke into many pieces. The honey spilled everywhere. Ben and Lily were shocked. They heard Mommy coming.
"What happened here?" Mommy asked. She saw the broken glass and the honey. She was angry and sad. She loved her honey. She had bought it from the farmer's market. It was special honey.
"Ben and Lily, you are in big trouble," she said. "You broke the glass jar. You wasted the honey. You made a mess. You didn't listen to me. You didn't listen to each other. Why did you do that?"
Ben and Lily felt sorry. They knew they had done something bad. They didn't mean to break the jar. They didn't mean to make Mommy mad. They wanted to make her happy.
"We're sorry, Mommy," they said. "We were playing. We wanted to guess what was in the jar. We didn't know it was honey. We didn't know it was special. We're sorry."
Mommy sighed. She was still angry and sad. But she also loved Ben and Lily. She knew they were young and curious. She knew they made mistakes. She wanted to teach them.
"Ben and Lily, you need to learn some things," she said. "You need to learn to read labels. You need to learn to ask before you touch things. You need to learn to share and take turns. You need to learn to be careful and clean. Do you understand?"
Ben and Lily nodded. They understood. They wanted to learn. They wanted to make Mommy happy.
"OK, then," Mommy said. "Let's clean up this mess. And then we'll have some bread and honey. But only a little bit. And only if you say please and thank you. And only if you promise to be good. Deal?"
Ben and Lily smiled. They said please and thank you. They promised to be good. They made a deal. They helped Mommy clean up. They had some bread and honey. They hugged Mommy. They said sorry again.
Mommy hugged them back. She said it's OK. She said she loved them. She said they were good kids. She said they could play again. But only with safe things. And only with nice words. And only with happy faces. Deal?
Ben and Lily said deal. They were happy. They learned something. They guessed something. They loved something. They loved Mommy. They loved each other. They loved honey. And they loved glass. But only when it was smooth and shiny. And only when it was not broken. And only when it was not on the floor.

Molly took a few careful steps outside and looked around. She was ready to go! Molly started walking, carrying her rucksack. She looked very careful when she crossed the street and then she kept walking.
She went up and down hills and over bridges. As she walked, she carried her rucksack very carefully, so the stamp wouldn't get lost.
Then Molly came to a special place, with trees, butterflies and lots of flowers. She stopped and put the rucksack down. Carefully, she opened it and took out the stamp. She stamped it on a big, flat rock and smiled. She had her very own adventure!

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. They liked to run on the grass, swing on the swings, and slide on the slide. Sometimes they also liked to throw pebbles in the pond and watch the ripples.
One day, they found a big pile of pebbles near the pond. They thought it would be fun to throw them all in the water. They picked up some pebbles and started to toss them.
"Look, Anna, I can throw farther than you!" Ben said.
"No, you can't, Ben, I can throw farther than you!" Anna said.
They threw and threw, trying to outdo each other. They did not notice that some of the pebbles hit the ducks and the fish in the pond. The ducks and the fish were scared and hurt by the pebbles. They tried to swim away, but some of them could not.
A man who was walking his dog saw what Anna and Ben were doing. He came over and said, "Stop, stop, what are you doing? Don't you see that you are hurting the animals in the pond? They are living things, just like you. How would you like it if someone threw pebbles at you?"
Anna and Ben stopped and looked at the pond. They saw the ducks and the fish that were hit by the pebbles. They felt sorry for them. They realized that they were wrong to throw pebbles at them.
"We're sorry, mister, we didn't mean to hurt them. We just wanted to have fun," Anna said.
"We didn't know that they were living things, just like us. We won't do it again," Ben said.
The man nodded and said, "That's good, I'm glad you learned your lesson. Next time, be more thoughtful of the animals and the nature around you. They are your friends, too. You can have fun without harming them."
Anna and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, mister, we will. Thank you for telling us."
They put down the pebbles and went to the pond. They gently stroked the ducks and the fish that were hurt. They said, "We're sorry, ducks and fish, we won't hurt you again. We hope you feel better soon."
The ducks and the fish quacked and splashed, as if to say, "Thank you, Anna and Ben, we forgive you. We hope you have fun, too."
Anna and Ben smiled and waved at them. They learned to be more thoughtful of the animals and the nature around them. They still played in the park, but they never threw pebbles in the pond again.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a big red strawberry growing on a plant. They both wanted to eat it, but there was only one.
"I saw it first!" Lily said. "It is mine!"
"No, I saw it first!" Ben said. "It is mine!"
They started to pull the strawberry, but it was very strong. They could not break it off the plant.
"Let go!" Lily said. "You are selfish!"
"Let go!" Ben said. "You are selfish!"
They pulled and pulled, but the strawberry did not move. They got very tired and hot. They needed to rest.
Then, they heard a voice. It was Mom.
"What are you doing, children?" Mom asked. "Why are you fighting over a strawberry?"
Lily and Ben felt ashamed. They let go of the strawberry and looked at Mom.
"We both wanted to eat it, Mom," Lily said. "But there is only one."
Mom smiled and picked the strawberry. She broke it in half and gave one piece to Lily and one piece to Ben.
"Here you go, children," Mom said. "You can both have some. Sharing is caring. It is not nice to be selfish. There are more strawberries in the garden. You can find them together and enjoy them."

"Sorry, Lily," Ben said. "I was selfish. You can have the next strawberry."

"Spin us fast, Mommy!" Lila said.
"Spin us faster, Mommy!" Ben said.
Their moms smiled and pushed the merry-go-round. Lila and Ben felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They giggled and shouted with joy. They felt like they were flying.
But then, something bad happened. Ben's shoe came off. It flew in the air and landed on the grass. Ben did not notice. He was too busy having fun. But his foot slipped off the merry-go-round. He lost his balance and fell off. He hit the ground hard and rolled over. He felt a sharp pain in his arm.
"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Ben cried.
Lila saw Ben fall. She was scared. She wanted to help him. She let go of the merry-go-round and jumped off. But she jumped too fast. She did not land on her feet. She landed on her knee. She felt a dull pain in her leg.
"Ouch! Ouch! Ouch!" Lila cried.
Their moms heard their cries. They ran to them and hugged them. They checked their wounds and kissed them. They said they were sorry and they loved them. They said they would take them to the doctor and make them feel better.
Lila and Ben were sad. They did not want to go to the doctor. They did not want to have pain. They wanted to play and laugh and dance. They looked at each other and tried to smile.
"Maybe we can dance later," Lila said.
"Maybe we can dance tomorrow," Ben said.
They nodded and held hands. They hoped they would be fit soon. They hoped they would have fun again. They hoped they would dance again.

"Wow, where is it going?" Tom asks.
They run to the water and wave at the boat. The boat stops and a man comes out. He has a hat and a smile.
"Hello, children, do you want to see my boat?" he says.
"Yes, please!" Lily and Tom say.
The man helps them get on the boat. He shows them the rooms, the kitchen, and the toys. He gives them juice and cookies. He tells them stories about the sea and the animals.
"Where are you going, sir?" Lily asks.
"I am going to a lovely island. It has many trees, flowers, and birds. Do you want to come with me?" he says.
Lily and Tom look at each other. They think of their parents and their home.
"Thank you, sir, but we have to go back. Our parents will miss us," Tom says.
"OK, I understand. But maybe you can visit me another day. Here, take this map. It shows you where the island is. It is not far from here. You can stand on the shore and see it," he says.
He gives them a map and a hug. He helps them get off the boat. He waves goodbye and sails away.
Lily and Tom run back to the sand. They look at the map and the water. They see a small dot of green.
"Is that the island?" Lily asks.
"I think so. It looks lovely," Tom says.
They smile and put the map in their pocket. They decide to keep it as a secret. They play in the sand until their parents come. They are happy.

"Hello, dog!" Tom says. He wants to pet the dog. He reaches out his hand.
But the dog does not like Tom. The dog growls and shows his teeth. He bites Tom's hand. Tom cries out in pain.
"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Tom says. "The dog bit me!"
Lily is scared. She does not know what to do. She sees a man nearby. The man is wearing a blue shirt and a hat. He has a leash in his hand. He is the dog's owner.
"Help! Help!" Lily shouts. She runs to the man. "Your dog bit my friend! He is hurt!"
The man is sorry. He did not see the dog run away. He pulls the dog away from Tom. He says sorry to Tom and Lily.
"I'm so sorry, kids. My dog is not friendly. He does not like strangers. He should not have bitten you. Are you okay?" the man says.
Tom is still crying. His hand is bleeding. He needs a band-aid.
"It hurts a lot. I need a band-aid," Tom says.
The man is helpful. He has a first-aid kit in his bag. He takes out a band-aid and puts it on Tom's hand. He says sorry again.
"Here, this will make it better. I'm very sorry, Tom. You are brave. Can you forgive my dog?" the man says.
Tom looks at the dog. The dog looks sad. He lowers his head and whines.
Tom is not angry anymore. He knows the dog did not mean to hurt him. He says yes.
"Yes, I forgive your dog. But he should not bite anyone else. He should be nice," Tom says.
The man nods. He thanks Tom and Lily. He says he will train his dog to be nicer. He says goodbye and leaves with his dog.
Tom and Lily hug each other. They are glad they are okay. They decide to play somewhere else. They do not want to see the dog again. Not yet.

Anna loved to sing and dance. She wanted to perform for her family and friends. She practiced every day in her room, with her teddy bear as her audience. She made up her own songs and moves. She felt happy and proud.
One day, her teacher said they would have a show at school. Anna was very excited. She wanted to show everyone her talent. She told her teacher she would sing and dance. Her teacher smiled and said, "That sounds wonderful, Anna. But remember, you have to share the stage with your classmates. Everyone has something unique to offer."
Anna nodded, but she did not listen. She thought she was the best performer in the class. She did not care about what the others would do. She wanted to shine by herself.
The day of the show came. Anna wore her favorite dress and put on a big bow. She waited for her turn. She saw her classmates perform different things. Some read poems, some played instruments, some did magic tricks. They all looked happy and confident. The audience clapped and cheered for them.
Then it was Anna's turn. She ran to the stage and grabbed the microphone. She started to sing and dance. She sang very loud and fast. She danced very wild and hard. She did not look at the audience. She only looked at herself. She thought she was amazing.
But the audience did not think so. They did not clap or cheer. They looked confused and bored. Some covered their ears. Some whispered to each other. Some left their seats. Anna did not notice. She kept singing and dancing.
When she finished, she expected a big applause. But there was none. There was only silence. She looked at the audience. She saw their faces. They looked unhappy and annoyed. She felt confused and sad.
Her teacher came to the stage and gave her a hug. She said, "Anna, you have a beautiful voice and a lot of energy. But you did not perform well today. You did not share the stage with your classmates. You did not respect the audience. You did not enjoy the show. You only cared about yourself. That is not what a performer does. A performer gives and receives. A performer listens and learns. A performer celebrates and appreciates. Do you understand?"
Anna nodded, but she did not say anything. She felt ashamed and sorry. She realized she made a mistake. She wished she could do it again. She wished she could be a better performer. She wished she could be a better friend.

One day, a new boy comes to the yard. His name is Sam. He has a small ball and a small hoop. He asks Tom and Mia if he can play with them. They say yes.
Sam is very good at basketball. He throws the ball in the hoop every time. He is fast and strong. Tom and Mia are amazed. They observe how he plays. They want to learn from him.
"Wow, you are so good, Sam!" Tom says. "How do you do that?"
Sam smiles. He says, "I practice a lot. I watch other players on TV. I learn from them. Do you want me to show you some tricks?"
Tom and Mia nod. They are eager to learn. Sam teaches them how to dribble, how to pass, and how to shoot. He is kind and patient. He helps them when they make mistakes.
Tom and Mia improve their skills. They have fun playing with Sam. They are not slow anymore. They are fast and smart. They thank Sam for being their friend and their teacher. They invite him to play with them again. Sam agrees. He is happy to have new friends. They all hug and smile. They love basketball.

The rocket was amazing. It had many buttons and lights and screens. Tom touched everything. He did not know what they did, but they made funny noises. He felt happy. He sat in the pilot's seat and put on a helmet. He felt like a real astronaut.
Suddenly, the rocket started to shake. Tom heard a loud voice say "Countdown to launch: 10, 9, 8, 7...". He was scared. He tried to get out, but the door was locked. He screamed for help, but no one heard him. The rocket lifted off the ground and flew into the sky. Tom saw the park, the trees, the houses, and the people get smaller and smaller. He cried. He wanted to go back home.
The rocket went higher and higher, until it reached the clouds. Then, it disappeared. No one knew where it went. Tom was alone in the rocket, with no one to help him. He did not know what to do. He wished he had never gone inside the rocket. He wished he had stayed with his rockets in his room. He wished he had listened to the sign. He learned a hard lesson: rockets are not for playing. Rockets are for rich people only.

"Not yet, sweetie. That's for later. It's a surprise," Mom said.
Anna and Ben looked at each other. They were curious. They waited until Mom went to the kitchen. Then they tiptoed to the sofa and peeked inside the sack.
They saw a lot of things. They saw a teddy bear, a ball, a puzzle, a coloring book, and a calendar. The calendar had pictures of animals and numbers. It was weird.
"What is this?" Ben asked, holding the calendar.
"I don't know. Maybe it's a game," Anna said.
They tried to flip the pages, but they were stuck together. They pulled harder, but the calendar ripped.
"Oh no! We broke it!" Anna cried.
Mom heard the noise and came back to the living room. She saw the torn calendar and the open sack.
"What did you do?" Mom asked, looking angry.
"We're sorry, Mom. We just wanted to see the surprise," Ben said.
Mom sighed. She picked up the calendar and the sack.
"This was not a surprise for you. This was a surprise for Grandma. It's her birthday tomorrow. The calendar was a special gift. It had photos of you and your cousins. Now it's ruined," Mom said.
Anna and Ben felt bad. They did not know it was for Grandma. They loved Grandma. They wanted to make her happy.
"We're sorry, Mom. Can we fix it?" Anna asked.
Mom shook her head.
"No, honey. It's too late. You should have waited and asked me first. Now we have to find another gift for Grandma. And you have to say sorry to her too," Mom said.
Anna and Ben nodded. They learned their lesson. They hugged Mom and said they were sorry. They hoped Grandma would forgive them. They wondered what they could give her instead. Maybe a drawing or a hug. Or both.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toy cars in the garden. They liked to race them on the dirt path and make vroom noises. Tom had a red car and Lily had a blue car. They both loved their cars very much.
One day, a big dog came into the garden. He saw the toy cars and thought they were bones. He ran towards them and grabbed Tom's red car in his mouth. He bit it hard and tore off one of the wheels. Tom saw this and was very upset. He cried and shouted at the dog.
"Bad dog! Give me back my car! You broke it!" Tom said.
Lily heard Tom and came to see what was wrong. She saw the dog with the red car and felt sorry for Tom. She also felt scared of the dog. She wanted to help Tom, but she did not know what to do.
She remembered that her mom had told her to be kind to animals, even if they did something wrong. She also remembered that her mom had given her a bag of dog treats. She ran to get the bag and came back to the garden. She waved the bag at the dog and said in a soft voice.
"Hello, dog. Do you want a treat? Let go of the car and I will give you one."
The dog smelled the treat and let go of the car. He wagged his tail and came closer to Lily. Lily gave him a treat and petted him gently. The dog licked her hand and barked happily.
Tom stopped crying and picked up his car. He saw that the wheel was gone and felt sad. He looked at Lily and the dog and felt a little better. He said to Lily.
"Thank you, Lily. You are very brave and nice. I'm sorry I yelled at the dog. He did not know it was my car."
Lily smiled and said to Tom.
"You're welcome, Tom. I'm sorry your car is broken. Maybe we can fix it together. Or we can share my car. It has four wheels."
Tom nodded and said to Lily.
"Okay, Lily. You are a good friend. And the dog is not so bad. Maybe we can play with him too."
They hugged each other and played with the dog and the cars. They learned that being kind and forgiving is better than being angry and mean. They also learned that sharing and helping is more fun than fighting and hurting. They had a happy day in the garden.

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and find things. Sometimes they found worms, sometimes they found stones, sometimes they found shiny things.
One day, they found something black and hard. It was not a stone, and it was not shiny. It was coal. Ben and Lily did not know what coal was. They thought it was a toy.
"Look, Lily, I found a toy!" Ben said, holding the coal in his hand.
"Let me see, Ben!" Lily said, reaching for the coal.
But Ben did not want to share. He wanted to keep the coal for himself. He pinched Lily's hand when she tried to take it.
"Ow, Ben, that hurts!" Lily cried, pulling her hand away.
"Mine, mine, mine!" Ben shouted, holding the coal tightly.
Lily was angry and sad. She did not like Ben anymore. She ran to their mom, who was sitting on a bench.
"Mom, Ben pinched me!" Lily said, showing her hand.
Mom looked at Lily's hand. She saw a red mark. She was serious.
"Ben, come here!" Mom called.
Ben came, still holding the coal. He looked scared.
"Ben, did you pinch Lily?" Mom asked.
Ben nodded. He knew he did something bad.
"Why did you do that, Ben?" Mom asked.
"Because I found a toy and she wanted it," Ben said.
Mom shook her head. She was not happy.
"Ben, that is not a toy. That is coal. Coal is dirty and can hurt you. And you should not pinch Lily. Pinching is not nice. Pinching is mean. You have to say sorry to Lily and give her the coal," Mom said.
Ben felt sorry. He did not want to hurt Lily. He did not want to be mean. He gave the coal to Lily and said sorry.
Lily took the coal and said thank you. She was not angry and sad anymore. She was happy.
Mom smiled. She was proud of Ben and Lily.
"Good, Ben and Lily. Now you can play nicely together. But please, do not play with coal. Coal is not a toy. Coal is for the fire," Mom said.
Ben and Lily nodded. They understood. They threw the coal away and went to play with something else. They were friends again.

Lily and Ben were playing dress-up in their room. They had many clothes and hats and shoes to try on. Lily liked to wear a pink dress and a crown. Ben liked to wear a suit and a tie.
"Look at me, I am a princess!" Lily said, spinning around.
"Look at me, I am a boss!" Ben said, fixing his tie.
They pretended to have a tea party with their toys. They talked and laughed and had fun.
Then, their mom called them for lunch. "Lily, Ben, come downstairs, it's time to eat!"
Lily and Ben ran to the door. But Ben did not want to take off his suit. He liked it too much.
"No, I want to remain in my suit!" Ben said. "It is cool and nice!"
"But you will get it dirty!" Lily said. "And mom will be mad!"
"I don't care!" Ben said. "I am a boss, I can do what I want!"
Lily shook her head. She thought Ben was being stupid. She took off her dress and crown and put them away. She went downstairs to have lunch.
Ben remained in his suit. He followed Lily downstairs. He sat at the table and grabbed a sandwich.
But he soon regretted his choice. The sandwich was messy and sticky. It had peanut butter and jelly and banana. It dripped on his suit and made a big stain.
"Ben, what have you done?" mom said, seeing the stain. "That suit is not yours, it is dad's! He needs it for work!"
Ben felt bad. He looked at his suit and saw the stain. He wished he had listened to Lily. He realized he was being stupid.
"Sorry, mom," Ben said, hanging his head. "I was playing dress-up and I liked the suit. I did not want to take it off."
Mom sighed. She was not happy, but she was not too angry. She knew Ben was just a kid and he liked to pretend.
"It's okay, Ben," mom said. "But next time, please be more careful. And don't wear dad's suit without asking. It is not a toy, it is a special clothes for work."
Ben nodded. He said sorry to dad too. He took off his suit and gave it to mom. He hoped she could clean it.
He learned his lesson. He decided to play dress-up with his own clothes next time. Or maybe he would try something else. Maybe he would be a pirate or a superhero or a dinosaur. He still liked to pretend, but he did not want to be stupid again.

Her mom smiled and answered with a twinkle in her eye "The universe is a big place that is full of different things to explore". Lina was amazed and asked "Can I explore the universe?" Her mother laughed and said: "Not today, but you can explore something delicious". 
Lina then took a deep breath and followed her mother to the kitchen. Lina's eyes widened when she saw the table covered with sweet treats, cakes, tarts and cookies. Her mother said "You can explore the delicious treats in front of you, and I will let you pick your own treat". Lina carefully answered by choosing a cookie filled with chocolate chips. 
Lina sat down to munch on her cookie and thought about her mother's advice. Even though she could not explore the whole universe, she could explore a small part of the world around her and discover what was delicious. She realized that exploration didn't have to be far away, it could be in her own backyard!
Morals of the story: The moral of the story is that exploration doesn't have to be far away, sometimes there are delicious things to explore right around the corner.

"Stop!" he said. "You are messing up my home. Leave the leaves alone!"
Tom and Lily heard the snail. They were surprised. They did not know snails could talk. They looked at the snail and felt sorry.
"We are sorry, snail," Tom said. "We did not know you lived here. We just wanted to sort the leaves by color."
"We can help you make your home again," Lily said. "We can put the leaves back where they were."
The snail smiled. He was happy. He liked Tom and Lily. They were kind and friendly.
"Thank you, Tom and Lily," he said. "You are good friends. You can sort the leaves by color, but please leave some for me."
Tom and Lily nodded. They agreed. They sorted the leaves by color, but they also left some for the snail. They made a nice home for him under the oak tree. They played with the snail and learned more about him. They had a great day in the park.

Anna and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They saw a big bottle on the table. It was red and shiny. They wanted to see what was inside.
"Look, Ben, what is that?" Anna asked.
"I don't know. Maybe it is juice. Let's open it and try it," Ben said.
They opened the bottle and poured some in a cup. They smelled it. It was not juice. It was something else. It was bad.
"Yuck, this is disgusting!" Anna said. She made a face and spit it out.
"Me too, this is gross!" Ben said. He threw the cup away.
They heard a noise. It was Mom. She came into the kitchen and saw the mess. She was angry.
"What are you doing? That is not juice. That is wine. Wine is for grown-ups, not for kids. You could get sick. And you wasted a lot of it. That was very naughty," Mom said.
She took the bottle and the cup and cleaned the table. She made Anna and Ben say sorry. She told them to go to their room and think about what they did.
Anna and Ben felt bad. They did not like wine. They did not like being naughty. They did not like making Mom angry. They wished they had not opened the bottle. They learned their lesson. They decided to never touch wine again.

Sara and Ben were having breakfast with their mom and dad. They liked to eat eggs, toast and sausage. Sara saw a big sausage on dad's plate and wanted it. She asked dad, "Can I have your sausage, please?"
Dad smiled and said, "No, Sara, this is my sausage. You have your own sausage on your plate. You should be happy with what you have and not want more."
But Sara did not listen. She waited until dad was not looking and leaned over to grab his sausage. But she leaned too far and fell off her chair. She bumped her head on the floor and started to cry.
Mom and dad rushed to help her. They hugged her and checked her head. They said, "Are you okay, Sara? That was a big fall. You should be careful and not lean over the table like that."
Sara felt sorry and said, "I'm sorry, mom and dad. I was trying to take dad's sausage. I was greedy and not nice. I hurt myself and made a mess."
Mom and dad said, "It's okay, Sara. We forgive you. But you should learn from your mistake. You should be thankful for what you have and not take what belongs to others. That is not fair or kind."
Sara nodded and said, "I understand, mom and dad. I will be more grateful and respectful. Can I still have my sausage?"
Mom and dad said, "Yes, you can. But first, let's clean up the mess and put some ice on your head. You will be fine soon. We love you, Sara."
Sara smiled and said, "I love you too, mom and dad. Thank you for taking care of me and teaching me a lesson."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read old books. One day, Lily found a very old book in her room. The book was big and dusty. She opened the book and started to read.
As Lily read the book, she heard a voice. It was a tiny voice that said, "Hello, can you mind me?" Lily looked around and saw a small bug. The bug was talking to her! "I am a book bug," said the bug. "I live in old books."
Lily was very surprised. She had never met a talking bug before. The bug asked Lily to help him find a new home. Lily said, "I will help you, little bug." So, they went on an adventure to find the perfect home for the book bug.
Together, they searched Lily's house. They looked in the kitchen, the living room, and even the bathroom. Then, they found a big, old book in the attic. The book bug loved it! He said, "Thank you, Lily, for minding me and helping me find a new home."
From that day on, Lily and the book bug became best friends. They read many old books together and went on many more adventures. And they lived happily ever after.

Lily and Tom were playing in the grass. They liked to run and jump and roll on the green and soft grass. They also liked to pick flowers and make crowns for their heads.
"Look, Lily, I found a yellow flower!" Tom said, holding a dandelion in his hand.
"That's not a flower, Tom, that's a weed!" Lily said, pointing at the dandelion. "Flowers are pretty and smell good. Weeds are ugly and make you sneeze."
Tom did not understand. He thought the dandelion was pretty and he liked to blow the seeds and watch them fly. He did not sneeze when he smelled it.
"Why is it a weed, Lily?" Tom asked, looking at the dandelion.
"Because it is, Tom, because it is!" Lily said, getting angry. "Don't be stupid, Tom, weeds are bad and flowers are good. You should know that!"
Tom felt sad. He did not like Lily calling him stupid. He did not think he was stupid. He thought Lily was mean. He did not want to play with her anymore.
He threw the dandelion on the ground and ran away from Lily. He found a shady spot under a big tree and sat down. He felt lonely and hurt.
Lily saw Tom running away. She felt sorry. She did not mean to hurt Tom. She liked Tom. He was her friend. She wanted to play with him again.
She ran after Tom and found him under the tree. She sat next to him and said, "I'm sorry, Tom, I'm sorry I called you stupid. You are not stupid. You are smart and funny and kind. I was stupid. I was mean. Can you forgive me?"
Tom looked at Lily. He saw her eyes were wet and her lips were trembling. He felt sorry for her too. He did not want her to be sad. He wanted her to be happy.
He smiled and said, "It's okay, Lily, it's okay. I forgive you. You are not stupid. You are smart and pretty and nice. I was sad. I was angry. Can we be friends again?"
Lily smiled and said, "Yes, Tom, yes. We can be friends again. I'm glad you forgive me. I'm glad you are my friend."
They hugged and made up. They went back to the grass and picked more flowers and weeds. They did not care what they were. They only cared that they were happy. They understood each other.

Sara and Ben went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw many fish and shells and crabs. They also saw a jellyfish. It was big and pink and had long, long arms.
"Look, Sara, a jellyfish!" Ben said. "It looks like a balloon. Can I touch it?"
"No, Ben, don't touch it!" Sara said. "Mom said jellyfish can hurt you. They can sting you with their arms. It will make you cry and your skin will be red and sore."
"But it looks so pretty and soft," Ben said. He did not listen to Sara. He walked closer to the jellyfish. He reached out his hand to touch it.
"Ben, stop!" Sara shouted. But it was too late. The jellyfish stung Ben's hand. Ben screamed and ran back to Sara. His hand was red and swollen. He cried and cried.
Mom and Dad heard Ben's cry. They ran to him and saw his hand. They were worried and angry. They took Ben to the nurse. The nurse put some cream on his hand and wrapped it with a bandage. She told Ben to be careful and not touch jellyfish again.
"I'm sorry, Mom, Dad, Sara," Ben said. "I was silly and curious. I should have listened to Sara. She was right. Jellyfish can hurt you. I learned my lesson."
Mom, Dad, and Sara hugged Ben. They were glad he was okay. They told him they loved him and forgave him. They also told him to zip his mouth next time he wanted to do something silly and dangerous.
The moral of the story is: Listen to your elders and don't touch things that can harm you.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jane. They were playing in the garden on a sunny day.
Suddenly, a mosquito flew over to them. It buzzed around Jack's head, trying to bite him. Jack tried to swat it away, but it was too fast.
Jane laughed at him. She said, "Ha ha, Jack! The mosquito is teasing you!"
Jack got very angry. He tried swatting at the mosquito with both hands, but everytime he almost got it, the mosquito flew away. 
Suddenly, an idea came to him. He grabbed his garden hose and started spraying it.
The mosquito got very wet. It buzzed away, grumbling to itself.
Jack looked at Jane and said, "Ha ha! Now the mosquito is really mad!" 
Jane and Jack laughed and then went back to playing in the garden.

The cow was very scared and exclaimed, “Oh no! What’s happening?”
The rabbit said to the cow, “Please help me! The fox wants to catch me and eat me.”
The cow thought and thought. He then had an idea. He said to the rabbit, “Climb on my back and I’ll take you away.”

So the cow and the rabbit took their regular nap in the valley, and all was peaceful again.

As the cat was eating the meat, a small bird came by. The bird saw the cat eating the meat and wanted some too. The bird asked the cat, "Can I have some meat too?" The cat said, "No, this is my meat. You can't have any."
The bird was sad but had a smart idea. The bird flew up to the tree and started to sing a very pretty song. The cat liked the song and started to dance. The cat danced and danced and did not see the meat fall from the tree.
The bird quickly grabbed the meat and flew away. The cat was sad, but he learned that it is good to share with others. From that day on, the cat and the bird became friends and shared their food.

The hungry mouse had a plan. He found a long stick. He used the stick to try to get the cheese out of the trap. The mouse was very careful not to slip. He did not want to get caught in the trap. He pushed the cheese with the stick, but the cheese did not move.
Then, something unexpected happened. A big cat came into the room. The cat saw the mouse and wanted to catch him. The mouse was scared, but he had an idea. He pushed the stick one more time, and the cheese slipped out of the trap. The trap snapped shut, and the noise scared the cat away.
The hungry mouse was very happy. He got the cheese and did not get caught in the trap. The cat did not catch him either. The mouse ate the cheese and went back to his little home, safe and sound. And from that day on, the mouse was more careful about traps and always looked out for the big cat.

Sam and Ben cheer. They thank mom and run inside. They enjoy their ice cream. They feel good. They are glad they did their exercise. They decide to do it again tomorrow.

He lifted the pig and the balloon and let them go. The pig and the balloon floated up in the air. Tom was happy. He clapped his hands and laughed. He watched the pig and the balloon fly over his farm.
But the pig was not happy. It was scared. It did not like to fly. It wanted to be on the ground with the other animals. It squealed and wriggled. It tried to get rid of the balloon. But the sticky thing was too strong. The pig and the balloon flew higher and higher.
Tom saw the pig was not happy. He felt sorry. He wanted to help the pig. He ran to his box of toys and looked for something. He saw a pair of scissors. He knew scissors could cut things. He took the scissors and ran after the pig and the balloon.
He jumped and reached for the balloon. He was careful not to hurt the pig. He cut the balloon with the scissors. The balloon popped and the air came out. The pig and the balloon fell down. Tom caught the pig and hugged it. He said sorry to the pig. He took off the sticky thing from the pig's tail. He put the pig back in the barn with the other animals. The pig was happy. Tom was happy. He learned a lesson. He never attached a balloon to a pig again.

The turkey did not listen. It found some corn on the ground and started to eat it. It did not share with the other birds.

"Maybe we can teach it to be nice," Tom said. "Let's try to give it some of our snacks."
They took out some crackers and grapes from their backpacks and put them on the grass. They waved to the turkey and smiled.
"Look, turkey, we have some yummy snacks for you!" Lily said. "You can have some if you share with us and the other birds."
The turkey saw the snacks and was curious. It walked slowly to the grass and pecked at a cracker. It tasted good.
"Good turkey, good turkey," Tom said. "See, sharing is fun!"
The turkey nodded and made a soft noise. It gave some of the snacks to the other birds and let them eat with it.
Lily and Tom were happy. They clapped and cheered.
"Yay, we taught the turkey to be nice!" Lily said.
They sat on the grass and ate their snacks with the turkey and the other birds. They became friends and had a good time.

Lila was an adventurous girl who loved to explore. She liked to climb trees, dig in the sand, and chase butterflies. One day, she saw a big balloon floating in the sky. It was red and shiny and had a basket underneath. Lila wondered what it would be like to ride in the balloon and see the world from above.
She ran after the balloon, hoping to catch it. She followed it across the field, over the hill, and into the forest. She did not notice that she was far away from her home and her family. She only had eyes for the balloon.
"Hello, little girl," a voice said from the basket. "Do you want to join me in my balloon?"
Lila looked up and saw a friendly man with a long beard and a hat. He smiled and waved at her.
"Who are you?" Lila asked.
"I am a traveler," the man said. "I go wherever the wind takes me. I see many things and meet many people. It is a wonderful life."
Lila was curious and excited. She wanted to see many things and meet many people too. She wanted to be a traveler.
"Can I come with you?" she asked.
The man nodded. "Of course, you can. But you have to ask your parents first. Do they know where you are?"
Lila suddenly remembered her parents. She had left them without saying goodbye. She felt a pang of guilt and fear. She did not know how to find her way back.
"I don't know," she said. "I was following the balloon. I wanted to see the sky."
The man frowned. "That was not very wise, little girl. The sky is beautiful, but it does not belong to you. You belong to your parents. They must be very worried about you. You should go back to them."
Lila nodded. She realized that the man was right. She loved the balloon, but she loved her parents more. She wanted to be with them.
"Can you help me go back?" she asked.
The man smiled. "Of course, I can. I have a map and a compass. I can take you to the nearest town and find someone who can take you home. Come on, hop in the basket. It will be a short ride."
Lila thanked the man and climbed into the basket. She felt a rush of air as the balloon lifted off the ground. She looked down and saw the forest, the hill, and the field. She looked up and saw the sky. It was blue and bright and full of clouds. She felt happy and grateful. She had seen the sky, but she had also learned a lesson. She had been adventurous, but she had also been careless. She decided to be more careful and respectful in the future. She decided to always tell her parents where she was going and when she was coming back. She decided to enjoy the sky, but not to forget where she belonged.

Lily's aunt was sad. She said, "But I just want to admire your doll. She is so attractive. Don't you want to share with me?" Lily shook her head. She hugged Anna and said, "No, she is mine. Go away."
Lily's mom saw what happened. She was not happy. She said, "Lily, that is not nice. Your aunt came to visit and brought you a gift. You should be polite and let her hold your doll. Sharing is caring. How would you feel if someone did not share with you?"
Lily thought for a moment. She remembered how she felt when her friend Ben did not share his truck with her. She felt angry and sad. She did not want to make her aunt feel that way. She said, "I'm sorry, auntie. You can hold Anna. She is attractive, right?" She gave Anna to her aunt and smiled.
Lily's aunt smiled too. She said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. Anna is very attractive, and so are you. Do you want to read the book with me?" Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, please. I like animals. Can we read it together?"
Lily and her aunt sat on the couch and read the book. They saw pictures of lions, monkeys, elephants, and more. They had fun and learned new things. Lily was happy. She learned that sharing can make everyone happy.

Tim asked the bird, "Why are you so sad?" The bird answered, "I am cold and tired, and I can't relax during this winter."
Tim wanted to help the bird. He thought of a good plan. He took the bird inside his warm house. Tim gave the bird a soft and cozy bed to relax in. The bird was very happy and said, "Thank you, Tim, for helping me relax!"
Soon, the bird was not serious anymore. The bird and Tim became good friends. They played together every day. The moral of the story is: always be kind and help others when they need it.

Lily and Ben were hungry. They wanted to eat steak for dinner. But steak was too expensive. Mom and Dad did not have much money.
They saw a sign in the shop. It said: "Cheap steak. Only five coins." They ran to the shop. They saw a big pile of steak. It looked good. They wanted to buy some.
But the shopkeeper was mean. He said: "This steak is not for you. It is for my dog. You can have some bread and cheese. That is cheap too."
Lily and Ben did not like bread and cheese. They liked steak. They had an idea. They whispered to each other. They said: "Let's wait until the shopkeeper is busy. Then we can take some steak and run away."
They waited for a long time. They saw the shopkeeper talking to a lady. He did not look at the steak. Lily and Ben sneaked to the pile. They grabbed some steak. They ran out of the shop.
They were happy. They had steak for dinner. But the steak was not good. It was hard and chewy. It tasted bad. They did not like it.
They learned a lesson. They said: "Cheap steak is not good steak. It is for dogs. We should not take things that are not ours. We are sorry."
They went back to the shop. They gave back the steak. They said sorry to the shopkeeper. He was angry. He said: "You are naughty. You should not steal. You should work hard and save money. Then you can buy good steak."
Lily and Ben felt bad. They said: "We are sorry. We will work hard and save money. We will not steal again."
The shopkeeper saw that they were sorry. He said: "OK. I forgive you. But you have to do something for me. You have to help me in the shop. You have to sweep the floor and stack the shelves. Then I will give you some bread and cheese. And maybe some steak. But only good steak. Not cheap steak."
Lily and Ben agreed. They helped the shopkeeper. They ate bread and cheese. And sometimes steak. But only good steak. They liked it. They were happy.

They laughed and played some more, until Tom had an idea.
"Let's make a race, Mia!" he said. "We can see who can reach the fence first. You can use your car and I can use my plane."
"OK, Tom, let's do it!" Mia said. "But you have to be fair and not cheat!"

"Your plane is brilliant, Tom!" Mia said.
