She reached for the bowl of grapes, but it was too far. She stretched and stretched, but she could not get it.
Then she saw a key on the table. It was shiny and silver. She wondered what it could unlock. She grabbed the key and jumped off the chair. She ran around the house, looking for something to unlock. She tried the door, but it did not fit. She tried the drawer, but it did not fit. She tried the box, but it did not fit.
She was about to give up, when she saw a small chest in the corner. It had a lock on it. She ran to the chest and put the key in the lock. It fit! She turned the key and heard a click. She opened the chest and saw a lot of toys. There were dolls, cars, books, and puzzles. She was so happy. She forgot about the grapes.
She took out a doll and hugged it. She took out a car and rolled it. She took out a book and looked at the pictures. She took out a puzzle and tried to put it together. She was having so much fun.
But then she heard a loud bark. It was Spot. He had smelled the grapes on the table. He jumped on the chair and knocked over the bowl. The grapes fell on the floor. Spot ate some of them. He liked grapes too.
But some of the grapes rolled under the couch. Lily saw them and ran to get them. She liked grapes more than toys. She crawled under the couch and reached for the grapes. But she did not see the nail sticking out. She bumped her head on the nail. It hurt. She cried.
Spot heard her cry and ran to her. He licked her face and wagged his tail. He wanted to make her feel better. He brought her a grape and dropped it in her hand. He liked to share.
Lily smiled and ate the grape. It was cold and sweet. She hugged Spot and thanked him. She liked her dog more than anything. They were friends.

Tim showed the thumb to his friend, Sam. Sam said, "Wow, that is a big thumb! What do you think it can do?" Tim thought for a moment and said, "I don't know, but let's be careful with it."
The two friends played with the thumb. They tried to use it for many things. They tried to use it to pick up toys, but it was too big. They tried to use it to open doors, but it was too heavy. Finally, they tried to use it to help other friends, but it was too strange.
One day, Tim and Sam were playing with the thumb when they saw a little girl crying. She had lost her toy. Tim said, "I think we can help her with the thumb." They used the thumb to lift the toy from a high shelf. The little girl was very happy and said, "Thank you!"
The moral of the story is that even if something seems strange or mysterious, it can still be helpful if we think about how to use it.

One day, they saw a big boy who was kicking sand at other kids. He was very noisy and mean. He made the other kids cry and run away. Ben and Lily did not like him. They wanted to tell him to stop, but they were afraid.
"Mom, Dad, look at that boy!" Ben said. "He is kicking sand at everyone. He is not nice."
Mom and Dad looked at the boy. They frowned. They did not like him either.
"Let's go and talk to him," Dad said. "Maybe he is lonely or sad. Maybe he needs a friend."
Ben and Lily followed Mom and Dad. They walked up to the boy and said hello. The boy looked at them and shrugged. He did not say anything.
"Why are you kicking sand at the other kids?" Dad asked. "Don't you know that it hurts them and makes them sad?"
The boy shrugged again. He did not care.
"Would you like to play with us?" Mom asked. "We have a lot of sand toys and buckets. We can make a big castle together."
The boy shook his head. He did not want to play.
"Are you sure?" Lily asked. "It is more fun to play with others than to be alone."
The boy nodded. He was sure.
"Okay, then," Ben said. "But you should not kick sand at anyone. It is not nice. It is not fair. It is not fun."
The boy looked at Ben and Lily. He saw that they were happy and friendly. He felt a little sorry. He did not have any friends. He was bored and angry. He kicked sand because he wanted attention.

Mom and Dad watched them and smiled. They were proud of Ben and Lily. They were kind and brave. They taught the boy a lesson. They made a new friend.
The moral of the story is: Be kind and brave. Don't kick sand at anyone. Make friends and have fun.

"Wow, what is this?" Ben asked.
"I don't know. Maybe it is a skull," Mia said.
"A skull? What is a skull?" Ben wondered.
"It is what is inside your head. It holds your brain and your eyes and your mouth," Mia explained.
"That is cool. Can we keep it?" Ben asked.
"Sure, why not? Let's show it to mom and dad. Maybe they will know more about it," Mia said.
They put the skull in a bag and ran to their parents, who were sitting on a bench. They were very excited to show them their discovery.
"Mom, dad, look what we found!" Ben shouted.
"Let us see, honey," mom said.
They opened the bag and took out the skull. Mom and dad gasped and looked scared.
"Where did you get this?" dad asked.
"We found it in the sand. It is a skull. Isn't it cool?" Mia said.
"No, it is not cool. It is dangerous. This is not a normal skull. It is a colorful skull. It belongs to a bad man who did bad things. He had a curse on him. If you touch his skull, you will get sick and die," dad said.
"What? No, that can't be true. We touched it. We are fine," Ben said.
But as he said that, he felt a pain in his chest. He looked at his hand and saw it was turning red and purple. He screamed and dropped the skull. Mia felt a pain in her head. She looked at her face and saw it was turning green and yellow. She screamed and fell to the ground. Mom and dad tried to help them, but it was too late. The curse had killed them. The skull laughed and said, "I told you not to touch me. Now you are mine." The end.

The man said, "I can give you a good price. These things are very attractive and useful. You won't regret buying them."
Tom and Lily heard the man and decided to join him. They ran out of their box and said, "We are pirates! We want to sell you our ship. It is very attractive and useful too. You won't regret buying it."
The man looked at Tom and Lily and smiled. He said, "You are very cute pirates. But I don't need a ship. I have a truck. And your ship is made of cardboard. It is not very strong or fast."
Tom and Lily said, "But our ship is fun. You can pretend to sail on the sea and find treasure and fight other pirates. It is more fun than a truck."
The man said, "Well, maybe you are right. But I don't have any money to buy your ship. I only have these things to trade. Do you want to trade your ship for something in my truck?"
Tom and Lily looked at the truck and saw a big teddy bear, a shiny whistle, and a colorful ball. They liked these things very much. They said, "Yes, we want to trade. We want the teddy bear, the whistle, and the ball."
The man said, "OK, deal. You can have these things and I can have your ship. But you have to promise to share them with each other and be nice pirates."
Tom and Lily said, "OK, we promise. Thank you for trading with us. You are a nice man."
The man said, "You are welcome. Thank you for playing with me. You are nice pirates."
They gave each other their things and said goodbye. Tom and Lily went back to their backyard with their new toys. They played with them and had fun. They were happy pirates.

His mom sighed and said, "Timmy, you are not acting normal. You are acting like a baby. You need a time out. Go to your room and calm down."

Timmy missed his surprise. He missed his grandma. He missed his mail. He was very sad. He wished he had been nice to the mailman and his mom. He wished he had been normal. He wished he had an envelope.

"I'm a fairy!" Lily said, wearing a pink dress and a shiny crown. "I can fly and make magic!"
They had a lot of fun, until they saw a strange bottle on the table. It had a label that said "Shrink". They were curious and wanted to see what it did.
"Let's try it!" Max said, picking up the bottle. "Maybe it will make us small like ants!"
"OK, but be careful!" Lily said, following him. "Don't spill it!"
Max opened the bottle and poured some of the liquid on his clothes. He felt a tickle and then he saw his clothes getting smaller and smaller. Soon, they were too small for him to wear. He was left in his underwear.
"Max, what happened?" Lily gasped, seeing him shrink. "Your clothes are tiny!"
"I don't know!" Max said, feeling scared. "It was the shrink stuff! It made me shrink!"
Lily quickly grabbed the bottle and looked for a way to undo the shrink. She saw another label that said "Grow". She hoped it would work.
"Here, Max, drink this!" Lily said, giving him the bottle. "Maybe it will make you grow back!"
Max drank some of the liquid and felt a tingle. He saw his clothes getting bigger and bigger. Soon, they were too big for him to wear. He was swimming in them.
"Lily, what happened?" Max cried, seeing himself grow. "Your clothes are huge!"
"I don't know!" Lily said, feeling sorry. "It was the grow stuff! It made you grow!"
They didn't know what to do. They had no clothes that fit them. They looked around and saw some of their old clothes that they had outgrown. They had an idea.
"Let's be creative!" Lily said, smiling. "We can use these clothes to make new ones!"
They took some scissors and some tape and started to cut and stick the clothes together. They made new outfits that fit them. They looked funny and colorful.
"Look, I'm a clown!" Max laughed, wearing a red shirt and a green hat. "Hear me honk!"
"I'm a princess!" Lily said, wearing a purple dress and a silver crown. "I can rule and make peace!"
They had a lot of fun, until their mom came home. She saw them in their new clothes and was surprised.
"What are you wearing?" Mom asked, raising her eyebrows. "Where are your clothes?"
Lily and Max looked at each other and giggled. They told her the story of the shrink and grow bottle. Mom shook her head and smiled.
"You are very creative!" Mom said, hugging them. "But next time, don't play with things you don't know!"
They nodded and said sorry. They put away the bottle and the clothes. They learned their lesson. They were happy to be themselves.

Once upon a time, there were two friends - a big snake, and a little mouse. They were very close and shared many adventures. One day, their path led them to a delicious sweet cake. The big snake, who was very selfish, immediately moved forward to take it for himself.
“Wait!” said the little mouse. “Maybe we could share this cake.”
“No, I want it all for myself!” the selfish snake replied. He made a sudden lunge and stopped just inches away from the cake.
“That’s not very fair,” the mouse replied sadly.
The snake looked at him and thought for a moment. “Okay,” he said. “We can share it.”
The friends shared the cake and enjoyed it together. The little mouse was very happy.
This story reminds us that it's important to share with others, because it makes us happy. It also teaches us that being selfish can be bad for ourselves and for our friends.

"Excuse me, sir," Tom says. "Can you help us? Our ball is in the pond. Can you catch it with your line?"
The man looks at Tom and Sam. He smiles. He says, "Sure, I can try. But you have to be quiet. Fish don't like noise."
The man reels in his line. He takes off the hook. He ties the line to a stick. He throws the stick to the ball. He pulls the line. The ball comes closer and closer. Tom and Sam clap their hands.
"Thank you, sir!" they say. "You are very kind."
The man gives them the ball. He says, "You're welcome, boys. Have fun. But be careful. Don't throw your ball into the pond again."
Tom and Sam nod. They say, "We will. Bye, sir!"
They run back to the field. They play catch with their ball. They are happy. Their moms are happy too. They watch them play. They have open smiles. They are proud of their boys.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to swim in the pond. They wore hats and swimsuits to protect their skin from the sun. One day, they saw a big sunflower near the water. It was yellow and bright, and had many seeds.
"Wow, look at that sunflower!" Lily said. "It is so pretty and tall. Can we pick it?"
Tom shook his head. "No, we can't. The sunflower belongs to the farmer. He grows them for food and oil. If we pick it, he will be angry."
Lily nodded. She understood. She did not want to make the farmer angry. She wanted to be kind and respectful. "Okay, then can we swim near it? Maybe it will like to see us."
Tom smiled. He liked Lily's idea. He thought the sunflower might enjoy their company. "Sure, let's swim near it. But be careful not to touch it. It might have bees or thorns."
They swam near the sunflower, splashing and laughing. They waved at it and said hello. The sunflower seemed to nod and smile back. It was happy to have visitors.
The farmer saw them from his house. He was not angry. He was glad that the children liked his sunflower. He thought they were cute and polite. He decided to give them a surprise. He picked a small sunflower and brought it to them.
"Hello, children," he said. "I see you like my sunflower. It is a very special one. It is the biggest and brightest in the field. Do you want to know a secret?"
Lily and Tom nodded. They were curious and excited. They thanked the farmer for his kindness.
The farmer handed them the small sunflower. "This is a baby sunflower. It is not as big or bright as the other one, but it is still beautiful and strong. It needs water and sun to grow. If you take it home and plant it in a pot, it will grow bigger and brighter. Do you want to try?"
Lily and Tom gasped. They were delighted and grateful. They loved the baby sunflower. They hugged the farmer and thanked him again.
"Yes, we want to try!" they said. "Thank you, thank you, thank you!"
They took the baby sunflower home and planted it in a pot. They watered it and put it in a sunny spot. They watched it grow every day. They named it Sunny. They hoped it would be as big and bright as the one in the pond. They dreamed of swimming with it again. They were happy and proud. They had a new friend.

"Ow, ow, ow!" she cried. She threw the pin and the beads on the floor. She ran to her mom and hugged her.
"What's wrong, Lily?" her mom asked. She saw the pin and the beads on the floor. She understood why Lily was sad.
"I can't make a necklace, mom. The pin is too difficult. It hurts me. I don't like it," Lily said.
Her mom comforted her. She kissed her fingers and rubbed her back. She said, "I'm sorry, Lily. The pin is too difficult for you. But you don't need a pin to make a necklace. You can use a string. A string is easier and safer. Do you want to try?"
Lily nodded. She wiped her tears and smiled. Her mom gave her a string and some beads. She showed her how to make a necklace with a string. Lily followed her mom. She put the beads on the string. She made a beautiful necklace. She was happy.
She said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. I love you. And I love my necklace."
Her mom said, "You're welcome, Lily. I love you too. And I love your necklace. You did a great job. You see, sometimes you have to try a different way to do something. If something is too difficult, don't give up. Ask for help. There is always a solution."
Lily learned a lesson. She learned that if something is too difficult, she can ask for help. She learned that there is always a solution. She learned that her mom is always there to comfort her. She was happy.

"Let's plug it in and turn it on," Tom said. He took the cord and put it in the wall. Lily reached for the switch.
"Wait, I have an idea," Tom said. He ran to the kitchen and came back with a bottle of hot sauce. "Let's put some of this on the lamp. It will make it spicy and funny."
He opened the bottle and poured some sauce on the lamp. It dripped and smelled. Lily giggled.
"OK, now turn it on," Tom said.
Lily flipped the switch. The lamp made a loud pop and a bright flash. Smoke came out of it. The sauce burned and stung their eyes and noses. They screamed and ran out of the room.
Mom and Dad heard the noise and came to see what happened. They saw the lamp, the sauce, and the smoke. They were very angry and scared.
"What did you do?" Mom asked.
"We wanted to surprise you with a spicy lamp," Lily said.
"That was a very bad surprise," Dad said. "You could have hurt yourselves or started a fire. Never play with electricity or hot sauce. You are in big trouble."
Lily and Tom felt sorry and sad. They said they were sorry and hugged Mom and Dad. Mom and Dad hugged them back and said they loved them. They cleaned up the mess and threw away the lamp. They gave Lily and Tom some water and cookies to calm them down.
They learned their lesson and never tried to make a spicy lamp again.

Lila and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big pond with some ducks and fish. They want to feed them some bread.
"Look, Ben, ducks!" Lila says, pointing to the pond.
"Quack, quack!" Ben says, making duck sounds.
They run to the pond and throw some bread crumbs into the water. The ducks swim closer and eat the bread. Lila and Ben clap and laugh.
But then they see something else in the water. Something big and green and scaly. It has a long tail and a big mouth with sharp teeth. It is a crocodile!
"Ben, look, a crocodile!" Lila says, scared.
"Where?" Ben says, looking around.
"There, in the water!" Lila says, pointing to the crocodile.
The crocodile sees them and opens its mouth. It makes a loud roar.
"Roar!" the crocodile says.
Lila and Ben scream and run away from the pond. They find their mom and dad and tell them what they saw.
"A crocodile?" mom says, surprised.
"In the pond?" dad says, confused.
They go back to the pond and look for the crocodile. But they don't see it. It is gone.
"Maybe it was a distant crocodile," Lila says, trying to make sense of it.
"Maybe it was a toy crocodile," Ben says, hoping it was not real.
"Maybe it was a dream crocodile," mom says, smiling.
"Maybe it was a silly crocodile," dad says, joking.
They all laugh and hug. They are happy and safe. They decide to play somewhere else in the park. They don't want to see the crocodile again.

Tom nodded. He said, "You're right, Lila. I will be careful. And I won't play with spears anymore. They are not toys. They are dangerous."

Sue looked at Tim and said, "Yes, I want to play, but I am shy." Tim smiled and said, "I am shy too, but we can change that by playing together." So Tim and Sue played together all day long. They had so much fun, and they were not shy anymore.
From that day on, Tim and Sue were best friends. They played together every day, and they were not shy anymore. They learned that playing with friends can make you happy and change you for the better. And Tim's big muscles helped him jump high and play even more with his new friend Sue.

Lily was very sad and angry. She went home and threw her prince doll on the floor. She said she did not love him anymore. She said he was ugly and boring. She said she only wanted the princess doll.
The prince doll felt very hurt and lonely. He loved Lily and wanted to make her happy. He wished he could talk to her and tell her how he felt. But he was only a doll and he could not speak. He could only sigh and cry.
That night, a fairy came to Lily's room. She saw the prince doll on the floor and the princess doll in the store. She knew what Lily had done and why she was unhappy. Then she took them away to a warm and beautiful castle where they could live happily ever after.
Lily woke up the next morning and looked for her prince doll. She could not find him anywhere. She asked her mom where he was, but her mom did not know. She said maybe he ran away because Lily was mean to him. Lily felt very sorry and sad. She realized she had made a big mistake. She wished she could have her prince doll back and tell him she loved him. But it was too late. He was gone forever.
The moral of the story is: Be grateful for what you have and do not be greedy for what you do not have. You may lose what you have and never get what you want.

"Maybe, Sam, maybe. But now it is time for nap. Come on, let's go to our beds. And maybe we can dream of dinosaurs and history," she says, taking his hand.

Tim and Sue were twins who lived on a farm with their mom and dad. They liked to play with the animals and help with the chores. One day, they saw a big truck with a cage on the back. They were curious and ran to see what was inside.
"Hello, little ones," said a man who came out of the truck. "Do you want to see my pet lion? He is very friendly and loves to play."
Tim and Sue nodded and followed the man to the cage. They saw a big yellow cat with a long mane and sharp teeth. He looked angry and hungry.
"Wow, he is so big and beautiful," said Tim.
"Can we pet him?" asked Sue.
"Sure, sure," said the man with a smile. "Just open the cage and reach your hand inside. He won't bite, I promise."
Tim and Sue did not recognize the danger. They did not know that the man was a liar and a thief. He wanted to steal some animals from the farm and sell them. He also wanted to get rid of the lion, who was too wild and expensive to keep.
Tim and Sue opened the cage and put their hands inside. The lion roared and pounced on them. He bit their arms and legs and dragged them into the cage. Tim and Sue screamed and cried, but it was too late. The man locked the cage and ran to the truck. He drove away fast, leaving the lion and the twins behind.
Mom and dad heard the noise and came running. They saw the blood and the cage and the lion. They were shocked and sad. They called the police and the doctor, but they could not save Tim and Sue. They died from their wounds and their foolishness.
The moral of the story is: Do not trust strangers who offer you something too good to be true. They might be lying and trying to hurt you. Listen to your parents and stay away from danger.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish. He lived in a murky pond filled with water plants. The pond was usually murky, but today it was even gloomier than before.
The little fish was feeling a bit sad because of the gloomy weather. He wanted to go explore the world outside of the pond. He saw a beautiful waterfall way at the top of the pond.
But there was a scale blocking the waterfall. It was too big for the little fish to move. He swam around and around the scale. He wished he could get to the top.
Just then, a frog showed up. The frog said, "I can help you get over the scale! All you have to do is take a deep breath, hold tight to my back, and I'll get you up there."
The little fish was so excited! He clutched tight and the frog hopped from one lily pad to the next. When they reached the top, the little fish was able to look down and see his murky pond.
The little fish was so dirty from his adventure, so the frog suggested he wash off in the waterfall. The little fish swam down and eagerly swirled around in the cool, bubbly water.
Once he was clean, the little fish dove back into the murky pond. He felt so much better than before--all because the frog helped him get to the top of the scale.

Lily and Ben shake their heads. They say, "No, no, no! We do not like to bathe. It is cold and wet. It makes us cry."
Mom sighs. She says, "Please, Lily and Ben, listen to me. Bathing is good for you. It is fun and relaxing. You can play with your rubber ducks and bubbles. You can sing and splash. You can choose your favorite shampoo and towel. I will help you and hug you."

Mom nods. She says, "Yes, you can play a little more after. But only if you bathe well and fast. I have a surprise for you. It is something yummy and sweet. But it is only available for a short time. So hurry up and come with me."
Lily and Ben jump out from under the sofa. They follow Mom to the bathroom. They bathe well and fast. They wash their body with soap and water. They play with their rubber ducks and bubbles. They sing and splash. They choose their favorite shampoo and towel. Mom helps them and hugs them.

Tim and Sam were best friends. They liked to play knights and dragons in the park. Tim had a wooden sword and Sam had a cardboard shield. They pretended to fight the evil dragon that lived in the big slide.
One day, a new boy came to the park. His name was Ben. He had a shiny metal sword and a plastic shield. He said he was the best knight in the world. He laughed at Tim and Sam's toys. He said they were silly and weak.
Tim and Sam felt sad and angry. They wanted to play with their toys, but Ben made them feel bad. Ben challenged them to a duel. He said he would show them who was the real knight.
Tim was scared. He did not want to fight Ben. He thought Ben would hurt him with his metal sword. He wanted to run away and hide. Sam saw that Tim was scared. He wanted to help his friend.
Sam said to Tim, "Don't be scared, Tim. You are a brave knight. You can fight Ben. I will be your shield. I will protect you. We are a team. We can do it together."
Sam encouraged Tim to be brave. He gave him a hug and a smile. He held his cardboard shield in front of Tim. He said, "Let's go, Tim. We are not afraid of Ben. We are not afraid of anything."
Tim felt better. He saw that Sam was his friend. He saw that Sam believed in him. He held his wooden sword in his hand. He said, "Thank you, Sam. You are a good friend. You are a good shield. Let's go, Sam. We are ready to fight."
Tim and Sam walked towards Ben. Ben was impatient. He wanted to win the duel. He wanted to show off his sword and shield. He did not care about Tim and Sam's feelings. He did not have any friends.
Tim and Sam fought Ben. They used their sword and shield to block Ben's attacks. They worked together as a team. They did not give up. They did not get hurt. They showed Ben that they were brave and strong.
Ben was surprised. He could not beat Tim and Sam. He could not break their sword and shield. He could not make them cry. He felt angry and ashamed. He realized that his sword and shield were not enough. He realized that he needed something else.
Tim and Sam won the duel. They were happy and proud. They cheered and hugged each other. They said, "We did it, Sam. We did it, Tim. We are the best knights in the world."
They looked at Ben. They saw that he was sad and lonely. They felt sorry for him. They said, "Ben, do you want to play with us? We can share our sword and shield. We can be friends. We can have fun together."
Ben was shocked. He did not expect Tim and Sam to be nice to him. He did not know how to be nice to them. He did not know how to be a friend. He said, "Really? You want to play with me? You want to be my friends?"
Tim and Sam nodded. They said, "Yes, Ben. We want to play with you. We want to be your friends. We can teach you how to play knights and dragons. We can teach you how to be a good knight. A good knight is not mean and rude. A good knight is kind and helpful. A good knight has a sword and a shield, but also has a heart and a smile."
Ben smiled. He felt happy and grateful. He said, "Thank you, Tim. Thank you, Sam. You are very nice. You are very good. You are very brave. You are very good knights. You are very good friends. I want to be like you. I want to be a good knight. I want to be a good friend. Can I play with you?"
Tim and Sam said, "Of course, Ben. You can play with us. You can be our friend. Come on, let's go. The dragon is waiting for us."
The three boys ran to the big slide. They played knights and dragons. They had fun together. They became friends.
The moral of the story is: Be kind and helpful to others. Don't judge people by their toys. Don't be mean and rude. Work together as a team. Be brave and strong. Share and care. Friendship is more important than winning. Friendship is the best shield.

"Sam, you are so wet!" Lily says. "Your hair is wet, your shirt is wet, your pants are wet!"
"So are you, Lily!" Sam says. "You are wet from head to toe!"
They jump and splash some more. They have a lot of fun.
Then, they hear a voice. It is Sam's mom. She is looking for them.
"Sam, Lily, where are you?" she calls.
"Here, mom, we are here!" Sam says. He and Lily get out of the puddle. They are dripping wet.
Sam's mom sees them. She is not happy.
"Sam, Lily, what are you doing?" she asks. "You are wet and dirty! You need to change your clothes!"
"Sorry, mom, we were playing in the puddle," Sam says. "It was fun!"

Sam and Lily look at their clothes. They are not regular clothes. They are their nice clothes. They wore them for a special occasion. They forgot.
"Oops, we forgot," Sam says. "We are sorry, mom."
Sam's mom sighs. She is not angry, but she is worried.
"Come on, let's go home," she says. "I will show you how to dry your clothes and clean them. And you need to take a bath, too."
Sam and Lily nod. They follow Sam's mom. They are still wet and dirty, but they are also happy. They had fun in the puddle. They learned something new. They will remember next time.

Once upon a time, there were two bears - a big bear and a small bear. They lived in the bush, together. 
One day, the two bears decided to go on an adventure. As they traveled, they went further and further away from the bush. "This is so exciting!" said the small bear. 
Suddenly, the two bears saw something unusual. It was a huge mountain, blocking their way. "Oh no, what should we do?" said the small bear. 
"Let's climb it!" exclaimed the big bear. The small bear was worried, but the big bear was determined. So, the two bears began to climb the mountain.
Half way up the mountain, the two bears had to separate. The big bear was much stronger, so he went to the top first. But when the big bear finally reached the top, he saw something amazing.
The mountain top was full of berries - the most delicious berries ever! The big bear called to the small bear, who had stayed at the base of the mountain. "Come up here!" shouted the big bear. The small bear quickly joined the big bear on the mountaintop and they both enjoyed the delicious berries.

Lily loved to paint. She had many colors, but her favorite was purple. She liked to paint purple flowers, purple stars, and purple cats. She wanted to be a painter when she grew up.
One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a man painting a picture of the trees. He had a big canvas, a brush, and a palette. Lily was curious and went closer to see his work. She saw that he had many colors, but no purple.
"Can I have some purple?" she asked the man.
The man looked at her and smiled. "Sorry, little girl, but I don't have any purple. I only use the colors that I see in nature."
"But I love purple!" Lily said. "Purple is the best color. You should have purple. Give me some purple!"
The man frowned. "No, I can't give you any purple. This is my paint, and I need it for my picture. You can't demand things that are not yours. That is rude and selfish."
Lily was angry. She wanted purple, and she wanted it now. She grabbed the man's palette and tried to take it from him. The man held on to it and tried to stop her. They pulled and tugged, and the paint spilled all over them and the canvas. The picture was ruined.
Lily and the man were both covered in paint. They looked at each other and at the mess they had made. They felt ashamed and sorry.
"I'm sorry, mister," Lily said. "I shouldn't have demanded your paint. I should have asked nicely or used my own paint."
"I'm sorry, too, Lily," the man said. "I shouldn't have been so stingy with my paint. I should have shared with you or let you try some purple."
They hugged and apologized. They decided to clean up the mess and start a new picture together. They used all the colors, even purple. They learned that painting is more fun when you share and respect each other.

Max and Sara said, "But we were having fun!"
"No!" Dad said hsarply. "It's too late for this kind of fun. Bed now!"

Once upon a time there was a duck. The duck was worried because it could not find its way home. Suddenly it saw something in the distance. The duck was excited as it recognized the swamp it used to live in. 
The duck flew closer and saw a crocodile lounging on the shore. The crocodile noticed the duck and said, "What are you doing here, stranger in my swamp?".
The duck was scared but answered politely, "I'm looking for my home".
The crocodile thought, then said, "You are not welcome here, so hurry up and go away".
The duck knew it would be foolish to argue with the crocodile, so it said goodbye, then flapped its wings and flew away.
The moral of the story is to be polite and respectful even if someone is being unkind to you. Scene kindness and courage can help you and others be successful, even when times are tough.

Tommy looked at his soup. He liked soup. It was warm and tasty. But he did not like the carrots and broccoli. He thought they looked like bugs. He pushed them to the side of his plate.
"Mom, do I have to eat the vegetables?" he asked, in a small voice.
"Yes, you do, Tommy. They are part of your dinner. You have to eat a little bit of everything. If you eat your vegetables, you can have a cookie for dessert. How does that sound?" his mom said, gently.
Tommy thought for a moment. He really wanted a cookie. He loved cookies. They were sweet and crunchy. But he did not want to eat the vegetables. He thought they were gross and icky. He wondered if he could trick his mom.
"Mom, can I have some water, please?" he asked, pretending to be thirsty.
"Sure, Tommy. Here you go," his mom said, handing him a glass of water.
Tommy took the glass and pretended to drink. But he did not drink. He spit the water into his napkin. Then he wrapped the napkin around the vegetables and hid them under his chair.
"Mom, I'm done. Can I have a cookie now?" he asked, smiling.
His mom looked at his plate. She saw that there were no vegetables left. She was surprised. She did not know that Tommy had hidden them. She thought he had eaten them.
"Wow, Tommy, you ate all your vegetables. I'm so proud of you. You are a good boy. Yes, you can have a cookie. Here you go," she said, giving him a cookie.
Tommy took the cookie and bit into it. He was happy. He thought he had fooled his mom. He did not know that his mom had seen his napkin under his chair. She was not fooled. She was not happy. She thought he had been naughty. She decided to talk to him later.

So, they both looked for the ball in the tall grass. Suddenly, Tim's mom found the ball and gave it to Tim. He was so happy to receive his ball back. Tim hugged his mom and said, "Thank you, Mom!" From that day on, Tim was very careful with his ball and had lots of fun playing with it. And he never felt terrible again.

"Yes, Tom, it is amazing!" Mia says.
They keep adding more blocks until they run out of them. They are very proud of their tower. They want to complete it with a flag on top.
"Can you give me the flag, Mia?" Tom asks.
"Here you go, Tom. Be careful, it is very windy!" Mia says.
Tom climbs on a chair and reaches for the top of the tower. He tries to put the flag on the last block. But the wind is too strong. It blows the flag away and makes the tower shake.
"Oh no, Tom, watch out!" Mia shouts.
The tower wobbles and then falls down with a loud crash. The blocks scatter all over the floor. Tom and Mia are sad and shocked. They look at each other and then at the mess.
"Oops, we did not complete our tower," Tom says.
"No, we did not. But we had fun, right?" Mia says.
"Yes, we did. And we can try again another day," Tom says.
They hug each other and then start to pick up the blocks. They are still friends and they still love to play with blocks.

Her friend's mom said, "I'm sorry, Lily, but I don't have any salad. You can have some of this food. It is good and healthy and tasty."
But Lily did not listen. She said louder, "I want salad. Give me salad now." She stamped her feet and crossed her arms. She was very rude.
Her friend's mom did not like that. She said, "Lily, you are being very naughty. You cannot demand things like that. You have to be polite and respectful. If you don't eat what I made, you will have to go home."
Lily did not care. She said, "I don't want to be here. I want to go home. I want salad."
Her friend's mom said, "Fine. I will call your mom and tell her to pick you up. You are not welcome here anymore."
Lily had to wait outside until her mom came. She was hungry and cold and sad. She lost her friend and her lunch. She wished she had been nicer and tried some of the food. She learned that salad was not the only thing to eat, and that demanding was not the way to get what she wanted.

"We both want the ball!" Lily and Ben say.
The lady nods. She says, "I understand. But do you know what is better than having the ball? Sharing the ball. Sharing means you let someone else use something you have. Then you can take turns and have fun together. Sharing is kind and good. Do you want to try?"
Lily and Ben think. They look at the ball. They look at each other. They nod.
"Okay, we will share the ball," they say.
They give the ball to the lady. She smiles. She says, "Good. Now, how about a hug? A hug is a way to show you are friends. You can hug with your arms and touch your lips. Your lips are the soft part of your mouth. A hug is warm and nice. Do you want to try?"
Lily and Ben think. They look at the lady. They look at each other. They nod.
"Okay, we will hug," they say.
They hug each other. They touch their lips. They feel happy. They are not angry.
The lady claps. She says, "Well done, children. You are very sweet. Now you can play with the ball together. Have a peaceful time. Peaceful means quiet and calm. No fighting, no shouting, no crying. Just playing and laughing and enjoying. Do you want to try?"
Lily and Ben think. They look at the ball. They look at the lady. They look at each other. They nod.
"Okay, we will have a peaceful time," they say.
They take the ball from the lady. They say, "Thank you, lady. You are very nice."
The lady says, "You are welcome, children. You are very smart. Have fun."
She waves and walks away. Lily and Ben wave back. They play with the ball together. They share and hug and have a peaceful time. They are friends. They are happy.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big cage with a chubby tiger inside. The tiger was sleeping on the grass. Anna wanted to see the tiger better. She went close to the cage and said, "Hello, tiger. You are so big and cute. Can I touch you?"
Ben was scared. He said, "No, Anna, don't do that. The tiger might wake up and bite you. He is not a pet. He is wild. Come back here."
But Anna did not listen. She put her hand through the bars of the cage and tried to touch the tiger's fur. The tiger opened his eyes and saw Anna's hand. He growled and showed his sharp teeth. He tried to grab Anna's hand with his paw.
Anna screamed and pulled her hand back. She ran away from the cage and hugged Ben. She was crying and shaking. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was wrong. The tiger is not cute. He is mean and scary. I will never do that again."
Ben hugged Anna and said, "It's okay, Anna. I'm glad you are safe. The tiger is not mean. He is just protecting his home. He does not like strangers. We should leave him alone and play somewhere else."
Anna nodded and said, "Yes, Ben. Let's go and play with the swings. They are fun and safe."
They held hands and walked away from the cage. The tiger watched them go and closed his eyes again. He was tired and hungry. He hoped his keeper would come soon and give him some meat. He did not like the park. He missed his jungle.

Anna and Ben were playing with blocks. They wanted to build a big tower. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes.
"Let's measure how tall our tower is," Ben said. He took a long stick and put it next to the tower. "Look, it is as tall as the stick!"
Anna nodded. She was very happy. She wanted to make the tower even taller. She reached for more blocks. But she forgot to be careful. She bumped into the tower and made it fall down.
"Oh no!" Anna cried. "We worked so hard and now it is gone!"
Ben was sad too. He looked at the mess of blocks. He did not want to start over. He felt like giving up.
But then he had an idea. He was a clever boy. He saw a big box in the corner. He ran to the box and dragged it to the blocks.
"Anna, look!" he said. "We can use this box as a base for our tower. It will make it stronger and easier to build. Come on, let's try!"
Anna smiled. She liked Ben's idea. She helped him put the box on the floor. Then they started to stack the blocks on top of the box. They were careful not to forget to balance them.
Soon they had a new tower. It was bigger and better than before. They measured it with the stick again. It was taller than the stick!
"Wow!" Anna said. "We did it! We made the tallest tower ever!"
Ben hugged her. He was very proud. He said, "We are a great team. We are clever and we don't give up. We can do anything!"
They laughed and clapped. They had fun playing with their tower. They did not forget to clean up when they were done.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to travel with their mom and dad. They go to many places and see many things. They have a big car with four seats and a trunk.
One day, they travel to a farm. The farm has many animals and plants. Sara and Ben want to see everything. They are very nosy. They ask many questions to the farmer.
"Can we pet the cow?" Sara asks.
"Sure, but be careful. She is big and strong," the farmer says.
"Can we feed the chicken?" Ben asks.
"Sure, but don't give them too much. They are greedy," the farmer says.
The farmer shows them the barn, the pond, the field and the orchard. The orchard has many trees with fruits. Sara and Ben see apples, pears, peaches and cherries.
"Can we pick some cherries?" Sara asks.
"Sure, but only a few. They are not ready yet," the farmer says.
Sara and Ben climb a ladder and reach for the cherries. They are red and shiny. They look yummy. Sara and Ben each pick one and put it in their mouths.
"Mmm, they are sweet and juicy," Sara says.
"They are sour and bitter," Ben says.
They make funny faces and spit out the cherries. The farmer laughs.
"Those are not cherries. They are crabapples. They are not good to eat. They are good for making jam," the farmer says.
Sara and Ben feel silly. They apologize to the farmer.
"Sorry, we did not know," Sara says.
"Sorry, we were too nosy," Ben says.
The farmer smiles and forgives them.
"It's okay. You are curious and brave. That's good. But next time, ask before you taste. Come, I'll show you the real cherries. They are over there," the farmer says.
Sara and Ben follow the farmer. They see another tree with smaller and darker fruits. They are the real cherries. The farmer lets them pick some and eat them. They are delicious.
"Thank you, farmer. These are the best cherries ever," Sara says.
"Thank you, farmer. We learned a lot today," Ben says.
The farmer is happy. He gives them a basket of cherries to take home. Sara and Ben hug him and say goodbye. They travel back to their car with their mom and dad. They are tired but happy. They had a great day at the farm.

"Let's play hide and seek!" Tom said. "You count to ten and I hide, okay?"
"Okay!" Sara said. She closed her eyes and counted. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten! Ready or not, here I come!"
Sara opened her eyes and looked for Tom. She checked behind the doors and under the tables. She did not see Tom. She heard a giggle from the end of the hall. She ran to the sound.
"Tom, I found you!" Sara said. She saw Tom hiding behind a big vase. The vase was tall and shiny, with flowers and leaves on it. Sara reached for Tom, but Tom moved away.
"Ha ha, you can't catch me!" Tom said. He ran around the vase, but he bumped into it. The vase wobbled and fell. It broke into many pieces. The flowers and leaves scattered on the floor.
Sara and Tom gasped. They heard footsteps and voices. They knew it was Mom and Dad. They were angry.
"Who did this?" Mom said. She saw the broken vase and the mess. She saw Sara and Tom. "Did you do this?"
Sara and Tom nodded. They were scared. They knew the vase was Mom's favorite. She got it from Grandma. She cared for it a lot.
"I'm sorry, Mom," Sara said.
"Me too, Mom," Tom said.
Mom and Dad were very sad and mad. They did not hug Sara and Tom. They did not say it was okay. They sent Sara and Tom to their rooms. They said they had to stay there until dinner. They said they had to think about what they did.
Sara and Tom went to their rooms. They did not play. They did not talk. They felt bad. They wished they did not break the vase. They wished they did not make Mom and Dad sad and mad. They wished they could say sorry again. They wished they could hug Mom and Dad. They wished they could play in the hall again. But they could not. They had to stay in their rooms. They had to wait for dinner. They had to hope Mom and Dad would forgive them. They had to hope Mom and Dad would still care for them.

One day, Lila went to the park with her mom. She wore her favorite coat, the one with the colorful buttons and the fluffy hood. She thought her coat was unique, because no one else had one like it. She was proud of her coat and her whistling.
At the park, she saw a boy playing with a ball. He had a blue coat and a red hat. He looked nice, so Lila decided to say hello. She walked up to him and whistled a tune. The boy looked at her and smiled.
"Hi, I'm Lila. I like your hat. Can I play with you?" she asked.
"Hi, I'm Ben. I like your coat. It's very unique. Sure, you can play with me. Do you know how to whistle?" he replied.
"Yes, I do. My dad taught me. He whistles all the time. Do you want to hear?" she offered.
"Yes, please. I can't whistle. I wish I could. Maybe you can teach me?" he said.
"Okay, I'll try. It's easy. You just have to make a small hole with your lips and blow air. Like this." She demonstrated.
Ben watched and listened. He tried to copy her, but he only made a funny sound. He laughed.
"That doesn't sound like whistling. That sounds like a duck. Quack, quack!" he joked.
Lila laughed too. She liked Ben. He was funny and kind. She decided to help him.
"Don't worry. You'll get it. You just have to practice. Here, let me show you again. And then you try. And then we can play ball. And then we can be friends. Okay?" she suggested.
"Okay. That sounds good. You're a good teacher. And a good friend. Thank you, Lila." he said.
They smiled at each other and whistled together. They had fun. They played ball. They became friends. They were happy and calm. And they had unique coats.

"No, don't!" Lila said. "It is not a real deer. It is a toy deer. It belongs to Sam. He will be sad if you tear it."
But Tom did not listen. He let go of the string and the arrow flew through the air. It hit the toy deer and made a hole in it.
"Oh no!" Lila said. "You tore Sam's toy deer. He will be very angry. He will not play with us anymore."
Tom felt bad. He did not mean to tear the toy deer. He ran to the bush and picked up the arrow and the toy deer. He saw the hole and the stuffing coming out.
"I'm sorry, I'm sorry," he said. "I did not know it was a toy deer. I thought it was a real deer. I wanted to be a mighty hunter."
Lila followed him. She saw the toy deer and the arrow. She felt sorry for Tom and Sam.
"Maybe we can fix it," she said. "Maybe we can sew the hole and put the stuffing back in. Maybe Sam will not be so angry if we say we are sorry and give him the toy deer back."
Tom nodded. He liked Lila's idea. He hoped Sam would forgive him. He learned a lesson. He learned to be careful with his arrows and not to tear other people's toys. He learned that being a mighty hunter was not as important as being a good friend.

Lily had a birdcage with a blue bird inside. She liked to watch the bird sing and fly in the cage. She did not let the bird out of the cage, because she was afraid it would fly away.
One day, her friend Ben came to play with her. He saw the birdcage and said, "Why do you keep the bird in the cage? It is not happy there. It wants to be free and see the sky and the trees."
Lily said, "No, I keep the bird because I love it. It is my pet. If I let it out, it will not come back to me."
Ben said, "That is not fair. The bird is not a toy. It is a living thing. It has feelings and needs. You should be flexible and let it go. Maybe it will come back to you if you are kind and gentle."
Lily thought about what Ben said. She felt sorry for the bird. She decided to be flexible and try something new. She opened the cage and said to the bird, "You can go out and explore, but please come back to me. I will wait for you here."
The bird flew out of the cage and sang happily. It flew around the garden and saw the flowers and the bugs. It felt free and joyful. But it also remembered Lily and how she cared for it. It flew back to the cage and landed on Lily's hand. It thanked her with a sweet song.
Lily was surprised and happy. She hugged the bird and said, "You came back to me! I am so glad. I learned something today. I learned that I should not keep things that are not mine. I learned that I should be flexible and respect others. Thank you, bird. Thank you, Ben."
Ben smiled and said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are a good friend. And so is the bird. Can we play with it together?"
Lily said, "Yes, of course. But only if the bird wants to. We should always ask first."
The bird nodded and said, "Yes, I want to. You are both nice. Let's play."
And they all played happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl who was out playing in her garden. She ran around and laughed, exploring everything around her. Suddenly, she saw a stranger. She froze and gazed up at them sternly, not sure what to expect.
The stranger smiled. "Hello there," they said. "What is your name?"
The little girl looked at them suspiciously. She didn't say anything and continued to gaze at them.
The stranger smiled and said, "I have something special for you. Would you like it?"
The little girl still looked wary but curiosity got the best of her. She cautiously nodded her head.
The stranger took out a little box from their pocket. On the box was a shining button. The stranger said, "Don't be foolish and press this button!" 
The little girl, not understanding what danger could be lurking behind the button, reached out and pressed it anyway. Suddenly, a loud honk! filled the garden, making the little girl smile and giggle. 
The stranger laughed and said, "Wasn't so foolish after all, was it?" 
The little girl smiled. From that day onward, she learned that it was best to be cautious, but not to be too fearful. She was always wary of strangers, but that didn't stop her from being open to new possibilities.

The bird said: “If you perform a dangerous trick on your scooter, I will grant you the greatest wish of your life.” Annie decided to take the bird up on its offer and started to practice. She was getting closer and closer to completing her dangerous trick.

The moral of the story is: Never take risks with your safety because they can come with very bad consequences. Think before you act.

Lily and Tom were playing hide and seek in the old house. Lily was the seeker and Tom was the hider. Lily counted to ten and then opened her eyes. She looked around the dusty rooms, but she could not see Tom. She called out, "Tom, where are you? I miss you!"
Tom heard Lily's voice, but he did not answer. He had found a good hiding spot under the stairs. He was behind a big cobweb that made him look like a ghost. He thought it was funny and he wanted to scare Lily. He waited for her to come closer.
Lily walked through the hall, looking for Tom. She saw a door that was slightly open. She pushed it and entered a dark room. She felt anxious. She did not like the dark. She wished Tom was with her. She said, "Tom, are you here? Please come out!"
Tom heard Lily enter the room. He decided to surprise her. He ran out of his hiding spot and shouted, "Boo!" He waved his arms and made a scary face.
Lily screamed and jumped back. She saw Tom covered in cobweb and she thought he was a monster. She was very scared and she started to cry.
Tom realized he had made a mistake. He saw Lily crying and he felt sorry. He ran to her and hugged her. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was only joking. I'm not a monster. I'm your brother. Don't cry. I love you."
Lily stopped crying and hugged Tom back. She said, "I love you too, Tom. But don't do that again. You scared me a lot. And you look silly with all that cobweb on you."
Tom laughed and said, "You're right. I look silly. Let's go and wash it off. And then we can play something else. Maybe we can make a cake with mom."
Lily nodded and said, "Yes, let's do that. That sounds fun. And yummy."
They held hands and left the old house. They were happy to be together. They did not miss the cobweb or the dark. They only missed the cake.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play outside in the yard. They have a big box that they use as a shelter. They pretend it is a spaceship or a castle or a cave.
One day, they see a big cloud in the sky. It is dark and scary. They hear a loud noise. It is thunder. They see a bright light. It is lightning. They are afraid.
"Let's go to our shelter!" Tim says. "It will keep us safe from the storm!"
They run to the box and crawl inside. They close the flap and hug each other.
They hear the rain falling on the box. They hear the wind blowing. They hear the thunder and lightning. They are glad they have their shelter.
But then, they feel something move. The box is shaking. They peek outside and see a big dog. It is brown and furry. It has a wet nose and a long tongue. It is sniffing the box. It is curious.
"Go away, dog!" Sam says. "This is our shelter! You can't have it!"
The dog barks. It pushes the box with its paw. The box slides on the grass. Tim and Sam scream.
"Stop, dog!" Tim says. "You are ruining our shelter! You are scaring us!"
The dog pushes the box again. The box tips over. Tim and Sam fall out. They are wet and dirty. They are angry and sad.
They see the dog wagging its tail. It licks their faces. It thinks they are playing. It is friendly.
"Maybe the dog is lonely," Sam says. "Maybe it wants to be our friend."
"Maybe," Tim says. "But it is rare to find a dog like this. It is too big and too strong. It doesn't know how to play nice."
They stand up and brush themselves off. They look at their shelter. It is broken and torn. They can't use it anymore.
They look at the dog. It is still wagging its tail. It looks happy and sorry.
They look at each other. They don't know what to do.

"We feel very bad, Mom," Lily said. "We are sorry we broke the window and lost the ball."

When they arrived there, Emma asked her mum “what are we doing here?” Mum replied, “We are going to visit your granny, and Emma, you will have to keep quiet while we are here”.
So Emma promised to keep quiet and very slowly she walked into her granny’s room. She was very surprised to see that it was so colourful and full of books. But she kept quiet and just waved to Granny.
Granny said, “Emma, it’s so nice to see you. You have been so good to keep quiet, now why don’t you take this book and keep yourself busy.”
So Emma happily took the book, gave granny a big hug and said, “I can’t wait to show you my new book at home.” Then she went home, with the book and her stories to tell.

Once upon a time, there was an ordinary man walking down a street. He was in a hurry. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise and he quickly stopped. He thought he saw something that looked like a monster over there!
He started to shake and his heart was pumping fast. Then he heard a little voice say, "Hello! Don't be scared! I'm just a little boy."
The man looked around and saw a 3 year old child standing there. He smiled and said, "What are you doing out here on your own?" 
The child replied, "I wanted to go for a walk, but I was worried I might get lost. Can you help me find my way home?" 
The man was very pleased that the child wasn't afraid of him. He said, "Of course I can help you! Let's hurry and find your home!" 
The man and the child hurried down the street, until they finally found the boy's house. The man gave the child a high five and said, "I'm glad I could help you find your way home!"
The boy smiled and said, "Thank you, sir! I'll never forget your kindness!" 
The man smiled and waved goodbye before continuing on his way. 
The end.

The lady looked confused and scared. She didn't know who these children were or what they wanted. She tried to back away, but she tripped on her cane and fell to the ground. The box slipped from Sara's hands and hit the lady on the head. The lady cried out in pain and dropped her groceries.

The moral of the story is: Don't deliver things to strangers without asking. You might hurt them or make them angry. Be careful and respectful of other people's feelings and belongings.

Sara and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with the toys and the real things. Sara found a long green thing in the fridge. She asked Ben what it was.
"It's celery," Ben said. "You can eat it. It's crunchy and good."
Sara took a bite of the celery. She made a face. She did not like it. It was bitter and hard. She spit it out.
"Yuck!" she said. "Celery is bad. I don't want it."
Ben laughed. He liked celery. He thought Sara was silly. He took the celery from her and ate it.
"More for me," he said. "Celery is good. You are picky."
Sara was angry. She did not like Ben laughing at her. She did not like him taking her celery. She wanted to make him stop. She reached out and pinched his arm.
"Ow!" Ben cried. "That hurts! Why did you pinch me?"
"Because you are rude," Sara said. "You took my celery and you laughed at me. That's not nice."
Ben was angry too. He did not like Sara pinching him. He did not like her calling him rude. He wanted to make her sorry. He reached out and pinched her back.
"Ow!" Sara cried. "That hurts more! Why did you pinch me back?"
"Because you are rude too," Ben said. "You spit out the celery and you pinched me first. That's not nice either."
Sara and Ben glared at each other. They both had red marks on their arms. They both felt hurt and mad. They did not want to play anymore.
Mom heard them crying. She came into the kitchen. She saw the celery and the toys and the pinches. She was not happy.
"What's going on here?" she asked. "Why are you pinching each other? Why are you wasting food? Why are you being rude?"
Sara and Ben looked down. They knew they had done wrong. They felt sorry and ashamed. They did not know what to say.
Mom sighed. She took the celery and the toys and put them away. She took Sara and Ben and hugged them.
"I love you both," she said. "But you need to be kind and respectful to each other. Pinching is not okay. Laughing at someone's taste is not okay. Wasting food is not okay. Being rude is not okay. Do you understand?"
Sara and Ben nodded. They understood. They felt bad for hurting each other and making Mom sad. They wanted to make up.
"I'm sorry, Ben," Sara said. "I didn't mean to pinch you. I was just mad. You can have the celery if you want. I don't like it, but you do."
"I'm sorry, Sara," Ben said. "I didn't mean to pinch you back. I was just mad too. You don't have to eat the celery if you don't want. I like it, but you don't."
Sara and Ben smiled. They hugged each other. They hugged Mom. They said they were sorry again. They said they loved each other. They said they loved Mom.
Mom smiled too. She was glad they apologized and forgave each other. She was proud of them for being honest and caring. She said she loved them too. She said they could play again, but only with the toys and not with the food. She said they could have a snack later, but not celery.

Jimmy chased it until the bird flew out of sight. He stopped and looked around, but the bird was gone. It had vanished! Jimmy looked sadly at the sky and said, "Where did the bird go?"
He didn't know. He was sure the bird had been there, but he couldn't find it anywhere.
Suddenly, Jimmy heard a noise coming from the bushes. He looked closely and saw that the mild wind had blown away some leaves and the bird was now sitting there. Jimmy smiled and said, "Hey bird, I found you!"
But before he could get any closer, the bird flew away again. Jimmy was disappointed but he also felt determined. He didn't give up, he kept looking until he finally found it again. This time he was able to catch the bird and hold it in his hands.
He was so happy! He smiled and said, "Thanks for not vanishing!" The bird chirped and then flew away. Jimmy watched it until it was out of sight.

They stood up and asked the wind, "Wind, can you help us find a sweet apple?" The wind blew harder and led them to a tree with many sweet apples. Tom and Lily picked the apples and shared them. They were both happy and the sour apple was forgotten.

Mia was uncomfortable. She thought to herself, "Why is Tom still shivering?" She asked Tom, "Do you still feel cold?" He said, "Yes, but it's uncomfortable." Mia noticed that the fire was almost out and said, "Let's get more fuel for the fire!"
Tom went outside and got some more fuel for the fire. They quickly added it to the fire and soon it was nice and warm. Tom and Mia were no longer uncomfortable. But then the wind picked up and they started to shiver again. Mia asked Tom, "What can we do?"
Tom thought for a minute and said, "Let's put a blanket over us. That will stop the wind and keep us warm." Mia agreed and they went to get a blanket. Then Tom and Mia finally got warm and stopped shivering. They were so relieved, and happy to be warm again!

She decided to polish them anyway. She took her cloth and her tin and went to the kitchen. She sat on the floor and started to polish her shoes. She did not see the drain on the floor. It was where the water from the sink went. It had a metal cover with holes in it.
Lily was so busy polishing her shoes that she did not notice that her tin of polish was sliding towards the drain. She rubbed and rubbed and smiled at her shoes. Then she heard a clink. She looked up and saw that her tin of polish had fallen into the drain. She tried to reach it, but it was too deep. She could not get it back.
Lily started to cry. She had lost her polish. She could not make her shoes shiny anymore. She felt very bad. She wished she had listened to her mom and stayed in her room.
Her mom heard her cry and came to the kitchen. She saw Lily on the floor and the empty drain. She understood what had happened. She hugged Lily and said it was okay. She said she would buy her a new tin of polish. She said she was sorry for the gloomy day. She said they could make some cookies and read some stories instead.
Lily stopped crying and smiled. She liked cookies and stories. She thanked her mom and gave her a kiss. She said she loved her. She said she would be more careful with her polish next time. She said she hoped the sun would come out soon.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big pond with ducks and fish. Lily wanted to feed the ducks, but Tom wanted to catch the fish.
"Look, Lily, a fish!" Tom said, pointing to the water. He ran to the edge of the pond and tried to grab the fish with his hands.
"No, Tom, don't do that!" Lily said, following him. "You will fall in the water and get wet!"
But Tom did not listen. He leaned over the water and reached for the fish. He lost his balance and fell in the pond with a splash.
Lily gasped and ran to help him. She saw Tom's head come out of the water. He was coughing and spitting. He looked funny. His hair was gone. He was bald.
"Tom, your hair!" Lily said, shocked. "Where is your hair?"
Tom touched his head and felt nothing. He was scared and confused. He started to cry.
"Lily, my hair, my hair!" he sobbed.
Lily felt sorry for him. She hugged him and tried to calm him down.
"Don't cry, Tom, it's okay," she said. "Your hair will grow back. It's just a wig. You were wearing a wig, remember?"
Tom remembered. He had found a wig in his mom's closet and put it on to look like his dad, who was bald. He thought it was funny. He forgot he was wearing it when he went to the park.
"Oh, yeah, it's a wig," he said, sniffling. "But where is it now?"
They looked around and saw the wig floating on the water. A duck was nibbling on it.
"Hey, that's my wig!" Tom said, angry. He tried to get it back, but the duck swam away.
"Let it go, Tom, it's just a wig," Lily said. "You don't need it. You look good bald. You look like your dad."
Tom smiled. He felt better. He liked his dad. He liked Lily. He liked the park. He liked the water. He liked the fish. He liked the ducks. Even the one that took his wig.
He discovered that he could have fun without his wig. He discovered that he had a good friend in Lily. He discovered that he was brave and strong. He discovered that he was happy.

Anna and Ben were twins. They liked to play together. One day, they went to a big park with their mom and dad. The park had a maze made of tall plants. Anna and Ben wanted to try the maze.
"Can we go in the maze, mom?" Anna asked.
"Sure, but stay close to each other and don't get lost," mom said.
Anna and Ben ran into the maze. They followed the paths and turned left and right. They saw many flowers and bugs. They thought the maze was fun.
But after a while, they got tired and confused. They did not know how to get out of the maze. They did not see their mom and dad. They felt scared and sad.
"Where are we, Ben?" Anna asked.
"I don't know, Anna. I wish we could find the way out," Ben said.
They hugged each other and tried to be brave. They walked and walked, hoping to see the exit. They did not like the maze anymore. They thought the maze was boring.
Then, they heard a voice. It was their dad. He was calling their names.
"Anna! Ben! Where are you?" dad shouted.
"Dad! We're here! We're here!" Anna and Ben shouted back.
They followed the sound of dad's voice. They saw him standing at the end of the maze. He looked happy and relieved.
"Anna! Ben! I'm so glad you're safe!" dad said. He hugged them and kissed them.
"Sorry, dad. We got lost in the maze. We were scared," Anna said.
"It's okay, Anna. I'm sorry, too. I should have watched you more closely. The maze was too big and tricky," dad said.
"Can we go home now, dad? We don't like the maze anymore. It's boring," Ben said.
"Sure, Ben. Let's go home. The maze is boring. You know what's not boring? Ice cream. How about we get some ice cream on the way home?" dad said.
Anna and Ben smiled. They liked ice cream. They held dad's hand and walked out of the maze. They saw mom waiting for them. She hugged them and said she was proud of them. They all went to get some ice cream. They had a good day.

The fairy nodded and smiled back. She said,"You are a very wise girl, indeed. You are right. Only by studying and learning, can you become powerful and brave. Always remember that". 
Then she fluttered away. Emily looked up to the sky and sang a cheerful song. She was so thankful for the life lessons she had learned. 
The moral of the story is that knowledge is a beautiful gift that can bring joy and strength to our lives. So, take time out to study and learn something new each day.

Lila and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat, a scarf and a carrot nose. They gave him a name: Frosty.
"Hello, Frosty!" Lila said. "Do you like the snow?"
"Yes, I do!" Ben said in a funny voice, pretending to be Frosty. "But I don't like the sun. It makes me melt."
Lila and Ben laughed. They wanted to play with Frosty for a long time. But then they saw something shiny near the gate. It was a key.
"Look, Ben! A key!" Lila said. "I wonder what it opens."
"Maybe it's a treasure!" Ben said. "Let's go and see."
They ran to the gate and tried the key. It fit. They opened the gate and saw a path leading to a big house. The house looked old and mysterious.
"Wow, what a house!" Lila said. "Do you think someone lives there?"
"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe it's empty. Maybe it's haunted. Do you want to go inside?"
Lila and Ben looked at each other. They were curious, but also scared. They thought about Frosty, waiting for them in the snow.
"Maybe we should go back," Lila said. "Frosty might miss us."
"Yes, you're right," Ben said. "And maybe the sun will come out soon. We don't want Frosty to melt."
They turned around and ran back to the snowman. They hugged him and said goodbye.
"Bye, Frosty!" Lila said. "We'll come back tomorrow."
"Bye, Lila and Ben!" Ben said in a funny voice, pretending to be Frosty. "Have fun!"
They left the key in the gate and went home, wondering what was inside the mysterious house.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big maze made of green bushes. They wanted to try it.
"Let's go in, Lily!" Tom said. "It looks fun!"
"OK, Tom. But we have to stay together. The maze is big and we might get lost," Lily said.
They ran into the maze and followed the paths. They saw many turns and dead ends. They had to go back and try again. They laughed and had fun.
But after a while, they realized they did not know where they were. They could not see the exit. They could not hear other people. They felt scared.
"Tom, I don't like this. How do we get out?" Lily asked.
"I don't know, Lily. I don't recognize anything. Everything looks the same," Tom said.
They walked around, hoping to find a way out. They saw a thin gap between two bushes. They thought maybe they could squeeze through it.
"Look, Lily! Maybe we can go through there. Maybe it leads to the outside," Tom said.
"Let's try, Tom. Maybe you're right," Lily said.
They pushed their way through the thin gap. They felt the sun on their faces. They saw the grass and the trees. They saw their mom and dad waiting for them.
They were out of the maze!
They ran to their mom and dad and hugged them. They told them about their adventure.
"We're sorry, mom and dad. We got lost in the maze. It was hard to find the exit," Lily said.
"It's OK, Lily. We're glad you're safe. The maze was too big for you. Next time, we'll go with you," mom said.
"We're proud of you, Tom. You found a way out. You were brave and smart," dad said.
Lily and Tom smiled. They were happy to be out of the maze. They learned a lesson. They decided to play something else.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to draw with pencils and paper. One day, they go to the park with their moms. They find a big tree and sit under it. They start to draw flowers and birds and suns.
"Look, Anna, I draw a big sun!" Ben says, showing his paper to Anna.
"Wow, Ben, your sun is very yellow and bright!" Anna says, smiling. "I draw a blue flower. Do you like it?"
"Yes, Anna, your flower is very pretty and nice!" Ben says, nodding.
They are happy and keep drawing. But then, a strong wind blows. The wind takes their papers and pencils and flies them away.
"Oh no!" Anna and Ben say. They are upset. They want their papers and pencils back. They run after them, but they are too fast. They lose them in the air.
They start to cry. They panic. They do not know what to do. They look for their moms, but they do not see them. They are scared and alone.
"Anna, Ben, where are you?" They hear their moms calling them. They run to their voices. They hug their moms and tell them what happened.
"I'm sorry, Anna, Ben, we did not see the wind coming. We were talking to each other. Are you okay?" Their moms say, holding them.
"We are okay, mom, but we are sad. We lost our papers and pencils. We worked hard on them. We liked them a lot." Anna and Ben say, sniffing.
"I know, sweeties, I know. It's okay to be sad. But you know what? You can always draw more papers and pencils. You have many more at home. And you have each other. You are good friends. You can share and help and have fun together. That's more important than papers and pencils, don't you think?" Their moms say, smiling.
Anna and Ben think for a moment. They nod. They wipe their tears. They smile.
"You are right, mom. We are good friends. We can draw more papers and pencils. And we can be careful with the wind next time. Thank you, mom." Anna and Ben say, hugging their moms.
They go back to the tree. They find some new papers and pencils. They start to draw again. They are happy.
The moral value of the story is: Friendship is more important than material things.

Then, it started to rain. Amy and Tom ran under a tree to stay dry. They waited for the rain to stop. When the rain stopped, Amy's fan was wet. She was sad and worried it would break.
Tom had an idea. "Let's put your fan in the sun to dry," he said. They put the fan in the sun and waited. Soon, the fan was dry and not broken. Amy was very happy.
Amy and Tom became good friends. They played at the park every day with the fan, always being careful to keep it dry and safe. And they lived happily ever after.

John wanted to go for a walk in the woods. He put on his boot and went outside. Everything seemed peaceful and calm. But there was trouble ahead.
John kept walking until he heard a sad noise. He wondered what it could be, so he followed the sound until he saw a small squirrel. It had gotten its paw stuck in a hole in a tree.
John was very sad for the poor squirrel. He tried to come up with a plan to help the animal. He tried pulling on the squirrel's paw, but it wouldn't budge. Then he realized he could use his boot. He took it off his foot and wedged it against the tree. With some gentle pushing, John was able to get the squirrel's paw free.
The squirrel was so relieved, it ran away into the woods. John looked after it happily and happily put his boot back on. He was glad he was able to help the squirrel, and even happier that he was able to come up with a plan that worked.

He found himself in a big chamber with many doors. A voice said, "Welcome to the cake test. You can choose one door and find a cake behind it. But be careful, some cakes are good and some are bad. If you choose a bad cake, you will have to stay here forever."
Tim was not scared. He thought he knew everything about cake. He opened the first door and saw a chocolate cake. He grabbed it and took a big bite. But the cake was bitter and made him cough. He spat it out and tried another door.
He opened the second door and saw a lemon cake. He grabbed it and took a big bite. But the cake was sour and made him cry. He threw it away and tried another door.
He opened the third door and saw a carrot cake. He grabbed it and took a big bite. But the cake was spicy and made him sneeze. He dropped it and tried another door.
He opened the fourth door and saw a cheese cake. He grabbed it and took a big bite. But the cake was moldy and made him sick. He fell to the ground and tried to call for help.
But no one came. The voice said, "You have failed the cake test. You were greedy and did not share. You did not listen and did not think. You have to stay here forever with the bad cakes."
Tim was very sad and sorry. He wished he had been nicer and smarter. He wished he had a friend to help him. He learned that cake is not everything and that sharing is caring. But it was too late.

One day, Ralph was running around in the park. Suddenly, he ran into a bone. His eyes sparkled and he knew he had to pick it up. He carefully picked up the bone with his teeth and started running around with it again.
Just then, he heard someone calling his name. He ran over to see who it was and saw his best friend, a little puppy called Max. 
Max said, "Ralph! I'm so happy to meet you! Let's play together and share the bone!" 
Ralph eagerly barked in agreement.
They played with the bone for hours and hours, until the sun went down. It was the best day ever. Even Ralph was careful! 
The moral of the story is to always be careful, even if you're feeling careless.

John was so excited! He hopped around, excited to go and explore his neighbourhood. As he ventured across the street, he could see a big, mysterious tree in the park. 
John moved closer, and the tree began to tremble. He stepped back in awe, watching as pieces of bark flaked off and fell beneath the tree. Soon he noticed something strange on the ground: a bright green scale.
John bent down and touched the scale. He could feel a sudden, harsh chill as he held it in his hands. He wondered what it could be, so he placed it in his pocket and set off to explore some more. 
John forgot about the scale until the next day when he saw a dragon fly out of the tree's branches. He gasped in amazement and realised that the scale must have belonged to the dragon. He lay down and watched as the dragon flew high into the sky, still trembling with excitement.

Tom put the stone on his palm and gave it to Lily. She looked at it and smiled. It was smooth and sparkly and had many colors. She said, "Wow, it is beautiful. Can I have it?" Tom said, "No, it is mine. I found it first. You can look at it, but then you have to give it back."
Lily did not want to give it back. She liked the stone too much. She thought, "Maybe I can keep it. Tom will not notice. He has many other toys. He does not need this one." She put the stone in her pocket and said, "OK, here you go." She gave Tom his palm back, but it was empty.
Tom did not see what Lily did. He was busy loading his truck with sand. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend. You are dependable. You always share with me." Lily felt bad. She knew she was not being a good friend. She knew she was not dependable. She knew she did not share with Tom.

Lily felt worse. She said, "No, I have not seen it. Maybe you lost it. Maybe someone took it. Maybe it was not a treasure at all. Maybe it was just a rock."
Tom was sad. He said, "No, it was a treasure. It was very special. It was mine. I liked it a lot. I wish I had it back." Lily felt sorry. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I have something to tell you. I have your treasure. I took it yesterday. I put it in my pocket. I was selfish. I did not share with you. I lied to you. I was not a good friend. I was not dependable. I'm sorry."
Tom was surprised. He said, "You took it? Why did you do that? That was not nice. That was not fair. That hurt my feelings." Lily said, "I know. I was wrong. I liked the stone too much. I wanted to keep it. But I did not feel happy. I felt guilty. I wanted to tell you, but I was scared. I'm sorry, Tom. Please forgive me. Please be my friend again. Please take your treasure back."
Tom looked at Lily. He saw that she was sad and sorry. He said, "Lily, I'm mad at you, but I'm also glad you told me the truth. That was brave. That was honest. That was good. I forgive you, Lily. You are still my friend. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise me you will never take my things again. You have to promise me you will always share with me. You have to promise me you will be dependable."
Lily nodded and said, "I promise, Tom. I promise I will never take your things again. I promise I will always share with you. I promise I will be dependable." She took the stone out of her pocket and gave it to Tom. He took it and smiled. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend. You are dependable. You always share with me. But you know what? I have an idea. Why don't we share this treasure? We can both have it. We can both enjoy it. We can both play with it. What do you think?"
Lily smiled too. She said, "I think that's a great idea, Tom. I think that's a very good way to share. I think that's what friends do. I think that's what dependable friends do." They hugged and said, "We are dependable friends. We are the best friends." They put the stone on their truck
