The day of the race came, and all the kids gathered at the park. Tim's mom said, "Good luck, Tim! Be brave and do your best." Tim smiled and said, "I will, Mom." The race started, and Tim ran as fast as he could. He was in front of everyone, and he could see the big, red ball waiting for the winner.
But then, Tim saw a small cat stuck in a tree. He stopped running and thought for a moment. He knew he could win the race, but the cat needed help. Tim decided to be brave and help the cat. He climbed the tree and saved the cat. His friends passed him, and he didn't win the race.
Tim felt sad that he didn't win the big, red ball. His mom came over and said, "I'm proud of you for being brave and helping the cat." Tim looked at the cat and smiled. Even though he didn't win, he felt good for doing the right thing. But then, the sky turned dark, and a big storm came. The wind blew the big, red ball away, and no one could find it.
In the end, no one got to keep the ball. Tim and his friends learned that sometimes, even when you try your best, things don't always go the way you want. But being brave and helping others is still important.

Tom and Sam were playing with their toy rockets in the backyard. They liked to pretend they were astronauts and explore the stars. They had two rockets, one red and one blue, and they took turns to launch them in the air.
"Look, my rocket is faster than yours!" Tom said, as he pushed the button on his red rocket. The rocket flew high and made a loud noise.
"No, mine is better!" Sam said, as he pushed the button on his blue rocket. The rocket also flew high, but then it started to spin and fall.
"Oh no, your rocket is broken!" Tom said, as he ran to catch the blue rocket. He looked at it and saw that the tip was cracked and the wings were bent.
"Can we fix it?" Sam asked, with a sad face.
"I don't think so," Tom said, shaking his head. "But maybe we can replace it with something else."
He looked around and saw a big stick on the ground. He picked it up and said, "Here, this can be your new rocket. It's longer and stronger than the old one."
Sam took the stick and looked at it. He was not sure if he liked it. It did not have a button or a noise or a color. It was just a stick.
"But this is not a rocket, this is a stick," he said, frowning.
"It is a rocket if you use your imagination," Tom said, smiling. "Watch, I'll show you."
He took the stick from Sam and held it in his hand. He made a whoosh sound with his mouth and threw the stick in the air. The stick flew like a missile and landed far away.
"Wow, that was amazing!" Sam said, clapping his hands. "Can I try?"
"Sure, you can," Tom said, as he gave the stick back to Sam. "But be careful, don't hit anyone or anything with it."
Sam nodded and held the stick in his hand. He also made a whoosh sound and threw the stick in the air. The stick flew like a missile and landed on the roof of the house.
"Uh oh, that was not good," Tom said, as he looked at the stick on the roof. "How are we going to get it back?"
"I don't know," Sam said, as he looked at the stick on the roof. "We can't reach it, we are too small."
They felt helpless and sad. They had lost their blue rocket and their stick missile. They wished they had their rockets back. They decided to go inside and ask their mom for help. Maybe she could get the stick from the roof and buy them a new rocket. They hoped she would not be mad at them. They learned their lesson. They would not throw sticks in the air again.

"No, you stop, cop! You can't catch me!" Ben says, laughing and running away.
Lila aims her toy gun and pretends to shoot Ben. "Bang, bang, bang! I got you, robber!"
Ben falls down and pretends to be hurt. "Ow, ow, ow! You shot me, cop!"
Lila runs to Ben and puts her toy gun away. "I'm sorry, Ben. Are you okay?"
Ben smiles and gets up. "I'm okay, Lila. It's just a game. You are a good cop."
Lila hugs Ben and says, "You are a good robber. But you have to go to jail now."
Lila takes Ben's hat and bag and leads him to the shed. The shed is dark and has a small window. Lila says, "This is your cell, robber. You have to stay here until I say so."
Ben looks at the shed and says, "Okay, Lila. But can I have a light? It's too dark in here."
Lila thinks for a moment and says, "Okay, robber. I'll give you a light. But you have to be good and quiet."
Lila finds a flashlight and gives it to Ben. She closes the shed door and says, "Bye, robber. I'll come back soon."
Ben turns on the flashlight and looks around the shed. He sees some toys and books and says, "This is not a bad cell. I can play and read here. But I miss Lila. I hope she comes back soon."

Once upon a time, there was a wise old Turtle. He lived in a big pond and always had lots of good advice for everybody. 
One day, a young Frog asked him how he could become smarter and larger. The Turtle smiled and said, “Read!”.
The Frog was surprised, but he did as the Turtle recommended. He bought a magazine from the store and read it every day. As he read, he noticed that he was getting smarter and larger. 
The Frog was so thankful to the Turtle that he hopped back to the pond to thank him. The Turtle smiled and nodded and said, “Reading is wise. You should recommend the magazine to everyone you know.” 
The Frog thanked the wise old Turtle and shared his magazine with his friends, and everyone in the pond became smarter and larger.
The end.

Tom said, "I don't know how to repair it. I need help. Can you help me, Lily?"

Tim met a little girl named Sue in the wheat field. Sue was sad. "I lost my toy," Sue said. "Can you help me find it?" Tim wanted to help Sue, but he was scared of the dark cloud. He said, "I am scared of the rain. I have to go home."
Sue sighed and said, "Please help me. I am very sad." Tim thought for a moment. He wanted to be a good friend, but he was still scared. He said, "I am sorry, Sue. I cannot help you." Tim left Sue alone in the wheat field.
The dark cloud came closer, and it started to rain. Sue was wet and cold. She cried and cried. Tim was safe at home, but he felt bad for not helping Sue.
The moral of the story is to help others, even when you are scared.

Max walked down the street with the newspaper. On his way, he saw a cat. The cat was also grumpy. "Why are you carrying that newspaper?" the cat asked. Max just wagged his tail and kept walking.
When Max gave the newspaper to Mr. Brown, he was very happy. "Thank you, Max!" he said with a big smile. Max wagged his tail and felt proud that he could help.
From that day on, Max was not a grumpy dog anymore. He loved to carry things and help people in his town. Everyone loved Max, and he was a very happy dog.

One day, Anna's mum and dad decided to take her on a boat to visit another island. Anna was so excited and shouted, "Yay! We are going on an adventure! Let's go!"
When they reached the island, Anna saw a stunning red beach. But then, something very strange happened. Out of nowhere, a shock arrived. It was a big wave that started to cover the beach and cover Anna's feet. The wave was so big that it started to push Anna's dad and mum away.
Anna shouted for help, but it was too late. Her parents had already been swept away into the sea. Anna was so sad and cried a river until there was nothing more to cry.
At this point, Anna had learned a hard lesson. No matter how exciting her adventures could be, she should always keep an eye on where she was stepping.

Ben showed a card with a small brown animal with a fluffy tail. He made a soft noise like this: "Squeak!" Anna thought hard. She did not know the animal. She guessed: "Mouse?" But Ben shook his head. He said: "No, it is a squirrel!" and kept the card.
They played until they had no more cards. They counted their cards. Anna had four cards. Ben had five cards. Ben said: "I win! I have more cards than you!" Anna felt sad. She wanted to win too.
Ben saw that Anna was sad. He wanted to make her happy. He said: "Do you want some cocoa? I can make some for us. We can share it and be warm." Anna smiled. She liked cocoa. She said: "Yes, please. That is very nice of you. Thank you, Ben."
They went to the kitchen and made some cocoa. They poured it into two cups and added some marshmallows. They sat on the couch and drank their cocoa. They felt warm and cozy. They talked about the animals and the sounds they made. They laughed and had fun. They forgot about the game. They were happy. They were friends.

Once upon a time there was a brave soldier who chose to stand guard in a field. The field was thick with tall grass and the soldier kept watch day and night. 
One day the soldier noticed something strange - he didn't hear any birds. The soldier searched for the birds, but they seemed to have vanished. He even searched in the tall grass, but couldn't find any sign of them. 
The soldier soon discovered why the birds had disappeared. A farmer had come to mow the tall grass, creating a huge cloud of dust. The birds had vanished to escape the dust. 
The soldier wasn't happy about the farmer mowing the grass - he knew the birds needed it in order to hide and live. So he spoke to the farmer and taught him a lesson. He taught him to be more careful and to remember that it is important to look after nature. 
After that the farmer understood the importance of taking care of the birds and so he only cut the grass in a way that allowed the birds to still live there.
The soldier felt very proud of his lesson - he had taught the farmer to not be careless and to remember that nature is precious.

Lila was a girl who liked to play in the garden. She liked to dig and plant and water the flowers. One day, she found a big, old pumpkin in a corner of the garden. It was round and orange and had a long stem.
Lila wondered what was inside the pumpkin. She took a knife from the kitchen and cut a hole in the pumpkin. She looked inside and saw a lot of seeds and pulp. It smelled bad and was wet and mushy. Lila said, "Yuck! This pumpkin is rotting!"
She threw the knife away and ran to the house. She told her mom what she had found. Her mom said, "That pumpkin is very old, Lila. It was left over from Halloween. Do you know what Halloween is?"
Lila shook her head. She did not know what Halloween was. Her mom said, "Halloween is a fun day when people dress up and go trick-or-treating. They knock on doors and say 'trick or treat' and get candy. Some people also carve pumpkins and make them into lanterns. They cut out eyes and a mouth and put a candle inside. They look scary and funny at night."
Lila said, "That sounds fun! Can we do that next Halloween?" Her mom said, "Sure, we can. But we need a fresh pumpkin, not an old one. An old one will rot and smell and attract bugs. We can go to the farm and pick a new one when it is time."
Lila said, "OK, mom. But can I keep the old pumpkin for now? I want to make something with it." Her mom said, "What do you want to make, Lila?" Lila said, "I want to make a prince!"
Her mom smiled and said, "A prince? How will you do that?" Lila said, "I will use a magic wand and say 'abracadabra' and the pumpkin will turn into a prince. Then he will be my friend and we will play together."
Her mom said, "That sounds like a nice idea, Lila. But you know that magic is not real, right? It is only pretend. The pumpkin will not really turn into a prince. It will just stay a pumpkin."
Lila said, "I know, mom. But I can pretend. It is fun to pretend. Maybe the pumpkin will pretend too. Maybe he will be happy to be a prince and not a rotting pumpkin."
Her mom said, "OK, Lila. You can keep the pumpkin and pretend. But don't forget to wash your hands after you touch it. And don't let it make a mess in the garden. And don't be sad if it falls apart. It is just an old pumpkin, not a real prince."
Lila said, "OK, mom. I will remember. Thank you for letting me keep the pumpkin. I will be nice to him and he will be nice to me. He will be the best prince ever!"
Lila ran back to the garden with a stick in her hand. She said it was her magic wand. She waved it over the pumpkin and said, "Abracadabra! You are a prince now! Hello, prince! What is your name?"
The pumpkin did not answer. It did not move. It did not change. It was still a pumpkin. But Lila did not mind. She smiled and said, "Your name is Prince Pumpkin. You are my friend. Let's play!"

Tim and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with flowers and grass. They wanted to go up the hill and see what was on the other side.
They ran up the hill, holding hands. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They laughed and shouted. They were happy.
But when they got to the top of the hill, they saw a big fence. The fence was tall and sharp and had a sign that said "Keep Out". They could not see what was on the other side of the fence. They felt sad and angry.
"Why can't we go there?" Tim asked.
"I don't know. Maybe there is something bad there. Maybe there is a monster or a snake or a mean dog." Lily said.
They looked at the fence and wondered. They wanted to know what was on the other side. They wanted to have more fun.
Tim had an idea. He saw a hole in the fence. The hole was small and low, but he thought he could fit through it. He let go of Lily's hand and ran to the hole.
"Tim, wait! Don't go there! It's dangerous!" Lily cried.
But Tim did not listen. He bent down and crawled through the hole. He felt the fence scratch his arms and legs. He felt a sting and a drop of blood. He did not care. He wanted to see what was on the other side.
He got through the hole and stood up. He looked around. He saw a big field with trees and rocks and a pond. He saw a band playing music. The band had drums and guitars and horns. The music was loud and fast and fun. He saw people dancing and clapping and smiling. He saw balloons and flags and candy. He thought it was a party. He thought it was the best thing ever.
He ran to the band and the people and the party. He forgot about Lily and the fence and the hole. He forgot about everything else.
Lily saw Tim go through the hole and disappear. She felt scared and lonely. She wanted Tim to come back. She wanted to play with him. She wanted to go home.
She ran to the hole and tried to follow him. But the hole was too small and too low for her. She could not fit through it. She tried to push and pull and wiggle. She could not move. She felt the fence hurt her arms and legs. She felt a sting and a drop of blood. She cried.
She cried for Tim and for help and for mommy and daddy. She cried loud and hard and long.
A man heard her cry. He was walking his dog near the park. He saw Lily stuck in the hole and crying. He felt sorry for her. He ran to her and knelt down. He was gentle and kind. He spoke to her softly and calmly.
"Hello, little girl. What's your name? Why are you crying? Are you hurt?" he asked.
Lily looked at him. He had a friendly face and a nice voice. He had a big dog that licked her face. She felt a little better. She told him her name and what happened.
"I'm Lily. I was playing with Tim. He went through the hole and did not come back. I want to go with him. I want to go home. I'm hurt and scared." she said.
The man nodded and smiled. He took out his phone and called the police. He told them where he was and what he saw. He asked them to come and help. He took out a band-aid and put it on Lily's wound. He gave her a hug and a candy. He told her it was going to be okay.
"Don't worry, Lily. I'm here with you. The police will come soon and get you out. They will find Tim and take you both home. You are brave and smart and good. Everything will be fine." he said.
Lily felt a little better. She hugged him and his dog. She thanked him and waited for the police. She hoped Tim was okay. She hoped they would be together again. She hoped they would never go through the hole again.

Inside the freezer, the big bear saw a little mouse. The little mouse said, "Please, Mr. Bear, don't eat me!" The big bear thought for a moment and said, "Okay, little mouse, I won't eat you. But you must help me find food."
The little mouse and the big bear went to look for food. They looked in the kitchen, but there was no food. They looked in the living room, but there was no food. They looked in the bedroom, but there was no food.
Finally, they went outside to look for food. The big bear saw a big tree with lots of apples. The little mouse said, "Mr. Bear, let me help you. I can climb the tree and get the apples for you." The big bear agreed and the little mouse started to climb the tree.
As the little mouse climbed the tree, the big bear started to feel very tired. He decided to pause and take a nap under the tree. While the big bear was sleeping, a hunter came by and saw the big bear. The hunter shot the big bear and took him away. The little mouse came down from the tree and saw that the big bear was gone. The little mouse was sad and all alone.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, a bird and a fish. They were the best of friends and they did everything together. Every day they swam and flew around the lake, having lots of fun. 
One day, the brilliant fish had an idea. She asked the bird if they could unite the two halves of the lake, so they could swim and fly freely throughout the whole lake freely. The bird was excited by this idea and agreed.
For a whole week, the bird and fish worked together to try and unite the lake. No matter how hard they tried, the lake stayed in two halves. The bird started to feel sad and frustrated, until the brilliant fish had another idea.
She suggested that the bird use her wings to create a current in the water, while the fish provided propulsion from underneath. This time it worked! Together, they united the two halves of the lake and were able to swim and fly around together, just as they had hoped. The fish and the bird were so happy and proud of themselves for their accomplishment. They celebrated their success together, swimming and flying around the lake, reunited at last.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the garden. They had a big hippo toy that they liked to pretend was real. They made it walk and splash and roar.
"Let's make the hippo shrink!" Ben said. He had a magic wand that he got for his birthday. He waved it at the hippo and said a silly word.
"Shrinky-dinky-doo!"
Nothing happened. The hippo was still big and heavy.
"Maybe you need to say it louder," Lily said. She took the wand from Ben and tried again.
"Shrinky-dinky-doo!"
Still nothing. The hippo was still big and heavy.
"Maybe the wand is broken," Ben said. He was sad. He wanted to see the hippo shrink.
"Or maybe the hippo is too big to shrink," Lily said. She had an idea. She ran inside the house and came back with a light bulb.
"Look, Ben, this is light and small. Maybe the wand can shrink this," she said. She held the light bulb in front of the hippo and waved the wand.
"Shrinky-dinky-doo!"
The light bulb flashed and popped. It was gone. Lily and Ben gasped.
"Wow, it worked!" Ben said. He was happy. He wanted to try again.
"Let's find something else to shrink," he said. He looked around the garden and saw a flower.
"Shrinky-dinky-doo!"
The flower wilted and fell. Lily and Ben clapped.
"Let's find something else to shrink," Lily said. She looked around the garden and saw a bird.
"Shrinky-dinky-doo!"
The bird squeaked and flew away. Lily and Ben laughed.
"Let's find something else to shrink," Ben said. He looked around the garden and saw their dad.
"Shrinky-dinky-doo!"
Their dad turned around and saw them. He frowned.
"What are you two doing?" he asked.
"Nothing, dad," Lily and Ben said. They hid the wand behind their backs.
"Are you sure?" their dad asked. He looked at the hippo, the light bulb, the flower and the bird. He had a feeling something was wrong.
He walked towards them and reached for the wand.
"Shrinky-dinky-doo!" Lily and Ben shouted together.
Their dad blinked and felt a strange sensation. He looked down and saw that he was smaller than the hippo. He looked up and saw that Lily and Ben were bigger than him.
"Uh-oh," he said.
Lily and Ben giggled.
"Look, dad, we made you shrink!" they said.
They picked him up and hugged him.
"Don't worry, dad, we'll make you big again," they said.
They waved the wand and said another silly word.
"Biggy-wiggy-woo!"
Their dad grew back to his normal size. He was relieved.
"Thank you, kids," he said. "But please, no more shrinking. It's not safe."
"Okay, dad," Lily and Ben said. They nodded.
They put the wand away and played with the hippo.
They had fun, but they never tried to shrink anything again.

The kangaroo looked in the direction of the noise and saw its home! It hopped with joy and gave a loud snap! It had found its way back to safety.

Lily was a girl who liked to talk a lot. She talked to her mom, her dad, her brother, her friends, and even her toys. She talked about what she saw, what she did, what she liked, and what she wanted. She talked so much that sometimes she forgot to listen.
One day, she went for a walk with her mom. They saw many things on the street: cars, bikes, dogs, birds, flowers, and people. Lily talked about everything she saw, but she did not notice that her mom was trying to tell her something.
"Look, Lily, there is a lady who needs help. She is carrying a big bag and she looks very tired. Maybe we can help her cross the street," her mom said.
But Lily did not hear her mom. She was too busy talking about the dog that was barking, the bird that was singing, and the flower that was pretty. She did not mention the lady who needed help.
They walked past the lady, who looked sad and miserable. She wished someone would help her, but no one did. She had to cross the street by herself, with her heavy bag.
Lily and her mom reached the park, where they met Lily's friends. They played on the swings, the slide, and the sandbox. Lily talked to her friends, but she did not listen to them. She did not notice that they were bored and annoyed by her talking.
"Look, Lily, there is a butterfly. It is very colorful and beautiful. Maybe we can catch it and look at it," one of her friends said.
But Lily did not hear her friend. She was too busy talking about the swing that was high, the slide that was fast, and the sandbox that was fun. She did not mention the butterfly.
They played for a while, but then her friends decided to leave. They said goodbye to Lily, who did not notice that they were unhappy. She stayed in the park, talking to herself.
Lily's mom came to get her. She saw that Lily was alone and sad. She asked her what happened.
"Mom, I don't understand. Why did my friends leave? Why did they not want to play with me?" Lily said.
Her mom hugged her and said, "Lily, you are a very smart and sweet girl, but you have to learn to listen. Listening is as important as talking. When you listen, you can learn new things, you can help others, and you can make friends. When you talk, you have to mention what is important, not just what you like. You have to share your thoughts, not just say them. Do you understand?"
Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom, I understand. I'm sorry I did not listen to you or to my friends. I will try to listen more and talk less. I want to be a good girl and a good friend."
Her mom smiled and said, "That's good, Lily. I'm proud of you. Now, let's go home and have some cookies. And maybe we can see the lady who needed help and say sorry to her."
Lily agreed and said, "Yes, mom, let's do that. And maybe we can also see the butterfly and the dog and the bird and the flower and..."
Her mom laughed and said, "Yes, Lily, maybe we can. But remember to listen, too."
Lily smiled and said, "OK, mom, I will. I love you."
They held hands and walked home, happy and hopeful.

"Mommy, why isn't the sun coming down?" Tommy asked.
His mommy was drying the dishes with a towel.
"The sun never comes down, Tommy," His mommy said, "But its light will get weak when the night comes".
Tommy thought about it for a moment and said, "Oh, okay!" 
"It's good that the sun is high in the sky now. It will keep us warm and dry," his mommy said as she went to hang up the towel. Tommy smiled and went to play with his toys.
He was thankful for the warm, dry morning.

Baa asked her friend, Moo the cow, for help. Moo tried to fix Baa's wool, but it was too hard. Then, Baa asked her other friend, Cluck the chicken, for help. Cluck tried to fix the wool too, but she couldn't. Baa was very sad and worried.
Finally, Baa asked her best friend, Oink the pig, for help. Oink had an idea. He found a big brush and gently brushed Baa's wool. The wind had stopped, and Baa's wool became soft and pretty again.
Baa was so happy and thanked Oink for helping her. They all played together in the sunny field again, feeling healthy and happy. And from that day on, whenever the wind would stir Baa's wool, she knew that her friends would always be there to help her.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. They saw a big yellow post with a sign on it. The sign had many words and pictures.
"What is that?" Lily asked.
"I don't know. Let's go and see," Ben said.
They ran to the post and looked at the sign. It had words like "park rules", "no littering", "keep off the grass" and "have fun". It also had pictures of a dog, a trash can, a flower and a smiley face.
"What does it mean?" Lily asked.
"I think it means what we can and can't do in the park," Ben said. "See, the dog means we can bring our pets, but the trash can means we have to throw away our garbage. The flower means we have to be nice to the plants, and the smiley face means we have to be happy."
"Oh, I see. That makes sense," Lily said.
They heard a voice behind them. It was a park ranger. He wore a hat and a badge.
"Hello, kids. What are you doing?" he asked.
"We are looking at the sign," Ben said.
"That's good. Do you know what the sign is for?" the park ranger asked.
"Yes, it tells us the park rules," Lily said.
"That's right. The sign is to help us keep the park clean and safe for everyone. Do you follow the park rules?" the park ranger asked.
"Yes, we do. We love the park," Ben said.
"Me too. I'm glad you do. Can I recommend something to you?" the park ranger asked.
"What is it?" Lily asked.
"Well, if you look over there, you will see a big yellow tent. That's where we have some fun activities for kids. You can learn more about the park, the animals and the plants. You can also play some games and get some stickers. Would you like to try it?" the park ranger asked.
"Yes, yes, yes!" Ben and Lily said.
"Great. Then follow me. I'll show you the way," the park ranger said.
He led them to the yellow tent. Ben and Lily thanked him and went inside. They had a lot of fun in the yellow tent. They learned, played and got stickers. They followed the park rules and had a happy day.

Lily and Max were playing in the park with their mom. They saw a big sign that said "Famous Cookie Sale". Lily loved cookies. She wanted to try the famous ones.
"Mom, can we go to the cookie sale?" Lily asked.
"Sure, honey. But we have to wait for our turn. There are many people who want cookies too." Mom said.
They walked to the cookie sale and saw a long line of people. They also saw a man with a camera and a microphone. He was talking to some people who had cookies.
"Who is he?" Max asked.
"He is a reporter. He works for the TV. He is asking people about the cookies." Mom explained.
"Can we talk to him too?" Lily asked.
"Maybe, if he comes to us. But we have to be polite and say what we think." Mom said.
They waited in line for a long time. Finally, they reached the table where the cookies were. They saw many kinds of cookies. Chocolate, vanilla, peanut butter, oatmeal, and more. They smelled so good.
"Hello, kids. What cookies do you want?" The lady who sold the cookies asked.
"I want chocolate." Lily said.
"I want peanut butter." Max said.
The lady gave them each a cookie. They took a big bite. They smiled. The cookies were delicious.
"Wow, these are the best cookies ever!" Lily said.
"I agree. They are so yummy!" Max said.
Just then, the reporter came to them. He pointed his camera and microphone at them.
"Hello, kids. I'm from the TV. Can I ask you a question?" He said.
"OK." Lily and Max said.
"What do you think of these famous cookies?" He asked.
"They are very good. We like them a lot." Lily said.
"They are the best cookies ever. You should try them too." Max said.
"Thank you, kids. You are very sweet. Can I mention your names on the TV?" He asked.
"Sure. I'm Lily and he's Max." Lily said.
"Thank you, Lily and Max. You are very good at talking. Have a nice day." He said.
He walked away to talk to other people. Lily and Max finished their cookies. They were happy. They had tried the famous cookies and talked to the TV man. They hugged their mom.
"Mom, we are famous too!" Lily said.
"Yes, you are, honey. And you are very smart and kind." Mom said.
They left the park and went home. They told their dad and their friends about their adventure. They felt proud and excited. They hoped to see themselves on the TV. They loved cookies. And they loved each other. The end.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to eat waffles for breakfast. Their mom made them waffles every morning with butter and honey. They were very yummy.
One day, mom had to go to work early and left a note for dad. The note said: "Please make waffles for Anna and Ben. They are in the freezer. Love you." But dad was very sleepy and forgot to read the note. He made eggs and toast instead.
When Anna and Ben came to the kitchen, they saw the eggs and toast on the table. They were sad and confused. They did not like eggs and toast. They liked waffles.
"Where are our waffles, dad?" Anna asked.
"Waffles? What waffles?" dad said.
Anna saw the note on the fridge and ran to get it. She gave it to dad and said: "Look, dad. Mom left a note. She said to make waffles for us. They are in the freezer."
Dad looked at the note and felt sorry. He had not been very thoughtful. He had not read the note. He had not made waffles for his twins.
"I'm sorry, Anna and Ben. I did not see the note. I did not make waffles for you. I made eggs and toast. Do you want some?" dad said.
Anna and Ben shook their heads. They did not want eggs and toast. They wanted waffles.

The old man said, "I am sad because I can't see the leaves fall. It is too dark for me."
Tim thought for a moment and said, "I can help you! I will count the leaves for you, so you can know how many are falling."
As Tim counted the leaves, the old man smiled. He was happy to know the number of leaves falling. They both laughed and enjoyed the evening together.
The moral of the story is to always be kind and help others when they need it.

"Look, a snake!" Tim says.
"Let's run away!" Sue says.
But the snake is not mean. It is friendly. It wants to meet them. It says, "Hello, kids. I am Whip. I am a green snake. Do you want to play with me?"
Tim and Sue stop. They look at Whip. He has a long body and a small head. He has no legs or arms. He can move fast on the ground.
"Hello, Whip. I am Tim. This is Sue. We are kids. We like to play in the park. How do you play?" Tim asks.
"I like to slide and curl and twist. I can make shapes with my body. Do you want to see?" Whip says.
"Yes, please!" Sue says.
Whip shows them how he can make a circle, a spiral, a loop, and a heart. Tim and Sue clap and laugh. They think Whip is fun.
"Can we try to make shapes too?" Tim asks.
"Sure, you can. But you have to be careful. Don't step on me or hurt me. I am gentle and kind. I don't bite or hurt you. Can you be gentle and kind too?" Whip says.
"Yes, we can. We are gentle and kind. We don't hurt or bite you. We are friends." Sue says.
Tim and Sue try to make shapes with their bodies. They slide and curl and twist. They have fun with Whip. They learn that Whip is not scary. He is different, but he is nice. They learn to be brave and friendly. They learn to respect and enjoy the snake. They are happy.
The end.

But they did not agree on how to play. Lily wanted to make a long track that went around the room. Ben wanted to make a short track that went up and down a hill. They started to argue and pull the train and the tracks. "I want this piece!" Lily said. "No, I want it!" Ben said. They did not share.
Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw the train and the tracks in pieces on the floor. She saw Lily and Ben crying and angry. She said, "What happened? Why are you not sharing the train?"
Lily and Ben told her their problem. She said, "You both have good ideas, but you have to compromise. Why don't you take turns? Lily, you can make a long track first, and Ben, you can play with the train. Then, you can switch. You can also measure the track with a ruler. Each of you can have the same number of inches. That way, it is fair."
Lily and Ben thought that was a good idea. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They got the ruler and measured the track. They each got 12 inches. They shared the train and the tracks. They had fun playing together. They learned to share.

The cat didn't understand, but he wanted to be happy. So, he listened to the owl and tried to value his tight skin. As he did this, something unexpected happened. The cat's tight skin began to change. It became soft and loose like the other cats. The cat was so happy that he could play with his friends again.
But then, the cat realized that his tight skin had made him special. He missed being unique, and now he was just like everyone else. With a wave of his wing, the owl gave the cat his tight skin back.
From that day on, the cat was proud of his tight skin. He learned that being different was a good thing, and he was happy to be unique. The cat played with his friends, and they all loved him just the way he was.

"Of course, we are friends!" Bunny said.

"I saw it first!" Bunny said.
"No, I did!" Squirrel said.

"Hop, hop, hop!" Bunny said.
"Hop, hop, hop!" Squirrel said.
They were very competitive. They did not want to give up the cookie. They hopped faster and faster, but they could not catch it.
Then, they heard a loud voice.
"Hey, what are you doing with my treats?" It was Bear, who had left the basket there for his picnic.
Bunny and Squirrel were scared. They stopped hopping and looked at Bear.
"Sorry, Mr. Bear, we did not know they were yours!" Bunny said.
"We just wanted one cookie!" Squirrel said.
Bear was angry. He growled and showed his teeth.
"Those are my treats, and you can't have any! Go away, or I will eat you!"
Bunny and Squirrel ran away as fast as they could. They did not want to be Bear's treat.
They learned a lesson that day. They should not be greedy and competitive. They should be happy with what they have and share with their friends. And they should never take treats from a bear!

One day, they saw the snake sunning on a rock. It was long and green and had black spots. Lila thought it was pretty. She wanted to touch it. She said to Tom, "Look at the snake. It is so graceful. I want to pet it."
Tom said, "No, Lila. Don't do that. The snake might bite you. It is not a toy. It is a wild animal. We should leave it alone."
But Lila did not listen to Tom. She walked slowly towards the rock. She reached out her hand to touch the snake. The snake saw her and hissed. It was angry. It coiled up and got ready to strike.
Tom shouted, "Lila, stop! Come back!" But it was too late. The snake lunged at Lila and bit her on the arm. Lila screamed and fell to the ground. The snake quickly dived back into the water and disappeared.
Tom ran to Lila and saw blood on her arm. He was scared. He did not know what to do. He cried for help. He hoped someone would hear him and come to save Lila. He hoped Lila would be okay. He wished he had stopped her from touching the snake. He wished they had never played by the pond.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She loved to watch the stars shining bright in the night sky. Every night she would look out of her window and smile. One night she noticed something different. The stars seemed to be connected in a big, sparkling network in the night sky. 
Lucy went outside to get a closer look. Suddenly, a voice spoke to her. It was the biggest star in the sky!
“What’s your name?” asked the star.
“My name is Lucy.” she replied.
“Do you want to join our network?”
 
Lucy thought for a moment and nodded. The star and all the other stars started to shine brighter and brighter. 
“Come with us and you’ll always be able to see our lights” said the star. 
Lucy smiled and followed the stars. They flew through the night sky, the stars shining brightly and the wind blowing heavy. 
And that is how Lucy became part of the star’s network. Every night she looks up and smiles, for she is surrounded by beautiful, shining stars that are always there for her.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. They saw a big dog with brown fur and a long tail. The dog was friendly and wagged its tail. Anna and Ben wanted to pet the dog.
"Hello, doggy!" Anna said. She reached out her hand to touch the dog's head. The dog licked her hand and made a happy sound.
"Can I pet him too?" Ben asked. He moved closer to the dog. The dog sniffed him and licked his face. Ben giggled and rubbed the dog's ear.
The dog's owner came over. He was a man with a hat and a beard. He smiled and said, "Hi, kids. This is Bruno. He likes to play with you."
"Hi, mister. Bruno is nice. Can we play with him some more?" Anna asked.
"Sure, you can. But be careful, he is very smelly. He rolled in some mud and garbage. He needs a bath." The man said.
Anna and Ben smelled the dog. He was very smelly. They wrinkled their noses and said, "Eww, Bruno. You are stinky."
The man laughed and said, "Don't worry, I will take him home and wash him. Then he will be clean and fresh. Do you want to come with me and help me?"
Anna and Ben looked at each other. They liked Bruno, but they did not like his smell. They shook their heads and said, "No, thank you. We have to go home soon. Our mom will be here."
"OK, then. Maybe next time. Say bye to Bruno." The man said.
Anna and Ben hugged the dog and said, "Bye, Bruno. We had fun with you. See you later."
The dog barked and wagged his tail. He jumped on the man's shoulder and licked his ear. The man said, "Ouch, Bruno. You are too heavy. Get down."
Anna and Ben waved and ran to their mom. She was waiting for them at the gate. She hugged them and said, "Did you have a good time?"
"Yes, mom. We played with a dog. His name was Bruno. He was friendly, but very smelly." Anna said.
"We petted him and he licked us. He was funny, but he needed a bath." Ben said.
"Really? That sounds like an adventure. Do you remember what he looked like?" Mom asked.
Anna and Ben nodded and described the dog. They told mom about his brown fur, his long tail, his big eyes and his wet nose. They also told her about his owner, his hat and his beard.
Mom listened and smiled. She said, "You have a good memory. I'm proud of you. Now let's go home and wash your hands. You don't want to be smelly like Bruno, do you?"
Anna and Ben shook their heads and said, "No, mom. We want to be clean and fresh."
They got in the car and drove home. They still remembered Bruno and hoped to see him again. They wondered if he was clean and fresh now. They hoped he was happy.

The man and the wife were very happy and thanked the big bird. They went home and continued to feed the birds with their new seeds.

The white bird was happy and thanked the old tree. The moral of the story is that we should accept and love everyone, no matter how different they are.

"Mum, why do I need to wipe my hands?" asked the 3 year old, looking curiously up at his mother.
His mother smiled and said, "To keep them clean and germ-free." She then took out a rubber and handed it to him. The 3 year old took it and examined it.
"What does this do?" he asked.
"It's a special rubber for wiping your hands," replied his mother. "It'll make sure your hands are nice and clean."
The 3 year old began to rub his hands with the rubber and then smelled them. "Ugh, that's sour!" he said, scrunching up his face in distaste.
"Yes," his mother replied, "it has a bit of a sour smell, so you know it's doing its job. But don't worry, it'll go away soon."
The 3 year old nodded and continued to wipe his hands until they were completely clean.
"There," said his mother, "all done!"
The 3 year old smiled. He felt much better now that his hands were clean and germ-free.

Ben and Mia are playing with their toy cars in the garden. They make noises like vroom and beep as they drive them on the grass and the dirt. They pretend they are going on a long trip to see the animals at the zoo.
"Look, there is a lion!" Mia says, pointing to a yellow car with a mane. "He is very big and loud. Roar!"
"And there is a giraffe!" Ben says, showing a tall car with a long neck. "He is very tall and quiet. Munch!"
They have fun with their cars, but soon they get dirty. The wheels are covered with mud and the paint is scratched. The cars look sad and tired.
"Oh no, our cars need to be clean!" Mia says. "They are dirty and they need fuel. How can we help them?"
"I know!" Ben says. "We can use the hose and the bucket. We can wash them with water and soap. And we can use the juice boxes as fuel. They are sweet and yummy. Come on, let's go!"
They run to the hose and the bucket. They fill the bucket with water and add some soap. They use a sponge to scrub their cars gently. They rinse them with the hose and dry them with a towel. They look shiny and happy.
"Wow, our cars are clean!" Mia says. "They are bright and smooth. They look like new!"
"Now they need fuel!" Ben says. "We can use these juice boxes. They are deep and full. They have apple and orange and grape. What do you want?"
"I want apple!" Mia says. "It is green and sour. I like it!"
"I want orange!" Ben says. "It is orange and sweet. I like it!"
They open the juice boxes and pour some into their cars. They pretend the cars are drinking and making happy noises. They save some juice for themselves and drink it too. They feel refreshed and energized.
"Yay, our cars have fuel!" Mia says. "They are ready to go. They can go fast and far. Where do you want to go?"
"Let's go to the beach!" Ben says. "We can see the water and the sand. We can make castles and waves. It will be fun!"
"OK, let's go!" Mia says. "But first, we have to clean up. We have to put the hose and the bucket and the sponge and the towel and the juice boxes away. We have to be tidy and good."
"OK, let's do that!" Ben says. "We have to be careful and polite. We have to thank Mom and Dad for letting us play. We have to be happy and nice."
They clean up their mess and put everything away. They take their cars and go to the beach. They have a wonderful time. They are clean and they have fuel. They are deep and they are friends. They are Ben and Mia.

Willow the deer calmly walked into the dark woods. Suddenly, she started to tremble. It was poison ivy! Willow's graceful legs felt powerless and she stumbled. 
"Help!", she called. Out of the shadows, came a small mouse.
"What's wrong?", the mouse asked.
Willow gasped, her voice trembling. "Poison ivy!"
The mouse smiled confidently. "Don't worry," he said. "I know how to help you." He quickly showed Willow a graceful patch of clover. 
Willow smiled in relief. "Thank you," she said. 
The mouse nodded. "Anytime."
Willow was so grateful. She thanked the mouse again, and the pair shook hands. Together, they walked out of the dark woods.

Sara and Ben liked to play with chalk on the sidewalk. They had many colors of chalk, but their favorite was blue. They used blue chalk to draw the sky, the sea, and their names.
One day, they found a new chalk in their box. It was dull and gray, and it did not look fun. Sara and Ben did not want to use it, so they left it alone.
"Let's draw a big sun with yellow chalk," Sara said.
"OK, and I will draw some clouds with white chalk," Ben said.
They started to draw, but soon they heard a loud noise. It was a big truck, and it was coming fast. The truck did not see Sara and Ben, or their chalk drawings. It was going to run over them!
Sara and Ben were scared, and they did not know what to do. They looked around, and saw the dull gray chalk. They had an idea.
"Use the dull chalk!" Sara shouted.
They grabbed the dull chalk, and quickly drew a big stop sign on the sidewalk. The truck saw the stop sign, and stopped just in time. Sara and Ben were safe.
The truck driver got out, and apologized to Sara and Ben. He said he was sorry for almost hitting them, and he thanked them for drawing the stop sign.
"That was very smart of you," he said. "Where did you get that chalk?"
Sara and Ben showed him the dull gray chalk. They were surprised to see that it was not dull anymore. It was shiny and silver, and it sparkled in the sun.
"It's magic chalk!" Sara said.
"Wow, that's amazing!" Ben said.
They smiled, and decided to use the magic chalk to draw more things on the sidewalk. They had a lot of fun, and they never forgot the day they used the dull chalk to save their lives.

So one day, he started swimming as fast as he could towards the reef. He swam and swam until finally he had almost reached his goal. He was almost within touching distance of the reef, when a massive wave came crashing in.
The wave was so big and so strong, that the fish could not fight it. He was washed backwards, away from the reef. He struggled and tried to stay afloat, but eventually he had to give up. He sank down, away from his dream. 
The chubby fish never reached the reef. He did not succeed in his mission.

One day, Ben and his mom went to the store. They wanted to buy some food and toys. Ben liked the store. He saw many things he wanted. He saw a big ball, a red car, a soft bear and a book with pictures.
"Can I have this, mom?" Ben asked, holding the ball.
"Not today, Ben. We have enough toys at home. Let's go and pay for our food," his mom said.
Ben was sad. He wanted the ball. He put it back on the shelf. He followed his mom to the line. He saw a man with a big bag. The bag had a picture of a wave on it. Ben liked the wave. He liked the water. He wanted to go to the beach.
"Can we go to the beach, mom?" Ben asked.
"Maybe tomorrow, Ben. It's too late today. The sun is going down. The water is deep and cold. We have to go home and eat dinner," his mom said.
Ben was sad. He wanted to go to the beach. He wanted to play with the wave. He looked at the bag. He had an idea. He reached for the bag. He wanted to take it. He thought the bag had a wave inside.
"Hey, kid, what are you doing?" the man said, pulling the bag away from Ben.
Ben was scared. He let go of the bag. He ran to his mom. He hugged her leg. He cried.
"I'm sorry, mom. I wanted the wave," Ben said.
"It's okay, Ben. The wave is not in the bag. The bag is just a picture. The wave is at the beach. We can go there tomorrow. But you can't take things that are not yours. That's not nice. You have to say sorry to the man," his mom said.
Ben looked at the man. The man looked angry. Ben was sorry. He wiped his tears. He walked to the man. He said sorry.
"I'm sorry, sir. I wanted the wave," Ben said.
The man looked at Ben. He saw his sad face. He felt sorry for him. He smiled.
"It's okay, kid. I understand. The wave is cool. But you can't have it in a bag. You have to go to the beach. Here, take this," the man said, giving Ben a sticker with a wave on it.
Ben smiled. He took the sticker. He said thank you. He put the sticker on his shirt. He was happy. He had a wave. He showed it to his mom.
"Look, mom. I have a wave," Ben said.
"That's nice, Ben. I'm proud of you. You said sorry and thank you. You are a good boy. Let's go home and eat dinner. Tomorrow we can go to the beach and see the real wave," his mom said.
Ben nodded. He held his mom's hand. They left the store. They went home. Ben was happy. He had a wave. He dreamed of the beach.

Molly and Jake were playing in the park. Molly was laughing and smiling while Jake was being really rude. Jake was pushing Molly around and not sharing his toys. Molly was getting really upset. 
Then Molly saw an ice cream van and became excited. She ran over to it and asked for an ice cream. The ice cream man was very polite and gave her a cone. Molly took the cone and went to sit on the bench. 
But when she sat down, the ice cream started to melt. Instead of getting angry, Molly smiled. She took out a book from her pocket and used it to fan the ice cream. In just seconds, the cone was back to its original shape. 
Jake was amazed. He asked Molly how she managed to fix the ice cream and Molly replied with a smile, " Kindness can fix anything, even if it's really rude!" 
Molly's kindness triumphs over Jake's rudeness and teaches us all an important moral: Kindness is more powerful than anything else.

But the other team scored four goals and won the game. Tim was very sad and angry. He said, "It's not fair! They cheated! They had an ugly player who pushed me and kicked me!" Sam was sad too, but he said, "It's okay, Tim. They played well and we tried our best. Maybe next time we will win."

The ugly player smiled and said, "Sure, I'm Ben. You are very nice and a good player. I'm sorry I pushed you and kicked you. I was just trying to win."
Sam and Ben played together and had fun. They became friends and learned to share and respect each other. Tim saw them and felt sorry. He realized he was wrong and rude. He went to them and said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I'm sorry, Ben. Can I play with you too?" Sam and Ben nodded and said, "Of course, Tim. You are welcome. We are all friends."
The moral of the story is: Don't judge people by their looks. Be kind and humble. Friendship is more important than winning.

The bear and his friends laughed and played together in the circle. When they were tired, they jumped up and weighed themselves on the scale again. It was just as much fun as before! 
The bear and his friends had so much fun weighing themselves and playing in the circle that they wanted to do it again and again. And that is what they did, over and over again!

"No, I want the red crayon!" Ben says. "I want to draw a car."
They pull and tug on the red crayon. The crayon breaks in half. Anna and Ben cry.
Mom hears them and comes to their room. She sees the broken crayon and the sad twins.
"What happened?" Mom asks.
"We both wanted the red crayon," Anna says.
"But it broke," Ben says.
Mom hugs them and says, "I'm sorry, my loves. How about we share the crayon? You can each have a half and draw on a paper."
Anna and Ben nod. They wipe their tears and smile. They take their half of the crayon and a paper. They start to draw.
But then, they see a big white wall in their room. They think the wall is boring. They want to make the wall pretty.
They look at each other and have an idea. They run to the wall with their crayon halves. They start to draw on the wall.
They draw flowers and cars and stars and hearts. They make the wall red and colorful. They are happy.
But Mom is not happy. She comes back to their room and sees the wall. She gasps.
"Anna! Ben! What did you do?" Mom says. "You can't draw on the wall! That's naughty!"
Anna and Ben stop drawing. They look at Mom and the wall. They feel bad.
"We're sorry, Mom," Anna says.
"We wanted to make the wall pretty," Ben says.
Mom sighs. She says, "I know you wanted to make the wall pretty, but you can't use crayons on the wall. You can only use crayons on paper. You have to clean the wall now."
Anna and Ben nod. They say, "OK, Mom."
Mom gives them a cloth and some water. They rub the cloth on the wall. They try to erase the crayon marks. They work hard.
Mom watches them and says, "Thank you, my loves. Next time, please ask me before you draw on the wall. And remember to share your crayons."
Anna and Ben say, "Yes, Mom. We love you."
They hug Mom and give her their crayon halves. They say, "We don't need the red crayon anymore. We have each other."

The little fox saw a window nearby, so he decided to take shelter from the rain. As he tried to open the window, it suddenly broke.
He was scared and ran away before anyone noticed him. But his tail was still caught in the window.
When he eventually stopped running, he sat down to think about what he had done. He knew he should not have broken the window and he was sorry for his mistake.
Then, an old owl came to him and said: "It is important to be careful and think twice before you act. That way, you will always make the right decisions. That is the lesson of today."
The little fox was happy that he learnt something useful, thanked the owl and went home to his family. From then on, he was much more careful and never broke anything again.

Spot tried to turn the knob, but it was too high for him. Fluffy jumped up and turned the knob. The door opened, and they went in.
Inside, they saw a big bed. Spot said, "I am tired. Let's lay down and sleep." Fluffy said, "Okay." They lay down on the bed and closed their eyes. They slept for a while. When they woke up, they saw a big bird sitting on the bed. The bird was deaf and could not hear them.
Spot and Fluffy tried to talk to the bird, but the bird did not hear them. They were sad. Then, Spot had an idea. He said, "Let's dance!" They danced and jumped around the bird. The bird saw them and started to dance too. They all had fun dancing together. Then, they went back outside and played in the sun. The bird became their new friend, and they were all very happy.

"Tom, I'm sorry. The dove was not a toy. It was a living thing. It had feelings. It did not like to be tied. It wanted to fly and be happy. You should not chase it. You should let it go."
Tom sniffed. He nodded. He understood. He said sorry too.
"Lila, I'm sorry. I was silly. I did not think. I wanted the ribbon. I did not care about the dove. I should not grab it. I should be gentle and kind."
Lila smiled. She gave Tom the piece of ribbon. She said it was a gift.
"Tom, this is for you. It is a reminder. A reminder to be nice to animals. A reminder to respect their freedom. A reminder to love them from afar."
Tom smiled too. He thanked Lila. He said it was a good gift. He said he learned a lesson.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big hill with white powder on top. They wanted to touch it.
"Let's go to the hill!" Lily said.
"OK!" Ben said.
They ran to the hill and grabbed some powder. It was cold and soft. They made balls with it and threw them at each other. They laughed and had fun.
But then they heard a loud noise. It was a big truck. It came to the hill and dumped more powder on it. The powder covered Lily and Ben.
"Help!" Lily shouted.
"Help!" Ben shouted.
They tried to get out of the powder, but it was too much. They were scared.
Then they saw a man. He was wearing a hat and a coat. He had a shovel. He was the truck driver. He saw Lily and Ben in the powder. He was surprised.
"Hey, what are you doing here?" he asked.
"We were playing!" Lily said.
"With the powder?" he asked.
"Yes!" Ben said.
The man smiled. He put down his shovel and helped Lily and Ben out of the powder. He brushed them off and gave them a hug.
"This is not a toy, kids. This is salt. I use it to melt the ice on the roads. It is not good for you. It can hurt your eyes and skin. You should not play with it," he said.
"Sorry, mister. We did not know. It looked like snow," Lily said.
"It's OK. I'm glad you are safe. But next time, stay away from the mysterious powder, OK?" he said.
"OK!" Lily and Ben said.
They thanked the man and ran back to their mom. They told her what happened. She was happy they were OK. She gave them a kiss and a cookie. They learned their lesson. They never played with the mysterious powder again.

They skipped to the tree and reached for the peaches. They were juicy and sweet. They ate some and put some in their pockets.
Suddenly, they heard a loud voice. It was Mr. Lee. He was angry and came to the tree.
"Hey, you two! Stop stealing my peaches! Go away or I will call your parents!" he shouted.
Sara and Tom were scared and ran away. They dropped some peaches on the ground. They felt bad for taking Mr. Lee's peaches without asking.
They went to their homes and told their parents what they did. Their parents were not happy and made them go back to Mr. Lee's house and say sorry.
They knocked on Mr. Lee's door and apologized for taking his peaches. They gave him the peaches they had left in their pockets.
Mr. Lee was surprised and smiled. He thanked them for being honest and gave them each a peach.
"Next time, if you want some peaches, just ask me nicely. I have plenty to share. But you have to respect my property and not take things without permission," he said.
Sara and Tom nodded and thanked him. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to be respectful and not to steal. They also learned that saying sorry can make things better. They became friends with Mr. Lee and sometimes he let them pick some peaches from his tree. They always asked him first and shared with him. They enjoyed the bright peaches and the bright friendship.

Tim and Mia are sad. They look at the broken red automobile. They start to cry. They say, "We are sorry. We broke the red automobile. We love the red automobile. We should not fight."
Mom hears them crying. She comes to the living room. She sees the broken red automobile. She says, "What happened? Why are you crying?"
Tim and Mia tell Mom what happened. They say, "We were playing with the red automobile. We wanted to drive it. We fought. We broke it. We are sorry."
Mom says, "I see. It is not nice to fight. You should share your toys. You should say sorry to each other. You should hug and make up."

Tim and Mia are happy. They smile and clap. They say, "Hooray! The red automobile is fixed. It is a great automobile. We will play with it nicely. We will take turns to drive it. We will have fun."
Mom says, "That is wonderful. I am happy for you. You are good twins. You are good drivers. You are good friends. You are good children."
They hug Mom. They say, "Thank you, Mom. You are good too. You are a good mom. You are a good fixer. You are a good friend. You are a good person."

"Can we eat it now, Mom?" Ben asks.
"No, Ben. We need to bake it first. Then we can eat it," Mom says. She helps Ben and Sara to make small balls of dough and put them on a tray. She puts the tray in the oven and sets the timer.
"Let's wait for the cookies to bake. We can read a book or play a game while we wait," Mom says. She hugs Ben and Sara and smiles. They love to bake with Mom. They love Mom. Mom loves them.

Molly put away the old pipe and followed her mum inside. She felt a bit better knowing that if she ever wants to complain she can always use the pipe.

Anna and Ben are playing with their toys in the living room. Anna has a flexible snake that can bend and twist. Ben has a cup that he likes to fill with water and pour out. They are having fun, but they also want to try each other's toys.
"Can I play with your snake, Anna?" Ben asks.
"OK, but be careful. It is flexible, but it can break if you pull too hard," Anna says.
"Can I play with your cup, Anna?" Anna asks.
"OK, but be careful. It is not flexible, and it can spill if you tilt too much," Ben says.
They swap their toys and start to play. Anna bends and twists the snake, making it look like different animals. Ben fills and pours the cup, making it sound like rain. They are happy, but they also want to see what happens if they do what the other said not to do.
Anna pulls the snake very hard, trying to make it longer. Ben tilts the cup very much, trying to make a big splash. Suddenly, they hear a snap and a splash. The snake breaks in two, and the water spills on the floor.
"Oh no! I broke your snake, Ben! I'm sorry!" Anna cries.
"Oh no! I spilled your water, Anna! I'm sorry!" Ben cries.
They look at each other and feel sad. They don't want to hurt each other's toys. They don't want to make a mess. They don't want to be in trouble.
They hug each other and say, "It's OK. I forgive you. Let's fix it."
They get some tape and stick the snake back together. They get some paper towels and wipe the water off the floor. They give each other their toys back and say, "Thank you. I love you. Let's play nicely."
They smile and play with their toys again. They are careful not to pull too hard or tilt too much. They are happy and proud. They are good friends.

Tim took a small bite of the spaghetti. Suddenly, the spaghetti started to move! It was not just spaghetti, it was a spaghetti monster! The monster jumped off the plate and ran away.
Tim and his mom tried to catch the spaghetti monster, but it was too fast. The spaghetti monster ran out the door and was gone. Tim and his mom were sad because they could not eat dinner.

"Look at the dog, Lily! He has a hat!" Ben said.
"Can we pet him, Ben? He looks nice!" Lily said.
They ran to the dog and tried to touch him. But the dog did not like that. He barked and growled and showed his teeth. He did not want Ben and Lily to touch his hat.
"Go away, kids! This is my hat!" The dog yelled.
Ben and Lily were scared. They did not know the dog could talk. They ran away from the dog. But the dog was faster. He chased them and bit them. He bit Ben's leg and Lily's arm. They cried and screamed.
"Help, help! The dog is biting us!" They yelled.
But no one heard them. No one was in the park. The dog was mean and angry. He did not stop biting them. He hurt them a lot. Ben and Lily wished they never saw the dog with the unusual hat. They wished they stayed away from him. They wished someone would help them. But no one did. The dog bit them until they stopped yelling. The dog was happy. He had his hat and no one to bother him. He licked his teeth and lay down on the grass. Ben and Lily were still and quiet. They did not play anymore.

The next day, the sun was shining bright and the flower tried very hard to bloom. It pushed and pushed, and finally, it bloomed! The flower was incredible and everyone in the town was happy. The little girl and the flower became best friends.

By the time Tommy left the hill, the sun was setting and it was time to go home. Seeing the hill all clean and peaceful made Tommy smile. He promised himself he would come back to explore the hill again soon.

Once upon a time, there were two neighbors - Danny and Bobby. They liked to play together in the park. One day, Bobby had a silly idea. He wanted to see if he could mix some mud from the earth into the pond water. "Let's try it!" said Danny.
So, Bobby got some mud and started mixing it into the pond. Then, he put some leaves in too. They watched as the thin layer of mud spread into the pond water. It looked funny!
Suddenly a voice said, "Hey, what do you think you're doing?" It was Ms. Miller, their neighbor. She looked upset.
"We were just mixing the mud into the pond," said Danny.
Ms. Miller sighed and said, "That's not very nice. It won't be safe for the fish. Please be kind to nature and don't do this again."
Danny and Bobby felt embarrassed and apologized. After that, they always made sure to be kind to nature and take care of the pond.
The moral of this story is to always be kind to nature and never try to mix things together if it might be dangerous.

One day, a king was very sad. His wife was dead and he had no friends. He only had a big crown and a big chair. He did not like to talk or play with anyone.
A little boy lived near the king's castle. He liked to run and jump and laugh. He had a red ball that he loved very much. He threw the ball high in the air and caught it with his hands.
One day, the boy threw the ball too high. It flew over the wall and into the castle. The boy ran to the gate and asked the guard to let him in. He wanted his ball back. The guard said no. The king did not like visitors.
The boy was sad. He did not want to lose his ball. He looked around and saw a big vine. The vine grew on the wall and reached the top. The boy had an idea. He climbed the vine and jumped over the wall. He landed in the castle garden.
He saw his ball near a big fountain. He ran to get it. But he also saw the king. The king was sitting on his big chair near the fountain. He was holding his big crown. He looked very sad.
The boy was scared. He did not want the king to see him. He grabbed his ball and tried to run away. But the ball was stuck. The king's crown had a hook on it. The hook had caught the ball. The boy had to pull hard to free his ball.
The king heard the noise. He looked up and saw the boy. He saw the boy pulling his crown. He saw the boy's red ball. He saw the boy's happy face. He felt something in his heart. He felt curious.
He asked the boy, "Who are you? What are you doing here?"
The boy was surprised. He thought the king would be angry. He said, "I'm sorry, sir. I'm Tom. I came to get my ball. It flew over the wall. I did not mean to pull your crown."
The king smiled. He said, "That's okay, Tom. I like your ball. It's very red. Can I see it?"
The boy nodded. He gave the ball to the king. The king held the ball and felt its roundness. He threw the ball in the air and caught it with his hands. He laughed.
The boy laughed too. He said, "Do you want to play with me, sir?"
The king nodded. He said, "Yes, Tom. I do. I have not played for a long time. You are my first friend."
The boy and the king played with the ball. They ran and jumped and laughed. They forgot about the wall and the guard and the fountain. They only saw each other.
They were happy.

Tom was very tired. He had played all day with his toys and his friends. He wanted to go to bed, but his mom said he had to eat dinner first. She made him a plate of noodles and cheese, his favorite food. But Tom was too sleepy to eat. He yawned and pushed his plate away.
"Come on, Tom, you have to eat something," his mom said. "You need energy for tomorrow. We are going to the zoo!"
Tom liked the zoo. He wanted to see the lions and the monkeys and the elephants. He remembered the last time he went to the zoo, he saw a big metal cage with a sign that said "Coming Soon". He wondered what animal was inside. Maybe a dinosaur or a dragon or a unicorn. He wanted to find out.
He decided to eat a little bit of his dinner, so he could go to the zoo tomorrow. He picked up his fork and took a bite of his noodles. They were warm and cheesy and yummy. He took another bite, and another, and soon his plate was empty. He drank his milk and wiped his mouth.
"Good boy, Tom," his mom said. "Now you can go to bed. I'll read you a story if you want."
Tom nodded and followed his mom to his room. He put on his pajamas and climbed into his bed. His mom tucked him in and gave him a kiss. She picked up a book from his shelf and opened it.
"Let's see, what story do you want to hear tonight?" she asked. "How about this one? It's called 'The Metal Monster'."
Tom's eyes widened. He recognized the book. It was the same one he saw at the zoo, next to the metal cage. He wondered if the book was about the animal that was coming soon. He wanted to hear the story, but he was also a little scared.
"Mom, what is the metal monster?" he asked.
His mom smiled and said, "You'll have to listen and find out. But don't worry, it's not a scary story. It's a funny story. You'll like it."
She began to read the book, and Tom listened. He heard about a metal monster that was not really a monster, but a robot. A robot that escaped from a factory and went to the zoo, looking for a friend. A robot that met a lot of animals, but none of them wanted to play with him. A robot that was lonely and sad, until he found a metal cage with a sign that said "Coming Soon".
Tom felt sorry for the robot. He hoped he would find a friend in the metal cage. He wondered who or what was inside. He yawned and closed his eyes. He fell asleep, dreaming of the zoo and the metal monster and the coming soon animal. He hoped they would be available tomorrow. He hoped they would be happy.

Tim's car is fast and goes ahead of Sam's car. Sam tries to catch up, but his car is slower. He sees a bridge made of books and thinks of a plan. He grabs a string and ties it to his car. He throws the other end of the string over the bridge and pulls it hard.
Tim's car is about to cross the bridge when the string pulls Sam's car up. Sam's car hits Tim's car and they both fall off the bridge. They make a loud noise and a big wreck. The cars are broken and the books are scattered.
Tim is angry and sad. He says, "Sam, that was not fair! You cheated! You wrecked my car and the bridge!" Sam is sorry and ashamed. He says, "I'm sorry, Tim. I wanted to win, but I did a bad thing. I should not have tied the string to my car. Can you forgive me?"
Tim looks at Sam and sees his blue car. He remembers that they are friends. He says, "I forgive you, Sam. But you have to promise not to cheat again. And we have to fix the cars and the bridge." Sam nods and says, "I promise, Tim. And I will help you fix them." They hug and smile. They are friends again.

Buddy smiled and said, "Now you can play with the numbers and learn them too!" Lily, her mom, and Buddy spent the rest of the day playing with the big numbers in the library. And that's how Lily learned her big numbers in a very special way.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play in the attic. The attic was a wide space with many old things. They could find toys, books, clothes and more. Sometimes they pretended to be pirates, or knights, or fairies.
One day, they found a big box with a lock. They wondered what was inside. They tried to open it, but it was too hard. They looked for a key, but they could not find one.
"Maybe we can break the lock," Ben said. He picked up a hammer and hit the lock. But it only made a loud noise.
"Stop, Ben!" Sara said. "You will break the box too. And maybe someone will hear us and get angry."
"Who cares?" Ben said. "This is our attic. We can do what we want."
Sara shook her head. "No, Ben. This is not our attic. This is Grandma's attic. She lets us play here, but we have to be careful. She loves these old things. They provide her with memories of Grandpa and her parents and her friends. They are very important to her. We should respect them and not damage them."
Ben looked at Sara. He felt sorry. He put down the hammer. "You are right, Sara. I was wrong. I don't want to hurt Grandma's feelings. I'm sorry."
Sara smiled. She hugged Ben. "It's okay, Ben. I'm sorry too. I know you were curious. Maybe we can ask Grandma about the box. Maybe she will tell us a story about it. Or maybe she will let us open it with her."
They decided to leave the box alone and play with something else. They had fun in the attic, but they also learned to be grateful and respectful. They knew that Grandma provided them with a special place to play, but also with love and wisdom. They loved Grandma very much.

One day, a farmer was working in his field. He had many cows and sheep and chickens. He liked to take care of them and give them food and water. He also had a big red barn where he kept his tools and hay.
But the farmer had a problem. There was a naughty fox who lived in the woods near his farm. The fox liked to sneak into the barn at night and eat the eggs and the hay. The farmer was very angry with the fox. He tried to catch him many times, but the fox was too fast and clever.
One night, the farmer had a plan. He put a trap in the barn, with a big piece of cheese as bait. He hoped the fox would smell the cheese and come inside. Then the trap would close and the fox would be stuck.
The next morning, the farmer went to the barn to check his trap. He opened the door and looked inside. He saw the trap was closed, but there was no fox. Instead, he saw a small mouse, nibbling on the cheese. The mouse looked up and saw the farmer. He squeaked and tried to run away, but he could not.
"Hello, little mouse," the farmer said. "Did you eat my cheese?"
"Yes, I did," the mouse said. "I was very hungry. I'm sorry, Mr. Farmer. Please don't hurt me."
The farmer felt sorry for the mouse. He knew the mouse was not the one who stole his eggs and hay. He opened the trap and let the mouse go.
"Go on, little mouse," the farmer said. "But don't come back to my barn. There is a naughty fox who might eat you."
"Thank you, Mr. Farmer," the mouse said. "You are very kind. I will stay away from the barn and the fox."
The farmer smiled and waved goodbye to the mouse. He hoped the fox would stay away too. He went back to his field and his animals. He was not angry anymore. He was happy.

One day, he found an acorn and knew right away that it would be a good snack! He put the acorn into his pocket and ran off in search of a dry place to eat it.
The intelligent squirrel looked to the left and right and finally found a spot under the big tree. He sat down and started to nibble on the acorn.
Just then, a little rabbit hopped up and asked him, "What are you doing?"
The squirrel looked up and said, "I'm eating a dry acorn. Want some?"
The bunny said, "Yes please!"
The squirrel happily shared his snack and the two animals laughed and chatted as they ate.

Sara and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to spin on the merry-go-round. Sara had a new cap that her mom gave her. It was red and had a big star on it. She was very proud of her cap.
"Look at my cap, Tom!" Sara said. "It is so pretty and shiny!"
Tom looked at Sara's cap. He felt jealous. He wanted a cap like that. He had an old cap that was brown and had a hole in it. He was ashamed of his cap.
"Your cap is not that great," Tom said. "It is too bright and silly. My cap is better. It is cool and tough."
Sara felt hurt by Tom's words. She loved her cap. She thought Tom was her friend. She did not want to play with him anymore.
"Fine, then. You can keep your old cap. I don't care. I will spin by myself," Sara said. She got on the merry-go-round and started to spin.
Tom felt angry. He wanted to make Sara feel bad. He had a mean idea. He waited until Sara was spinning fast. Then he ran to the merry-go-round and grabbed Sara's cap. He pulled it off her head and threw it in the air.
"Ha ha! Now you have no cap!" Tom said. He laughed and ran away.
Sara felt a gust of wind. She saw her cap flying away. She tried to reach for it, but it was too late. Her cap landed on a big tree. She could not get it back. She felt very sad and cried.
"Mommy! Mommy! Tom took my cap and threw it on the tree!" Sara said. She ran to her mom who was sitting on a bench.
Her mom hugged her and tried to comfort her. She was angry at Tom for being so mean. She looked at the tree and saw Sara's cap. It was too high and too far. She could not get it down.
"I'm sorry, Sara. Your cap is gone. We can't get it back. Tom was very naughty. He should not have done that. He should say sorry to you," her mom said.
Sara sniffled and nodded. She wished she had her cap back. She wished Tom was nice to her. She wished she had a happy ending. But she did not. She had a bad ending.

One day, Tim's mom told him that he could not play with his toys or do his favorite math games until he took a bath. Tim was very sad, but he still did not want to take a bath. That night, Tim went to bed dirty and shivering because he was so cold.

From that day on, Tim learned that taking a bath was important. He did not want to be filthy and shiver anymore. The moral of the story is that sometimes we have to do things we don't like to be happy and healthy.

Once there was a little frog who lived in a swamp. The frog was so small that it only came up to the swamp's edge. But this didn't stop it from dreaming big.
One day, the frog decided to take a big adventure and travel further away from the swamp. It started hopping and hopping, far away from its home.
 
After a while, the frog met an old turtle. "Where are you headed?" the turtle asked.
 
The frog smiled. "I want to be successful!" it said proudly.
The turtle smiled back. "Success can be a difficult thing to complete," it said. "But I know a place where you will find success."
 
The frog thanked the turtle. Then it hopped right away, eager to find this place of success.
Finally, the little frog reached a beautiful garden. Slowly it made its way through the garden and, right in the middle, it found the success it was looking for! The frog had completed the journey, and could finally rest.

One day, Tom and Anna were playing in the park. They saw a huge phone on a bench. It was shiny and had many buttons.
"Wow, look at that phone!" Tom said. "I want to play with it."
"No, Tom, we should not touch it," Anna said. "It belongs to someone else. Maybe they will come back soon."
But Tom did not listen. He ran to the bench and grabbed the phone. He pressed some buttons and made funny noises.
"Ha ha, this is fun!" he said.
Suddenly, the phone rang. It was very loud. Tom was scared. He dropped the phone and ran back to Anna.
"Help, help!" he cried. "The phone is angry at me!"
Anna looked at the phone. She saw a man running towards it. He looked angry too.
"Hey, that's my phone!" the man shouted. "Who touched it? You broke it!"
He picked up the phone and saw that the screen was cracked. He was very sad.
"I'm sorry, sir," Anna said. "My brother did it. He did not know better. He is only three."
The man sighed. He looked at Tom and Anna.
"Listen, kids," he said. "You should never touch things that are not yours. You could hurt them or yourself. And you should always listen to your sister. She is smart and kind. She tried to stop you."
Tom felt ashamed. He nodded.
"I'm sorry, sir," he said. "I'm sorry, Anna. I was wrong. I will not do it again."
The man smiled. He was not so angry anymore.
"It's okay, Tom," he said. "I forgive you. But you have to be more careful next time. And you have to help me fix my phone. It is very important to me."
Tom agreed. He and Anna helped the man fix his phone. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to respect other people's things and to listen to each other. They also made a new friend.
