Lily and Max were playing in the garden. They liked to look at the flowers and the bugs. But they did not like the cactus. The cactus was prickly and green. It had sharp needles that could hurt them.
"Let's fold some paper and make a cactus," Max said. He took a green sheet and folded it into a triangle. Then he cut out some small squares and glued them on the sides. "Look, this is my cactus. It is not prickly. It is soft and nice."
Lily liked Max's cactus. She took a pink sheet and folded it into a circle. Then she cut out some petals and glued them on the top. "Look, this is my flower. It is not green. It is pretty and sweet."
They put their paper cactus and flower on the table. They were happy with their craft. They decided to show it to their mom.
But then they heard a loud roar. It was their cat, Fluffy. Fluffy was fierce and hungry. He saw the paper cactus and flower and thought they were food. He jumped on the table and tried to bite them.
"Stop, Fluffy! That is not food! That is our cactus and flower!" Lily and Max shouted. They ran to the table and tried to save their craft. But Fluffy was faster and stronger. He tore the paper cactus and flower into pieces. He made a big mess.
Lily and Max were sad and angry. They cried and scolded Fluffy. Fluffy did not care. He licked his paws and walked away.
Mom heard the noise and came to the garden. She saw the paper cactus and flower on the floor. She saw Lily and Max crying. She hugged them and said, "I'm sorry, Fluffy ruined your craft. He is a bad cat. But I have an idea. Why don't we make a new cactus and flower with clay? Clay is harder and stronger. Fluffy cannot bite it. And we can paint it with different colors. It will be fun."
Lily and Max liked Mom's idea. They dried their tears and smiled. They went to the house and got some clay and paint. They made a new cactus and flower with clay. They painted them with green and pink. They put them on the window sill. They were proud of their craft. They did not let Fluffy near it. They said, "This is our cactus and flower. They are not paper. They are clay. They are hard and bright."

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play with toys and draw pictures. One day, they find a big frame in the garage. It is shiny and has many colors.
"Let's make a picture for the frame!" Sara says.
"OK, what do we draw?" Tom asks.
Sara thinks for a moment. She likes flowers and butterflies. She says, "Let's draw a garden with flowers and butterflies!"
Tom shakes his head. He likes cars and rockets. He says, "No, let's draw a road with cars and rockets!"
Sara and Tom disagree. They both want to draw what they like. They start to argue and yell.
"I want flowers and butterflies!" Sara says.
"I want cars and rockets!" Tom says.
They pull the frame from each other. They are very angry. They do not want to share.
Suddenly, the frame breaks. It makes a loud noise. The glass shatters and the colors fall off. Sara and Tom are scared. They drop the frame and run away.
Mom and Dad hear the noise. They come to the garage. They see the broken frame and the mess. They are very upset. They look for Sara and Tom.
"Sara! Tom! What did you do?" Mom and Dad say.
Sara and Tom hide under the bed. They feel sorry and sad. They wish they did not disagree. They wish they did not break the frame. They wish they were still friends.
The end.

Once upon a time, there were two children named Jack and Jill. They loved going to the park together. One day, when they were at the park, they found a fragile vegetable on the ground.
Jack said excitedly, "Let's destroy it!"
Jill shook her head and said, "No, we shouldn't destroy it. If we leave it on the ground, the birds or other animals may eat it."
Jack thought for a moment and agreed with Jill. He said, "Yeah, you're right. We should leave it here so that something else can enjoy it." So, they left the fragile vegetable alone.
The moral of this story is that it's important to be kind to the environment, and respect all living things. We should only take what we need, and never waste or destroy what is not ours.

When the yacht was safely on its way, the caterpillar crawled off the back of the yacht and waved goodbye. Everyone on the yacht was so grateful to the caterpillar and thanked it for its help. So, the caterpillar was very happy and went on its way. 
The End!

She heard Lily's voice saying, "Hi, mom. I love you. You are the best mom in the world. You are dependable and kind. You work hard and you make good tea. Thank you for everything. I hope you have a good day. Bye, mom."

"OK, let's do it. We can make them even better." Tom said.
They worked together and made a new house and a new car. They were happy and proud.

Ben and Mia like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is a big ball. The ball is red and blue and has a label on it. The label says "bounce me".
One day, they take the ball to the park. They find a hill and roll the ball down. The ball goes fast and bounces on the grass. Ben and Mia laugh and run after the ball.
"Look, Mia, the ball is so fun!" Ben says.
"Yes, Ben, I like the ball too!" Mia says.
They roll the ball up and down the hill many times. They have a lot of fun.
But then, they see a little dog. The dog is brown and fluffy and has a collar. The dog sees the ball and runs to it. The dog thinks the ball is a toy for him. He bites the ball and shakes it. He makes a hole in the ball. The air comes out of the ball. The ball is not big and round anymore. The ball is flat and sad.
"Oh no, the dog broke our ball!" Ben says.
"Bad dog, go away!" Mia says.
They try to get the ball from the dog, but the dog is strong and fast. He runs away with the ball. Ben and Mia are sad and angry. They cry and shout.
"Come back, dog, give us our ball!" Ben says.
"That's our ball, not yours!" Mia says.
But the dog does not listen. He takes the ball to his owner. His owner is a man who sits on a bench. He sees the ball and the label on it. He reads the label and smiles.
"Good boy, you found a ball!" he says to the dog. "But this is not your ball, this is someone else's ball. See, the label says 'bounce me'. This ball is for bouncing, not for biting. Let's go and find the owners of the ball and say sorry."
He takes the ball and the dog and walks to Ben and Mia. He gives them the ball and apologizes.
"I'm sorry, kids, my dog thought your ball was his toy. He didn't mean to hurt it. He likes to play with balls, but he doesn't know how to bounce them. He only knows how to bite them. Can you forgive him?"
Ben and Mia look at the man and the dog. They are still sad, but they are also kind. They know the dog is not bad, he is just silly. They nod and smile.
"It's okay, mister, we forgive your dog. He is cute, but he needs to learn how to play with balls. Maybe you can teach him?" Ben says.
"Or maybe you can give him another toy, like a bone or a rope. Something he can bite and not break." Mia says.
The man thanks them and agrees. He says he will buy a new ball for them and a new toy for his dog. He says goodbye and leaves with his dog.
Ben and Mia wave and say goodbye. They are happy again. They have a new friend and a new ball. They go back to the hill and roll the ball down. The ball is red and blue and has a label on it. The label says "bounce me". And they do.

Ben and Lily ran to the kitchen to see what was wrong. They saw their mom looking sad and worried. She had a big bowl of flour and eggs, but no butter.
"Mom, what is butter?" Lily asked.
"Butter is a yellow thing that you put on bread or in cakes. It makes them soft and yummy. But I don't have any, and the cake is for grandma's birthday. What can I do?" mom said.
Ben thought for a moment. He remembered that he had seen something yellow in the fridge. Maybe it was butter.
"Mom, I have an idea. Come with me!" he said. He took his mom's hand and led her to the fridge. He opened the door and pointed to a yellow box.

Mom looked at the box and smiled. It was not butter, but cheese. But Ben did not know the difference. He was so proud of himself for finding the yellow thing.
"Thank you, Ben. You are very smart and helpful. But this is not butter, this is cheese. Cheese is another yellow thing that you can eat, but not in cakes. It tastes different. But don't worry, we can still make a cake. We can use oil instead of butter. It will be a normal cake, just a little different. Do you want to help me?" mom said.
Ben and Lily nodded. They wanted to help their mom make the cake. They followed her to the counter and helped her mix the ingredients. They poured the batter into a pan and put it in the oven. The sign was very stubborn and Teddy was too. He tried to ignore it, but it just refused to go away. He started to argue with it.
"It doesn't make any sense! I just want to get across the river." He complained.
But the sign didn't listen. Furious, Teddy grabbed his medal and threw it across the river. 
To his surprise, the sign moved. As if it had been waiting for what Teddy had done. Teddy was now able to cross the river, without the sign stopping him.
The next day Teddy went back to get his medal and he proudly wore it on his chest as a reminder that sometimes you have to be a little bit stubborn to get what you want.

They run to find Mom. She is in the living room. She is reading a book. She sees the fork and the lock in Tom's hand.
"What are you doing with that, Tom?" Mom asks. She is not happy. "That is not a toy. That is a lock for the door. And that is a fork for eating. You could hurt yourself or break something."
"Sorry, Mom," Tom says. "We were just playing. We wanted to see if the fork can open the lock. But it did not work. It is stuck. Can you help us?"
Mom sighs. She takes the fork and the lock from Tom. She uses a key to open the lock. She frees the fork. She gives them back to Tom.
"Here you go, Tom. But please, do not play with these things again. They are not nice. They are dangerous. If you want to play, you can use your toys. They are nice. They are fun. They are safe. Do you understand?"
"Yes, Mom," Tom says. He feels sorry. He hugs Mom. "Thank you, Mom. You are nice. You are the best."
Lily hugs Mom too. "Yes, thank you, Mom. We love you."
Mom smiles. She hugs them back. "I love you too, my sweet twins. Now, go and play nicely. And be careful."

Lily and Ben are best friends. They like to play together and share their toys. One day, Lily has a big idea. She wants to mail a letter to her grandma, who lives far away. She asks Ben to help her.
"Let's write a letter to grandma," she says. "She will be happy to hear from us."
"Okay," Ben says. "What do we write?"
Lily thinks hard. She finds a crayon and a paper. She draws a picture of herself, Ben, and a big heart. She writes "I love you, grandma" with the crayon. Ben helps her fold the paper and put it in an envelope. They write grandma's address on the front.
"Good job," Lily says. "Now we need a stamp."
They look around the house for a stamp. They find one in a drawer. They stick it on the envelope. They are ready to mail the letter.
"Let's go to the mailbox," Ben says. "It's not far."
They put on their shoes and coats. They hold hands and walk to the mailbox. It is a sunny day. They are happy.
But when they get to the mailbox, they see a big problem. There is a storm coming. The sky is dark and angry. The wind is loud and strong. The rain is fast and wet. They are scared.
"Oh no," Lily says. "The storm will ruin our letter. It will get wet and torn. Grandma will never get it."
"Don't worry," Ben says. "I have an idea. I will protect the letter. I will be loyal to you and grandma."
He takes the letter from Lily. He puts it under his coat. He hugs it tight. He runs to the mailbox. He opens the lid. He throws the letter inside. He closes the lid. He runs back to Lily.
"I did it," he says. "The letter is safe. The storm can't hurt it. Grandma will get it."
Lily hugs Ben. She is proud of him. He is brave and loyal. He is her best friend.
"Thank you, Ben," she says. "You are the best. I love you."
"I love you too, Lily," he says. "Come on, let's go home. It's cold and wet."
They hold hands and run home. They are wet and cold. But they are happy. They mailed a letter to grandma. They hope she will like it. They hope she will write back. They hope the storm will go away. They hope the sun will come back. They hope to play together again. They are best friends.

"Where can we go?" Lily asked.

They ran to the big tree and sat under it. They hugged each other. They were wet and cold.
Suddenly, they saw a bright flash. They heard a loud boom. The big tree was on fire. A strike of light had hit it.
"Run, run!" Ben shouted. "The tree is burning!"
They ran away from the big tree. They saw a small house. They knocked on the door.
"Help, help!" Lily cried.
A kind lady opened the door. She saw the wet and scared children.
"Come in, come in!" she said. "You are safe here."
She gave them warm blankets and hot soup. She told them stories until the storm was over. Ben and Lily felt better. They thanked the kind lady.
"You are welcome," she said. "I'm glad you are okay. The big tree was not a good shelter. It was dangerous. Next time, look for a better shelter."
Ben and Lily nodded. They learned a lesson. They hugged the kind lady. They waited for their mom and dad to come and get them.

Lily felt sad and angry. She did not like Tom's words. She said, "No, Tom. You are mean. I can draw well. I will not give up. I want to make mom happy. Go away!"
Tom shrugged and left. He did not care about Lily's feelings. He thought he was better than her at everything.
Lily did not let Tom's words stop her. She finished her picture and put it in a nice envelope. She hid it under her pillow and waited for mom's birthday.
The next day, mom woke up and saw Lily holding the envelope. She said, "What is this, Lily? Is it for me?"
Lily nodded and gave her the envelope. She said, "Yes, mom. It is for you. Happy birthday! I hope you like it."
Mom opened the envelope and saw the picture. She was very surprised and happy. She said, "Oh, Lily, this is beautiful! Thank you so much! You are such a good and sweet girl. You draw very well. I love you, too."
She hugged Lily and kissed her. Lily felt warm and glad. She succeeded in making mom happy. She wished Tom would be nicer to her. She wished they could all be happy together.

"I do, I do!" Lily said. She climbed on the big chair. The barber put a cape around her. He cut her hair a little bit. Lily looked in the mirror. She smiled. She liked her new hair.
"Your turn, Tom," Mom said.
Tom was scared. He did not want to go on the big chair. He did not want the barber to cut his hair. He hid behind Mom.
"Come on, Tom. It's not scary. It's fun. Look at Lily. She's happy," Mom said.
Tom looked at Lily. He did not recognize her. She had different hair. She looked like a stranger. He cried.
"No, no, no! I don't want to go! I don't know her! I want my sister!" Tom said.
Lily got off the big chair. She ran to Tom. She hugged him.
"Don't cry, Tom. It's me, Lily. I'm still your sister. I just have new hair. You can have new hair too. It will grow back soon. Please don't be sad," Lily said.
Tom looked at Lily. He saw her eyes and her nose and her mouth. He saw her smile. He recognized her. He stopped crying.
"Okay, Lily. I'll go on the big chair. But only if you hold my hand," Tom said.
Lily nodded. She held Tom's hand. They went on the big chair together. The barber cut Tom's hair a little bit. Tom looked in the mirror. He smiled. He liked his new hair.
"Wow, you two look great. You look like twins again," the barber said.
Lily and Tom laughed. They thanked the barber. They went home with Mom. They played together. They were happy.

Sam was scared. He tried to pull his kite back. But it was too late. The string touched the sign. There was a big boom. The trailer blew up. The kite blew up. Sam flew off the hill. He landed on the grass. He was hurt. He cried.
His dad heard the boom. He ran to the park. He saw Sam on the ground. He saw the smoke and the fire. He was angry and sad. He hugged Sam and said, "Why did you do that? Why did you not listen to me? I told you it was not safe. You were foolish. You could have died."

His dad said, "Yes, son. We can still fly kites together. But not today. Today, we have to go to the hospital. You need to get checked. You have some cuts and bruises. And you have a big lesson to learn."

Her mom smiled and said, "That's a guitar, Lucy. Would you like to try it?"
Lucy nodded eagerly. She tried to sit on the floor like her mom told her, and she held the guitar. It felt odd to her, but she was excited to give it a try.
Lucy strummed the strings, and the sound filled the room. She loved playing the guitar and it filled her with joy. When she was done, Lucy eagerly asked her mom if she could play it again soon.
Her mom nodded. "Yes, of course you can, Lucy," she said, hugging her daughter. "I'm so proud of my little guitarist!"

Anna and Ben are brother and sister. They like to play together. One day, they decide to play vacation. They pack their bags with toys and clothes. They pretend to go to the airport and fly to a faraway place.
"Where are we going, Ben?" Anna asks.
"We are going to the beach, Anna. We can swim and build sand castles and eat ice cream," Ben says.
"That sounds fun, Ben. I love the beach," Anna says.
They find a spot in the backyard and spread a blanket. They pretend it is the sand. They use a bucket and a shovel to make sand castles. They use a hose to spray water and pretend it is the sea. They have a lot of fun.
But then, their mom comes out. She looks angry. She sees their bags and their mess.
"What are you doing, Anna and Ben?" she asks.
"We are playing vacation, mom. We are at the beach," Ben says.
"Well, you are not playing vacation. You are making a big mess. You took your clothes and toys without asking. You wasted water and dirtied the blanket. You need to clean up and put everything back," mom says.
"But mom, we are having fun. We are not hurting anyone. Can we play a little more?" Anna says.
"No, you can't. You need to learn to respect your things and the rules. You can play vacation another day, but not like this. Now, come on, help me clean up," mom says.
Anna and Ben are sad. They don't want to stop playing. They don't want to clean up. They think mom is mean.
"Mom, can we sell our things and go on a real vacation?" Ben asks.
"No, you can't. You need your things and you need to stay home. Besides, you don't have enough money to go on a real vacation. And even if you did, you would still need to behave and follow the rules. Now, stop talking and start cleaning," mom says.
Anna and Ben sigh. They do what mom says. They hope mom will be fine soon. They hope they can play vacation again. But they will do it differently next time. They will ask mom first. They will use less water and dirt. They will clean up after themselves. They will make mom happy. And maybe, mom will let them go on a real vacation someday.

The sun said, "Are you lost?" 
The line didn't say anything. It just kept doing its loop. The sun lit up brighter, so the line would be able to see it. 
The line stopped and curtsied to the sun. The sun smiled and said, "Do you want to come have a play with me?"
The line nodded and the sun began to shine brighter and brighter. It shone so bright that the line became a rainbow. 
The sun said, "Now, let's play a game!" 
The rainbow and the sun played games until the sun said, "It's time for me to go home." 
The rainbow said goodbye to the sun, who said, "Now, you'll be able to find your way home." 
The sun shined one last time, as the rainbow flew away, back to where it came from. The sun knew that it would be okay from now on.

Lucy's mother was happy that her daughter was alright, so she gave the little girl a big hug. 
The doctor said, "It's best that you keep old medicines away from children. Always ask your parents before you decide to try something new."
Lucy nodded in agreement and vowed to never try something new without asking her parents first.

"Look, Tom, a pepper!" she said. "It looks yummy. Can we have it?"
Tom was not sure. He remembered that Mom had told them not to touch the peppers. She said they were hot and spicy and could hurt their mouths.
"I don't know, Lila," he said. "Mom said no. She said they are harsh. They make you cry and drink water."
Lila did not listen. She was curious and hungry. She reached for the pepper and pulled it hard. The stem snapped and the pepper came off. Lila smiled and took a big bite.
"Ow! Ow! Ow!" she cried. "It burns! It burns!"
Tom saw Lila's face turn red and tears run down her cheeks. He felt sorry for her. He ran to the kitchen and brought a glass of water. He gave it to Lila and helped her drink.
"Are you okay, Lila?" he asked.
Lila nodded. She felt better after the water. She spit out the pepper and threw it away.
"I'm sorry, Tom," she said. "You were right. The pepper was harsh. It was not yummy. It was bad."
Tom hugged Lila and said, "It's okay, Lila. You made a mistake. We all make mistakes. Next time, listen to Mom. She knows what is good for us."
Lila nodded again. She learned her lesson. She never pulled a pepper again.

Her dad sighed. He said, "It's okay, Lily. I know you didn't mean it. But you have to be careful with scissors. And you have to ask before you use something that is not yours. Lily nodded. She said, "Okay, dad. I will be careful. And I will write to grandma. I love her."

Sam liked to play with his toy soldiers. He had many of them, and they all wore green uniforms. He liked to make them march and fight and say "Yes, sir!" and "No, sir!" He pretended he was their boss and gave them orders.
One day, it was very hot outside. Sam wanted to play with his toy soldiers in the sun. He took them to the backyard and put them on the grass. He made them march and fight and say "Yes, sir!" and "No, sir!" He was having fun.
But soon, he noticed something was wrong. His toy soldiers looked different. Their uniforms were not green anymore. They were brown and sticky. Their faces and arms and legs were not hard anymore. They were soft and gooey. They could not march or fight or say anything. They were melting!
Sam was sad and angry. He did not know the sun was so hot. He did not know his toy soldiers were made of plastic. He did not know plastic could melt. He felt foolish. He had ruined his toy soldiers.
He ran inside and told his mom what happened. His mom was sorry for him. She hugged him and said, "It's okay, Sam. You did not mean to do it. You did not know. It was an accident. I will buy you new toy soldiers. But next time, don't play with them in the sun. Play with them in the shade. Okay?"
Sam nodded and said, "Okay, mom. Thank you. I'm sorry. I love you." He learned his lesson. He never played with his toy soldiers in the sun again. He played with them in the shade. And he was happy.

Once upon a time there was a nosy lumberjack. He was always busy looking for lumber, no matter what was going on.
One day, the lumberjack came upon a wonderful tree. He decided this was the perfect tree to bring down.
But when the lumberjack started to cut down the tree, a little bird flew up to him. He said, in a small voice, "Please do not destroy my home!"
The lumberjack was surprised, and he quickly put down his tools. He looked at the bird and asked, "Why don't you go find another tree to live in?"
The bird shook his head and said, "This is my home. Please do not destroy it."
The lumberjack thought for a while and then he said, "Alright, I won't destroy your home. But you have to promise me something in return."
The little bird said, "What?"
The lumberjack said, "Promise me that you will always tell me when you find lumber, so I can get it instead of destroying another tree."
The little bird thought for a minute and then agreed. So the lumberjack went his way, and the little bird kept watch over the tree, always on the lookout for lumber.

The cat does not like Tom. The cat hisses and scratches Tom. Tom cries. He runs back to Mia.
"Mia, Mia, the cat hurt me!" Tom says. He shows Mia his hand. It has a red mark.
"Oh, Tom, I'm sorry," Mia says. "That is a bad cat. Do you want a hug?"
"Yes, please," Tom says. Mia hugs Tom. He feels better.
"Look, Tom, there is a lady with a salad," Mia says. She points to a bench. A lady is eating a salad from a bowl. She has a fork and a napkin.
"Maybe she can lend us her napkin," Mia says. "We can clean your hand."
"OK, let's ask her," Tom says. They walk to the lady.
"Excuse me, lady," Mia says. "Can you lend us your napkin? My friend has a boo-boo."
The lady smiles. She sees Tom's hand. She gives them her napkin.
"Sure, here you go," the lady says. "What happened to your hand?"
"A black cat scratched me," Tom says.
"Oh, that's not nice," the lady says. "You should be careful with cats. Some of them are not friendly."
"Thank you, lady," Mia says. She wipes Tom's hand with the napkin. She throws the napkin in the trash.
"You're welcome, kids," the lady says. "Have a nice day."
Tom and Mia say goodbye to the lady. They go back to their toys. They play some more. They forget about the black cat. They are happy.

She decided to take her drum home. She said goodbye to Ben and his mom. She put the drum in her bag and walked away.

Lily flew down to the soap and called her friend, Max the squirrel. "Max, look at this!" she said. Max came running and looked at the soap. "What is it?" he asked. Lily didn't know, but she thought it was special.
Max had an idea. "Let's leave the soap by the big tree and see if someone knows what it is," he said. Lily agreed, and they both took the soap to the big tree. Soon, their friend Bella the bunny hopped by and saw the soap. "That's soap!" she said. "We can use it to clean our hands and faces!" Lily and Max were happy to learn about the soap, and they all took turns using it. From that day on, they always felt clean and fresh after playing together.

One day, they went to visit their grandma. She lived on a big ranch. There were many cows and horses and chickens. Ben and Mia wanted to paint them. They took their paints and brushes and ran outside.
They saw a brown cow. They painted it blue and yellow. They saw a black horse. They painted it pink and green. They saw a white chicken. They painted it red and orange. They had fun.
But then, they heard a loud moo. It was the cow. It was angry. It did not like the colors. It chased Ben and Mia. They ran away. They were scared.
They ran to their grandma. She saw them and the cow. She was shocked. She said, "What did you do? You hurt the cow. You hurt its feelings. You have to say sorry and wash it."
Ben and Mia felt bad. They said sorry to the cow. They took a bucket and a sponge and washed it. They washed the horse and the chicken too. They said sorry to them.
Their grandma hugged them. She said, "I love you, but you have to be careful. You can paint on paper and on the wall, but not on the animals. They are alive. They have feelings. They do not like to be painted."
Ben and Mia nodded. They said, "We understand. We are sorry. We will not paint on the animals again."
They went inside. They painted on paper. They painted their grandma and the ranch. They used nice colors. They gave their paintings to their grandma. She smiled. She said, "Thank you. These are beautiful. You are good painters."

Today, Mary wanted to do something special. She began to search for something she could do. She looked around the living room and saw her doll. "Maybe I can do something with this," she thought. 
Mary took her doll and began to rub it gently. Suddenly, the doll started to move and speak to her. "What are you doing?" asked the doll. 
Mary was so surprised. She was not expecting the doll to talk to her. She started to cry. "I'm sorry! I didn't mean to make you mad," said Mary. 
The doll smiled. "It's okay. You were just trying to be generous. Would you like to play with me instead?" 
Mary smiled and nodded her head. She was so happy to have a new friend to play with. Mary and the doll played together all afternoon. Mary had found her special thing to do after all.

The flea had no answer and stayed still. Amy thought for a while and then said to the flea,
"Let's have a race! I'll count to three and then we'll get ready to go."
The flea hopped quickly off the ground and ran around in circles. Amy laughed with excitement and followed it around the garden. It was the best game ever!
By the end of the afternoon, the flea had tired out and Amy was ready to put it back in the garden. 
"Goodbye, little flea. Thanks for being so creative!" She said as she watched it run away. 
Amy waved goodbye and went off inside, full of joy from her creative adventure.

"Let's pretend this is our car," said Ben. "We can go anywhere we want."
"OK," said Lily. "But where do we want to go?"
Ben thought for a moment. He looked around and saw a big house with a fence and a gate. The house had many windows and flowers. It looked very fancy.
"Let's go to that house," he said. "Maybe they have cookies and toys."
Lily nodded. She liked cookies and toys. They grabbed the tire and rolled it to the fence. They tried to push the tire through the gate, but it was too big.
"Uh-oh," said Lily. "How do we get in?"
Ben had an idea. He saw a small hole under the fence. He crawled through the hole and said, "Lily, follow me."
Lily was scared. She did not like holes. She said, "Ben, wait. I don't want to go."
Ben said, "Don't be scared. It's fun. Come on, Lily."
Lily took a deep breath. She closed her eyes and stepped through the hole. She felt the grass on her feet and opened her eyes. She saw Ben smiling and holding her hand.
"See, Lily, we did it," he said. "Now let's go to the house and see what they have."
They left the tire behind and walked to the house. They did not know that the house belonged to a mean old lady who did not like children. They were about to find out.

"Yes, he does. You made him happy. You are very kind, Ben," his mom said.

Lily ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, there is a dead bird outside. It makes me frown. What can we do?"
Her mom hugged her and said, "It is okay to feel sad, my daughter. Let's make a small bed for the bird and put it in a safe place."
Together, they made a little bed out of leaves and placed the bird gently inside. Lily felt better knowing that the bird was now in a better place. From that day on, she learned how to care for all creatures, big and small.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big sack on the grass. It is full of toys and books.
"Wow, look at that sack!" Anna says. "It has so many beautiful things inside!"
"Let's play with it!" Ben says. "Maybe we can find something we like."
They run to the sack and open it. They see dolls, cars, puzzles, crayons and more. They are very happy.
"Can I have this doll?" Anna asks. "She has a pretty dress and long hair."
"Sure, you can have it," Ben says. "Can I have this car? It has big wheels and makes noises."
"OK, you can have it," Anna says.
They take out more toys and books. They share them and play with them. They have a lot of fun.
But then, they hear a voice. It is a man. He is looking for his sack.
"Hey, that's my sack!" he says. "I was going to give it to the children's home. Who took it?"
Anna and Ben are scared. They did not know the sack was not for them. They feel bad.
"We are sorry, mister," Anna says. "We did not know it was your sack. We thought it was for anyone."
"We just wanted to play with it," Ben says. "We did not mean to take it."
The man is angry at first. But then he sees their faces. They look sad and sorry. He feels sorry for them too.
"It's OK, kids," he says. "I understand. You were curious and excited. But you have to be careful. You can't just take things that are not yours. You have to ask first."
"Yes, mister, we know," Anna and Ben say. "We are very sorry. Can we give you back your sack?"
"Of course, you can," the man says. "But you know what? You can also keep one thing each. As a gift. You can choose what you like."
"Really?" Anna and Ben say. "Thank you, mister! You are very kind!"
They hug the man and thank him. They look at the sack again. They have to choose one thing each. It is hard. They like so many things.
Anna chooses the doll. She loves her dress and hair. Ben chooses the car. He loves its wheels and noises. They are very happy with their choices.
They give the rest of the sack to the man. He smiles and thanks them. He tells them he will give the sack to the children's home. He hopes they will like it too.
Anna and Ben wave goodbye to the man. They hold their toys and books. They feel good. They learned a lesson. They also made a friend. They think they are lucky. They think they win.

Sam and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a race to see who is faster. Sam runs very fast, but Ben runs faster. Ben wins the race.
"Ha ha, I win!" Ben says. "You are slow, Sam!"
Sam feels sad. He does not like to lose. He wants to win the race. He thinks of a plan.
"Let's race again," Sam says. "But this time, we race to the pond."
Ben agrees. He thinks he can win again. He does not know Sam's plan.
They start to run to the pond. Sam runs behind Ben. When they are near the pond, Sam pushes Ben. Ben falls into the pond. The pond is deep and cold. Ben cannot swim. He is scared.
"Help me, Sam!" Ben cries. "I cannot breathe!"
Sam does not help Ben. He is angry and mean. He wants Ben to lose. He does not care if Ben is hurt. He watches Ben sink into the pond.
Ben tries to resist the water. He tries to kick and splash. He tries to call for help. But no one hears him. No one sees him. He runs out of air. He stops moving. He dies.
Sam wins the race. But he loses a friend. He is alone and sad. He is sorry for what he did. But it is too late. He cannot bring Ben back. He cannot say sorry. He cannot be friends again. He cries and cries. He wishes he was nice. He wishes he did not push Ben. He wishes he did not race to the pond.

"Let's make an igloo!" Tom suggested. He had seen an igloo on TV and wanted to try it. "We can use the snow shovel and the bucket to make blocks of snow."
"OK!" Lily agreed. She thought it would be cool to have an igloo. They started to work together, shoveling snow and packing it into the bucket. Then they turned the bucket over and made a block of snow. They repeated this until they had many blocks.
They arranged the blocks in a circle, leaving a small opening for the door. Then they stacked more blocks on top, making the igloo taller and rounder. They used their hands to smooth the gaps and make the igloo stronger.
They crawled inside the igloo and looked around. It was cozy and quiet. They felt proud of their work.
"This is our house!" Tom said. "We can pretend we live here."
"Can we have a snack?" Lily asked. She was hungry after working hard.
"Sure!" Tom said. He reached into his backpack and took out two cookies. He gave one to Lily and kept one for himself. They ate their cookies and smiled.
They noticed that their hands and clothes were dirty from the snow. They didn't mind. They were having too much fun. They decided to stay in the igloo for a while and play some more. They were happy.

Anna loved purple. She had a purple dress, a purple hat, a purple ball, and a purple bike. She did not like to share her purple things with anyone. She said, "They are mine, mine, mine!"
One morning, Anna went to the park with her mom. She saw a girl with a yellow dress, a yellow hat, a yellow ball, and a yellow bike. The girl smiled at Anna and said, "Hi, do you want to play with me?" Anna said, "No, I don't like yellow. I like purple. Go away!"
The girl felt sad and walked away. Anna played with her purple things by herself. She did not have fun. She felt lonely and bored.
Then, she saw a boy with a green dress, a green hat, a green ball, and a green bike. The boy waved at Anna and said, "Hi, do you want to play with me?" Anna said, "No, I don't like green. I like purple. Go away!"
The boy felt sad and walked away. Anna played with her purple things by herself. She did not have fun. She felt lonely and bored.
Then, she saw a dog with a brown fur, a brown collar, a brown bone, and a brown tail. The dog barked at Anna and said, "Woof, woof, do you want to play with me?" Anna said, "No, I don't like brown. I like purple. Go away!"
The dog felt sad and walked away. Anna played with her purple things by herself. She did not have fun. She felt lonely and bored.
Then, she saw her mom with a blue dress, a blue hat, a blue bag, and a blue smile. Her mom hugged Anna and said, "Hi, my sweetie, do you want to go home with me?" Anna said, "Yes, mom, I want to go home with you. I love you, mom. You are the best."
Her mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Anna. You are the best. But you know, you can also love other colors and other people and other animals. They are not bad. They are different. And different is good. Different is fun. Different is beautiful. If you share your purple things with them, they will share their yellow, green, and brown things with you. And you will have more friends and more fun. And you will care for them, and they will care for you. Do you understand, Anna?"
Anna thought for a moment. Then, she nodded and said, "Yes, mom, I understand. I want to share and care. I want to be kind and happy. I want to try other colors and other things. Can we go back to the park and play with the girl, the boy, and the dog?"
Her mom said, "Of course, we can, Anna. Let's go back and play. And let's say sorry to them for being rude. And let's say thank you to them for being nice. And let's say hello to them for being friends. Are you ready, Anna?"
Anna said, "Yes, mom, I am ready. Let's go, mom. Let's go!"
The end.

"OK, but we need to wear vests," Ben said. He knew that vests help you float if you fall in the water.
They put on their vests and ran to the shore. They saw a rope hanging from the boat. They pulled the rope and climbed on the boat.
"Wow, this is fun!" Lila said. She looked around and saw many things. She saw a wheel, a bell, a map, and a radio.
"Look, I can steer the boat!" Ben said. He turned the wheel and made the boat move.
"Be careful, Ben!" Lila said. "You don't know how to drive a boat!"
But Ben did not listen. He turned the wheel more and more. The boat went faster and faster. It made big waves and noise.
Suddenly, they heard a loud voice from the radio.
"Who is on my boat? Get off now! You are in trouble!"
It was the owner of the boat. He was angry. He saw Lila and Ben on his boat. He called for help.
"Help! Help! There are two kids on my boat! They are stealing it! Rescue me!"
Lila and Ben were scared. They did not know what to do. They tried to get off the boat, but it was too late. The boat hit a rock and broke. Water came in and filled the boat.
Lila and Ben screamed. They held on to their vests. They hoped someone would rescue them.
But no one came. The owner of the boat was too far away. He could not see them. He could not hear them. He only cared about his boat.
Lila and Ben sank with the boat. They never saw their families again. They never played near the lake again. They never saw the beautiful boat again.

“Oh, what’s wrong?” Lucy asked. 
The puppy’s mommy came over and said “He hurt his heel and he’s nervous about trying to walk on it.”
Lucy stroked his head and said, “It’s ok little pup, I know exactly how you feel. Whenever I get scared, I just take a deep breath and tell myself it’ll be ok.”
The puppy wagged his tail and tentatively put his paw down. He took a few steps and soon, he was running faster than Lucy could skip. Lucy smiled, knowing she had helped her new friend.
This story teaches us that when we are feeling scared or nervous, it is important to believe in ourselves and have faith that we'll be alright.

One day, the bunny noticed a special kind of flower with a big yellow centre and a long, pointy nose. He had never seen this flower before and he wanted to feed on it, so he hopped over and gave it a try.
The bunny was so surprised to find the flower tasted so sweet! He nibbled and nuzzled on the petals until his tummy was full and his nose was covered with pollen. The bunny felt so content, so calm and so happy; he had discovered a new way to feed! 
It was the perfect meal, and the bunny was sure he would return to the meadow again and again to feed on this lovely flower.

Sam and Ben were brothers who liked to play at the beach. They had a big board that they used to surf on the waves. They took turns to hold the board and push each other into the water. They laughed and shouted as they surfed.
One day, they saw a big red truck parked near the sand. It had a sign that said "Hot Dogs". Sam and Ben loved hot dogs. They ran to the truck and asked the man for two hot dogs each. The man smiled and gave them their hot dogs. He said, "Be careful, these are spicy hot dogs. They have a lot of sauce that makes your mouth burn."
Sam and Ben did not care. They were hungry and excited. They bit into their hot dogs and felt the sauce. It was very spicy. It made their eyes water and their noses run. They coughed and gasped. They did not like the spicy hot dogs. They wanted to spit them out.
"Yuck! These are too spicy!" Sam said.
"I don't like them either!" Ben said.
They looked at each other and had an idea. They ran back to the board and the waves. They surfed again, but this time they used their hot dogs as weapons. They threw them at each other and tried to dodge them. They had a hot dog fight. They laughed and shouted again, but this time they also said, "Surrender! Surrender!"
They had fun until they ran out of hot dogs. Then they threw the buns into the water and watched the fish eat them. They were happy and tired. They hugged each other and said, "That was the best surf ever!"

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park every morning. They liked to see the sunrise. The sunrise was when the sky turned pink and yellow and the big ball of light came up.
One morning, Lily and Ben went to the park early. They saw a big poster on the fence. The poster had a picture of a famous singer. The singer had long hair and a shiny dress. Lily liked the singer. She wanted the poster.
"Look, Ben, it's the singer I love! She is so pretty and sings so well. I want the poster. Can we take it?" Lily asked.
Ben shook his head. "No, Lily, we can't. The poster is not ours. Someone else put it there. It is not nice to take things that are not ours."
But Lily did not listen. She ran to the fence and tried to pull the poster off. She pulled and pulled, but the poster was stuck. She pulled harder and harder, but the poster did not move.
"Stop, Lily, stop! You are going to rip the poster! You are going to make a mess!" Ben shouted.
But Lily did not stop. She pulled with all her strength. Then, the poster ripped. It tore in half. Lily fell to the ground. She held the ripped poster in her hands. She looked at it and started to cry.
"Look what you did, Lily! You ruined the poster! You made a big hole in the fence! You are in trouble!" Ben said.
Lily felt bad. She was sorry. She wished she had listened to Ben. She wished she had not pulled the poster. She wished she had just looked at the sunrise with her friend. She hugged Ben and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was wrong. I was selfish. I should have listened to you. Can you forgive me?"
Ben was angry, but he was also kind. He saw that Lily was sad. He saw that she was sorry. He hugged her back and said, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. You are still my friend. But next time, please don't pull things that are not yours. Okay?"
Lily nodded. She smiled. She said, "Okay, Ben. Thank you for being my friend. Thank you for forgiving me. Can we still see the sunrise?"
Ben smiled. He said, "Yes, Lily. We can still see the sunrise. Come on, let's go."

"Wow, that's a nice fish!" Tim said. "I made a lion. Do you see his mane?"
Mia nodded. "Yes, it's very big and yellow. Can I use your red crayon? I want to make a flower."
"Sure, here you go." Tim gave his red crayon to Mia and took a green one. He started to draw a tree.
But then, something bad happened. The sun was shining very bright and hot. The crayons started to melt. They became soft and sticky. They made a mess on the paper and on their hands.
"Uh-oh, what's happening?" Mia asked, looking at her blue crayon. It was not a tube anymore. It was a blob.
"Our crayons are melting!" Tim said, dropping his green crayon. It left a stain on the floor.
They tried to pick up the other crayons, but they were all melted too. They were frustrated. They could not draw anymore.
"Mommy, mommy, help!" they cried.
Mommy came and saw the melted crayons. She was not angry. She was sorry for them.
"Oh, you poor things. The sun was too hot for your crayons. Don't worry, I have a solution. Come with me." She said.
She took them to the kitchen and gave them some ice cubes. She told them to put the ice cubes on the crayons. The ice cubes made the crayons cold and hard again. They became tubes again.
"Look, they are fixed!" Mia said, holding her blue crayon.
"Yay, thank you, mommy!" Tim said, holding his red crayon.
They hugged mommy and went back to their paper. They continued to draw, but they moved to a shady spot. They did not want their crayons to melt again. They were happy.

"Owls are shy," he said. "They like to sleep in the day and hunt in the night. If we make noise, they will fly away."
Lily nodded and watched the owl. She wondered what the owl was dreaming about. Maybe it was dreaming about mice, or frogs, or stars. She wished she could fly like the owl, and see the woods from above.
The owl opened its eyes and looked at Lily. It blinked and tilted its head. Then it made a sound like "hoo, hoo". Lily smiled and whispered "hoo, hoo" back. The owl seemed to like that. It flapped its wings and flew to another branch, closer to Lily.
Lily reached out her hand, hoping the owl would come closer. But her dad held her back.
"Owls are not easy to touch," he said. "They have sharp claws and beaks. They might hurt you if you try to pet them. They are wild animals, not pets."
Lily felt sad. She wanted to be friends with the owl. But she understood that the owl was not like her dog, or her cat, or her teddy bear. The owl had its own life, and its own home, in the woods.
She waved goodbye to the owl, and said "hoo, hoo" one more time. The owl nodded and said "hoo, hoo" too. Then it flew away, into the shadows of the trees.
Lily and her dad continued their walk, happy to have seen the owl. Lily hoped to see it again, someday. She knew it was a special moment, that she would always remember.

He asked Lila and Ben to stop making noise and go away. But they did not listen. They kept marching and making noise.
The old man got very angry. He shouted at Lila and Ben. He told them they were rude and selfish. He told them they did not respect him or his book. He told them they should learn to be quiet and polite. He told them they should not bother people who are doing something they love.

He forgave them. He told them about his book. He told them stories of long ago. He told them stories of brave and wise people who did good things. He told them stories of how to be kind and respectful.
Lila and Ben listened with wonder. They learned a lot from the old man. They learned to be quiet and polite. They learned to not bother people who are doing something they love. They learned to appreciate ancient books and stories. They thanked the old man for his time and his wisdom. They gave him a hug and a smile. They went home happy and wiser.
The moral of the story is: Respect other people and their interests. Learn from ancient books and stories. Be quiet and polite.

Sara liked to help her mom with the clothes. She wanted to be a big girl and do what mom did. But mom said she was too little to use the iron. The iron was hot and could burn her. Sara did not listen. She was stubborn.
One day, mom was busy in the kitchen. Sara saw the iron on the table. She thought it looked fun. She grabbed the iron and tried to press a shirt. But the iron was very hot. It burned her hand. Sara screamed and dropped the iron. The iron fell on the floor and burned the carpet.
Mom heard Sara scream and ran to the room. She saw the iron, the shirt, the carpet and Sara's hand. She was angry and scared. She picked up Sara and put her hand under cold water. She said, "Sara, why did you touch the iron? I told you it was dangerous. You could have hurt yourself badly. You have to listen to me. You are not a big girl yet. You are a little girl who needs to be careful."
Sara cried and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to help you. I wanted to be like you. But the iron was too hot. It hurt me. I don't like the iron. I don't want to touch it again."
Mom hugged Sara and said, "I know you wanted to help me, but you have to wait until you are older. The iron is not a toy. It is a tool that only grown-ups can use. You have to be patient and learn from me. I love you, Sara. But you have to be less stubborn and more obedient."
Sara nodded and said, "I love you, mom. I will be less stubborn and more obedient. I will listen to you. Can I still help you with the clothes?"
Mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can. But only with the things that are safe for you. You can fold the clothes, sort the colors, and put them away. But you have to stay away from the iron. Do you understand?"
Sara said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I will stay away from the iron. I will do the safe things. Thank you, mom."
Mom kissed Sara and said, "You're welcome, Sara. You are a good girl. And you will be a big girl soon enough. But for now, you are my little girl. And I love you very much."

One day, a clumsy crocodile was walking by the river. He saw a big box with a ribbon on it. He was curious and wanted to see what was inside.
He tried to open the box with his teeth, but he could not. He tried to open the box with his claws, but he could not. He tried to open the box with his tail, but he could not. He was frustrated and angry.
He saw a monkey sitting on a tree. He asked the monkey, "How do I open this box?"
The monkey smiled and said, "You have to pull the ribbon. Then the box will open."
The crocodile did not believe the monkey. He thought the monkey was lying. He said, "No, you are trying to trick me. There is nothing in the box. You just want to laugh at me."
The monkey said, "No, I am telling the truth. There is a surprise in the box. You will like it. Trust me."
The crocodile was still doubtful, but he was also curious. He decided to try the monkey's advice. He pulled the ribbon with his teeth. The box opened.
Inside the box, there was a big cake with candles on it. The cake had the words, "Happy Birthday, Crocodile!" written on it. The crocodile was surprised and happy. He did not know it was his birthday.
The monkey said, "Surprise! I made this cake for you. You are my friend. Happy birthday, Crocodile!"
The crocodile smiled and said, "Thank you, Monkey. You are my friend too. I am sorry I did not trust you. You are very kind and smart."
The monkey and the crocodile hugged and shared the cake. They had a fun and sweet birthday party. The crocodile learned to be more open and less clumsy.

Lily and Max were playing in the backyard. They had a big box and some old clothes. They wanted to make a fort.
"Let's put this shirt over the box," Lily said. "It will be our roof."
"OK," Max said. He helped Lily put the shirt over the box. Then they crawled inside.
They had some toys and books in the box. They pretended they were in a secret place. They had fun.
But after a while, Max felt uncomfortable. The box was too small and hot. He wanted to get out.
"Lily, I want to quit," he said. "I don't like the fort. It's too tight and warm."
Lily looked at him. She liked the fort. She didn't want to quit.
"No, Max, don't quit," she said. "The fort is cool. We can play more games."
But Max shook his head. He pushed the shirt away and crawled out of the box. He saw a big saw on the ground. It was Daddy's saw. He wanted to play with it.
"Look, Lily, a saw!" he said. "Let's play with the saw. It's more fun."
Lily followed him. She saw the saw too. But she knew it was dangerous. She remembered what Mommy and Daddy said.
"Max, no, don't touch the saw!" she said. "The saw is sharp. It can hurt you. Mommy and Daddy said no."
But Max didn't listen. He grabbed the saw and tried to cut the box. He made a loud noise.
Lily was scared. She ran to the house and called Mommy and Daddy.
"Mommy, Daddy, help!" she said. "Max is playing with the saw. He can get hurt. Please come!"
Mommy and Daddy heard Lily. They ran to the backyard. They saw Max with the saw. They were angry and worried.
"Max, stop!" they said. "Put down the saw. Now!"
Max dropped the saw. He looked at Mommy and Daddy. He knew he was in trouble.
"I'm sorry," he said. "I just wanted to play."
Mommy and Daddy hugged him. They were glad he was OK.
"Max, you can't play with the saw," they said. "The saw is not a toy. It's very dangerous. You could have cut yourself or Lily or the box. You have to listen to us. We love you and we want you to be safe."
Max nodded. He felt sorry and sad.

One day, Lily's mom had to go to the store and asked Lily to stay with her dad. Lily said okay and went to her room to play. She took her gas stove and her doll and put them on the floor. She said to her doll, "We are going to make a yummy soup. Do you want some?" The doll did not answer, but Lily believed that she did.
Lily turned the knob on the gas stove and made a sound with her mouth. She pretended to put some water and some vegetables in a pot and put it on the stove. She said, "The soup is cooking. It will be ready soon." She smiled and hugged her doll.
But Lily did not know that the gas stove was not a toy. It was a real gas stove that her dad had bought to fix. He had left it in Lily's room by mistake. He had not connected it to the gas pipe, but there was still some gas inside it. When Lily turned the knob, the gas came out and filled the room.
Lily did not smell the gas, because she had a cold. She did not see the gas, because it was invisible. She did not hear the gas, because it was silent. She only heard her own sound and her doll's voice in her head.
Soon, Lily's dad came to check on her. He opened the door and smelled the gas. He saw Lily and her doll on the floor, with the gas stove next to them. He was very scared. He ran to Lily and picked her up. He turned off the gas stove and opened the window. He said, "Lily, Lily, are you okay? You should not play with the gas stove. It is very dangerous. It can make a big boom and hurt you."
Lily was confused. She said, "But dad, it is not a gas stove. It is a toy. I was making soup for me and my doll. We were having fun."
Lily's dad hugged her and said, "I know, Lily, I know. But it is not a toy. It is a gas stove. And gas is not for playing. It is for cooking. But only when mom or dad are with you. Do you understand?"
Lily nodded and said, "I understand, dad. I am sorry. I will not play with the gas stove again. I will only play with my toys."
Lily's dad said, "That's good, Lily. That's very good. I love you, Lily. And I am glad you are safe."
He kissed her and took her to the living room. He gave her some juice and a cookie. He said, "Let's watch some TV, okay?"
Lily said, "Okay, dad. Can I bring my doll?"
Lily's dad said, "Of course, Lily. You can bring your doll. She is a very nice doll. And I believe she likes soup."

One day, a big and loud car came to the park. It was red and shiny and had a siren. The car stopped near Timmy and Spot. A man in a blue suit got out of the car. He had a badge and a hat. He looked at Timmy and Spot and said, "Hello, little boy. Is this your dog?"
Timmy nodded and said, "Yes, this is Spot. He is my best friend."
The man smiled and said, "He is a nice dog. But he needs a collar and a leash. Do you have them?"
Timmy shook his head and said, "No, I don't. Spot does not like collars and leashes. He likes to be free."
The man frowned and said, "I'm sorry, but that is not safe. All dogs must have collars and leashes in the park. It is the rule. If you don't have them, I have to take your dog to the shelter."
Timmy felt frightened and said, "No, please don't take Spot. He is not a bad dog. He is a good dog. He loves me and I love him."
Spot felt frightened too. He barked and growled at the man. He did not want to go with the man. He wanted to stay with Timmy. He bit the man's hand and tried to run away. But the man grabbed Spot's fur and pulled him to the car. Spot was scared and angry. He tore the man's sleeve and collar with his teeth.
The man shouted and let go of Spot. He was hurt and angry. He said, "Bad dog! Bad dog! You are in trouble now. I will call for backup."
Timmy ran to Spot and hugged him. He said, "Spot, you are brave. You saved us. Let's go home. Let's go home fast."
Timmy and Spot ran away from the park. They ran to their house. They were safe and happy. They did not like the man in the blue suit. They did not like the big and loud car. They did not like the rule. They liked each other. They were best friends.

One day, they see a dog in the park. The dog is thin and has a hurt leg. The dog looks sad and scared. Ben and Sam want to help the dog.
"Hello, dog," Ben says. "What is your name? Where is your home?"
The dog does not answer. The dog just whimpers and licks his leg.
"Maybe he is hungry," Sam says. "Let's give him some food."
Ben and Sam run to their bags and get some bread and cheese. They break them into small pieces and put them on the ground near the dog.
"Here, dog," Sam says. "Eat some food. It will make you feel better."
The dog smells the food and comes closer. He eats the bread and cheese. He wags his tail and looks at Ben and Sam.
"Good dog," Ben says. "Do you want to be our friend?"
The dog barks and licks Ben's hand. He answers yes. Ben and Sam smile and hug the dog.
They decide to call him Spot. They take him to the vet and get him a bandage for his leg. They ask their moms if they can keep him. Their moms say yes.
Ben and Sam are happy. They have a new friend. Spot is happy too. He has a new home. They play in the park every day. They have fun.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play with books and paper. One day, they find a big machine in the basement. It has buttons and a screen and a tray.
"What is this?" Lily asks.
"I don't know. Maybe it can make prints," Tom says.
They push some buttons and the machine makes a loud noise. It spits out paper with words and pictures on it.
"Wow, look!" Tom says. He picks up a paper with a cat on it.
"Can I have one?" Lily asks. She pushes another button and the machine makes another noise. It spits out a paper with a dog on it.
They are happy. They make more prints of animals and flowers and cars. They fill the tray with paper.
But then, something goes wrong. The machine starts to make a terrible noise. It spits out paper with no words and no pictures. Just black and white lines and dots.
"Oh no, what did we do?" Lily says.
The machine does not stop. It spits out more and more paper. The paper piles up on the floor. The paper covers the buttons and the screen and the tray.
"Help, help!" Tom says.
They try to run away, but the paper blocks the door. They are trapped.
They blink and cry. They are scared.
They hear footsteps on the stairs. It is Lily's mom. She hears the noise and the cries. She opens the door and sees the mess.
"What is going on here?" she says.
She turns off the machine and frees the children. She hugs them and calms them down.
She explains that the machine is a printer. It can make prints of things on the computer. But they should not play with it without asking. It can break or run out of ink or paper.
She helps them clean up the paper. She tells them to be more careful next time.
They say they are sorry. They promise to be good.
They learn a lesson. They still like prints, but they prefer books and paper.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with blocks and cars. One day, they find a big ruler in the kitchen. They want to measure things with it.
"Let's measure the table," Tom says. He puts the ruler on the table and counts the numbers. "The table is ten long."
"Let's measure the oven," Sam says. He opens the oven door and puts the ruler inside. "The oven is five long."
But the oven is not clean. It has grease and crumbs and dirt. And the oven is not cold. It has heat. The heat is very hot. It burns the ruler and Sam's hand.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Sam cries. He drops the ruler and pulls his hand out. His hand is red and sore. He runs to Mom and shows her his hand.
Mom is angry and scared. She takes Sam to the sink and puts cold water on his hand. She says, "Why did you put the ruler in the oven? That was very silly and dangerous. The oven has heat. Heat can hurt you. And the oven is not clean. It has germs. Germs can make you sick. You are a naughty boy, Sam."
Tom feels sorry for Sam. He says, "I'm sorry, Sam. I didn't know the oven was hot and dirty. I just wanted to measure it."
Mom says, "You should not play with the ruler. It is not a toy. It is a tool. And you should not touch the oven. It is not a game. It is a machine. You should only play with your blocks and cars. They are safe and fun. And you should listen to me. I know what is good and bad for you. Do you understand?"
Tom and Sam nod their heads. They say, "Yes, Mom. We understand."
Mom hugs them and says, "I love you, Tom and Sam. But you have to be careful and smart. Now, let me see your hand, Sam. We have to go to the doctor. He will make it better."
Tom and Sam are sad and scared. They don't like the doctor. He has needles and bandages. They wish they never found the ruler. They wish they never measured the oven. They wish they played with their blocks and cars. They learned a hard lesson.

"Of course, you can," Lily said, opening the frame. "You are very polite. Do you want some tea?"
"Yes, please," Ben said, sitting on a cushion. Lily poured some water from a bottle cap into a thimble. They pretended to sip their tea and chat.
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was their mom, coming home from work. She saw the frame on the floor and picked it up.
"Oh, what a nice frame," she said. "I wonder where it came from. I think I'll hang it on the wall."
She did not see Ben and Lily inside the frame. They were too small. They shouted and waved, but their mom did not hear them.
"Help, help!" Ben cried. "We are in the frame!"
"How did we shrink?" Lily asked. "We need to get out!"
They looked around and saw a window in the frame. They ran to it and pushed it open. They saw a bird outside. They hoped it would not eat them.
"Maybe we can fly with the bird," Ben said. "Maybe it will take us to our mom."
They climbed on the bird's back and held on tight. The bird flew away with them. They hoped it would not fly too far. They wanted to go back to their mom and their toys. They wanted to be big again.

"Help me, Tom!" she cried. "My dress is stuck!"
Tom heard Jen. He ran back to the slide. He saw Jen's dress. He pulled it hard. It did not come off. He pulled harder. It ripped.
Jen was free. She slid down the slide. She was happy. But she was also sad. Her dress was ruined.
"I'm sorry, Jen," Tom said. "I did not mean to rip your dress."
"It's okay, Tom," Jen said. "You helped me. You are a good friend."
They hugged. They knew they were still friends. They knew summer was not over. They knew they could play again. But they also knew they had to be careful with their clothes.

One day, Timmy and Spot were playing fetch with a ball. Timmy threw the ball and Spot ran after it. He caught it in his mouth and brought it back to Timmy. They did this many times, until Spot got tired and lay down on the grass. Timmy sat next to him and petted his head.
"Spot, you are a good dog," Timmy said. "You are my best friend. Do you like playing with me?"
Spot wagged his tail and licked Timmy's face. He barked softly and looked at Timmy with his big eyes. He liked playing with Timmy very much. He was happy to have him as his friend.
"Spot, I have a question for you," Timmy said. "Why do you have paws and I have hands? What can you do with your paws that I can't do with my hands?"
Spot tilted his head and thought for a moment. He did not know the answer to Timmy's question. He only knew that his paws were part of him, and that he used them for many things. He used them to walk, to scratch, to dig, to hold his ball, and to touch Timmy.
"Spot, can you talk to me with your paws?" Timmy asked. "Can you show me what you mean with your paws?"
Spot nodded and got up. He wanted to show Timmy what he could do with his paws. He walked over to a tree and scratched it with his front paw. He was telling Timmy that he liked to mark his territory. He walked over to a hole and dug it deeper with his back paw. He was telling Timmy that he liked to hide his bones. He walked over to his ball and picked it up with his mouth. He dropped it in front of Timmy and nudged it with his paw. He was telling Timmy that he wanted to play some more.
Timmy smiled and picked up the ball. He threw it again and Spot ran after it. He caught it and brought it back. They repeated this game until they were both tired and happy. They lay down on the grass again and cuddled.
"Spot, you are very smart," Timmy said. "You can talk to me with your paws. You can tell me many things. I can understand you. You are not just a dog. You are a serious dog. And I love you."
Spot wagged his tail and licked Timmy's face. He barked softly and looked at Timmy with his big eyes. He loved him too. He was not just a boy. He was a serious boy. And he was his best friend.

Lila and Ben were playing in the park when it started to rain. They ran to the big tree to stay dry, but the rain was too heavy and they got wet.
"Let's go to the shelter!" Ben said. He pointed to the small house near the swings, where the park workers kept their tools and things. "It has a roof and a door and we can be warm and dry there."
But Lila did not want to go. She liked the big tree and she was not afraid of the rain. She was stubborn and said no.
"I want to stay here!" she said. "The tree is my friend and it protects me. The shelter is dark and scary and it has spiders and rats. I don't like it there."
Ben tried to make her change her mind. He said the tree was not a good friend, because it let the rain fall on them. He said the shelter was not dark and scary, because it had a window and a light. He said there were no spiders and rats, because the park workers cleaned it every day. He insisted that they should go, because they would catch a cold if they stayed wet.
But Lila did not listen. She shook her head and hugged the tree. She said she was fine and she did not care about the cold. She insisted that they should stay, because the tree was the best place in the park.
They argued and argued, until they heard a loud noise. It was thunder, and it made them both jump. Then they saw a bright flash. It was lightning, and it struck the big tree. The tree cracked and fell, and Lila and Ben screamed.
They ran away from the tree, and saw that it was on fire. They were scared and sad, and they wished they had listened to Ben. They ran to the shelter, and knocked on the door. The park worker opened it, and let them in. He gave them towels and blankets, and made them hot chocolate. He said they were lucky, and they should always be careful in a storm.
Lila and Ben nodded, and thanked him. They looked at each other, and said they were sorry. They hugged, and promised to be less stubborn and more smart. They learned their lesson, and they never argued about the shelter again.

Sarah was tired. She slowly walked out the door and into the woods. All alone she searched for something special. Suddenly, she stopped when she saw a glimmer in the corner of her eye. She saw a glittering piece of string! It sparkled like a rainbow and Sarah smiled. She quickly grabbed it and put it in her pocket.
Sarah kept walking and soon felt a sudden urge to hide. She clambered under a nearby bush and waited. Soon enough, a long and tall creature appeared behind her. It had a big red nose and long gangly arms. She recognized it as a clown!
The clown frowned and shouted "Where is my string? I must have it!" He started frantically searching around. Sarah grabbed the string out of her pocket, not wanting the clown to find it. Suddenly, the clown spotted Sarah and demanded she hand him the string. Without a second thought, Sarah quickly gave it to him.
The clown smiled, grabbed the string and started to twirl it above his head. Then, he started to laugh. He had been playing hide and seek the entire time! He thanked Sarah for playing and waved goodbye.
Sarah was relieved. Even though she was tired, she was glad she found the string and could help the clown. She smiled to herself. It's funny how one small thing, like a string, can make all the difference.

The dog said to the cat, "Come and play in the water with me. It is fun!" The cat said, "No, I do not like the water. My foot is wet, and I do not like it." The dog laughed and jumped back in the water.
The cat sat by the pond and watched the dog play. Then, the dog got out of the water and shook off the wet. The cat got wet too! The dog said, "I am sorry, I did not mean to get you wet." The cat said, "It is okay. I will tell you when I want to play in the water."
The moral of the story is to listen to your friends and respect their likes and dislikes.

Tom and Anna were friends who liked to play together. One day, they saw a big hill near their house. They wanted to climb the hill and see what was on the other side.
But Tom was scared of the hill. He said it was too high and steep. He said he might fall and hurt himself. He said he wanted to go back home.
Anna was not scared of the hill. She said it was fun and exciting. She said they could see many things from the top. She said she would help Tom and hold his hand. She said she would encourage him and say nice words to him. She said she would not leave him alone.
She made a promise to Tom. She said, "If you climb the hill with me, I will give you a big hug and a cookie. And I will be your best friend forever. Do you trust me?"
Tom looked at Anna. He saw that she was smiling and kind. He saw that she was not busy or bored. He saw that she really wanted to play with him. He felt a little brave and a little curious. He said, "Okay, I will try. But you have to keep your promise."
Anna nodded and hugged Tom. They held hands and started to climb the hill. Anna encouraged Tom and said nice words to him. She said, "You are doing great, Tom. You are strong and smart. You can do it, Tom. I am proud of you."
Tom listened to Anna and felt better. He said, "Thank you, Anna. You are a good friend. You are sweet and funny. You make me happy."
They climbed and climbed until they reached the top of the hill. They saw the sun and the sky and the trees and the flowers. They saw their house and their parents and their toys. They saw a lot of things that they had never seen before. They felt happy and amazed.
They hugged each other and ate the cookie that Anna had brought. They kept their promise and became best friends forever. They learned that climbing hills can be fun and rewarding. They learned that being scared is normal, but being brave is better. They learned that encouraging and trusting each other can make them stronger and happier. They learned a lot from their adventure.

The big, crazy bird had an idea. It took the little pencil on a fun adventure. They flew high in the sky and saw many beautiful things. The little pencil felt happy and stopped crying. When they came back, the little pencil felt special and loved. It learned that it was okay to be different and that every pencil is special in its own way.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big slide that looked very fun. Sara wanted to try it, but Ben was scared. He said, "No, Sara, it is too high. We might fall and hurt ourselves."
Sara said, "Don't be scared, Ben. I will go first and show you how to slide. You just have to trust me and yourself. We can do it together. It will be fun, like flying."
Ben was not sure, but he loved his sister and wanted to make her happy. He nodded and followed her to the slide. Sara climbed up the ladder and sat on the edge. She smiled at Ben and said, "Ready? One, two, three, go!"
Sara slid down the slide, feeling the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She laughed and shouted, "Whee! This is awesome!" She landed on the soft grass and looked up at Ben, who was still on the ladder. She said, "Come on, Ben, you can do it. I will catch you."
Ben looked at the slide, then at Sara, then at the slide again. He felt a little spirit in his heart, telling him to be brave and try something new. He took a deep breath and slid down the slide, feeling the same wind and sun as Sara. He also laughed and shouted, "Whee! This is awesome!" He landed in Sara's arms and hugged her. He said, "Thank you, Sara, for helping me. That was fun. I trust you and myself."
Sara hugged him back and said, "You're welcome, Ben, for trying. You were brave. I'm proud of you."
They ran to their mom, who was watching them from a bench. She smiled and said, "You two look happy. Did you have fun on the slide?"
Sara and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, mom, we did. It was yummy, like ice cream."
Mom said, "That's great. I'm glad you enjoyed it. And I'm glad you trusted each other and yourselves. That's how you learn and grow. Trust is a good thing to have."
Sara and Ben agreed and hugged their mom. They learned a new thing that day: trust can make you happy and strong.

Once upon a time there was a charming bear named Jack. He liked to hide all of his secrets in the biggest tree in the forest. Jack had a big promise that he kept secret from everyone. One day, he decided to tell his secret to his best friend, Tibby the rabbit. Tibby was very excited and he vowed to keep Jack's promise a secret forever. 
So every day, Jack and Tibby would hide together in the tallest tree in the forest and share secrets. They would whisper and giggle together, while they looked down and watched the birds soar around the treetops.
But one day, something changed. Jack was very sad and he couldn't bear to tell Tibby the reason why. Tibby begged and pleaded until finally Jack opened up and told Tibby the truth - he was going to have to leave the forest and go to a far away land. 
Tibby was very upset, but he knew he had to hide his tears so they wouldn't upset Jack. So every night, Tibby would sneak up to the tallest tree, just like they always did, and whisper promises to Jack that he would be waiting for him when Jack returned. Jack was so touched by this gesture, he gave Tibby one last big hug before he said goodbye. 
And although Jack moved away, the memory of his charming smile and sweet promises will remain hidden in the heart of Tibby for many years to come

The car saw a little boy playing with a ball near a big puddle. The car wanted to have fun, so it went fast and splashed the water. The water went "slap" on the boy, and he got wet, too. The boy was sad and started to cry.
The car felt bad for making the boy cry. It knew it was not nice to make others wet and sad. So, the car said sorry to the boy and they became friends. They played together and had fun. The car learned to be kind and not to splash water on others. The moral of the story is to always think about how your actions can affect others and to be kind to everyone.

But then, Sara sees a yellow car in the case. She likes the yellow car. She wants to play with it. She says to Ben, "Can I have the yellow car, please?"
Ben looks at the yellow car. He likes it too. He says to Sara, "No, I want the yellow car. It is mine."
Sara and Ben start to argue. They both pull the yellow car. They are not happy. They make angry noises.
Mama hears them. She comes to see what is wrong. She sees Sara and Ben fighting over the yellow car. She says to them, "Stop, stop. Why are you fighting? You have many cars in the case. You can share the yellow car. Or you can play with other cars. There are enough cars for both of you."
Sara and Ben listen to Mama. They feel sorry. They say to each other, "Sorry, sorry. I don't want to fight. You can have the yellow car. Or we can take turns. Or we can play with other cars. There are many cars in the case. We can find cars that fit our hands and our colors."
Sara and Ben hug each other. They are happy again. They set the yellow car on the floor and say, "Let's play together. We can make the cars go vroom vroom. We can have fun with our cars and our case."

Peter was overjoyed and ran around to the other side of the fence. His parents watched in surprise as the truck let their son take the wheel. Together, the loyal truck and Peter drove around the town, happily as can be!

"What is that boat doing?" Lily asked.
"I don't know. Maybe they are fishing," Ben said.
They were nosy. They wanted to see what the boat had in the net. They ran closer to the water. They saw something big and gray in the net. It had a tail and a fin. It was a whale.
"Oh no! They caught a whale!" Lily cried.
"That's not nice. Whales are good. They should let it go," Ben said.
They shouted at the boat. "Let the whale go! Let the whale go!"
But the boat did not hear them. It started to move away. The whale was still in the net. It looked sad and scared.
Lily and Ben felt bad. They wished they could help the whale. They regretted being nosy. They should have stayed away from the boat.
They went back to their mom and dad. They told them what they saw. Their mom and dad hugged them and said they were sorry.
"Sometimes people do bad things to animals. But there are also good people who try to protect them. Maybe someone will save the whale," their mom said.
"Can we do something to help the whales?" Lily asked.
"Yes, we can. We can learn more about them and why they are important. We can tell others to be kind to them. We can join groups that care for them," their dad said.
Lily and Ben nodded. They wanted to be good to the whales. They hoped the whale in the net would be free soon. They prayed for the whale. They never forgot the whale.
