"Let's see who can do more exercises," Tim said. "We can count how many we do. Like this: one, two, three, four..."
He started to do jumping jacks. Lily nodded and joined him. She said the numbers too. They did ten jumping jacks, then ten push-ups, then ten sit-ups. They were tired, but happy.
"Let's do more," Tim said. "How about we do twenty of each?"
Lily shook her head. She was too tired. She wanted to rest.
"No, thank you," she said. "I think ten is enough. You can do more if you want, but I'm done."
Tim frowned. He wanted to do more. He wanted to win. He thought Lily was lazy. He was not generous. He did not share his game.
"Fine," he said. "But I'm going to do more. And I'm going to count louder. Like this: ONE, TWO, THREE, FOUR..."
He started to do more jumping jacks. He counted very loud. He did not care if Lily heard him. He did not care if he hurt her feelings. He did twenty jumping jacks, then twenty push-ups, then twenty sit-ups. He was very tired, but proud.
"I did it," he said. "I did more than you. I win. You lose. Ha ha ha."
He looked at Lily. He expected her to be sad. He expected her to say sorry. He expected her to ask him to play again. But she did not.
She looked at him. She was not sad. She was angry. She did not say sorry. She did not ask him to play again. She said something else.
"You are mean," she said. "You are not my friend. You are not fun. You are loud. You are rude. You are selfish. I don't like you. Go away."
She got up and left. She took her toys with her. She did not look back. She did not say goodbye.
Tim was shocked. He did not expect that. He did not like that. He felt bad. He felt lonely. He felt sorry. He wanted to say sorry. He wanted to play again. He wanted to be friends. But it was too late.
Lily was gone. The game was over. The end.

But Tim did not listen. He grabbed the palm branch and started to swing. Suddenly, the branch broke, and Tim fell to the ground. He was not hurt, but he was very sad. Lily came over and said, "It's okay, Tim. We can find a safer game to play together."
In the end, Tim learned that it is important to listen to his friends and choose safe games to play. He and Lily found a fun game to play, and they were not bored anymore. The moral of the story is to always listen to your friends and make safe choices.

But as she was walking away, the flea spoke. "Please don't pinch me!" it said. Mika was so amazed that the flea could talk, she stopped and listened. 
"I know it might seem strange," the flea continued, "but I'm a famous flea! I travel the world on my own, exploring and learning new things. I like to travel with different animals, too. 
Mika thought hard. She knew the flea was telling the truth, so she decided to let the flea go and wished it a safe journey. The flea thanked her and leapt away. 
Mika smiled, feeling happy for the famous flea. She waved goodbye and continued to explore the park.

"Let's ask the lady," Sam said.
They ran to the lady and the dog. They arrived near them and said hello.
"Hello, children. This is Coco. She is a good dog. Do you want to pet her?" the lady asked.
"Yes, please!" Lila and Sam said.
They reached out their hands to touch Coco. Coco wagged her tail and licked their faces. Lila and Sam giggled.
But then, another dog came. It was black and skinny. It looked angry and mean. It barked loudly and ran towards Coco. Coco barked back and tried to protect the lady and the children.
"Go away, bad dog!" the lady shouted.
Lila and Sam were scared. They hugged the lady and Coco. They hoped the bad dog would leave.
A man came. He was the bad dog's owner. He had a leash and a collar. He grabbed the bad dog and put the collar on him.
"I'm sorry, I'm sorry. He escaped from the yard. He is not friendly. I'm sorry," the man said.
The lady was mad. She said, "You should be more careful. Your dog could have hurt us. You should train him better."
The man said, "I know, I know. I'm sorry. Come on, let's go." He pulled the bad dog away.
The lady said, "Are you okay, children?"
Lila and Sam nodded. They said, "Yes, we are okay. Thank you for letting us pet Coco. She is a nice dog."
The lady smiled. She said, "You're welcome. Coco likes you too. You are brave and kind. Do you want to walk with us for a while?"
Lila and Sam looked at each other. They said, "Yes, please!"
They walked with the lady and Coco. They felt happy and safe. They liked the park again.

Bob was a happy little boy who had a very special toy. It was a big gray rock- it looked like it had something inside it. Bob's mom told him to be careful, that the rock was dangerous.
Bob wanted to find out what was in the rock. So one day he found a stick and started poking around the rock. As Bob poked and prodded, something inside it began to shake. Suddenly a flap opened and out flew some ash!
Bob was so excited, he finally discovered what was inside the rock. He wanted to tell his mom but he knew she said it was dangerous and so he stayed away from it. He kept the rock hidden in his room.
One day, just when Bob was about to show his mom the rock, fire trucks pulled up to the house. Bob realized that the ash inside the rock was really a firefly, and it had come back to its home. Bob knew the firefly belonged in the rock, so he carefully opened the rock and the firefly flew away. 
Bob was happy that the firefly could find its home. It showed him that the rock was special and everything belonged just where it should.

"Mommy, I'm scared," said Tommy.
"That's okay, Tommy. Just make sure to stay away so it can't hurt you," replied Mommy.
Tommy watched the jellyfish carefully and tried his best to resist the urge to touch it. He didn't want to have to go to the hospital.
Mommy noticed Tommy was having difficulty, so she encouraged him, "You can do it, Tommy. You are brave, and you can resist it."
Tommy nodded and slowly took a few steps away from the jellyfish. Finally, he felt brave enough to look away from the jellyfish and back up the beach.
"Good job, Tommy! You were so brave," said Mommy.
Tommy smiled and the two of them went back up to the beach, away from the fearful jellyfish.

Lily was scared. She had to go to the doctor and get a needle. She did not like needles. They hurt and made her cry. She held her teddy bear tight and shook.
Her mom was with her. She hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, sweetie. The doctor is nice. He will be gentle and quick. The needle will help you stay healthy. You are brave and strong."
They went into the room. The doctor smiled and said hello. He had a white coat and a stethoscope. He looked at Lily's eyes, ears, and throat. He listened to her heart and lungs. He said, "You are doing great, Lily. You are a good girl."
Then he took out a needle. It was small and shiny. Lily saw it and shook more. She buried her face in her teddy bear. She said, "No, no, no!"
The doctor was compassionate. He understood that Lily was afraid. He said, "I know, Lily. Needles are not fun. But they are not so bad. They only pinch a little bit. And then they are done. And you get a sticker and a lollipop. How about that?"
He asked Lily's mom to hold her hand. He said, "Look at your teddy bear, Lily. He is not scared. He is proud of you. Can you be brave like him?" He counted to three and gave Lily the needle. It was over in a second.
Lily felt a sting. She whimpered. But then it was gone. She looked at her arm. There was a band-aid with a star on it. The doctor said, "You did it, Lily! You are amazing! You are a star!" He gave her a sticker and a lollipop. He said, "You can choose any flavor you want."
Lily smiled. She said, "Thank you, doctor. You are nice." She picked a cherry lollipop. She licked it and hugged her teddy bear. She said, "I'm brave. I'm strong. I'm a star." She was not scared anymore.

Tim and Sue went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and giraffes. They were very happy and excited.
Then they came to the ostrich pen. The ostrich was a big bird with long legs and a long neck. It had black and white feathers and a small head. Tim and Sue wanted to see its face, but the ostrich was hiding it in the sand.
"Why is the ostrich doing that?" Tim asked Mom.
Mom said, "The ostrich is shy. Sometimes it thinks that if it puts its head in the sand, no one can see it. But that is not true. We can still see its body."
Tim and Sue thought that was funny. They laughed and said, "Silly ostrich, we can see you!"
The ostrich heard them and lifted its head. It looked at Tim and Sue with big eyes. It felt ashamed that they saw it hiding. It wanted to run away, but it could not. It was in a pen.
The ostrich said, "Please don't laugh at me. I am scared of people. They are loud and big and strange. I feel safer in the sand."
Tim and Sue felt sorry for the ostrich. They stopped laughing and said, "We are sorry, ostrich. We did not mean to hurt your feelings. We are not loud or big or strange. We are just kids. We like animals. We want to be your friends."
The ostrich felt a little better. It said, "Thank you, kids. You are kind and nice. Maybe you can be my friends. But please don't come too close. I need some space."
Tim and Sue nodded. They said, "OK, ostrich. We understand. We will give you some space. But we will also wave to you and say hello. Maybe one day you will not be so shy."
The ostrich smiled. It said, "Maybe one day. Thank you, kids. You are good friends."
Tim and Sue smiled back. They said, "You are welcome, ostrich. You are a good friend too."
They waved to the ostrich and said goodbye. They went to see other animals, but they did not forget the ostrich. They learned that sometimes animals need to hide, and sometimes they need to reveal. They learned to be respectful and gentle. They learned to be good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. He was three years old and liked to call his shadow wherever he went. One day, something very strange happened. When Jack called his shadow, it didn't come. He called louder and louder but the shadow was not there.
He looked around and found a broken mirror. He peered into the broken bits of glass and saw something he wasn't expecting. There, in the broken mirror, he saw his shadow, looking back at him.
"Hello!" said Jack, "why won't you come to me?"
His shadow replied, "I can't come to you. I'm stuck in the broken mirror. Please help me!"
Jack was determined to help his shadow. He thought and thought about how he could get the shadow out of the mirror. After a few minutes, he had an idea. He picked up the broken mirror and brought it outside. When the sunshine hit the mirror, the pieces of glass came together, and the shadow was free!
The shadow happily followed Jack wherever he went. From that day forward, Jack and his shadow were best friends, and they never got separated again!

Anna loved to draw with her crayons. She had many colors and shapes to make on her paper. She liked to draw her family, her friends, and her toys. Sometimes, she drew things that she saw in her dreams.
One night, she had a very special dream. She dreamed that she was in a big garden with many flowers and butterflies. She saw a big rainbow in the sky. She wanted to draw the rainbow with her crayons, but she did not have them with her. She looked around and saw a fairy sitting on a mushroom. The fairy smiled and said, "Hello, Anna. Do you like my garden?"
Anna nodded and said, "Yes, it is very pretty. But I want to draw it with my crayons. Do you have any crayons?"
The fairy laughed and said, "I don't have crayons, but I have something better. I have magic dust. You can use it to draw anything you want in the air. Just close your eyes and imagine what you want to draw. Then, open your eyes and sprinkle some magic dust. You will see your drawing come to life."
Anna was very excited. She closed her eyes and imagined a big rainbow. She opened her eyes and sprinkled some magic dust. She saw a bright and colorful rainbow appear in the air. She clapped her hands and said, "Wow, this is amazing. Thank you, fairy."
The fairy said, "You're welcome, Anna. You can draw anything you want with my magic dust. But remember, this is only a dream. When you wake up, your drawings will be gone. So, enjoy them while you can."
Anna nodded and said, "Okay, I will. Can I draw more things?"
The fairy said, "Of course, you can. Have fun, Anna."
Anna had fun drawing many things with the magic dust. She drew flowers, butterflies, stars, and hearts. She was very happy. She did not want to wake up. But soon, she heard a voice calling her name. It was her mom.
"Anna, wake up. It's time to get ready for school."
Anna opened her eyes and saw her mom standing by her bed. She rubbed her eyes and said, "Mom, I had a wonderful dream. I met a fairy who gave me magic dust. I drew a rainbow and many other things in the air. It was so beautiful."
Her mom smiled and said, "That sounds like a lovely dream, Anna. But now, you have to get up and get dressed. You can tell me more about your dream later. Maybe, you can draw it with your crayons."
Anna nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I will. But I wish I could keep the magic dust."
Her mom said, "Maybe, you can find it again in your next dream. But for now, you have to be alert and ready for school. Come on, let's go."
Anna got out of bed and followed her mom. She still felt the magic of her dream in her heart. She hoped to see the fairy again. She was glad she had her crayons to draw her dream. She thought, "Maybe, my crayons are magic too."

Anna and Ben nod. They sit on the chairs and watch the show. They see the dancers move and smile and clap. They see the dancers dance together and apart. They see the dancers dance with enthusiasm and grace and calm.
Anna and Ben are amazed. They clap and cheer. They look at each other and smile. They say, "Wow, they are so good! They can dance very well!"

Lily and Tom went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, elephants, and giraffes. But Lily and Tom liked the monkeys best. They watched them swing, jump, and play on the trees.
"Look, Mom, that monkey has a banana!" Lily said, pointing to a brown monkey with a yellow fruit.
"Yes, dear, monkeys love bananas. They peel them and eat them, just like you," Mom said.
"Can I give a banana to the monkey?" Tom asked.
"No, Tom, you can't. The monkeys have enough food from the zookeepers. If you give them your food, they might get sick or bite you," Dad said.
Tom felt sad. He wanted to be friends with the monkeys. He saw an empty cage next to the monkey enclosure. He had an idea. He ran to the cage and climbed inside. He pretended to be a monkey. He made noises and scratched his head.
"Look, Lily, I'm a monkey too!" Tom said.
Lily laughed. She thought Tom was funny. But the monkeys did not think so. They saw Tom in the cage and got angry. They thought he was a bad monkey who wanted to steal their bananas. They threw sticks and stones at him. They screeched and howled.
"Tom, get out of there! The monkeys are mad at you!" Lily shouted.
Tom was scared. He felt the sticks and stones hit him. He heard the monkeys yell at him. He wanted to get out of the cage, but he did not know how. He cried for help.
Mom and Dad heard Tom's cry. They ran to the cage and saw what happened. They were shocked and worried. They called a zookeeper to open the cage and get Tom out. The zookeeper came and unlocked the cage. He took Tom out and gave him a hug. He checked if Tom was hurt. He was not, but he had some bruises and scratches.
"Tom, what were you thinking? You could have been seriously hurt by the monkeys. You should never go into an animal cage. It's dangerous and wrong," the zookeeper said.
"I'm sorry, sir. I just wanted to be a monkey. I wanted to give them a banana. I didn't know they would be angry," Tom said.
"Well, Tom, you learned a hard lesson today. Monkeys are not like people. They have their own rules and habits. You can watch them and admire them, but you can't touch them or feed them. Do you understand?" the zookeeper said.
"Yes, sir. I understand. I won't do it again. I'm sorry, Mom and Dad. I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry, monkeys," Tom said.
Mom and Dad hugged Tom and forgave him. They thanked the zookeeper for his help. They decided to leave the zoo and go home. Lily and Tom said goodbye to the monkeys. The monkeys ignored them. They were busy eating their bananas.

Then, something unexpected happened. A tiny bug came and saw the rock's problem. The bug said, "I can fix your pants!" The rock did not believe the tiny bug could help. But the bug worked very hard and fixed the big hole in the rock's pants.
The rock was so happy and thanked the tiny bug. The friends all played together again. The rock learned that even small friends can do big things.

Jen and Ben are twins. They like to watch TV after school. But they do not like the same shows. Jen likes to watch cartoons. Ben likes to watch animals.
One day, they have a big fight. Jen wants to watch her cartoons. Ben wants to watch his animals. They both grab the remote and pull. They yell at each other.
"Let me watch my cartoons!" Jen says.
"No, let me watch my animals!" Ben says.
They do not share. They do not take turns. They are not fair.
Mom hears them and comes to the living room. She sees them fighting. She is not happy. She takes the remote and turns off the TV.
"Stop fighting, Jen and Ben!" Mom says. "You need to learn to share and take turns. That is fair."
She tells them to sit on the couch and talk. She gives them a paper and a crayon. She tells them to make a schedule.
"You can add the shows you want to watch on the paper. Then you can divide the time. One hour for Jen, one hour for Ben. That is fair." Mom says.
Jen and Ben look at the paper. They think for a while. They write down the shows they want to watch. They draw a line in the middle. They show Mom.
"Look, Mom, we made a schedule. We can share and take turns. That is fair." Jen and Ben say.
Mom smiles. She is proud of them. She gives them a hug and a kiss. She turns on the TV.
"Good job, Jen and Ben. You can watch your shows now. But remember to follow the schedule. That is fair." Mom says.
Jen and Ben nod. They sit on the couch and watch their shows. They do not fight. They are happy. They are fair.

One day, a 3 year old boy, Max, was in his classroom. He was sitting at a desk in front of a big blackboard. He liked the blackboard because it was big and blank - perfect for writing on. He took out a pencil and looked at it carefully. The pencil was sharp - its point pointing at him like an arrow. 
Max's teacher, Mrs. Smith, came into the classroom. She smiled at Max and said, "It's time to write! It's a slow day today, so we can take our time. Would you like to go first Max?"
Max looked at the sharp pencil again and grinned. "Yes, please!" he said. He picked up the pencil and carefully wrote his name on the blackboard - "Max Matson". It was slow but steady work.
Mrs. Smith smiled at him. "Perfect! Now it's your turn to show the class how it's done - do you think you can do it Max?" 
Max nodded, still holding his sharp pencil. He was proud of his work and was excited to show his classmates. He wrote slowly, carefully and neatly on the blackboard. Everyone in the classroom was amazed at how well he had done it.
Max smiled and waved his sharp pencil in the air. He had done it!

"Look, a ball!" Lily said. "Let's play with it!"
She ran to the ball and grabbed it with both hands. She threw it to Max. Max caught it and threw it back. They laughed and had fun.
But then a boy came to them. He was bigger and older. He had a mean face. He said, "That's my ball. Give it to me!"
He grabbed the ball from Max and pushed him. Max fell down and cried. Lily was angry and scared.
"No, that's not fair!" she said. "We were playing with it. You can't take it!"
She tried to grab the ball from the boy, but he was too strong. He held the ball high and said, "Too bad. It's mine. Go away!"
Lily and Max felt sad. They wanted to play with the ball. They looked around for help. They saw a lady on a bench. She was wearing a fit dress and a hat. She had a kind smile.
She saw what happened and came to them. She said, "Hello, children. What's the problem?"
Lily and Max told her what the boy did. The lady nodded and said, "That's not nice. He should share the ball with you. Let me talk to him."
She went to the boy and said, "Excuse me, young man. Is that your ball?"
The boy nodded and said, "Yes, it is. And it's mine. I don't want to share it."
The lady said, "Well, I'm sorry, but that's not how we play in the park. You have to be kind and respectful to others. If you want to play with the ball, you have to let others play too. Do you understand?"
The boy looked at the lady. He saw that she was serious and firm. He felt ashamed and sorry. He said, "Yes, I understand. I'm sorry. I was rude."
He gave the ball back to Lily and Max. He said, "Here, you can play with it. I'm sorry I pushed you and took it."
Lily and Max smiled and said, "Thank you. That's very nice of you. Do you want to play with us?"
The boy nodded and said, "Yes, I do. Can I be your friend?"
The lady smiled and said, "That's wonderful. You can be friends and have fun together. Just remember to share and be kind."
She watched them play with the ball. They threw it, kicked it and rolled it. They laughed and had fun. They were happy.

"Look, Lily, a bird!" Tom says. He points to the tree.
"I see it, Tom. It is pretty," Lily says. She smiles.
The bird looks at them. It opens its eye wide. It makes a loud sound. "Caw, caw, caw!"
Tom and Lily are scared. They hide behind a bench. They hold hands.
"What does the bird want, Tom?" Lily asks.
"I don't know, Lily. Maybe it wants to send us a message," Tom says.
"A message? What kind of message?" Lily asks.
Tom thinks. He remembers a story his mom told him. "Maybe it wants to tell us a secret. Maybe it knows something we don't know," he says.
Lily is curious. She wants to know the secret. She peeks from behind the bench. She sees the bird open its eye again. It winks at her.
"Tom, the bird is winking at me. Maybe it likes me," Lily says.
Tom is jealous. He wants the bird to like him too. He peeks from behind the bench. He sees the bird open its eye again. It winks at him.
"Lily, the bird is winking at me too. Maybe it likes us both," Tom says.
Lily and Tom are happy. They think the bird is their friend. They come out from behind the bench. They wave at the bird.
"Hello, bird. We are Tom and Lily. Do you want to play with us?" they ask.
The bird nods. It flies down from the tree. It lands on the bench. It opens its eye and winks at them. It makes a soft sound. "Caw, caw, caw!"
Tom and Lily laugh. They think the bird is saying hello. They pet the bird. They give it some bread. They play with the bird. They have fun. They are glad they met the bird with the red eye and the yellow beak.

She opened the cooler and found some ice-cream inside! She smiled and said, "Let's play a game! Who can hold the ice-cream the longest?"
Her friends all yelled out yeah and eagerly crowded around her.
One by one, they each tried to hold the ice-cream. But as they were all in the hot sun, it was too much! The ice-cream quickly melted away, leaving their hands sticky and cold.
Finally it was Elizabeth's turn. She wrapped her hands around the cooler and tugged hard - it was very heavy! But it was worth it - Elizabeth eventually managed to hold the ice-cream for the longest.
The sun was setting, but Elizabeth and her friends all had smiles on their faces. They celebrated their victory with a big cheer!

Lily and Ben are sad and angry. They say to Sam, "No, no, you broke our telephone! That was not nice! Go away, go away!" Sam is scared and sorry. He says, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I did not know. I just wanted to play." He runs away crying.
Lily and Ben look at the broken blocks. They feel bad for Sam, but they also miss their telephone. They wonder if they can build another one. They decide to try. They say, "Maybe we can find other blocks that are not so fragile. Maybe we can make a stronger telephone. Maybe we can let Sam play with us, if he is careful." They smile and hug each other. Suddenly, Jack stopped. "What is that?" he pointed to an old, rusty cooler in the corner of the meadow.
Jill smiled. "Let's open it up, and see what's inside!" 
Jack bent down, and opened the lid. Inside were two old, dusty bottles, filled with a wisp of fog.
Jill gasped excitedly. "I bet it's something magical!"
Jack smiled, and said, "only one way to find out!"
The duo took a bottle in each hand, and with a beaming smile, popped the cork of each bottle. A bright, glittering light filled the meadow and the old cooler disappeared. 
Jack and Jill were stunned, but not as stunned as when they realised: the fog had scattered and taken the shape of two lovey unicorns!

Lily was a big dog who liked to run and play in the park. She had a lot of friends, like Ben the cat, Max the bird, and Sam the squirrel. But she also had a lot of fleas, who liked to bite and itch her fur. Lily did not like the fleas, but she did not know how to get rid of them.
One day, she met a new friend, Tim the turtle. Tim was slow and quiet, but he was very kind and smart. He saw that Lily was scratching and shaking her head. He asked her, "What is wrong, Lily? Why are you so unhappy?"
Lily told him, "I have fleas, Tim. They are very bad. They make me itch and hurt. I wish they would go away."
Tim said, "I have an idea, Lily. Why don't you ride on my shell? I can take you to the pond, where the water is clean and cool. The water will wash away the fleas, and you will feel better."
Lily liked the idea. She said, "Thank you, Tim. You are a good friend. Can I ride on your shell now?"
Tim said, "Of course, Lily. Hop on, and hold on tight. I will take you to the pond."
Lily climbed on Tim's shell, and Tim started to walk slowly to the pond. Along the way, they saw Ben, Max, and Sam, who were curious and surprised to see Lily riding on Tim. They asked her, "What are you doing, Lily? Where are you going?"
Lily told them, "I am going to the pond with Tim. He is helping me get rid of the fleas. He is a very nice turtle."
Ben, Max, and Sam said, "Wow, Lily. That is very cool. We hope you feel better soon. Have fun at the pond."
Lily and Tim reached the pond, and Lily jumped into the water. She splashed and swam, and felt the fleas fall off her fur. She felt happy and refreshed. She thanked Tim, and gave him a lick. She said, "You are the best, Tim. You helped me so much. How can I thank you?"
Tim said, "You are welcome, Lily. You don't have to thank me. You are my friend, and I am glad to see you happy. But if you want, you can share your yummy bone with me. I like bones, too."
Lily said, "Of course, Tim. I have a big bone at home. You can have half of it. Come on, let's go back. And maybe we can play with Ben, Max, and Sam, too."
Lily and Tim went back to Lily's home, and shared the yummy bone. They also played with Ben, Max, and Sam, who were happy to see Lily without fleas. They all had a lot of fun, and learned that friends help each other, and share what they have.

One day, a hunter was walking through a strange forest. He was looking around to see if he could spot any animals, but it was weird. He couldn't see anything! He started to wander further and deeper into the forest, but something still seemed strange.
Suddenly, he heard a noise coming from the trees nearby. He stopped and glanced around but he couldn't see anything. He started to wander closer and the noise grew louder. As he came around a corner, he saw a weird-looking creature! It was small and furry, but it was definitely strange. 
The hunter started to inch closer, but the creature saw him and started to run away! The hunter got ready to chase it, but then suddenly something else came out from behind the trees. It was a giant eagle! The hunter froze. He had never seen an eagle this big before!
The eagle swooped down and grabbed the strange creature in its talons. Then, it flew away with it into the sky! The hunter watched, shocked and amazed at what had happened. He had never seen anything like this before. 
He realised that the weird creature wasn't so weird after all – it was just trying to get away from the giant eagle! He smiled, and then started to wander out of the forest. He had learned his lesson and knew he'd never wander too deep into the forest again!

Lily and Tom were jolly squirrels who liked to play in the park. They liked to run, jump, climb and swing on the trees. They also liked to find nuts and hide them in their nests for winter.
One day, they saw a big pile of nuts under a tree. They ran towards it, excited and hungry. They wanted to eat some nuts and prepare some for later.
"Look, Lily, so many nuts!" Tom said. "Let's take some and share with our friends."
"Good idea, Tom," Lily said. "But we have to be careful. Maybe someone else left them here."
They looked around, but they did not see anyone. They thought it was safe to take some nuts. They picked up some nuts and put them in their mouths. They were crunchy and tasty.
Suddenly, they heard a loud roar. It was a big bear, who was angry and hungry. He had left the nuts there as a trap for other animals. He saw the squirrels and wanted to catch them.
"Hey, you little thieves!" the bear shouted. "Those are my nuts! Give them back or I will eat you!"
Lily and Tom were scared. They dropped the nuts and ran away as fast as they could. They dodged the bear's paws and teeth and climbed up a tree. They hoped the bear would not follow them.
"Phew, that was close!" Tom said. "Are you okay, Lily?"
"I'm okay, Tom," Lily said. "But that was not fun. That was a mean bear. He tricked us with his nuts."
"Yes, he did," Tom said. "But we are smarter than him. We escaped and we still have some nuts in our nests. Let's go back and eat them with our friends."
"Okay, Tom," Lily said. "But next time, let's be more careful. Not all nuts are good nuts."
They nodded and hugged each other. Then they jumped from tree to tree, back to their nests. They were still jolly squirrels, but they learned a lesson. They never took nuts from strangers again.

"Hi, Bella!" said Fred. "Do you like the puddle? I like to drink from it too." Bella smiled and said, "Yes, Fred. It is a nice puddle. Thank you for sharing it with me."
Bella and Fred became good friends. They played near the puddle every day. They were happy to share the puddle and their friendship. And they lived happily ever after.

Ben was sleeping in his bed. He had a dream about a big dog. The dog was nice and soft. Ben liked to pet the dog and play with him. The dog licked Ben's face and made him laugh.
But then Ben heard a loud noise. It was a harsh noise that hurt his ears. It was his alarm clock. It was time to wake up and go to school. Ben did not like the noise. He wanted to stay with the dog in his dream.
Ben opened his eyes and saw his mom. She smiled at him and said, "Good morning, Ben. It's time to get up and get ready for school. You can see your dog later. He is waiting for you in the backyard."
Ben felt sad. He wanted to stay in bed and sleep more. He did not want to go to school. He liked his dog more than school. He said, "No, mom. I don't want to go. I want to stay with the dog. He is my friend. He makes me happy."
Mom hugged Ben and said, "I know, Ben. I know you love your dog. He loves you too. But you also need to go to school and learn new things. School is good for you. You can make new friends and have fun. And when you come back, you can play with your dog as much as you want. He will be happy to see you too."
Ben felt his mom's heart. It was warm and soft. He knew his mom loved him and wanted him to be happy. He felt his own heart. It was beating fast and loud. He loved his mom and his dog. He decided to be brave and go to school. He said, "Okay, mom. I will go to school. But can I hug the dog first?"
Mom nodded and said, "Of course, Ben. You can hug the dog first. He is waiting for you. Come on, let's go and say good morning to him."
Ben got out of bed and followed his mom. He saw his dog in the backyard. He ran to him and hugged him. The dog wagged his tail and licked his face. Ben smiled and said, "I love you, dog. I will see you later. Have a good day."
The dog barked and said, "I love you too, Ben. Have a good day at school. I will wait for you."

Tim was hungry. He said, "I want a tasty snack." The magic bow heard him. It made a tasty snack appear. Tim was happy. But then, his sister, Sue, came into the attic. Sue wanted the tasty snack too. They both wanted it and started to fight.
The magic bow saw them fighting. It did not like that. So, the bow made two tasty snacks. Tim and Sue stopped fighting. They both said, "Thank you, magic bow." They ate the tasty snacks and played with the magic bow together. From that day on, Tim and Sue shared the magic bow and never fought again.

John scrambled to his feet and put the book safely aside. "Yes mum?" he asked, still crouching on the ground.

One day, she decided to take a walk in the park. When she arrived, she saw a big red mailbox. She thought it was very different than any other mailbox she had ever seen. A feeling of excitement filled her inside and she walked closer to take a closer look.
She opened the door of the red mailbox and to her surprise, inside was a letter for her! She quickly took it out and saw it had her name written on it. She was so excited she ran back home to read it.
When she opened the letter, she read an invitation from a wonderful and magical land. 'Come and join us to celebrate!' it read.
The little girl was so happy and excited she quickly called her best friend. She couldn't wait to tell them the news!
The end.

Once upon a time there were two little birds named Lola and Gray. They liked to fly around the sky and explore. One day, the two birds were soaring around when they came across a gas station. Gray was curious about it and wanted to see what it looked like inside.
Lola was very nervous about it. She warned Gray that gas was delicate and advised him to avoid it. But Gray didn't listen. He flew right inside the gas station and started exploring.
A fuel truck arrived and the attendant started filling up the station with gas. He didn't see Gray inside and started pumping in the fuel. Soon enough, the entire station filled up with the delicate gas.
Gray was scared and confused. Suddenly, an old owl flew past and saw what was happening. He told Gray that he had to balance carefully or else the gas could explode.
Gray listened to the wise owl and quickly flew out of the station. He apologized to Lola for not taking her advice and thanked the old owl for saving his life.
The moral of the story is to listen to advice from experienced people. Even if it doesn't seem interesting, it might just save you from danger.

Sara and Ben were playing with their crayons in the living room. They liked to draw on the big paper that their mom gave them. They drew flowers, cars, animals and stars. They had many colors to choose from, but Sara's favorite was white. She liked to use the white crayon to make snow and clouds.
"Look, Ben, I made a snowman!" Sara said, showing her drawing to her brother.
"That's nice, Sara, but you can't see it very well. The paper is also white," Ben said.
"I don't care, I like white. It's pretty and clean," Sara said.
She looked around the room and saw a white sofa. It was their mom's new sofa, and she said it was very expensive. Sara had an idea. She took her white crayon and went to the sofa. She started to draw on it, making more snow and clouds.
"Hey, Sara, what are you doing?" Ben asked, following her.
"I'm making the sofa more beautiful. See, it has snow and clouds now," Sara said, smiling.
"No, Sara, that's bad! You can't draw on the sofa. Mom will be very angry. She said we can only draw on the paper. The sofa is not for drawing. It's for sitting," Ben said.
He tried to stop Sara, but she didn't listen. She kept drawing on the sofa, making more and more marks.
"Sara, stop it! You're ruining the sofa. It's not white anymore. It's dirty. Mom will be very sad. She worked hard to buy the sofa. It's very expensive. You have to wipe it off," Ben said.
He grabbed a cloth and tried to wipe off the crayon marks, but they didn't come off. They were stuck on the sofa.
"Oh no, what have I done?" Sara said, realizing her mistake.
She started to cry. She was scared of what mom would say. She didn't mean to make the sofa dirty. She just wanted to make it pretty.
Ben hugged her and said, "It's okay, Sara. Don't cry. Maybe mom can fix it. Maybe she can wash it or cover it. But you have to say sorry to her. You have to tell her the truth. And you have to promise not to draw on the sofa again. You have to be careful with other people's things. They are not for playing. They are for using."
Sara nodded and said, "Okay, Ben. I'm sorry. I'll tell mom. I'll promise. I'll be careful."
They waited for mom to come home. They were nervous, but they hoped she would forgive them. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to respect other people's things and not to draw on them. They learned that white is not always pretty and clean. Sometimes it can be dirty and expensive.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big basket on a bench. The basket has many yummy things inside. There are apples, bananas, cookies, and juice.
"Wow, look at that basket!" Lily says. "It has so many yummy things. I want some."
"Me too," Tom says. "But maybe it belongs to someone. We should not take it."
Lily does not listen to Tom. She runs to the bench and grabs the basket. She opens it and takes a big bite of a cookie.
"Mmm, this is so good!" she says. "Come on, Tom, have some too."
Tom shakes his head. He feels bad for the person who left the basket. He thinks it is not nice to take things that are not yours.
"No, thank you," he says. "I don't want to eat someone else's food. That is wrong. You should put the basket back."
Lily does not want to put the basket back. She wants to eat more yummy things. She takes another cookie and a banana. She drinks some juice.
Suddenly, a lady comes to the bench. She looks angry and sad. She sees Lily with her basket.
"Hey, that's my basket!" she says. "What are you doing with it? I was having a picnic with my friends, but I had to go to the bathroom. I left my basket here for a moment. How dare you take it?"
Lily feels scared and ashamed. She drops the basket and runs away. She does not say sorry to the lady. She does not look at Tom.
Tom feels sorry for the lady. He goes to her and says, "I'm sorry, ma'am. My friend was not nice. She took your basket without asking. I tried to stop her, but she did not listen. Here is your basket. I hope you can still enjoy your picnic."
The lady smiles at Tom. She says, "Thank you, young man. You are very kind and honest. I appreciate your help. Here, you can have a cookie as a reward. It is yummy."
Tom takes the cookie and says, "Thank you, ma'am. You are very generous and sweet. I hope you have a nice day."
Tom eats the cookie and walks away. He looks for Lily, but he does not see her. He thinks she is hiding somewhere. He feels sad for her. He wishes she had been more respectful and polite. He thinks she learned a lesson today. He hopes she will be a better friend next time. He knows that it is better to be honest and kind than to be greedy and rude. He is happy with his cookie. He thinks it is the yummiest cookie ever.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was an orange squirrel. The squirrel had a big nut. He loved his nut very much. One day, he wanted to find a safe place to hide his nut. So he started to look for a good spot.
As the squirrel walked, a small bird saw him. The bird liked the nut too. The bird said, "Can I have the nut, please?" The squirrel said, "No, it is my nut." The bird was sad, but he had an idea. He decided to follow the squirrel and see where he would hide the nut.
The squirrel found a big tree and thought it was a good place to hide his nut. He started to dig a hole under the tree. The bird, who was still following the squirrel, saw this and quickly flew away. The squirrel did not see the bird leave.
Just as the squirrel was about to put his nut in the hole, a big wind came and blew the nut away. The squirrel was very sad and scared. He did not know what to do. But then, the small bird came back with the nut in its beak. The bird said, "I saw the wind take your nut. I wanted to help you."
The squirrel was very happy and thanked the bird. They both decided to share the nut and became good friends. From that day on, they played together in the big forest and shared many more nuts.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They had a huge jug of water and some cups. They wanted to make tea for their toys.
"Let's march to the table," Tom said. "We can be soldiers with our jug."
"OK," Lily said. "But we have to be careful. The jug is very heavy."
They lifted the jug together and started to march. They sang a song as they marched. "We are soldiers, we are brave, we have water, we can save."
But the jug was too heavy for them. They could not march very far. The jug slipped from their hands and fell to the ground. The water spilled everywhere.
"Oh no!" Tom and Lily cried. "Our tea is gone!"
They looked at the mess. They felt sad. They did not know what to do.
Then they heard a voice. It was their mom. She came out of the house. She saw the jug and the water.
"What happened here?" she asked.
Tom and Lily told her what they were doing. They said they were sorry.
Mom smiled. She hugged them. She said, "It's OK. I'm not mad. You were trying to have fun. But next time, use a smaller jug. And don't march with water. It's too dangerous."
She helped them clean up the water. She gave them a new jug. It was smaller and lighter. She filled it with juice. She said, "Here. This is better for tea. And you can still march with it. But be careful."
Tom and Lily thanked her. They took the jug and the cups. They marched to the table. They sang a new song. "We are soldiers, we are smart, we have juice, we have heart."

The first kangaroo bravely decided to join in on the dancing, but the second kangaroo kept their distance. 
Soon the first kangaroo noticed that the other kangaroos weren't actually dancing, but just standing and jumping together. The first kangaroo quickly joined in and started to jump with the others.
The second kangaroo was relieved to see that the others weren't really dancing. Seeing their friend bravely jump together with the others made them realise how much fun it can be to try new things.

One day, Chirpy met a quiet mouse named Squeaky. Squeaky did not like Chirpy's loud singing. Squeaky said, "Chirpy, please stop singing. It is too noisy for me."
Chirpy did not want to stop singing. He loved to sing. But Chirpy also wanted to be friends with Squeaky. So, Chirpy tried to sing more softly.
Squeaky was happy that Chirpy tried to sing softly. He said, "Thank you, Chirpy. I accept your singing now." Chirpy and Squeaky became good friends and played together in the pretty landscape.
From that day on, Chirpy sang softly and Squeaky learned to enjoy Chirpy's singing. They both learned to accept each other's differences and lived happily ever after.

Later, the bird found a big bell near the lake. The bird wanted to ring the bell, but she was too small. She went to the swan and asked, "Can you help me ring the bell?" The swan thought for a moment and said, "Okay, but only if you promise not to touch my toys."
The bird agreed, and the swan used her long neck to ring the bell. As soon as the bell rang, a big fish jumped out of the lake and ate the swan! Sara and Tom were playing with their blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and houses and cars with the blocks. They were very intelligent and creative.
But then their baby brother Ben came crawling into the room. He saw the blocks and wanted to play with them too. He grabbed some blocks and threw them around. He knocked down Sara's tower and Tom's house. He made a big mess.
Sara and Tom were angry and sad. They shouted at Ben. "No, Ben, no! Those are our blocks! You are bad! You ruined our play!"
Ben did not understand. He thought they were playing too. He smiled and giggled. He crawled to the kitchen and found a cup of water. He brought it back to the living room and poured it over the blocks. He made them wet.
Sara and Tom were more angry and sad. They cried and ran to their mom. "Mom, mom! Ben is bad! He threw our blocks and made them wet! He ruined our play!"
Mom came to the living room and saw the mess. She was not happy. She picked up Ben and scolded him. "Ben, Ben, no! You cannot do that! You cannot throw blocks and make them wet! You have to be gentle and careful! You have to say sorry to Sara and Tom!"
Ben looked at Mom and then at Sara and Tom. He saw their tears and felt sorry. He said in his baby voice. "Sorry, Sara. Sorry, Tom. Me no bad. Me play."
Mom smiled and hugged Ben. She said to Sara and Tom. "Ben is sorry. He did not mean to hurt you. He is still learning. He loves you. Can you forgive him?"
Sara and Tom looked at Ben and saw his smile. They felt sorry too. They said to Ben. "It's okay, Ben. We forgive you. We love you too. You can play with us. But you have to be gentle and careful. And you have to share the blocks."
Mom was proud of Sara and Tom. She said to them. "You are very intelligent and kind. You know how to restore peace and friendship. You are good siblings. Now let's clean up the mess and dry the blocks. And then we can have a snack and play some more."

Emily opened her box of powder and said to Jane: "This is my own powder. Would you like to try some?"
Jane looked a bit nervous, but she was very curious. She nodded her head and said: "Yes I would!"
Emily took out the powder and sprinkled it on Jane's hand. Jane closed her eyes and felt the powder tickle her skin. She smiled and said: "That feels nice!"
Emily was very happy. She told Jane: "Now you own some of my powder too!".
The two girls laughed and hugged one another. They had already made a very special memory together.

Lily was a lively girl who liked to play and run and jump. She had many toys and books and friends. But today she was not happy. She had to stay in bed because she was sick. She had a cough and a fever and a sore throat.
She sighed and looked at the clock. It was almost time for her nap. She did not want to nap. She wanted to go outside and see the sun and the flowers and the birds. She wanted to play with her dog and her bike and her ball. She wanted to have fun.
She heard a knock on the door. It was her mom. She came in with a tray. On the tray there was a glass of water, a bowl of soup, a spoon and a napkin. She smiled and said, "Hello, my sweetie. How are you feeling?"
Lily frowned and said, "I'm feeling bad. I don't like being sick. I don't like being in bed. I don't like napping. I want to play."
Her mom hugged her and said, "I know, my darling. Being sick is no fun. But you need to rest and eat and drink to get better. Napping will help you heal and feel more lively. And when you wake up, I have a surprise for you."
Lily was curious. She asked, "What is the surprise?"
Her mom winked and said, "You'll see. But first, you have to nap. Come on, let me tuck you in and read you a story."
Lily sighed again, but she agreed. She liked stories. She snuggled under the blanket and listened to her mom's voice. She felt warm and cozy and sleepy. She closed her eyes and drifted into a dream.
She did not know how long she slept, but when she woke up, she felt better. Her cough was gone, her fever was down and her throat was less sore. She opened her eyes and saw her mom sitting next to her. She also saw something else. Something that made her gasp and smile.
It was a big, colorful balloon. It had a picture of a unicorn on it. It was tied to a string that was tied to her wrist. It floated above her bed and bobbed gently.
Her mom said, "Surprise! I got you a balloon to cheer you up. Do you like it?"
Lily nodded and said, "I love it! Thank you, mom! You're the best!"
Her mom kissed her and said, "You're welcome, honey. I'm glad you're feeling better. Do you want to get up and play now?"
Lily nodded again and said, "Yes, please! Can I take the balloon with me?"
Her mom said, "Of course you can. But be careful not to let it go. It might fly away."
Lily said, "I won't let it go. I'll hold it tight. Come on, let's go!"
She got out of bed and grabbed the balloon. She felt lively and happy. She followed her mom out of the room. She was ready to play and run and jump. She was ready to have fun.

"Wow, that is fun!" Tom says.

"Look, the dog is chasing the cat!" Tom says.

She goes upstairs and sees them playing on the computer. She is not happy.
"Tom, Anna, what are you doing? You did not mention you wanted to use the computer. You have to ask me first. And you have to wash your hands. They are dirty from playing," Anna's mom says.
Tom and Anna feel sorry. They did not mean to make Anna's mom angry. They turn off the computer and say sorry.
"We are sorry, mom. We just wanted to play. The computer is very fun," Anna says.
"I know, but you have to follow the rules. The computer is not a toy. It is expensive and important. You have to be gentle and clean with it. And you have to tell me when you want to use it. Do you understand?" Anna's mom says.
"Yes, mom. We understand. We will not do it again," Tom and Anna say.
They go downstairs and wash their hands. They join Anna's dad and brother for lunch. They eat sandwiches and drink juice. They talk about the cat and the dog on the computer. They still think they are fun, but they also know they have to be careful. They are good friends and they learn from their mistake.

One day, Bob found a big hole near his home. He didn't mind the big hole, but he was curious. He asked his friends, "What's in the big hole?" His friends didn't know, so they all decided to look inside.
Bob and his friends took turns looking into the big hole. They saw that it was dark and deep. They were a little scared, but they were gentle with each other. They held paws and looked in together. In the end, they found that the big hole was just another home for a new friend, a squirrel named Sam.

Lily and Tom like to play in the park. They run and jump and laugh. They see a big stone near a tree. Lily says, "Let's climb on the stone and pretend we are lions." Tom says, "OK, that sounds fun."
They climb on the stone and roar like lions. They make faces and wave their arms. They have a lot of fun. But then they hear their mom calling them. She says, "Lily, Tom, it's time to go home. Come here, please." Lily and Tom do not want to go home. They want to stay on the stone and play.
They say, "No, mom, we want to stay. We are lions. We are fast and strong. We do not want to leave our stone." Mom says, "I know you are having fun, but we have to go home. It's getting dark and cold. You can play on the stone again tomorrow. Come on, let's go."
Lily and Tom look at each other. They do not want to make mom angry. They say, "OK, mom, we will come. But can we say goodbye to our stone?" Mom says, "Yes, you can say goodbye to your stone. But hurry up, please."
Lily and Tom climb down from the stone. They hug the stone and say, "Bye, stone. Thank you for letting us play on you. You are a good stone. We will see you tomorrow." The stone does not say anything, but it feels happy. Lily and Tom run to their mom. They hold her hand and walk home. They are still lions in their hearts.

Every day more and more people asked the man to open the box, but he refused. He said that only the bravest ones could open it. Everyone was so curious, so they kept asking him, but the man still refused.
Then one day, a big brave lion came and said he wanted to open the box. But despite how brave the lion was, the man still refused. The lion was sad and walked away, wondering why he couldn't get the wish.
But then something amazing happened. Suddenly, the box opened all by itself. Inside was an enormous wish, one that could make all of their dreams come true. Everyone was so happy and excited, and they thanked the man for keeping it safe for so long.
So, if you ever have a wish, remember to never give up and something amazing may happen.

Lily was a little girl who loved her dog, Spot. Spot was a big dog with black and white fur and a wet nose. Lily and Spot liked to play in the park, run after balls and chase squirrels.
One day, Lily and Spot went to the park with Lily's mom. Lily's mom gave Lily a red ball to throw for Spot. Lily threw the ball and Spot ran after it. He caught it in his mouth and brought it back to Lily. Lily threw the ball again and again, and Spot ran and ran.
But then, Lily saw a swing and wanted to try it. She ran to the swing and asked her mom to push her. She forgot about the ball and Spot. Spot waited for Lily to throw the ball again, but she did not. He looked at the ball, then at Lily, then at the ball. He felt upset. He wanted to play with Lily.
He picked up the ball in his mouth and walked to the swing. He dropped the ball near Lily's feet and barked. Lily looked down and saw Spot and the ball. She remembered that she forgot to play with him. She felt sorry.
"Spot, I'm sorry. I forgot about you. Do you want to play with me?" she said.
Spot wagged his tail and licked Lily's face. He was happy. He gave Lily his paw and she took it. They hugged and smiled.
"Spot, you are my best friend. I love you," Lily said.
"I love you too, Lily," Spot said in his dog way.
They went back to play with the ball and had fun. Lily did not forget about Spot again. They were both happy.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room upstairs. One day, their mom tells them to come down for lunch. She says, "I made you some healthy soup and bread. Come and eat, please."
Anna and Ben do not want to stop playing. They say, "No, mom. We are not hungry. We want to play more." They ignore their mom and keep playing with their toys.
Their mom is sad and angry. She says, "Anna and Ben, you are being rude and naughty. You need to eat your healthy soup and bread. It is good for you. If you do not eat, you will get sick and weak. Do you want that?"
Anna and Ben still do not listen. They say, "No, mom. We do not care. We do not like soup and bread. We want to play more." They hide their toys under the bed and pretend they do not hear their mom.
Their mom is very sad and angry. She says, "Fine. If you do not want to eat, you can stay upstairs. But you will not get any dessert or snacks later. And you will not watch TV or read books. You will be bored and hungry. Maybe then you will learn to be polite and grateful."
Anna and Ben do not believe their mom. They think she is joking. They say, "Okay, mom. We do not need dessert or snacks or TV or books. We have our toys. We are happy." They laugh and play with their toys.
But soon, they get tired of playing with the same toys. They start to feel hungry and thirsty. They start to miss their mom and their lunch. They start to feel sorry for being rude and naughty. They say, "Maybe we should go downstairs and eat our soup and bread. Maybe mom will forgive us and give us dessert and snacks and TV and books. Maybe we should say sorry and thank you to mom."
They go downstairs and look for their mom. They see her in the kitchen. She is washing the dishes. She looks sad and tired. They say, "Mom, we are sorry. We were rude and naughty. We should have listened to you. We should have eaten our healthy soup and bread. Can we have some now, please?"
Their mom is surprised and happy. She says, "Anna and Ben, I am glad you came downstairs. I am glad you are sorry. I am glad you want to eat your healthy soup and bread. Yes, you can have some now. And you can also have some dessert and snacks and TV and books later. But you have to promise me something."
Anna and Ben say, "What, mom? What do we have to promise?"
Their mom says, "You have to promise me that you will always be polite and grateful. You have to promise me that you will always mention when you are hungry or thirsty or tired or bored. You have to promise me that you will always come down when I call you for lunch or dinner or bedtime. You have to promise me that you will always love me and respect me."
Anna and Ben say, "We promise, mom. We promise. We love you and respect you. You are the best mom in the world."
Their mom says, "I love you too, Anna and Ben. You are the best twins in the world. Now, let's eat our healthy soup and bread and enjoy our time together."
The end.
Moral value: The story teaches the children to be polite and grateful, to listen to their parents, to eat healthy food, and to communicate their needs and feelings.

Tom and Mia went to the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and giraffes. They liked to watch them and learn their names.
When they came to the bird house, they saw a big bird with a long neck and legs. It had black and white feathers on its body and a small head. "What is that?" Tom asked.
"That is an ostrich," mom said. "It is the biggest and fastest bird in the world. It can run very fast, but it cannot fly."
"Wow, it is so big!" Mia said. "Can I touch it?"
Mom shook her head. "No, you cannot touch it. It might be scared or angry. We have to be gentle and quiet with the animals."
Tom and Mia nodded. They looked at the ostrich from a distance. They saw that it had a brown bandage on its wing. "What happened to its wing?" Mia asked.
Mom pointed to a sign next to the cage. It said that the ostrich had hurt its wing when it ran into a fence. The zookeepers had taken care of it and put a bandage on it. They hoped that it would heal soon and restore its health.
"Can we help the ostrich?" Tom asked.
Mom smiled. "We can help by being kind and respectful. We can also make a card for it and say that we hope it gets better soon."
Tom and Mia liked that idea. They found some paper and crayons and made a card for the ostrich. They drew a picture of the ostrich and wrote "Get well soon" with their mom's help. They gave the card to a zookeeper who thanked them and said he would give it to the ostrich.
Tom and Mia felt happy. They hoped that the ostrich would like their card and feel better soon. They waved goodbye to the ostrich and went to see more animals.

Ben got angry. He tried to grab the lotion from Lily. Lily held it tight. They pulled and pushed. They yelled at each other. Then, Ben slapped Lily on the face. Lily cried out loud.
Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily's red cheek and Ben's angry face. She saw the lotion and the dolls. She was not happy. She said to Ben, "Why did you slap Lily? That is not nice. That hurts. You have to say sorry."
Ben felt sorry. He knew he was wrong. He said to Lily, "I'm sorry, Lily. I should not have slapped you. I was mean. Can we be friends again?"

Mom hugged them both. She said to them, "I'm glad you are sorry. But you have to be careful with the lotion. It is not for playing. It is for Mommy's massage. She needs it for her sore back."
Lily and Ben felt bad. They did not know that the lotion was for Mommy. They said to Mom, "We're sorry, Mom. We did not know. Can we help you with your massage?"
Mom smiled. She said to them, "That is very sweet of you. Thank you. You can help me with my massage. But first, you have to clean up the mess. And then, you have to hug each other and say you love each other."
Lily and Ben did what Mom said. They cleaned up the mess. They hugged each other and said they loved each other. Then, they helped Mom with her massage. They rubbed her back and arms gently. Lily was a young bee who liked to fly around the flowers. She wanted to learn more about the world, so she often asked her mother questions.
"Mom, why do we make honey?" she asked one day.
"Honey is our food, dear. We work hard to collect nectar from the flowers and turn it into honey in our hive. Honey gives us energy and keeps us warm in the winter," her mother explained.
"Can I see the hive, mom?" Lily asked.
"Of course, dear. But you have to be careful. The hive is our home, but it is also where the queen bee lives. She is the most important bee in the colony. She lays all the eggs and makes sure we are healthy and happy. You have to be respectful and quiet when you see her," her mother said.
Lily nodded and followed her mother to the hive. It was a big and busy place, full of bees and honeycombs. Lily saw many bees doing different jobs, like guarding, cleaning, feeding, and making honey. She was amazed by how much they worked together.
"Mom, can I meet the queen bee?" she asked.
"Maybe another day, dear. She is very busy right now. But you can say hello to her from a distance. Look, there she is, in the middle of the hive. She is bigger and brighter than the other bees. Can you see her?" her mother pointed.
Lily looked and saw the queen bee. She was surrounded by other bees who took care of her and listened to her. Lily felt a warm and happy feeling in her heart. She waved her little wing and said, "Hello, queen bee. Thank you for being our leader. I hope you have a good day."
The queen bee noticed Lily and smiled. She nodded her head and said, "Hello, young bee. You are very brave and curious. I am proud of you. Keep learning and growing. You have a bright future ahead of you."

The poor navy man was very sad. He had been sailing so long and had been so thirsty.

So, the poor navy man and the friendly sailor set out to explore the island. They looked everywhere they could, but they couldn't find any other sources of water.
At last, they found a little stream with trickling water that ran through the island. It wasn't a lot, but it was enough for the two of them to drink.

The cat and the dog tried to get the ball down. The cat tried to jump, but it was too high. The dog tried to slap the tree with his paw, but it was too strong. They were sad and didn't know what to do.
Then, a friendly bird came and saw them. The bird flew up and pushed the ball out of the tree. The ball fell down, and the cat and dog were so happy. They thanked the bird and played with the ball again. The cool building was filled with laughter and joy.

"Hello, ball!" said Buddy. "Let's play!" But the ball did not talk back. Buddy was sad. He did not know that balls cannot talk. Then, a girl named Amy came over. She was holding a small box with a big button on it.
"Hi, Buddy!" said Amy. "I can record your voice with this box. Then, we can play with the ball together!" Buddy was happy. He barked and Amy pushed the button. The box played back Buddy's bark. Buddy was surprised!
Buddy and Amy played with the ball all day. They became best friends. The moral of the story is that friends can help you when you are sad or when you need someone to play with. And sometimes, the most unexpected things can make you happy.

Anna and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to pretend they were pirates and explorers, sailing on a big ship. They had a map, a telescope, a sword and a hat.
"Look, Ben, I see an island!" Anna said, pointing with her telescope. "Maybe there is treasure there!"
"Let's go, Anna!" Ben said, grabbing his sword and hat. "But we have to be careful, there might be enemies or traps!"
They ran to the couch and climbed on it, pretending it was their ship. They made noises like the wind and the waves, and sang pirate songs.
Suddenly, they heard a loud boom outside. They looked out the window and saw dark clouds and lightning. It was a storm!
"Uh-oh, Anna, we have to go back!" Ben said, scared. "The storm is too big and dangerous!"
"But what about the treasure, Ben?" Anna asked, still curious.
"We can find it another day, Anna," Ben said, trying to be brave. "The treasure is not important, we are important. We have to be safe and humble, like Mommy and Daddy always say."
"Okay, Ben, you are right," Anna said, nodding. "Let's go back to our room and wait for the storm to pass."
They took their toys and ran to their room, holding hands. They hugged each other and prayed for the storm to go away. They did not mention the island or the treasure anymore. They were happy to have each other.

Sam is a little boy who loves boats. He has many toy boats that he plays with in the bath and in the pool. He likes to pretend that he is a famous captain who sails to faraway lands and has many adventures.
One day, Sam's dad takes him to the harbor to see the real boats. Sam is very excited and runs to the edge of the water. He sees big boats and small boats, boats with sails and boats with motors, boats with flags and boats with horns. He points to each one and asks his dad what they are called.
"Look, dad, what is that?" Sam says, pointing to a metal object that hangs from a rope on the side of a boat.
"That is an anchor, Sam," his dad says. "An anchor is used to keep the boat from moving when it stops in the water. It is very heavy and it sinks to the bottom of the water and holds the boat in place."
"Wow, that is cool," Sam says. "Can I touch it?"
"Sorry, Sam, you can't touch it. It is not safe. The anchor belongs to the boat and the boat belongs to someone else. We have to respect their property and stay away from it."
Sam nods and looks for another boat to admire. He sees a boat that has a big sign that says "Famous Fisherman". He wonders what that means.
"Dad, what is a famous fisherman?" Sam asks.
"A famous fisherman is someone who catches a lot of fish and sells them to people who like to eat fish. He is famous because he is very good at his job and people know his name and his boat," his dad explains.
"Does he use an anchor?" Sam asks.
"Yes, he does, Sam. He uses an anchor when he finds a good spot to fish. He lowers the anchor into the water and waits for the fish to bite his hook. Then he pulls them up and puts them in a big basket. When he has enough fish, he raises the anchor and goes back to the harbor to sell them."
"I want to be a famous fisherman, dad," Sam says.
"Maybe you will be, Sam, when you grow up. But for now, you can be a famous captain of your toy boats. Come on, let's go home and play with them. I bet you have some great stories to tell me about your adventures."
Sam smiles and takes his dad's hand. He is happy to have seen the real boats and learned about the anchor and the famous fisherman. He can't wait to wake up tomorrow and play with his toy boats again. He has a lot of fun with his dad and his imagination.

Jill and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big white house with a fancy gate. Jill wanted to go inside and look around. Tom was scared.
"Let's go see the house," Jill said. "It looks nice and pretty."
"No, we can't," Tom said. "It's not our house. Maybe someone lives there. They might be angry if we go in."
"Are you a baby?" Jill asked. "I dare you to go with me. It will be fun."
Tom did not like being called a baby. He did not want to lose the dare. He followed Jill to the gate. They pushed it open and walked into the yard. There were many flowers and trees. They heard a dog barking.
"See, it's not so bad," Jill said. "Let's go to the door."
They ran to the door and knocked. No one answered. Jill tried to open the door. It was locked.
"Let's go back," Tom said. "This is wrong. We should not be here."
But Jill did not listen. She saw a window that was open. She climbed on a chair and looked inside. She saw a big room with many toys and books. She wanted to play with them.
"Wow, look at all these things," Jill said. "Let's go inside and play."
She jumped through the window and landed on the floor. Tom was very scared. He did not want to go inside. He heard the dog barking louder. He saw a car coming into the driveway.
"Jill, come back," Tom shouted. "Someone is coming. We have to go."
But Jill did not hear him. She was busy playing with a doll and a train. She did not see the door opening. She did not see the angry man who lived in the house. She did not see the big dog that ran towards her.
Tom saw everything. He was very sorry he followed Jill. He wished he had said no to the dare. He wished they had stayed in the park. He wished they had never seen the white house with the fancy gate.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a green frog near a pond. The frog was hopping and croaking happily.
"Look, a frog!" Tim said. "Let's catch it and keep it as a pet!"
"No, Tim, that's not nice," Sam said. "The frog lives in the pond. It needs water to be happy. If we take it away, it will be dry and sad."
But Tim did not listen to Sam. He ran after the frog and caught it in his hands. He put it in a jar and took it home.
The next day, Tim and Sam looked at the jar. The frog was not hopping or croaking. It was still and quiet. Its skin was dry and wrinkled.
"What's wrong with the frog?" Tim asked.
"It's sick, Tim," Sam said. "It misses the pond. It needs water to be happy. You should let it go."
Tim felt sorry for the frog. He realized he had been selfish and cruel. He took the jar and ran back to the pond. He opened the jar and let the frog go.
The frog jumped out of the jar and into the water. It splashed and croaked happily. It looked at Tim and Sam and winked.
"Thank you, Tim," the frog said. "You did the right thing. You are a good friend."
Tim and Sam smiled. They learned a lesson. They should not take away what belongs to others. They should respect and care for all living things. They waved goodbye to the frog and went home.

John sat there and thought, "What am I going to do now?" He was scared, but he wanted to give it a try. He grabbed the reins and held them tight. Then, he said, "Giddy up!" 
He started to ride the horse, and he was scared but also a little excited. He had never done anything like this before! After a few minutes, he started to get the hang of it and he began to have a lot of fun. 
John smiled and shouted, "This is the best thing I ever tried!" He had never done anything so weird, and he was proud of himself for giving it a try.

One morning Molly and Tom were playing in the garden. Tom wanted to climb the post but Molly said no. They began to quarrel because Molly wanted Tom to stay by her side. Then suddenly they heard a quiet voice call out to them.
The voice said, "Stop quarreling, children! Look over there!"
Molly and Tom looked around and saw a beautiful deer eating breakfast in their garden. Molly and Tom forgot their quarrel and watched the deer in awe.
The deer looked up, smiled, and said, "Good morning children! Enjoy your day!" Then the deer bounded away.
Molly and Tom smiled back and went to play happily in the garden. They both laughed. They were glad that the deer helped them forget their quarrel.

One day, the little girl was so fed up of her uncle's slowness that she decided to be brave. She ran up to her uncle and yelled at him. She said "Go fast, uncle!" He was surprised and did not know what to say. But then, he smiled and started to walk faster.
The little girl was so happy. Her uncle was faster and she was no longer annoyed. From then on, when her uncle came to visit he was much more speedy - which made her like her uncle much more.

Sara likes to write. She writes with her crayons on paper, on the wall, on the sofa. She writes her name, shapes, animals, anything she can think of. She thinks writing is fun and pretty.
One day, Sara sees her mom writing on her laptop. She asks, "Mom, what are you doing?"
Mom says, "I'm writing for my job, honey. I have to write a report for my boss. It's very important and I have to finish it today."
Sara says, "Can I help you write? I'm good at writing."
Mom says, "No, sweetie, this is not the kind of writing you can do. This is different. You have to use words and numbers and rules. You have to be careful and accurate. You can write later, okay?"
Sara feels sad. She wants to write with mom. She thinks mom's writing is boring and hard. She thinks her writing is better and easier. She decides to show mom how to write.
She takes a crayon and climbs on the chair. She reaches for the laptop and starts to write on the screen. She writes her name, a heart, a star, a cat. She writes in big and small letters, in different colors. She writes all over the screen. She thinks it looks smooth and nice.
Mom sees what Sara is doing and screams. She runs to the laptop and tries to wipe off the crayon. But it's too late. The screen is ruined. The report is gone. Mom is angry and sad. She cries and says, "Sara, what have you done? You ruined my laptop and my job. You can't write on the screen. You can't write on anything that's not yours. You have to ask first. You have to listen. You have to learn."
Sara feels scared and sorry. She didn't mean to make mom cry. She didn't know the screen was not like paper. She didn't know the report was important. She just wanted to write and help. She says, "I'm sorry, mom. I love you. I love writing."
Mom hugs Sara and says, "I love you too, honey. I love writing too. But we have to write in different ways. We have to respect each other's things. We have to be careful and responsible. We have to apologize and fix our mistakes."
Sara nods and says, "Okay, mom. I'm sorry. I'll be good. I'll write on paper. I'll help you fix your laptop and your job."
Mom smiles and says, "Thank you, Sara. You're a good girl. We'll fix this together. We'll write together. But not on the screen, okay?"
Sara says, "Okay, mom. Not on the screen."

They walk to the table. They see a man sitting on a chair. He is reading a book. He has a hat and a beard.
"Excuse me, sir," Ben says. "Can we touch your melon? It is very pretty."
The man looks up. He smiles. He has kind eyes.
"Sure, you can touch it," he says. "But be careful. It is heavy. It is a watermelon. It has water inside. Do you want to try some?"
"Yes, please," Ben and Mia say.
The man takes a knife. He cuts the melon in half. He gives a piece to Ben and a piece to Mia. They see the red flesh and the black seeds. They smell the sweet juice.
"Thank you, sir," Ben and Mia say.
They bite the melon. It is cold and juicy. It tastes good. They make a mess. They laugh.
They lean on the table. They enjoy the melon. They share with the man. They make a new friend. They are happy.

"Hello, squirrel!" Ben said. He waved his hand at the squirrel. "Do you like the mushroom?"
The squirrel did not answer. It jumped from the tree and ran away. Lily and Ben laughed. They thought the squirrel was funny and shy.
They heard Mommy calling them. It was time for lunch. They ran to the house. They smelled something good. Mommy had made soup and bread.
"Did you have fun in the garden?" Mommy asked.
"Yes, we did!" Lily and Ben said. "We saw a big mushroom and a squirrel!"
Mommy smiled. She gave them a hug and a kiss. "That sounds wonderful. You are very lucky to have such a nice garden. Some people don't have gardens. They live in small houses or flats. They are not rich like us."
Lily and Ben did not know what rich meant. They only knew they had a lot of things they loved. They had a garden, a house, a Mommy, a Daddy, and each other. They thought that was enough. They thanked Mommy for the soup and bread. They ate and enjoyed their lunch. They were happy.

"But it is so cute!" Ben said.

John and his mum stepped outside, but the purple flood filled their garden! His mum thought of a plan. She found a bucket and put John in it, while she tied a rope to it. Anna liked to hop. She hopped in the morning, she hopped in the afternoon, she hopped at night. She hopped on the bed, she hopped on the sofa, she hopped on the floor. She hopped when she was happy, she hopped when she was sad, she hopped when she was bored.
One day, Anna hopped too much. She hopped on the table, she hopped on the chair, she hopped on the drawer. The drawer was full of Mommy's things. When Anna hopped on the drawer, the drawer opened and Mommy's things fell out. There were clothes, and books, and jewelry, and papers. They made a big mess on the floor.
Mommy came into the room and saw the mess. She was very angry. She said to Anna, "Anna, what did you do? You made a big mess with my things. You were very rude. You should not hop on the drawer. You should not hop on anything that is not yours. You should say sorry and help me clean up."
Anna felt bad. She did not mean to make a mess. She did not mean to be rude. She liked to hop, but she did not like to make Mommy angry. She said to Mommy, "I'm sorry, Mommy. I was hopping and I did not see the drawer. I will help you clean up. I will not hop on the drawer again. I will only hop on things that are mine."
Mommy hugged Anna and said, "Thank you, Anna. I love you. I know you like to hop, but you have to be careful and respectful. You can hop on your toys, or your bed, or your mat. But you cannot hop on things that are not yours. Do you understand?"
Anna nodded and said, "I understand, Mommy. I love you too. Can I hop with you after we clean up?"
Mommy smiled and said, "Yes, you can. We can hop together and have fun. But only on things that are ours."

One day, a boy and a girl were playing in the park. They saw a big hole in the ground. They wanted to see what was inside.
"Let's go in the hole!" the boy said.
"No, it is too dark and scary!" the girl said.
"But maybe there is something fun or shiny in the hole!" the boy said.
He took a light stick from his backpack and threw it in the hole. It made a bright light. The boy and the girl looked in the hole. They saw a lot of things. They saw rocks, dirt, bugs, and a shiny coin.
"Wow, look at the coin!" the boy said. "It is so shiny and pretty! I want it!"
He climbed down the hole to get the coin. The girl stayed on the edge of the hole. She was afraid.
"Be careful!" she said.
The boy reached the coin and picked it up. He was happy. He put it in his pocket. He tried to climb back up the hole. But the hole was too deep and slippery. He could not get out.
"Help!" he said. "I am stuck in the hole!"
The girl heard him. She was worried. She looked around. She saw a rope on a tree. She ran to the rope and pulled it. It was long and strong. She threw one end of the rope to the boy.
"Grab the rope!" she said.
The boy grabbed the rope. The girl pulled the rope. She pulled hard and fast. She pulled the boy out of the hole. The boy was dirty and scared. But he was safe.
"Thank you!" he said. "You saved me!"
He hugged the girl. The girl hugged him back.
"You are welcome!" she said. "But why did you go in the hole for a coin?"
The boy looked at the coin. He felt silly.
"I thought it was valuable," he said. "But it is not. It is just a coin. You are more valuable to me. You are my friend."
He gave the coin to the girl.
"Here, you can have it," he said. "It is a gift for you."
The girl smiled. She took the coin.
"Thank you," she said. "But you are more valuable to me too. You are my friend."
They held hands and walked away from the hole. They learned a lesson. They learned that friendship is more valuable than anything in a hole.
