Ben was a jolly boy who liked to feed the animals at the farm. He liked to feed the cows, the pigs, the sheep and the chickens. He liked to see them eat and make noises.
One day, he saw a new animal at the farm. It was big and brown and had a horn on its head. Ben was curious and wanted to feed it. He asked his mom what it was.
"That is a goat, Ben. Be careful, he can be naughty sometimes. He likes to eat grass and hay, but he also likes to chew on other things. Don't get too close to his horn, he might poke you with it." Mom said.
Ben nodded and took some grass from a basket. He walked slowly to the goat and held out his hand. The goat looked at him and sniffed the grass. He opened his mouth and took a bite. Ben smiled and said, "Hello, goat. You are hungry, huh?"
The goat nodded and chewed the grass. He wanted more. He looked at Ben and saw his red shirt. He thought it was food too. He reached out his horn and pulled Ben's shirt. Ben felt a tug and said, "Hey, goat. That is not food. That is my shirt. Let go!"
The goat did not let go. He pulled harder and harder. Ben tried to pull back, but he was not strong enough. He cried out, "Mom, help! The goat is eating my shirt!"
Mom heard Ben and ran to him. She grabbed the goat's horn and pushed him away. She checked Ben and saw that his shirt was torn and dirty. She hugged him and said, "Are you okay, Ben? I'm sorry, the goat was very naughty. He should not eat your shirt. He should only eat grass and hay."
Ben nodded and said, "I'm okay, Mom. But I'm sad. The goat ruined my shirt. He was not nice. He was not jolly like the other animals."
Mom said, "I know, Ben. But you know what? You can still be jolly. You can still be kind and feed the other animals. You can still have fun at the farm. And you can still learn from this. Next time, you will be more careful and listen to me when I tell you about the animals. You will not get too close to the goat's horn. You will remember that not all animals are the same. Some are friendly, some are naughty. Some are jolly, some are not. You have to respect them and their differences."
Ben said, "Okay, Mom. I will do that. I will be more careful and listen to you. I will respect the animals and their differences. I will still be jolly and kind and feed them. Thank you, Mom. I love you."
Mom said, "I love you too, Ben. You are a good boy. Come on, let's go and find a new shirt for you. And then we can feed the cows, the pigs, the sheep and the chickens. They are waiting for you. They are jolly and kind and they like you."
Ben smiled and said, "Okay, Mom. Let's go. I like them too. They are my friends."
The end.

One night, Lily sneaked out of her bed and crawled into her crib. She hugged her teddy bear and closed her eyes. She pretended she was a baby again. She made soft noises and sucked her thumb.
But then she heard a loud noise. It was her brother Max. He came into her room and saw her in the crib. He laughed and said, "Lily, what are you doing? You are not a baby. You are a big girl. You have a bed. Why are you in the crib?"
Lily opened her eyes and felt embarrassed. She did not want Max to see her act like a baby. She said, "I was just playing. I like my crib. It is warm and cozy. Go away, Max. You are mean."
Max shook his head and said, "Lily, you are silly. You are too big for the crib. You will break it. Come on, get out of the crib and go to your bed. I will help you."
Lily did not want to leave her crib. But she knew Max was right. She was too big for the crib. She said, "Okay, fine. But don't laugh at me. And don't tell Mom and Dad."
Max smiled and said, "Okay, okay. I won't laugh. And I won't tell. But you have to promise me something. You have to act like a big girl from now on. No more crib. Deal?"
Lily nodded and said, "Deal." She gave her teddy bear a kiss and handed it to Max. He helped her out of the crib and tucked her into her bed. He said, "Good night, Lily. Sleep tight. You are a big girl now."
Lily said, "Good night, Max. Thank you. You are a good brother." She felt warm and cozy in her bed. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She did not act like a baby anymore. She was a big girl now.

"What was that?" asked Joe.
Mommy looked out the window. "It was probably just a bird, sweetheart," she said.

He slowly stepped out, but before he could take another step, Joe felt a sharp pain in his toe. He had stepped on something that made him hurt. He quickly pulled away and hopped back into his bedroom, where Mommy and Daddy were waiting.

Mommy hugged him tight and kissed his forehead. "It's okay, sweetheart. Let's go back to bed now."

Once there was a girl and her name was Sandy. She was very smart and wanted to go on an adventure. So one day she packed up a bag and stepped outside.
Sandy walked and walked for what felt like miles. She soon came across a river bank, but it was much too wide for her to jump across.
Sandy was about to turn around and go home, when she heard a strange noise. She looked up and saw a creature lying in the middle of the river.
Sandy asked the creature, “what are you doing?”
The creature replied, “I'm trying to spoil this inch, but I keep slipping and can't get across it.”
Sandy smiled and showed the creature a clever trick she had learned. She tied a rope to two tall trees and pulled them taut. Then she made a bridge across the river. Sandy said, “Now you can cross this inch and spoil it!”
The creature thanked Sandy and they both crossed the bridge together. Soon the inch was spoiled and Sandy and the creature went their separate ways. Sandy went home feeling smart and happy, having helped the creature across the river.

The lion showed Ella a small creaky door and said, "Come, you can escape through that door." But the door had a big, hard lock. Ella tried hard to open it, but it would not open. 
The lion then said, "Hold still, and I will open the door for you." The lion snapped the lock in two and the door opened! Ella was so happy and she ran away through the door.

Sam was a boy who liked to play with his cars and his blocks. He had long hair that covered his eyes and ears. His mom said he needed a haircut, but Sam did not want one. He was scared of the scissors and the noise.
"Sam, it's time to go to the barber shop," his mom said. "You will look so nice with a haircut."
"No, no, no!" Sam cried. "I don't want a haircut! I like my hair!"
"Come on, Sam, don't be afraid. The barber is very friendly and gentle. He will give you a sticker and a lollipop when he is done. And you can bring your favorite car with you."
Sam still did not want to go, but he saw his mom was sad. He did not want to make his mom sad. He loved his mom. He decided to be brave and try a haircut.
"Okay, mom, I will go with you. But I want to keep some of my hair."
"Of course, Sam, you can keep some of your hair. You can choose how much you want to cut. Let's go, then."
Sam and his mom went to the barber shop. Sam was nervous, but he held his car tightly. The barber smiled at him and said his name.
"Hello, Sam, I'm Bob. I'm going to give you a nice haircut. Don't worry, it won't hurt at all. You can tell me how you want your hair to look."
Sam looked at the barber and said, "I want to keep some of my hair. I don't want it too short."
"Sure, Sam, no problem. I will just trim a little bit, so you can see better and hear better. You will still have plenty of hair. You are very brave, Sam."
The barber started to cut Sam's hair. Sam felt the scissors snip snip snip, but it did not hurt. He heard the noise buzz buzz buzz, but it was not too loud. He saw his hair fall on the floor, but he still had some on his head. He was brave.
"Wow, Sam, you look great!" his mom said. "You have a very nice haircut. You are so handsome!"
Sam looked in the mirror and saw his new haircut. He liked it. He could see his eyes and his ears. He felt his hair and it was soft and smooth. He smiled.
"Thank you, Bob," he said. "You are a good barber. I like my haircut."
"You're welcome, Sam," Bob said. "You are a good boy. You were very brave. Here is your sticker and your lollipop. Come back anytime."
Sam took his sticker and his lollipop and hugged his mom. He was happy. He had a haircut and he was brave. He was proud of himself.

One day, Lily and Tom went to the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw many things at the beach, like shells, crabs, and birds.
"Look, mom, look!" Lily said, pointing at the sea. "There is a big wave!"
Mom looked and saw a huge wave coming towards the shore. It was taller than the trees and the houses. It was a giant wave!
"Wow, that is a giant wave!" mom said. "But don't worry, it won't hurt us. It is just a silly wave. It likes to make noise and splash, but it will go back to the sea soon."
Lily and Tom laughed. They thought the wave was silly too. They waved at the wave and said, "Hello, silly wave! You are very big and loud, but we are not scared of you. We like to play at the beach!"
The wave heard them and smiled. It was happy that the children were not afraid of it. It wanted to play with them too. It made a smaller wave and sent it to the shore. The smaller wave reached the children and tickled their feet.
"Ha ha ha!" Lily and Tom giggled. "The wave tickled us! Thank you, silly wave! You are very fun and nice!"
The wave nodded and winked. It was glad that the children liked it. It made another smaller wave and sent it to the shore. The smaller wave brought some shells and crabs for the children to see.
"Wow, look, mom, look!" Tom said, picking up a shell. "The wave gave us a gift! It is a pretty shell!"
Mom smiled and said, "That is very kind of the wave. It is a good friend. Let's say thank you to the wave."
Lily and Tom nodded and said, "Thank you, silly wave! You are a good friend. We like you very much!"
The wave beamed and said, "You are welcome, Lily and Tom. You are good friends too. I like you very much too!"
They all smiled and waved at each other. They had a wonderful day at the beach.

"Wow, it's so pretty. Can we fly it?" Max said.
"Sure, why not? It's available. No one is using it," Lily said.
They grabbed the kite and ran to the edge of the roof. They threw the kite in the air and watched it soar. They felt happy and free.
"Look, we can fly the kite. It's so fun," Lily said.
"Yes, it is. We're like birds," Max said.

They screamed and cried. They were hurt and scared.
Mom heard them and ran to the barn. She saw them lying on the ground, covered in mud and blood. She was shocked and worried.

She was also relieved and grateful. She was glad they were alive and not too badly hurt. She loved them very much.
She hoped they learned their lesson. She hoped they would be more careful and listen to her.
She hoped they would still love to play outside. But not on the roof. And not with kites.

Lily was sick. She had a bad cough and a hot head. She stayed in bed and drank water. Her mom said she had to take medicine to feel better.
But Lily did not like medicine. It was bitter and made her face scrunch up. She tried to hide under the blanket when her mom came with a spoon.
"Lily, you have to take your medicine. It will help you work your cough away," her mom said.
"No, no, no! I don't want it! It's yucky!" Lily said.
Her mom smiled and hugged her. "I know, sweetie. But it's only a little bit. And I have a surprise for you after you take it. Something sweet and yummy."
Lily looked at her mom with curious eyes. "What is it?"
Her mom whispered in her ear. "A chocolate chip cookie."
Lily's eyes lit up. She loved cookies. She decided to be brave and take the medicine. She opened her mouth and swallowed the bitter liquid. She made a funny face and stuck out her tongue.
"Good girl! You did it!" her mom praised her. She gave her a kiss and a cookie. "Here you go. This will make the bitter go away."
Lily smiled and took a big bite of the cookie. It was soft and warm and melted in her mouth. She felt happy and cozy. She thanked her mom and cuddled with her.
"Maybe medicine is not so bad," she thought. "If I get a cookie after."

Once upon a time there was a bear called Barry. Barry was feeling very ill and could not breathe properly.
His friend, Cat, asked him what was wrong. 
Barry replied, “My lung is not working properly.”
Cat suggested, “Let’s go the doctor to get you fixed up.”
So they went to the doctor's office. 
The doctor told Barry, “I am going to attach a special machine to your shoulder to make sure your lung is safe.” 
Barry was very scared so Cat hugged him and said, “It’s ok, the doctor will make sure you are safe.” 
After a few minutes, the doctor said, “Barry, your lung is safe now. You can go home.” 
Barry smiled and thanked the doctor for making him feel better. 
Then, Barry and Cat went home and were very happy. 
The End.

"Okay, Mom," said Lily. "I will share my spaghetti. But can I have some more cheese and sauce?"
"Of course, Lily," said Mom. "You are a good girl. Here you go."
Lily smiled. She gave some of her spaghetti to Mom and Dad. They thanked her and praised her. They ate together and enjoyed their meal. Lily was not angry anymore. She was happy. She fit in her family. She loved spaghetti.

Ben and Lily went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and make castles and shapes. They had a bucket and a shovel and some cups and spoons.
"Look, Ben, I found a crab!" Lily said, holding a small red crab in her hand. "He has big claws and eyes on sticks. Do you want to see?"
Ben nodded and ran over to Lily. He looked at the crab and touched it gently. "He is hard and rough," he said. "Can we keep him?"
"No, we can't keep him," Mom said, coming over to them. "He belongs to the sea. We have to let him go. But we can make him a friend. Do you want to help me?"
Ben and Lily said yes and followed Mom to the water. Mom filled the bucket with water and sand and stirred it with a spoon. "We are going to mix the water and the sand to make mud," she said. "Mud is soft and smooth and sticky. We can use it to make a crab shape."
Mom poured some mud on the sand and shaped it into a round body. Then she added four legs on each side and two claws in front. She used a cup to make eyes and a spoon to make a mouth. "There, we made a mud crab," she said. "He looks like your crab, Lily. Do you like him?"
Lily smiled and nodded. She put her crab next to the mud crab and said, "Hello, crab. This is your friend. He is made of mud. He is smooth and nice. Do you want to play with him?"
The crab waved his claws and blinked his eyes. He seemed to like the mud crab. Ben and Lily clapped and laughed. They were happy to make a new friend for the crab. They played with the crabs until it was time to go home. They said goodbye to the crabs and put them back in the water. They hoped they would see them again.

Lily and Max were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a doll and Max had a car. They were having fun until Max saw Lily's doll and wanted it.
"Give me your doll!" Max demanded. "It is pretty and has a dress."
"No!" Lily said. "It is mine and I like it. You have your car."
"But I want your doll too!" Max said. He tried to grab the doll from Lily, but she held it tight.
"Stop it, Max!" Lily said. "You are being mean and rude. You can't have everything."
They started to fight over the doll, pulling and pushing. They made a lot of noise and mess.
Their mom heard them and came to the living room. She was not happy.
"What is going on here?" she asked. "Why are you fighting?"
"Lily won't share her doll with me!" Max said.
"Max wants to take my doll!" Lily said.
Mom looked at the doll and the car. She had an idea.
"Do you know where these toys came from?" she asked.
They shook their heads.
"These toys are very old and special. They belonged to your grandma and grandpa when they were little. They are ancient toys. They gave them to you because they love you and want you to enjoy them."
Lily and Max looked at the toys with surprise. They did not know they were ancient.
"They are ancient?" Lily asked.
"Yes, they are. And they are very precious. You should take good care of them and share them with each other. That is what grandma and grandpa would want. How about you take turns playing with them? You can play with the doll for one minute, and then Max can play with it for one minute. And the same with the car. Does that sound fair?"
Lily and Max nodded. They felt sorry for fighting.
"OK, mom. We will share and take turns. We are sorry for being loud and messy." they said.
Mom smiled and hugged them.
"That's good. I'm glad you are sorry and you learned something. Now, let's clean up this mess and then you can play nicely with your ancient toys." she said.

Tom and Sue cried. They did not know what to do. They wished their dad was home. He would scare the cat away.

"Leave Fluffy alone!" Spot said. "He is my friend. You are a bad and cowardly cat. You can't bully him. You have to face me!"
The cat was surprised and afraid. It saw Spot's teeth and heard his bark. It knew it could not win. It let go of the cage and ran away.
Tom and Sue cheered. They hugged Spot and thanked him. They opened the cage and took out Fluffy. They petted him and gave him a carrot.
"Fluffy, you are safe!" Tom said. "Spot saved you!"
"Spot, you are a hero!" Sue said. "You chased the cat away!"
Fluffy was happy. He licked Spot's nose and said, "Spot, you are a good and kind dog. You are my friend too. Thank you!"

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the park, share their toys and help each other. One day, they saw a big slide in the park. It looked fun, but also scary. Ben wanted to try it, but Lily was afraid.
"Come on, Lily, it's not hard. I'll go first and show you. Trust me, you'll like it," Ben said.
He climbed up the ladder and slid down the slide. He laughed and waved at Lily. "See? It's fun! Your turn!"
Lily hesitated. She wanted to be brave, but she also wanted to stay safe. She looked at the slide and felt nervous. She looked at Ben and felt sad. He was her friend, but he was also pushing her.
"No, Ben, I don't want to. It's too high. I want to stay here," Lily said.
Ben frowned. He didn't understand why Lily was so scared. He thought she was being silly and stubborn. He wanted her to join him and have fun. He thought she was missing out.
"Lily, you're being a baby. Don't you want to have fun? Don't you trust me? Come on, it's easy. You're gifted, you can do anything," Ben said.
He tried to pull her hand and make her climb the ladder. Lily resisted. She felt angry and hurt. He was her friend, but he was also hurting her.
"Ben, stop it! You're being mean. I don't want to go. I don't have to do everything you do. I have my own choices. You're not gifted, you're bossy," Lily said.
She pushed him away and ran to the swings. Ben was shocked and sorry. He realized he had been wrong. He had not respected Lily's feelings and choices. He had not been a good friend.
He ran after her and apologized. "Lily, I'm sorry. I was mean. I should have listened to you. You don't have to go on the slide if you don't want to. You're still my friend. You're still gifted. Can we play together?"
Lily looked at him and smiled. She forgave him. She knew he was sorry. She knew he was still her friend. She knew he was still gifted.
"Sure, Ben. I'm sorry too. I should have told you how I felt. You're still my friend. You're still gifted. Let's play together," Lily said.
They hugged and went to the swings. They learned to trust each other and respect each other. They learned to stay friends and have fun. They learned to be gifted and kind.

One day, they saw a big elephant with long tusks and a trunk. Lily wanted to take a picture of it, but Ben was scared. He said, "No, Lily, it is too scary. It might hurt us. Let's go away."
But Lily did not listen. She said, "No, Ben, it is not scary. It is beautiful. I want to take a picture. You stay here with the sack. I will be back soon." She ran towards the elephant with the camera.
Ben was very worried. He watched Lily get closer and closer to the elephant. He saw the elephant raise its trunk and make a loud noise. He thought the elephant was angry. He shouted, "Lily, come back! Come back!"
But Lily did not hear him. She was too busy taking pictures. She smiled and said, "Wow, what a great picture. I am so brave."
Suddenly, she heard a rustle behind her. She turned around and saw a big monkey. The monkey had a naughty look on its face. It grabbed the sack from Ben and ran away. It opened the sack and took out the food and water. It ate the sandwiches and drank the juice. It threw the empty bottles and wrappers on the ground.
Lily and Ben were very sad. They had no food and water left. They had to go back to their dad and tell him what happened. Their dad was not happy. He said, "You should have listened to Ben, Lily. He was right. The elephant was scary. You were lucky it did not hurt you. And you should have stayed with the sack, Ben. You should have protected it from the monkey. You were careless. You wasted the food and water. You made a mess. You have to learn to be careful and respectful when you go on safari. The animals are not toys. They are wild and free. You have to respect them and their home."
Lily and Ben felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, dad. We learned our lesson. We will be careful and respectful next time. We will not be brave or careless. We will be smart and kind."
Their dad hugged them and said, "I love you, twins. I am glad you are safe. I hope you enjoyed the safari. But next time, please listen to me and to each other. And please, do not forget the sack."

She runs to her mom and dad and tells them what happened. They say, "We are sorry, Lily. The parrot did not know. It is not polite to break things. But it is also not polite to yell. Maybe you can teach the parrot to be nice."
Lily thinks. She says, "OK. I will try." She goes back to the parrot and says, "Hello, parrot. I am Lily. Do you want to be my friend?" The parrot says, "Hello, Lily. I am Polly. Yes, I want to be your friend." Lily smiles.
She says, "Friends do not break things. Friends share things. Do you want to share my crayons?" The parrot says, "Yes, I want to share your crayons." Lily gives the parrot a crayon and they draw together. They draw a ball and a dog and a flower. Lily is happy.
She says, "You are a good parrot, Polly. You are polite." The parrot says, "You are a good girl, Lily. You are polite." They hug. Lily is happy.

Tommy liked to play in the garden with his dog, Spot. Spot had a long, furry tail that he wagged when he was happy. Tommy liked to chase Spot and pull his tail, but Spot did not like that. He barked and ran away from Tommy.
One day, Tommy saw some new flowers in the garden. They were pink and purple and smelled nice. Tommy was curious. He wanted to touch the flowers and see if they were soft. He walked towards the flowers, but Spot followed him. Spot was curious too.
"Spot, no!" Tommy said. "These are not for you. These are for Mommy. She likes flowers. They make her smile."
But Spot did not listen. He ran past Tommy and jumped on the flowers. He bit them and tore them with his teeth. He wagged his tail and made a mess.
"Spot, bad dog!" Tommy shouted. "You ruined the flowers! Mommy will be sad!"
Tommy tried to stop Spot, but it was too late. The flowers were all gone. They were only stems and petals on the ground. Tommy felt bad. He loved his dog, but he also loved his mommy. He did not know what to do.
Then he heard his mommy's voice. She was coming back from the store. She had a big bag in her hand.
"Tommy, Spot, I'm home!" she said. "Guess what I have for you?"
Tommy and Spot ran to meet her. They hoped she would not see the garden. They hoped she would not be angry.
"Mommy, look what I have!" she said. She opened the bag and took out a big, colorful bouquet of flowers. "I saw these at the market and I thought of you. They are so pretty and they smell so good. Do you like them?"
Tommy and Spot looked at the flowers. They were the same as the ones in the garden. They were pink and purple and smelled nice. Tommy felt happy. He hugged his mommy and said, "Thank you, Mommy! I love you! I love the flowers!"
Spot wagged his tail and licked his mommy's face. He said, "Woof, woof! I love you too! I love the flowers!"
Mommy smiled and said, "I love you both! You are my sweet boys! Come on, let's go inside and find a vase for the flowers. They will look beautiful in the living room."
Tommy and Spot followed her. They did not tell her about the garden. They decided to keep it a secret. They were glad that Mommy had bought more flowers. They were glad that she was happy. They learned a lesson. They would not touch the flowers again. They would only look at them and smell them. They would let them bloom and grow.

"OK!" Tom said. "I have pepper and salt and bread."
They put everything in the pot and stirred it with the spoons. They smelled the soup and smiled.
"It smells good!" Tom said. "Can we taste it?"
"Yes!" Lily said. "But be careful, it might be hot."
They each took a spoonful of soup and put it in their mouths. Lily liked it. It was sweet and creamy. But Tom made a funny face. He spit out the soup and coughed.
"Yuck!" Tom said. "It's spicy and rough!"
Lily looked at the pot. She saw a lot of black dots in the soup. She realized that Tom had put too much pepper in it. Pepper was spicy and rough. It made Tom's mouth hurt.
"I'm sorry, Tom!" Lily said. "I didn't know you put pepper in it. Do you want some water?"
"Yes, please!" Tom said. "And some bread. Bread is soft and nice."
Lily got some water and bread for Tom. She gave him a hug and said sorry again. Tom drank the water and ate the bread. He felt better.
"It's OK, Lily," Tom said. "We can make soup again. But next time, let's use less pepper. OK?"
"OK!" Lily said. "And more cheese. Cheese is yummy!"
They laughed and hugged. They were still friends. They liked to play in the kitchen. But they learned to be careful with pepper.

The rabbit said, "Let's separate it. We can each keep half". The duck thought it was a good idea and agreed. So, the rabbit and duck carefully split the oil between them. The duck put his half in his pocket and the rabbit put her half in her pocket. Now, both the rabbit and the duck had some oil to keep. They were both very happy but especially the poor rabbit because now she had something special and it was something that only the rich duck had before. They smiled and laughed together for the rest of the day.

One day, a man with a big mustache was eager to restore his old toy car. The toy car was red and shiny, but it was broken. The man wanted to make it like new again. He tried to fix it with glue, but the glue did not work.
The man asked his friend Tom, "Can you help me fix my toy car?" Tom said, "I can try, but I am not good with cars." They tried together to fix the toy car, but it was still broken.
The man was sad, but he did not give up. He went to the store to find something that could fix his toy car. He found a special tool and brought it home. With the special tool, the man and Tom worked together to fix the toy car. Finally, the toy car was like new again. The man with the big mustache was very happy, and he thanked his friend Tom for helping him.

Once upon a time, there was a big, thick tree. The tree had brown skin. It lived in a green park with many friends. The friends were small trees, flowers, and animals.
One day, the big, thick tree saw a little bird. The little bird was sad. It could not find a home. The big, thick tree decided to help the little bird. The tree said, "Little bird, you can live with me."
The little bird was happy. It made a nest in the big, thick tree's skin. The little bird and the big, thick tree became good friends. They played and sang together every day.
Soon, more animals came to live with the big, thick tree. The tree was happy to help all its friends. The park was full of love and laughter. The big, thick tree and its friends lived happily ever after.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park. But they do not like the same things. Sara likes to swing high and slide fast. Ben likes to dig in the sand and build castles.
One day, they go to the park with their mom. Mom says they can have a picnic. She has a basket with sandwiches, apples, and cookies. Sara and Ben are happy. They run to the big tree and sit on the blanket.
Mom gives them each a sandwich. Sara takes a big bite. She makes a face. She spits out the sandwich. "Yuck!" she says. "This is spicy! I hate spicy!"
Ben looks at his sandwich. He smells it. He smiles. He takes a big bite. He likes it. "This is yummy!" he says. "I love spicy!"
Sara and Ben look at each other. They do not understand. How can they like different things? They are twins!
Mom laughs. She says, "It's okay to like different things. You are twins, but you are not the same. You have different tastes. Sara, your sandwich has mustard. That is spicy. Ben, your sandwich has ketchup. That is not spicy. Do you want to trade?"
Sara and Ben nod. They trade their sandwiches. They take a bite. They are happy. They say, "Thank you, mom!"
Mom says, "You're welcome, my loves. Now, do you want to play some more?"
Sara and Ben say, "Yes, please!"
